name: Bigger Linda

entries: Thundering through the streets of Drakkenheim with a crash, the infamous pet of the Queen of Thieves has mutated and enlarged to unfathomable proportions. The Haze swirls around it, and octarine energy pulses in its sunken eye sockets. The broken hafts of weapons and old arrows are embedded into its scales, stuck deeply between its regenerated flesh. Its spined back is illuminated by webs of glowing octarine veins; its wide snout is filled with jagged teeth. As it opens its maw wide, the building contaminated energy at the back of its throat begins to glow.

If {@creature Big Linda|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} ever escapes the confines of the {@creature Queen of Thieves|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}, the beast will no doubt return to the ruins of Drakkenheim and immediately seek out new hunting grounds. However, Big Linda's containment has stunted her true growth potential. Once freed, the longer Big Linda spends directly exposed to the energies the Haze, the more she grows. As she grows, new mutations begin to form, further amplifying her ferocity, predatory senses, and resilience. If left unchecked, Big Linda might become the apex predator of Drakkenheim—Bigger Linda.

name: Bilbo Baggins

entries: ...he looked and behaved exactly like a second edition of his solid and comfortable father, got something a bit queer in his make-up from the Took side, something that only waited for a chance to come out.

In the year 2965, Bilbo is a vigorous Hobbit—At seventy-five he is very much the same as he was at fifty, at the time of his remarkable disappearance and surprising return. On the surface, the son of Bungo Baggins and Belladonna Took is a prime example of a respectable Hobbit. He is a great lover of pipe-weed, good food, and fine waistcoats, and lives in one of the cosiest Hobbit-holes in the Shire. But this is not all there is to Mr Baggins.

Bilbo's unexpected journey with Thorin Oakenshield and company changed him profoundly, setting him apart from his fellow countrymen. Perhaps that adventure provided a spark that ignited his Tookish and more adventurous side, and he certainly returned from Erebor a wealthier Hobbit. All this estranged him from much of the (admittedly tedious) Shire society, leading him to focus on his own, peculiar lifestyle, the company of friends, and working on his diary.

Twenty years after his great adventure, Bilbo remains curious about news from outside the Shire, and is always gathering rumours and bits of lore to add to his personal records—he is planning to turn his private diary into a real book.

entries.name: Encountering Bilbo
entries: The Bagginses have lived in the neighbourhood of The Hill from time out of mind, and Bilbo has no desire to break that long-standing tradition. His address is at Bag End, Underhill, Hobbiton, and it's at Bag End that the Hobbit is likely to be found, probably having tea, or standing at the door, smoking a {@item pipe|TLotRR}. That said, his experiences with Thorin's Company and a Dragon have awakened in him a certain appetite for adventure, and sometimes he stays away from home for much longer than is considered appropriate in the Shire. When travelling further away than Buckland, or Michel Delving, he is often in the company of Dwarves.

If encountered outside the Shire, Bilbo might carry his Elf-dagger, Sting, sheathed at his side. But he has yet to encounter a danger that might require him to use it—if threatened, the Hobbit displays an uncanny ability to disappear almost instantly, a talent far outstripping the normal Hobbitish affinity for escaping notice. He always remembers to bring a {@item pocket-handkerchief|TLotRR} along.

entries.name: Bilbo as a Patron
entries: Unbeknownst to his fellow Hobbits who just consider him to be strange, if not completely mad, Bilbo knows a lot about the world outside the Shire, and is well aware of its dangers. He keeps himself as informed as he can, exchanging tidings with travellers and by writing and receiving letters. When he learns about potential threats that might affect the Shire, he does what he can to enlist the help of anyone who might do something about it.

Being a Hobbit of considerable means, Bilbo is all too happy to arrange hospitality, finance expeditions, and to generally encourage those who would dare to go out and have adventures. He provides support merely in return for a good story and perhaps a souvenir or keepsake—he is especially interested in maps, and geographical lore in general, which he uses to amend his own charts.

Contrary to this inclination towards hosting a veritable rogues gallery of guests from far afield, he is growing increasingly isolated when it comes to his fellow Hobbits. He finds them staid, close-minded, and demonstrates little patience for their shenanigans and petty foibles. To the eyes of the Shire-folk, Bilbo is becoming more and more an eccentric recluse.

rows: By choosing the {@action Meet Patron|TLotRR} undertaking to visit Bilbo you additionally raise the Fellowship rating by +1 until the next Fellowship Phase.

entries.name: Bilbo's Magic Ring
entries: Bilbo found many valuable things in the course of his last adventure, but the greatest treasure he brought back is one he doesn't know much about. It's the magic ring he found in an underground cave, under the Misty Mountains, and that he has kept a great secret. To him, it's a precious commodity, as wearing it makes him {@condition invisible}—a quality that Bilbo finds invaluable when unpleasant callers come looking for him.

This ring has been in Bilbo's possession for more than twenty years now, and what in the beginning seemed nothing more than a curiosity to the Hobbit is slowly developing a growing hold over his mind. He keeps it in the pocket of his waistcoat upon a fine silver chain at all times, and has developed the habit of slipping a finger or two in the pocket to touch it, as if to reassure himself that it's still there.
{@i An impossibly thin figure passes through the trees, its skin and clothes formed of curling silver birch bark. The autumn leaves that adorn its crown whisper strangely in the breeze.}

Birch sirens are a less common variety of treant that often live together in family units called copses. These sirens are more malicious than their larger counterparts and delight in luring travelers deeper into dangerous woodland with their haunting melodies.

entries.name: Shadow Wood
entries: The largest population of birch sirens lives in the Shadow Realm, in the rarely traveled portions of forest that span the region. Occasionally, birch sirens are coerced to lend aid and protection to shadow fey rangers who hunt such dangerous woods.

entries.name: Elven Origins
entries: Birch sirens are rumored to have been created by the magic of the elves. These tree-folk were once guardians of vast orchards and beautiful gardens, contributing to the wonder of such places with their alluring songs. When the elves began to fade from the world, so too did the purpose of the birch sirens, and now they exist as cruel shadows of their former selves.

name: Birdfolk Dockmaster
entries: It may be odd to see birdfolk working the docks and ships of Saltar's Port, but the sea is a way of life for some folk. Jobs in the seafaring industry are as lucrative as they are tough. For the birdfolk that choose to ply their trade on the water, life is about order and efficiency. One improperly stowed barrel or poorly lashed line can spell disaster on the sea. Dockmasters take their marine jobs very seriously.

name: Birdfolk Farmer
entries: Simple farmers can be found across the Wood, providing necessary food and supplies to the cities. There are many places in Humblewood where digging up large heaps of soil would either be impractical or damaging to the forest. While traditional farms exists in Humblewood, the majority of farms are built in the canopies in or around cities. Farming in the canopy consists of growing flowering
moss gardens or fruit-bearing vines on the branches of perch trees. Canopy farms can also include the raising of large insects for food, or silkworms for clothing.

name: Birdfolk Guard
entries: Aspiring recruits from all over the Wood flock to the Perch Guard headquarters in the capital of Alderheart to join their ranks. After successful training, these newly sworn guards return to their home perch. They serve with pride, acting as the perch's first line of defense. Under the Humblefolk Treaty, members of the Perch Guard are tasked to aid nearby villages on the forest floor whenever necessary. In larger cities like Alderheart, the Perch Guard are also responsible for dealing with inner city issues such as robbery, bar fights, and investi-gating and arresting criminals.

name: Birdfolk Militia
entries: In smaller perches, where a guard force may be minimal or nonexistent, town security consists of a locally-organized militia. Anyone can enlist in these groups, provided they are upstanding citizens. They can be called upon by the Perch Guard to perform duties ranging from policing streets to supplementing military efforts.

name: Birdfolk Sailor
entries: For birdfolk who take up the seafaring trade, their home is as much on the ocean as it is at port. They relish the salt spray and stiff winds, finding the closed spaces of forest life to be stifling compared to the wide-open expanse of the sea.

entries.name: Peculiar Design
entries: Birdfolk ship design often causes confusion among other seafaring races due to the relative absence of rigging. While cordage is needed to keep sails in place and cargo stored, nets and climbing ropes prove less necessary when the crew is capable of limited flight. A birdfolk sailor can simply lash a rope to their leg, open their wings, and let the ocean breeze carry them up to the sails or to a lookout post on the main mast.

name: Birdfolk Skeleton
entries: Deceased birdfolk granted a semblance of life through necromantic spells don't have memory per se, but their skeletal bodies retain familiarity with tasks they performed in life. They also remain skilled with weapons they wielded in life, making them useful guards or servants.

entries.name: Unnatural Life
entries: Animated skeletons are common among the practitioners of the necromantic arts. Even at the Avium, where necromancy is forbidden in practice, it is taught in theory. A common exception is the use of animated skeletons for menial tasks around the college. The reanimation of birdfolk who did not give their express consent in life is seen as a violation of their memory, so these skeletons usually consist of former college staff who desired to stay and help long past their own time. Not all scholars agree that even this relatively benign form of necromancy should be allowed, while others don't see why permission from the dead should be necessary, believing that "dead is dead". Though the consent policy remains in place, heady debates over the ethics of certain forms of necromancy have resulted in the shunning of more morally flexible scholars.

name: Birdfolk Skirmisher
entries: The bulk of the Perch Guard's military force are a light infantry called "The Spears." They train relentlessly with polearm weapons perfectly suited for branch-to-branch combat. Many are also skilled at ranged attacks with these weapons, as well as performing special diving maneuvers, making them an even greater threat to enemies below. In times of peace, skirmishers often serve as skilled hunters, following the direction of trackers to collect enough food for entire villages.

Birdfolk in need of coin and lacking any moral scruples can find lucrative work as hired henchmen for one of Alderheart's various criminal factions. These common thugs often fight dirty, and are quick to flee when things don't go their way.

name: Bita, the Council Speaker
entries: Bita is a bright gallus whose elegant white plumage resembles that of a peacock. As the Birdfolk Council's Speaker, she is always first to address those who have been granted an audience with the Council. She takes her duties as the Speaker and as a Council member very seriously. Despite her profound affection for Humblewood and its citizens, she often comes off as severe and cold. Bita believes in doing what's best for the folks of the Wood, and sometimes this means making level-headed, tough decisions. Bita uses the {@creature noble} stat block, adjusted with the racial traits of a bright gallus. She is lawful good.

_copy.name: The Company of the Black Crown

entries: Palest Westruun was not a king, but his new statue in the Opal Ward is often called the {@creature Black King|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}, a subtle jab at the city's previous "Black King," the tyrannical dragon Umbrasyl. The high priest of the First Bastion blessed both the {@creature Black King|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} and {@book Westruun|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Westruun} itself when the statue was unveiled on the anniversary of {@book Westruun's|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Westruun} reclamation, saying, "May the {@deity The Lawbearer|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|Lawbearer} grant us all strength of spirit when chaos next threatens our peaceful civilization. When that time comes, may the {@creature Black King|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} unsheathe his sword to rally our people and lead {@book Westruun|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Westruun} to victory."

When the safety of all of {@book Westruun|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Westruun} is threatened, the {@creature Black King|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} will animate and defend its people, becoming a {@creature Black King|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|stone golem with a speed of 60 feet, Charisma and Intelligence scores of 18 (+4), and the ability to speak Common}. Its personality is dour but determined—regal and single-minded in its desire to protect its city and its people.
{@note See {@book The Black King|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|7. The Black King} for more information on this NPC.}

The black knight commander strikes an imposing figure upon its chosen mount; one that inspires bloodlust in its allies and fear in its foes. Devoted to its own twisted code, the black knight commander has a sense of honor but spares no compassion for those who stand in its way. Whether the knight fights for a dark lord or a demonic god, all its foes will be trampled into the dust and their families slaughtered so there can be no revenge. The only victory is a total victory.

items.name: Blackjack Mel

entries: A short and scrawny man in his late thirties stands before you with a funny-looking but clean-shaven mug and greasy slickedback hair. He wears a black padded jacket and buckled slacks that appear distinguished at first glance but are actually quite shabby and worn.

Blackjack Mel is the Queen of Thieves most trusted advisor. That is to say that she doesn't trust him at all, but knows that he is afraid of her, and will do her bidding as long as she pays him more than others. She pays in protection and a good position. No one is more manipulated by the Queen of Thieves' than Blackjack Mel, who handles much of her communications and business deals with the local gangs.

entries.name: Personality Trait
entries: I can always make a deal with the right angle, I just gotta pitch it the right way. I don't give up when the mark doesn't take the bait, just try something new!

entries.name: Ideal
entries: We're all in this for ourselves. You scratch my back, I'll scratch yours.

entries.name: Bond
entries: Listen, I got some close connections with some powerful people. You wanna meet the Queen of Thieves? Stick with me. We'll go places together. Just uh, watch out you don't piss anyone off, okay?

entries.name: Flaw
entries: I'm a compulsive liar, so what? Yeah, sometimes even
I get confused by my own lies, but the truth can always do with a little exaggeration, it makes life more interesting

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Blackjack Mel is a coward, a swindler, and a thief. He is often surrounded by Thugs and Assassins who protect him; Mel rarely draws a blade. His overconfidence relies on his company, and he will often only take a stab at someone if they are held down.

Mel's first line of defense is his mouth. He will double-cross, backstab, swindle, and con even his allies to ensure his own survival. He knows a lot of information about a lot of things and will use his well of secrets to bargain for his safety. He is also clever and will usually only divulge half of a fact to save his life, ensuring the other half will be granted once his safety is ensured. He knows very well that information is what keeps him alive, and he isn't about to use up that usefulness.
Mel flees without question at any opportunity if he feels threatened, and often keeps a {@item Potion of Invisibility|XDMG} on his person for just such instances.
All bets are off when you're dealing with this thug. He's got info on anything for a price or a threat.
{@i This headless giant has a large mouth in its chest with eyes bulging out on either side of it.}

entries.name: Always Hungry
entries: Blemmyes are brutes that savor humanoid flesh, and they see all humanoids as potential meals. Some even have the patience to tend groups of humans, goblins, or halflings like unruly herds, farming them for food and fattening them up for maximum succulence.

entries.name: Cannibals
entries: So great is their hideous hunger that blemmyes are not above eating their own kind; they cull and consume the weakest specimens of their people when other food is scarce. The most terrible habit of these monsters is that they seldom wait for their food to die, or even for a battle to conclude, before launching into a grisly feast.

name: Bloated Dreg

entries: A gurgling moan emerges from the dark as the slopping footsteps of a bloated form emerges. Its rippling, sagging flesh is wet and dripping. Its rotund face and soggy skin are covered in boils, blisters, and leaking sores. Wet, acidic saliva dribbles down its chin, leaving trails of burned flesh. The Dreg's one arm is a mass of writhing slick tentacles. As its mouth opens, a low gurgling sound slowly builds.

People who are submerged in contaminated water often become Bloated Dregs. These half-drowned unfortunates are found near bodies of water throughout the city, such as the sewers or near the Drann River. They have absorbed so much contaminated water into themselves that it festers and mixes with their stomach acids, producing a corrosive bile that they hurl towards their foes. Often a Bloated Dreg will only leave the water for a few hours before finding another puddle of sludge or a contaminated pool to rest in.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Survival|XPHB} or {@skill Nature|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks to {@action Study|XPHB} a Bloated Dreg, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (5+) Corrupted by Contaminated Water
entries: You know the creature is an Aberration with a Swim speed, and it can breathe underwater.

entries.name: (10+) Slow and Polluted
entries: You recognize the Bloated Dreg's Acid Spray attack.

entries.name: (15+) Mockery of Humanity
entries: You are aware of the Bloated Dreg's highest and lowest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Bloated Dreg shuffles aimlessly through Drakkenheim, stopping to rest in places where contaminated water has built up, or in pools of delerium sludge. It produces large amounts of acidic bile in its guts that it expels when threatened. A Bloated Dreg will retreat to its watery home when threatened, trying to hide amongst the contaminated liquids.

entries: Aberration.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Monster Blood, Contaminated Ichor, Acidic Bile.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Eyes, Heart, Brain, Guts, Flesh.

entries.name: Bones:
entries: Skull, Spine, Ribs.

entries.name: Hair:
entries: Hair.

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Skin.

entries.name: Dust:
entries: Aberrant Dust.
Don't drink the water, don't go into the water, and by no means let the thing that came out of the water bite you!

name: Bloated Gastromorph
entries: Often whispered of in folk tales and legends, most frequently as a warning to children regarding the gruesome consequences awaiting those who recklessly indulge, the Bloated Gastromorph is an incarnation of gluttony and selfishness. This horrific creature has been transformed and twisted by the final stages of a {@spell Curse of Ravenous Hunger|GrimHollowPG24}.

Those afflicted become an enormous, slug-like monster possessing multiple fist-like claws, a wicked tentacular tongue, and a giant, voracious maw of gnashing teeth. Often dwelling in dank ruins of once-great castles, a Bloated Gastromorph cares about nothing but consuming every morsel of flesh it encounters, living or not. Bereft of memories of their prior lives, these creatures dwell fully in this new existence of unfettered consumption.

name: Bloated Hive

entries: Dripping with sweet smelling pus and mucus, the creature shuffles about on spindly limbs like a gangly ape. It has long gnarled fingers and an emaciated whip-cord thin frame. Where there should be a head there is instead a mass of pulsing flesh covered in gaping pores that extend down its neck and across its shoulders. Its body writhes with thousands of bugs crawling beneath its skin and swarming around its head. They burrow in and out of open wounds and sores and buzz in and out of its pores. It smells faintly of honey and sweat, and gurgles painfully amidst the chorus of buzzing and clicking of insects, as if the thing is painfully aware of its wretched state.

The Bloated Hive is a product of contamination that seems to have turned people into walking hives of insects. Some suspect the honey farms on the outskirts may have been the main source of these strange mutations, causing the apiarists and their hives to warp together, fusing into a grotesque and tortured creature. Their upper torso and head are now a writhing mass of open pores like a beehive, with bugs swarming in and out. They lumber around the ruins looking for nesting places where their hive can thrive. Many Bloated Hives operate alone, but sometimes a much more horrifying event occurs, where a single colony begins to occupy multiple Bloated Hives, forming a horrifying network.

The Bloated Hive tends to hide itself in the dark corners of ruins, often seeking the most damp and warm locations in the city. Many hives have been found along the Drann River within the Inner City, a large group of them living under Champion's Bridge, and even more in the sewers, Queen's Park Garden, and a sparse few in the woods to the north of Drakkenheim. Whenever traversing into dark and damp areas in the city, be on the lookout for an increase in insect activity and the sound of buzzing.

A Bloated Hive cannot speak, and acts on the whims of its occupants more so than its own free thought. Its mind is now a broken thing, connected inherently to the hive mind of a swarm of insects, but within that is a tortured human struggling for sentience. Some Bloated Hives have been known to respond to kind words, trinkets of their former selves, or music they recognize. Though these moments of subtle sentience are fleeting, as the hive reacts quickly to the feeling of an unwanted psyche struggling for dominance within the hive mind and could trigger a frenzied tantrum if not handled delicately.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks to {@action Study|XPHB} a Bloated Hive, recognizing the following based on their result:

entries.name: (5+) Sightless Awareness
entries: You know the creature's {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities} and senses.

entries.name: (10+) Endless Insects!
entries: You are aware of the creature's Spawn Swarm action and Disrupt the Hive trait.

entries.name: (15+) Frail
entries: You recognize the Bloated Hive's strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Bloated Hive is usually a solitary creature that spends its time cowering in dark corners living out its cursed life as nothing more than a conduit for its colony. In combat, they focus entirely on keeping their distance from threats and spawning swarms of insects to defend themselves. If cornered, the Bloated Hive uses its Claws and Distracting Swarm before moving back into the shadows and attempting to escape and find a new nest.

Larger packs of Bloated Hives are much braver and more violent, and actively hunt and pursue targets until their numbers are less than their prey. Places where large colonies gather are dangerous. The Bloated Hives work in unison to protect their nests. Only if they become outnumbered do they flee.

name: Blodhamar
entries: Disgruntled giant thinking about his future.
{@b Background:} Former smith to thursir jarl Ulli Wotanson at the Kjothall fortress in Thursrike.
{@b Personality Traits:} Mutters curses in Giant with every swing of the hammer.
{@b Bonds:} His tools and his craft.
{@b Flaws:} Few things smaller than him seem worth his attention.
{@b Wants:} Blodhamar does not care to die in service to the cult. He fights only in self-defense.
{@b Talking to Blodhamar:} He can tell the PCs that Thyrin the Black and the other leaders are in the northwestern tower (Area 23).

items: In exchange for amnesty, Blodhamar agrees to repair the gate mechanism in the gatehouse tower (Area 8), should the PCs succeed on a {@dc 14} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check.
Blodhamar refuses to fight any of the cult's defenders and expects the PCs to protect him in exchange for his service.
Blodhamar can break his chains with an action.

entries: {@i This bent-backed crone has long, leathery arms and cruel, flesh-shearing talons. Her face is a misshapen mass of leathery flesh with a bulbous nose, like a gnarled knot on an old oak tree, and her hair falls in ringlets of wriggling worms.}

Blood hags have long skulked on the fringes of society. The hags prey on mankind, stealing seed to propagate, blood to satisfy their insatiable thirst, and faces as trophies of these short-lived and bloody trysts.

entries.name: Worm Hair
entries: A blood hag's hair is a morass of wriggling worms, ever-thirsty for fresh blood.

items.name: Blood Leech
entries: Although the practice of draining a patient's blood to draw out illness and disease is long discredited, many apothecaries understand the value of transfusing blood during surgical procedures. However, storing the blood long term can be a problem. Apothecaries have solved by modifying normal leeches with occult science, transforming the creatures into living blood bags. While these bloodletting techniques are of dubious therapeutic value to patients, they make an effective method for collecting samples from lessthan-willing subjects.

Though often benign in nature, these bloated leeches can be turned to violent purpose by an apothecary willing to use the creatures in such a manner. During combat, an apothecary may dispatch the leeches against their foes, then call the creatures back to themselves to heal using their foe's blood.

entries.name: Blood Leeches

entries: The black, plump wriggling form of the leech squirms and crawls. Its oily, slick skin is wet and slippery. It lets out a high-pitched screech as it lunges towards its prey.

Leeches are a common creature kept in large quantities in apothecaries' laboratories. Aside from their standard practical uses of bloodletting and transfusions, they have also been the subjects of early apothecary experimentation. Different forms of leeches have been designed to better suit apothecaries' needs. Some Alienists have designed leeches that attach directly to the brain stem, allowing the leech to eat the intellect and thoughts of other creatures. Mutagenists have designed leeches that can harness the arcane energies found in mageborn blood.

items: {@b Leech Variants:} Ambitious apothecaries have used leeches in different ways. There are two mutant variations of the Blood Leech.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Arcana|XPHB} or {@skill Medicine|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks to {@action Study|XPHB} a leech, learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (10+) Quick Swimmers
entries: You know the leech's Swim speed and senses.

entries.name: Blood Leech:(15+) Blood Transfer.
entries: You know of the Blood Leech's Blood Drain and Blood Infusion.

entries.name: Mind Leech:(15+) Brain Eater.
entries: You are aware of the Mind Leech's Mind Leech's Brain Drain and Thought Infusion.

entries.name: Spell Leech: (15+) Arcane Ingestion.
entries: You recognize the Spell Leech's Spell Drain.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Leeches attempt to get close to a target to Bite and Attach to them. They do not retreat, as they are driven by their basic need to feed on the blood of others and nothing else.

entries: Monstrosity.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Monster Blood, Goopy Ooze, Mucus.

entries: Brain, Guts.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Mandibles.

entries: Skin.
Those who've turned their back on both the Seraphs and the Daemons? That way lies madness.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Bloodbonded still possess the damaged and scarred remnants of their past devotions. When a bloodbonded dies, its blood still pulses and gives off light as it did when it was alive. One vial of this blood can be harvested from a single bloodbonded with a successful {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}) check. Drinking it within one day causes the user to be affected by a bless spell. When the spell ends, the user suffers one level of exhaustion.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
items.entry: Bloodbonded are victims of their own foolish choices, worshipping false gods and then being driven mad by the ruse.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
items.entry: Bloodbonded use their followers as weapons, even causing them to explode in a wave of fiery blood, which damages nearby creatures.

name: Bloodmire Treant
entries: The Syre Wood was home to numerous great trees and treants, but the swiftness of the Legion's assault left the forest's defense in the hands of Syre and his sprites. As such, the blood of Malfuriel has rapidly tainted the various treants of the swamp just as it altered the other wildlife. Those unlucky enough to draw a bloodmire treant's ire will face all of nature's wrath as well as the foul blood magic of Malfuriel, as these cursed treants possess the ability to animate pools of bloodwater into ooze-like forms as an additional means of defense.

name: Blowbelly Pufferfish
entries: Blowbelly pufferfish are generally docile creatures but are easily startled. If they feel threatened, they inflate instantly to an enormous size. Anyone touching their prickly skin can get injected with doses of toxins. When a blowbelly pufferfish dies, they burst, sending a spray of poisonous spines in all directions.
Blowbelly pufferfish are often found bobbing along coral reefs and on the sandy bottom of the sea.

name: Bodil
entries: Captive Trollheim warrior

name: Body Snatcher
entries: Body Snatchers are humanoids who have been transformed by a {@spell Curse of Damned Aging|GrimHollowPG24}. Notoriously difficult to locate, Body Snatchers frequently hide in plain sight, since they essentially resemble their host creature. It's common that when on the trail of a Body Snatcher, monster hunters and investigators find themselves trailing a step behind the creature. The only evidence that typically remains is the withered and discarded skin sack of their latest victim.

Body Snatchers possess an amorphous form, which they use to inhabit the bodies of their victims, living inside them as a parasite that consumes their being from the inside. The Body Snatcher takes complete control of its host body, enhancing it with supernatural capabilities. The only sign that an individual has been invaded by a Body Snatcher is their erratic behavior and rapid aging—a host body can appear to age a lifetime in a matter of a few weeks.

While far from helpless, Body Snatchers prefer to avoid detection, engaging enemies only in dire circumstances or when changing hosts. They typically make every effort to complete the latter in seclusion to maintain their gruesome charade.

name: Body Snatcher

entries: This patchwork monster of stitched-together corpses oozes black ichor from its seams. The figure is a hulking form, about 7 feet tall with broad shoulders and a hunched back. Its head seems small compared to its body, with pale white eyes highlighting sunken dark sockets. A lipless mouth forces the creature into a constant menacing grimace. Draped in a thick black trench coat and wide brimmed hat while smelling of sulfur and brimstone, the unsettling humming and mumbling of the creature echoes in the ears of those it is about to grab. The most unsettling feature is the creature's four arms, which end in massive, oversized hands, each with eight long, spindly fingers. The creature shifts from shadow to shadow effortlessly, in a haunting ghost-like fashion unusual for its size.

Stitched together from the remains of numerous corpses and animated through forbidden alchemical processes, the Body Snatcher roams the darkness. Created by a deranged doctor to abduct subjects for gruesome experiments, it lingers in shadows, waiting for unwary travelers to seize and vanish into the night.

Empowered by the night, the Body Snatcher uses shadow to drain the vitality and energy of those it grabs, weakening them as they attempt to resist and escape. Shadows wrap around it, helping it hold its victims in place while it absconds with them into the darkest corners of the night

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Medicine|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks to Study a Body Snatcher, learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (10+) Emotionless Undead
entries: You know the Body Snatcher's condition {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: (15+) Shadowy Energy
entries: You are aware of its Clinging Shadows trait.

entries.name: (20+) In the Dark of Night
entries: You recognize the Body Snatcher's Sunlight Weakness trait.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Body Snatcher sticks to dimly lit areas or places of complete darkness. It teleports up to a creature and attempts to grapple it, teleporting away as soon as it has one or two targets in its hands. Often the Body Snatcher will emerge from tunnels or secret entrances to its lair. They do not travel far from the labs they were created in and often have easy points of escape to disappear once they have a victim in hand.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Undead.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Monster Blood, Contaminated Ichor.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Eyes, Heart, Brain, Guts.

entries.name: Bones:
entries: Skull, Spine.

entries.name: Hair:
entries: Stitches, Hair.

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Skin.

entries.name: Dust:
entries: Undead Dust.

name: Bojack

entries: This creature, which appears to be a dead horse flopped on its back, convulses and its stomach suddenly splits open, exposing its intestines and organs. Long, spindly, arachnid-like legs violently sprout from its torso as its stomach opens into a maw filled with sharp jagged teeth formed from the splayed rib cage of the beast. The horse legs limply hang in the air, as the creature skitters towards you with intense speed, intestines flapping around its maw like a sickly tongue. The head of the horse dangles lifelessly, but its mouth still gnashes and salivates acidic bile.

Many valiant warriors have ridden into Drakkenheim mounted on a loyal steed, not realizing that the rubble and wreckage filling the streets makes the ruins an unsuitable environment for a horse. Often, these poor animals must be abandoned not long after entering the ruins, injured from the unstable terrain. Prime targets for other predators, the horses are often tragically slaughtered. However, when their corpses are left behind, a parasite-like mutation festers within them, causing their skin to erupt with spider-like limbs, pincers, and maws.

Disguising themselves as mere corpses strewn across the dark and misty streets of the ruined city, one can hardly differentiate a Bojack from a dead horse. With their spider limbs they can scurry along walls and ceilings with ease, and barely make a sound. They move with lightning-fast speed, able to scuttle across a city street in mere seconds. This terrifying speed, ease of traversing the terrain, and ability to disguise itself have made them a deadly threat to adventurers in the city.

One of the most horrifying recorded encounters with Bojacks in Drakkenheim came from an early report from Hooded Lantern scouts investigating old stables south of Champion's Gate near the city outskirts. They reported finding "piles of dead horses buzzing with large, mutated flies feasting on the meat." The report goes on to speak of several of the horse corpses suddenly "bursting open" with "insectoid legs and a horrible maw formed from the splayed rib cage of the dead beasts." The report describes the speed and ferocity displayed in the immediate strike, with nearly an entire squad of eight Hooded Lantern scouts ripped to shreds in only a matter of seconds while the remaining Lanterns fled back out of the city.

One of the surviving Hooded Lanterns, Sten Livingston Sr., was brave enough to volunteer to lead the following expedition into the ruins. On the road into the city a dead and bloated horse corpse lay on the side of the road. Livingston stopped his troops and approached the beast with weapons drawn, kicking the corpse to check if it would spring to life. The corpse remained motionless. It has since become a tradition spread through the Lanterns, and even into new adventuring parties, to kick the horse on the way into Drakkenheim. Many have chalked this up to a sign of good luck, not realizing the harrowing story and the lives lost that caused this strange tradition.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks to Study a Bojack, learn the following based on their result:

entries.name: (10+) Parasitic Mutation
entries: You recognize the Bojack's {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities} and senses.

entries.name: (15+) Acidic Ambusher
entries: You're aware of the creature's Corrosive Mucus and Impaling Limbs attacks.

entries.name: (20+) Fast and Cunning
entries: You know the Bojack's strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Bojack is an ambush skirmisher. It waits for the opportune moment to strike, attempting to surprise as many targets as possible. After it surprises its prey, it attacks with its Impaling Limbs or Corrosive Mucus and uses its Predatory Cunning to move out of melee range.

The Bojack can climb walls and will try and skitter up buildings or behind walls, springing back out to attack before escaping again. If brought below 20 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, the Bojack attempts to {@action Dash|XPHB} away and {@action Hide|XPHB}.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Monstrosity.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Monster Blood, Contaminated Ichor, Acidic Bile, Mucus.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Heart, Guts, Glands.

entries.name: Bones:
entries: Spine.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Blades.

entries.name: Hair:
entries: Fur, Hair.

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Skin.

name: Bolgrim Boar-Scar
entries: Bolgrim first appears in {@adventure Down the Wolf Barrow|NorthlandsSagas|1} and leads the {@adventure Assault on Hvalfell|NorthlandsSagas|4}. Ylsa succeeds him as the characters' main foil with the cult in Wotan's Gauntlet and Attack on Birgkrona.

{@i This small, leering water spirit resembles a cross between a gray frog and a damp scarecrow, with small tendrils sprouting from all its extremities. It has water wings seemingly made out of jellyfish flesh.}

entries.name: Swamp Robbers
entries: Known as uriska in Draconic, the bolotis are small, swamp-dwelling water spirits which delight in drowning unsuspecting victims in shallow pools and springs, then robbing the corpses of whatever shiny objects they find. Bolotis use their magical vortex abilities to immobilize their victims and drag them to a watery death. They delight in storing up larders of victims under winter ice or under logs.

entries.name: Fond of Allies
entries: Bolotis sometimes team up with miremals and will-o'-wisps to create cunning ambushes. They are happy with a single kill at a time.
{@i Thousands of tiny bones coalesce into a humanoid form, then disperse in a clattering swarm the next moment. The bones rustle as the creature moves, a sound like sand sliding down a dune.}

entries.name: Spies and Sneaks
entries: Bone collectives are not primarily fighters, preferring to spy and skulk. However, when cornered, they fight fearlessly, seeking to strip the flesh from their foes. They wear robes or cloaks to pass as humanoid, as they know that most creatures find them disturbing.

entries.name: Commanders and Servants of Undeath
entries: Bone collectives' long finger bones and hooked claws help them ascend and control zombie mounts, and their magic allows them to control small groups of undead. This undead affinity occasionally leads them to serve as spies or spymasters for necromancers, darakhul, vampires, or liches.

entries.name: Feed on Society
entries: Bone collectives join societies around them, whether human, goblin, or ghoul. They prey on the living and the dead, to replenish lost bones. They produce a reddish venom that drains the luster of life from victims. Those who survive can describe the horrifying red smile of the collective's venom‑coated fangs.
{@i The cracked skull scurries forward on bone-white legs, crab claws raised.}

entries.name: Skull Shells
entries: Much like an enormous hermit crab, bone crabs inhabit the remains of large fish, humanoids, and other creatures. A bone crab's spiny, ivory-white legs blend in perfectly with bones and pale driftwood. When lacking bones, these crabs gnaw cavities into chunks of driftwood or coral to make a shelter, cementing bits of shell and debris to their portable homes. They drag aquatic prey above the high tide line and leave it to fester in the hot sun. The crabs can pick corpses clean in a few hours, and their hunting grounds are littered with cracked and sun-bleached bones—the perfect hiding place for these littoral predators.

entries.name: Scavengers of Memory
entries: Bone crabs are voracious scavengers. They live in seaside crags and coves, where they use their specialized chelae to crack open skulls and feast on the brains. Some crabs retain fragments of memory from those they devour, and these crabs recognize friends or attack the foes of those whose skulls they wear.

entries.name: Pack Hunters
entries: Bone crabs hunt in packs, preying on seabirds and creatures stranded in tidal pools. Centuries of feeding on brains has left the crabs with a rudimentary intelligence and a psychic connection with fellow packmates. They use this to alert each other to danger, potential prey, or a threat to their territory. Although bone crabs cannot be domesticated, they can be convinced to nest in particular areas, attacking intruders while ignoring the area's regulars.

entries.name: White Ghost Shivers
entries: Because they eat carrion, bone crabs carry a dangerous disease known as white ghost shivers. This disease wracks victims with fever and delirium. Sailors and others who eat a bone crab's unwholesome, diseased flesh rarely survive it.

{@i Dank winds sweep up skeletons, both humanoid and animal. They blow forward, reaching out for living creatures like a clawed hand of bone. A scattering of bones rolls across the ground, then rises into the air, billowing like a sheet}.

entries.name: Swarms of Fallen
entries: On rare occasions, the pugnacious spirits of fallen undead join together, bonded by a common craving: to feel alive again. They gather up their bones from life, as well as any other bones they come across, and form bone swarms.

entries.name: Nomadic Undead
entries: These swarms ravage the countryside wresting life from living creatures, grabbing livestock, humanoids, and even dragons, digging in their claws in an attempt to cling to life. Bone swarms with one or more sets of jaws wail constantly in their sorrow, interrupting their cries with snippets of rational, but scattered speech declaiming their woes and despair.

entries.name: Cliff and Pit Dwellers
entries: Bone swarms gather near cliffs, crevasses, and pits in the hope of forcing a victim or an entire herd of animals to fall to its death, creating more shattered bones to add to their mass.
"Do you really need all of your bones? Are you sure I couldn't just snack on a few? I'll gladly pay you for them."

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Bone trader lairs have many, many bones. Depending on how successful and powerful the bone trader is, it may also have the equipment and belongings of people it has killed or of the minions it employs. Its bone armor is infused with a peculiar magic.

Smashing the armor into a paste and mixing it with appropriate amounts of coagulant from a herbalism kit allows it to be applied it to a shield or weapon. This paste, called {@item ready gunk|GrimHollowLairsEtharis} (see Appendix A of {@adventure Lairs of Etharis|GrimHollowLairsEtharis|21}), can be completed with a successful Wisdom check ({@dc 10}) by someone proficient with a herbalism kit. This process takes 10 minutes.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
items.entry: A bone trader is most dangerous in its lair, where it can use its collection of bones to defend itself.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
items.entry: A bone trader can charm its opponents and is often defended by a small gang of intimidated or charmed creatures.

items.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
items.entry: Like other fey, bone traders can be tantalized by a deal and may be willing to negotiate rather than fight, even if it seems to have the upper hand or is actively winning a battle

name: Boneflayer

entries: {@i Voracious Carrion Eater}

Boneflayers are cruel, vulture-like creatures that originated from a broken fey pact. The creatures aren't content to wait for something to die and instead make their own carrion to gorge upon—they delight in snatching prey in their talons, carrying it into the air, and dropping it to its death. Boneflayers earn their name by using their sizeable, filth-riddled beaks to cleave flesh from bone and hoard the meat until it ages enough for them to enjoy.

Cults sometimes use boneflayer killing grounds as a source of bones to burn in ritual bonfires, occasionally making pacts with the creatures to pay or trade for the creature's castoffs. Villages that fear boneflayer attacks ward them off with thundering drums or gongs whenever they circle overhead.

entries.name: Secret
entries: A lingering result of the fey bargain that created them, boneflayers are disoriented and diminished by loud, thunderous noises.

name: Bonemonger Femur
entries: Little is known about astral hermits thanks to their propensity to set up shop in hard-to-reach locations. They are far-travelling aberrations, each developing extremely specific obsessions such as light, words, or bones. Astral hermits study their area of interest in meticulous detail, using it as a medium through which to learn more of the world.

entries.name: Corporeal Forms
entries: A male astral hermit is made up of two bodies: his heart and his hearth. An astral hermit's hearth is a maze-like construction at the centre of which is a portal to the Astral Plane. The astral hermit's heart is how he presents himself to the world. Usually, this is in a form that is inviting to creatures of that plane, a tactic which ensures plentiful trade.

entries.name: Reproduction
entries: Male and female astral hermits lead two very different existences. A male astral hermit's hearth is his bower, and his heart can never travel further than a few hundred feet from it. The abundance and richness of its treasures (which to the common person may appear as worthless relics) help to impress females of the species, which flit through the Astral Plane searching for portals into the hearth's of other hermits. When a union is formed, eggs are produced and jettisoned into the astral expanse.

entries.name: Crafters and Enchanters
entries: Astral hermits are innately magical beings, able to imbue items or creatures with enchantments shaped by their subject of obsession. Unable to travel far from their hearths, astral hermits create reputations of skill with enchanting and use that as the currency with which they trade for relics that further fuel their obsession.

entries.name: Bonemonger
entries: The bonemonger's obsession is bones. Fossilised, inscribed, splintered, or fresh, the bonemonger can read the history of every bone that passes him, learning much of the creatures to which they once belonged. The bonemonger has also learnt to animate these bones with his necromantic magic, allowing them to act as guards, workers, and scouts. The bonemonger chooses the form of a tiny white rabbit as his heart, an unassuming form that is nevertheless extremely deadly when threatened.
