Just like the classic tale of Venus vs. Cyclops except this one can teleport and shoot beams.

name: Cyclops Stormcaller
entries: When {@creature cyclops|MM|cyclopes} are born beneath a raging storm, they sometimes grow up different—smaller than the rest, sickly and weak. Most of these stormborn {@creature cyclops|MM|cyclopes} are relentlessly bullied and beaten for their tiny stature, and many die before adulthood. Those who survive do so because of the magic the {@deity The Stormlord|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|Stormlord} has bestowed upon them—intentionally or otherwise. As {@creature cyclops|MM|cyclopes} are generally unfamiliar with magic, the power of a stormcaller awes and terrifies them, and many see stormcallers as nothing short of the manifestation of a god.

entries.name: Storm Worship
entries: Their fellow {@creature cyclops|MM|cyclopes} may assume that the might of a stormcaller is akin to godliness, but many stormcallers hunger for greater power. A cabal of stormcallers regularly gathers in the {@book Daggerbay Mountains|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Daggerbay Mountains} at an ancient elven temple called the Skyneedle (in Elvish, ira'fallai; in Giant, "Tall Zappo-Zappo"). There, they conduct strange rituals to commune with an entity they call the Eye of the Storm—and with every ritual, their power grows.

However, the Eye of the Storm is no avatar of the {@deity The Stormlord|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|Stormlord}, but a vengeful {@creature storm giant} named Eyvindr, who's posing as a demigod and intent on raising an army to exact retribution on the {@book Council of Seven Scepters|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|6|Council of Seven Scepters}. He'll have to risk revealing himself to the stormcallers eventually—but not until he believes that his control over his cyclops devotees is absolute.

images.altText: A cyclops with two arms outstretched palms facing the sky, one arm is lit in reddish light. Blue lightning streaks behind the cyclops.

name: Cyglops
entries: Cyglopes are the result of a destructive mutation of the same phenomenon that creates geletons. These massive, hulking oozes take on a giant-like form and lumber through forests, collecting whatever skeletal remains they can find to reinforce their bodies and reanimate as thralls. Concentrated necrotic magic resides in the singular eye of a cyglops, which can be released as a focused beam of destructive force.

entries.name: Daelkyr

entries: A daelkyr knows secrets mortals can't comprehend and has plans they can't understand. Some sages believe that the daelkyr are artists and that worlds are their canvas; they destroy civilizations and unleash monsters because, to them, this is a thing of beauty. Others say that the daelkyr exist beyond time, and that their actions only make sense when viewed over the course of millennia. Still others assert that any creature that can understand the motives of the daelkyr will immediately turn to their cause—that it is dangerous to study the daelkyr too closely, lest their revelations destroy all prior understanding and identity. While they may be enigmatic, the daelkyr are unquestionably evil; they shatter innocent lives and entire civilizations without any remorse.

entries.name: Unifying Theme
entries: Each daelkyr has a unique theme. Belashyrra is tied to sight, Orlassk to stone, and Dyrrn to corruption and evolution. This theme is reflected in the daelkyr's appearance, in the minions it employs, and in the symbionts it creates. If the daelkyr is an artist, the theme is its medium. If it's a conqueror, the theme defines its weapons and the world it seeks to create. Additionally, each daelkyr holds secrets and revelations relating to its specific theme—secrets mortal minds can't comprehend. While in Belashyrra's presence, people may remember things they've seen and forgotten. Around Orlassk, they may feel numb... as if their flesh is becoming stone.

entries.name: Alien and Unsettling
entries: In an encounter with a daelkyr, consider ways to express its alien nature, such as the following:

items: A daelkyr can teleport 30 feet as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. This reflects the idea that the daelkyr are loosely bound to space and time. The daelkyr shifts in space, but you can't remember it moving. You could represent this as a constant, casual effect; even outside of combat, the daelkyr shifts between spaces, unbound by the concept of distance or time.

The appearance of a daelkyr is subjective. The basic facts are constant: a daelkyr is a Medium bipedal creature, and its equipment doesn't change. Beyond this, its appearance reflects its theme blended with its alien nature; for example, Orlassk typically appears as a humanoid in stone armor, with its face hidden behind a stone mask. But after people encounter a daelkyr, those who compare notes may find they disagree on the details. The daelkyr might appear as someone the viewer knows, or its appearance could shift mid-conversation. This is not something the daelkyr controls, and it's not considered a beneficial trait; it's simply part of their alien nature.

Daelkyr have telepathy with a range of 120 feet. This is their primary form of communication and is intended to be broader in scope than typical telepathy. A daelkyr can communicate with any number of creatures within range at once, projecting a thought much as other creatures project sound. Typically when a daelkyr "speaks," all creatures receive the same message, but the DM might decide that one or more creatures receive a different message. And just as people see different things when they look at a daelkyr, two people can perceive a daelkyr's "speech" in very different ways. One may feel as though the daelkyr is speaking aloud with a strange, alien voice. Another may hear the speech of the daelkyr as the voice of a dead lover, whispering in their ear. Another may not be able to remember actually hearing the daelkyr speak; instead, they just remember its words existing, as if they've always known them.

The Alien Mind feature of the daelkyr reflects the idea that the way that the daelkyr experience reality is so alien that any creature who tries to read their thoughts—to see the universe as they do—may become catatonic.

entries: Any encounter with a daelkyr should be horrifying, driven by its alien, unknowable nature. The actions of the Lords of Dust and the Dreaming Dark make sense; the quori seek to control humanity's dreams, while the Lords of Dust strive to release their bound overlords. The actions of the daelkyr are just as deadly and destructive, but we cannot understand what they want, and those who attempt to do so often become their cultists.

name: Dagon

entries: Vast, Polyphemous-like, and loathsome, it darted like a stupendous monster of nightmares to the monolith, about which it flung its gigantic scaly arms.
entries.from: H.P. Lovecraft, Dagon

entries: Dagon is a deep one who has grown to enormous size. Perhaps millions of years old, this cruel tyrant of the undersea realm strives to free Cthulhu from his deep slumber in the sunken city of R'lyeh. Dagon is the high priest of Cthulhu among the Deep Ones. Under his direction, that loathsome species seeks to infiltrate and overwhelm the terrestrial realms.

entries.name: Unwitting Servitors
entries: Dagon sits at the head of the cults established among human villages by the deep ones. Careful to avoid calling too much attention to their true aims, these cults ultimately serve Cthulhu but few in their ranks know this. The cult, under the direction of their deep one leaders, offers aid to Cthulhu cults and works to foil those who would hunt down and destroy them. To most of the humans caught in this scheme, Dagon is a benevolent sea deity who offers excellent fishing and good weather.

entries.name: Hidden Horrors
entries: While Dagon is considered the most powerful of the deep ones, other, similarly ancient creatures have gained similar levels of power. Deep one writings refer to Mother Hydra, an entity said to be Dagon's equal. Who can say what other terrors may lurk in the ocean's depths.

entries.name: Storm of the Century
entries: Dagon rarely interacts with mortals, but does intervene when a particularly bothersome foe arises or to preserve a critical aspect of his cult. Dagon's magic manifests as a halo of arcane, stormy sea waters that swirl around him. This destructive energy allows him to emerge on shore and walk through a village, town, or fortress that troubles his cult. This magic lashes out at the place, battering to ruin and slaying those within. When authorities come to investigate, they find a ruin that seems to have been devastated by a terrible storm. Dagon and the deep ones always ensure that no survivors remain to contradict this assumption.

name: Dani Jenkin
entries: Dani was born to {@creature Walter Jenkin|CrookedMoon24|Walter} and {@creature Gilly Jenkin|CrookedMoon24|Gilly} within a couple of weeks of their move to the mayoral manor to serve {@creature Wendel Somerton|CrookedMoon24|Mayor Somerton's} family. Now ten years old, she senses the ghosts and disturbing forces around her, knowing things a child shouldn't. Though she cannot yet control her abilities, her bond with the powers of the Old Ways grows.
{@i Intelligence gleams in the eyes of the well-dressed ghoul. It smiles a greeting, barely revealing sharp teeth.}

entries.name: Imperial Cunning
entries: In the lightless depths, an empire of devouring ambition grows and plots and dreams. They call themselves the People, but the people of the surface world call them the Lords Subterranean, the Ghoul Imperium, or simply the Empire of the Ghouls. To them, if you are not a member of the People, you are food.

entries.name: Darakhul Fever
entries: Spread mainly through bite wounds, this disease makes itself known within 24 hours by swiftly debilitating the infected. An infected creature must make a {@dc 17} Constitution saving throw after every long rest. On a failed save, the victim takes 14 ({@dice 4d6}) necrotic damage, and its hp maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the damage taken. This reduction lasts until the victim finishes a long rest after the disease is cured. The victim recovers from the disease by making two consecutive successful saving throws. Greater restoration cures the disease, while lesser restoration gives the victim advantage on the next saving throw. Primarily spread among Humanoids, the disease can affect ogres, and therefore other Giants may be susceptible. If a creature dies while infected with darakhul fever, roll a {@dice d20}, add the character's Constitution modifier, and find the result on the Adjustment Table below to determine what Undead form the victim's body rises in.
{@i This proud and commanding darakhul meets every threat with a steely gaze and a blade crackling with necrotic power.}

entries.name: Imperial Authority
entries: All darakhul and ghouls automatically acknowledge the commanding presence of a general but may not automatically obey depending on the relationship between them.

entries.name: Hungry Dead Nature
entries: Darakhul generals don't require air or sleep.

name: Dark Confessor

entries: Dressed in robes of black and red that stand as a mockery to the garb often worn by members of the Sacred Flame, and clutching an ornate golden staff with a crimson orb in one hand, and a shimmering spectral maul in the other, these Dark Confessors call forth unholy curses and spirits from the abyss to bend to their will. Their pale skin, sunken black eyes, and sharp fangs stand as a grim reminder that even the holy can succumb to the whims of vampiric lords.

When the Court of the Night seeks to infiltrate a community, their first priority is to corrupt its leaders, especially their most bitter rivals in the Faith of the Sacred Flame. Thus, the flamekeepers or local priests are often targeted in particular to be transformed into vampire spawn. When these devout worshipers become vampire spawn, they are known as Dark Confessors. Their divine powers twist and warp into dark, corrupted magic under the influence of vampiric forces. In undeath, they channel that same potent energy, now converted into terrifying vampiric sorcery, which they wield to serve their masters. As Dark Confessors, they lead sinister rites and unholy rituals, gathering more followers to the cause of their vampiric overlords.

With their natural authority and sway over commonfolk, Dark Confessors manipulate communities to fall under the influence of vampire lords. They often foster cult-like followings, leading the people into pledging allegiance to their dark masters. These cults believe that by proving their loyalty, they might escape the curse of undeath and servitude. Entire towns and villages have succumbed to the charismatic influence of a Dark Confessor, their inhabitants abandoning former beliefs and swearing unwavering fealty to their vampire lords, hoping this grim devotion will save them from a far worse fate.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Religion|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Religion|XPHB}) checks when taking the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine a Dark Confessor, learning the following based on the result.

entries.name: (5+) Unnatural Resistance
entries: You recognize the Dark Confessor's damage {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}.

entries.name: (10+) Deadly Response
entries: You are aware of the Dark Confessor's Bloody Rebuke Reaction.

entries.name: (15+) Weaknesses
entries: You are aware the vampire's Regeneration is temporarily halted by Radiant damage, and its Vampire Weaknesses.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: In the first round of combat, the Dark Confessor casts {@spell Spirit Guardians|XPHB}. It uses its Claws to attack anyone who comes within its melee reach. The Dark Confessor then proceeds to attack with its Spiritual Maul.
If there are enemies grouped close to one another, the Dark
Confessor uses Unholy Light on them.
The Dark Confessor flees if it is below 50 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or takes steady Radiant damage.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Undead.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Monster Blood.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Eyes, Heart, Brain, Guts, Flesh.

entries.name: Bones:
entries: Skull, Spine, Ribs.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Teeth, Claws.

entries.name: Hair:
entries: Hair

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Skin.

entries.name: Dust:
entries: Undead Dust.

name: Dark Growth

entries: The remains of a corpse is splayed across a ruined wall. A chaotic mass of jet-black brambles and vines pours from its torso, clinging to the nearby stonework. Branches have burst from its form, and its neck erupts into another mass of plant matter. The skull is severed from the body with its jaw unhinged and hanging in a horrible expression, stuck in place by the writhing vines. Throughout this Dark Growth, flowers bloom in iridescent neon hues and the smell of sweet pollen and decaying flesh fills the air. You hear gentle whispers from a distant voice, distinctly familiar and beckoning.

{@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} causes most plants to wither and die, but some thrive on it, absorbing water and delerium from the soil to mutate into deadly flora. In Drakkenheim's urban wasteland, suitable plots of fertile soil are scarce outside {@link Queen's Park Garden}, necessitating a creative adaptation to proliferate. These Dark Growths take root in the bodies of creatures through their infectious, delerium-infused spores.

Emitted from their blooming flowers, these spores drift silently throughout the air until they enter another creature's body through the ears, mouth, or nose. Once inside, these spores can lay dormant for some time, slowly contaminating their host with internal mutation which slowly decay their flesh and bone from within, transforming it into an ideal place for the Dark Growth to germinate. When the creature succumbs to contamination, or dies with the spores within it, the plant awakens. Consuming the internal organs of the dying infected, it suddenly and violently sprouts. Often, this transformation occurs so suddenly that the creature remains walking around, the Dark Growth using the corpse as a mobile shell so it may plant in an ideal location to spread future spores.

One apothecary reports a case where a knight returning from a mission into the Inner City had survived the journey relatively unscathed save for an excursion into the gardens where a puff of what they thought was pollen from strange iridescent flowers got in their eyes. The knight thought little of it, suffering no immediate effects. After returning to Emberwood, the knight complained of stomach cramps, nausea, and headaches, eventually passing out from the pain. The apothecary performed an emergency surgery, cutting the patient open only to have their intestines burst out like a barrage of meaty, thorn-covered brambles that attempted to strangle the apothecary. Their intestines had been completely replaced with plant matter that had fused into their guts.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Nature|XPHB}) checks to {@action Study|XPHB} a Dark Growth, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (5+) Contaminated and Thriving
entries: You are aware of the Dark Growth's {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: (10+) Deadly Spores
entries: You recognize the creature's Infection Spores action.

entries.name: (15+) Kill it with fire!
entries: You know the creature's Vulnerability to Fire, and its strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: A Dark Growth is a simple-minded plant. It uses Mimicry to lure passing creatures towards it, often mimicking the sounds of children or people in need. It entangles and infests any target near it, infecting it with its spores. The creature is a stationary plant and does not flee.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Plant.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Contaminated Ichor, Sap.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Flowers.

entries.name: Bones:
entries: Stems.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Spores, Needles.

entries.name: Hair:
entries: Leaves.

entries.name: Dust:
entries: Plant Dust.

name: Dark Growth Shambler

entries: Staggering from the shadows is a gaunt humanoid with pale flesh and a hunched form. Vines and branches protrude from its gaping mouth and push through its flesh throughout its body. Flowers emerge from these growths, blooming in iridescent neon hues. A smell of sweet sugar and decaying flesh fills the air, and whispers begin to issue from it even though the creature's mouth doesn't move.

Sometimes, when the body of one infected with {@creature Dark Growth|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Dark Growths} bursts open in the moment of their death, the body does not immediately collapse and decay. Instead, the creature shambles around, its body still intact, but with vines and thorny black branches bursting from its eye sockets, mouth, and flesh, its body now a protective shell for the plant within.

{@i This figure is dressed in black robes, and every part of its body that isn't covered by robes is wrapped in gray bandages. It wields blood‑stained sickles in each bandaged hand and moves with menace.}

The lowliest of the dark folk, the dark servants are also the most numerous. They cover their skin completely to shield it from even a single mote of light. Dark servants are without empathy and prefer the company of other dark folk. Murderous and cruel, they have difficulty interacting with non‑dark folk for long.

entries.name: Dark Folk
entries: Dark folk arose when a line of human wizards swore allegiance to shadow gods and passed this shadow power to their children. Easily mistaken for humans at a glance, the dark folk long ago diverged from their ancestors.

entries.name: Shadows Among Light
entries: Dark folk most often live near humanoid settlements. They worship the powers of darkness and shadow in secret, spreading their corruption in the dead of night and in darkened cellars. They often work nocturnal jobs as undertakers, night soil collectors, alchemists, or night watchmen, escaping the unrelenting glare of the sun.

entries.name: Darkened Blood
entries: Sometimes a family line carries the tiniest seed of darkness, and a dark folk is born. These pale children face difficult lives, often singled out and shunned by peers for the dark nature they can't ever fully hide. Though most dark folk look human, dark folk can descend from any humanoid (though they lose all traits associated with their heritage).

name: Dark Young

entries: An enormous writhing mass formed of ropy black, earthwormlike tentacles. Something like twenty feet tall. Here and there, across the surface were great puckered mouths that dripped green goo. Beneath its central mass, two or three thicker tentacles terminated in enormous black hooves, on which it stamped forward. It carried the visage of some ancient gnarled tree when its shape was cast against the moon. The smell was appalling, like the stench of open graves.
entries.from: Malleus Monstrorum Volume I: Monsters of the Mythos

entries: These horrid abominations are the "young" referred to in Shub-Niggurath's epithet: "Black Goat of the Woods with a Thousand Young." They are closely connected to her and are found only in areas where she is worshiped. The dark young act as proxies for Shub-Niggurath, crawling from the darkness to accept sacrifices and devour the unwary.

entries.name: Noxious Heralds
entries: The dark young are the first of Shub-Niggurath's servitors to contact a cult. Those who worship the Black Goat of the Woods engage in primal rituals that require gratuitous bloodletting and fleshy offerings. In return, the dark young heed their call. They provide a cult with brute force, smashing its enemies and protecting it from outsiders. However, if the cult fails to provide a steady stream of sacrifices, the dark young may cull its weakest members, devouring them to slake its hunger and 'encourage' the cult to become more aggressive toward outsiders.

entries.name: Corrupting Influence
entries: The presence of a dark young shifts and warps the natural world. The plants in a 5-mile radius centered on its lair grow thick and verdant, creating natural barriers to dissuade explorers and intruders. Cultists learn the hidden paths that crisscross the area, allowing them to move in relative ease while intruders struggle. Animals become overly aggressive and vicious, attacking non-cultists on sight. In game terms, treat the area as {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. A DC 20 Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check and 1d4 hours of searching allows a traveler to uncover the pathways. A DC 25 Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check is needed to use the trail to reach the cult's lair.
{@i A constant shimmer surrounds this short, winged creature. Staring at it is eye-watering and confusing, like a distant desert mirage, though it's scant yards away.}

entries.name: Desert Mirage Fey
entries: Daus are creatures of haze and illusion. They stand three feet tall, with sandy skin, and are surrounded by a shimmering aura like a heat haze. They are flighty, physically weak, and unfocused, but agile in body and wit.

entries.name: Lazy and Bored
entries: Their ability to magically provide for themselves in most material ways tends to make daus lazy and hedonistic. As a result, daus are often friendly and eager for company. They invite friends and strangers alike to rest in their lairs, partake in their feasts, and share their stories.

entries.name: Sticklers for Etiquette
entries: However, a dau's hospitality turns to cruelty when guests breach its intricate rules of etiquette.
Sometimes it's darkest after the dawn.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Dawndrinkers have a special organ that stores and processes light the way that other creatures digest food. Most of the creature's body disintegrates after it dies, but this light stomach remains. Someone who has proficiency with alchemist's supplies, cook's utensils, or an herbalism kit can prepare the stomach with other ingredients worth 25 gp. If the preparer succeeds on a {@dc 13} Wisdom or Intelligence check, the organ makes a tasty, sweet meal for up to four creatures. After partaking, those creatures add 60 feet to their darkvision range for 24 hours, those that lack darkvision gain it to a range of 60 feet. All partakers also gain blindsight to a range of 10 feet for the same duration.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
items.entry: A dawndrinker is a cunning predator that can easily hide and move in shadow. It greatly lessens and even extinguishes light sources.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
items.entry: A dawndrinker can sense light, its food, at a great distance. The monster is also resistant to fire, absorbing some of its energy, and immune to radiant damage, which is a source of quick nourishment for the dawndrinker.

items.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
items.entry: A dawndrinker's attacks can temporarily take away the victim's ability to perceive light.

entries: {@i Enormous clouds of orange and green butterflies add a reek of putrefaction to the air, stirred by the flapping of delicate wings.}

entries.name: Demon-Haunted
entries: A death butterfly swarm results when a rare breed of carrion-eating butterfly, drawn en masse to the stench of decay, feeds on the corpse of a fiend, demon, or similar creature.

entries.name: Dizzying and Poisonous
entries: The colorful, chaotic flapping of the insects' wings blinds and staggers those in its path, allowing the swarm to necrotize flesh from those it overruns. Attracted to rotting material, the swarm spreads a fast-acting, poison on its victims, creating carrion it can feed on immediately.

entries.name: Devour the Undead
entries: Undead creatures are not immune to a death butterfly swarm's poison. A swarm can rot an undead creature's animating energies as easily as those of the living. Given the choice between an undead and living creature, a death butterfly swarm always attacks the undead, finding ghouls and vampires particularly appealing. Some good-aligned forces regard summoning these swarms as a necessary evil.

name: Death Coach
entries: Known across the land in myth and song as a specter of terror, the death coach is a manifestation of death and harbinger of woe. This smoky black carriage pulled by horses dark as midnight is one with its headless driver. Within the carriage are countless wailing souls, but their screams go unheard. The legends claim that seeing the coach is to court misfortune, and hearing your name uttered by the coachman is an instant death sentence, as he instructs you to board the carriage with the other damned passengers.

entries.name: Undead Nature
entries: A death coach doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.

name: Death Shroud

entries: Delightful companions when tracking; they don't speak and they get as excited as me when identifying the cause of a corpse's demise—a useful trait when discerning your prey's favourite meals. Just don't take them to a mortuary. People are so touchy about their relatives' flesh sacks.
Type: Undead
Creature Component: Undead spellcaster
Bonus Tamer Improvement: Recycle and +2 Hit Dice

A death shroud can be created by combining cloth imbued with necromantic energy with flesh free of a soul. One blast of biomantic energy later and you have an animate, cloth-wrapped limb. A death shroud actively recruits fresh corpses into its own form, temporarily increasing its size and strength. Over time, some of these additions stick, and the death shroud can grow to a mass of writhing limbs, heads, and torsos.
If any of the death shroud's traits or actions require saving throws, it is always against the death shroud's save DC, as calculated below.

entries.name: Save DC
entries.text: 8 + the tamer's proficiency bonus + the death shroud's Intelligence modifier

entries.name: Monster Trainer
entries: In addition to the improvements you can normally give your companions, you can choose to grant the death shroud the following improvements using your Monster Trainer feature:

entries.name: Recycle
Prerequisite:
entries: become a tamer's companion.

entries.name: Type
entries: Active (action or reaction).

As a reaction when the death shroud kills a creature with its Slap or Lich Slap attacks, or as an action when the death shroud is within 5 feet of a corpse that has been dead for no longer than 1 hour, the death shroud absorbs some of the corpse's mass into itself. The death shroud regains hit points equal to one roll of the corpse's Hit Die and gains the same number of temporary hit points. In addition, if the corpse is equal to or larger than the death shroud, the death shroud's size increases by one size category until its tamer finishes a short or long rest. The death shroud's size can increase by no more than one category in this way. If there isn't enough room for the death shroud to double its size, it attains the maximum possible size in the space available. While its size is increased in this way, the death shroud has advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws, it gains a +2 bonus to the attack roll of its Slap attack, and its Slap attack deals an extra {@damage 1d4} bludgeoning damage on a hit.

entries.name: Growth I
Prerequisite:
entries: 3rd-level tamer.

entries.name: Type
entries: Passive (companion).

The death shroud's size increases to Small and its Hit Die size increases to a d6 (its hit point maximum consequently increases by 1 for each of its Hit Dice). The damage die of its Slap increases to a d6 and its Lich Slap to a d10.

entries.name: Hulking Protector
Prerequisite:
entries: 3rd-level tamer.

entries.name: Type
entries: Active (reaction).

When a creature the death shroud can see attacks a target that is within 5 feet of the death shroud, it can use its reaction to decrease the damage the target takes by {@damage 1d10}, provided the attack is against a creature other than the death shroud. When the death shroud's tamer reaches 13th level in the tamer class, this damage reduction increases to {@damage 2d10}.

entries.name: Grave Robber
Prerequisite:
entries: 5th-level tamer.

entries.name: Type
entries: Active (bonus action), Passive (companion & tamer).

The death shroud is always under the effects of the {@spell detect magic} spell, which has a radius equal to the death shroud's blindsight. If the death shroud uses its action to see magical auras, these are also visible to its tamer. In addition, the death shroud can use its bonus action to use its thieves' tools to disarm a trap or open a lock, or to take the Use an Object action.

entries.name: Growth II
Prerequisite:
entries: 5th-level tamer, Growth I.

entries.name: Type
entries: Passive (companion).

The death shroud's size increases to Medium and its Hit Die size increases to a d8 (its hit point maximum consequently increases by 1 for each of its Hit Dice). The damage die of its Slap increases to a d8 and its Lich Slap to a {@damage 2d6}.

entries.name: Multiattack
Prerequisite:
entries: 5th-level tamer.

entries.name: Type
entries: Active (action).
As an action, the death shroud makes two attacks with any combination of Slap and Lich Slap.

entries.name: Undead Fortitude I
Prerequisite:
entries: 5th-level tamer.

entries.name: Type
entries: Passive (companion).

The death shroud gains a +1 bonus to its AC. In addition, if damage reduces the death shroud to 0 hit points, it must make a Constitution saving throw with a DC of 5 + the damage taken, unless the damage is radiant or from a critical hit. On a success, the death shroud drops to 1 hit point instead.

entries.name: Corpse Investigator
Prerequisite:
entries: 9th-level tamer, Grave Robber.

entries.name: Type
entries: Active (action), Passive (tamer).

As an action, the death shroud can cast the {@spell speak with dead} spell without requiring material components, allowing its tamer to ask the corpse questions. This spell ends early when the death shroud is dismissed. After the death shroud uses this action, it can't do so again until its tamer finishes a short or long rest. In addition, the death shroud's tamer gains proficiency in the Medicine skill.

entries.name: Undead Fortitude II
Prerequisite:
entries: 9th-level tamer, Undead Fortitude I.

entries.name: Type
entries: Passive (companion).

The death shroud gains a +1 bonus to its AC. This improvement is in addition to the bonus from Undead Fortitude I. The DC for the Constitution saving throw it makes when reduced to 0 hit points equals the damage taken, unless the damage is radiant or from a critical hit.

entries.name: Growth III
Prerequisite:
entries: 13th-level tamer, Growth II.

entries.name: Type
entries: Passive (companion).

The death shroud's size increases to Large and its Hit Die size increases to a d10 (its hit point maximum consequently increases by 1 for each of its Hit Dice). The damage die of its Slap attack increases to a d10 and its Lich Slap to {@damage 2d8}.

entries.name: Undead Fortitude III
Prerequisite:
entries: 13th-level tamer, Undead Fortitude II.

entries.name: Type
entries: Passive (companion).

The death shroud gains a +1 bonus to its AC. This improvement is in addition to the bonuses from Undead Fortitude I & II. It can make the Constitution saving throw when reduced to 0 hit points even if the damage is radiant or from a critical hit.

entries.name: Swarm
Prerequisite:
entries: 17th-level tamer, Growth III.

entries.name: Type
entries: Active (action).

As an action, the death shroud deconstructs itself into eight {@creature ghoul||ghouls} which last for 1 minute. While in this state, the tamer can issue a single command as an action to all eight ghouls, which they follow to the best of their ability. The tamer can't use its Bolster, Psychic Bond, Malleable Presence, Switcheroo, or Magnificent Presence features to affect any of the ghouls. The tamer can dismiss the death shroud if at least on ghoul is within range of the tamer. When it does so, the nearest ghoul returns to the vessel—where it reverts to a death shroud and remains unconcious and remains unconscious until its tamer finishes a long rest—and all the other ghouls drop dead. Alternatively, if at least one ghoul is alive at the end of the minute and is on the same plane of existence as the tamer, the death shroud returns to its vessel and remains unconscious until its tamer finishes a long rest. If all ghouls die, the death shroud returns to its vessel with 3 levels of exhaustion and remains unconscious until its tamer finishes a long rest. if the tamer is on a different plane of existence to all of the ghouls when the minute ends or when the last ghoul dies, the death shroud dies.
{@i This fungal creature's head extends up and out in an orange and red cap with white spots. A vicious-looking fanged maw dominates its face.}

entries.name: Mushroom Farmers
entries: These sentient mushroom folk tend the forests of fungi in the underworld and are allies of the darakhul. Despite their ominous name, deathcap myconids are chiefly farmers. They cultivate dozens of species of mushrooms anywhere they have water, dung, and a bit of earth or slime in the underworld deeps. For this reason, other races rarely attack them. The ghouls do not eat them, and they cannot be made into darakhul.

entries.name: Toxic Spores
entries: Although deathcaps are mostly peaceful, their spores are toxic and sleep-inducing. They make excellent allies in combat because their abilities tend to punish attackers, but they aren't especially lethal on their own. They use their poison and slumber spores to full effect against living creatures and typically flee from constructs and undead. They count on their allies to fend off the most powerful foes.

entries.name: Clones
entries: Deathcap myconids live in communal groups of related clones. They reproduce asexually, and an elder and its offspring can be nearly identical in all but age. These clone groups are called deathcap rings. Myconids build no huts or towns, but their groups are defined by their crops and general appearance. Indeed, many sages claim that the deathcaps are merely the fruiting, mobile bodies of the forests they tend, which is why they fight so ferociously to defend their forests of giant fungi.
{@i A shadowy figure flickers in and out of view. Its indistinct shape betrays a sylvan ancestry, and its eyes are malevolent blue points of light.}

entries.name: Fey Undead
entries: A deathwisp is a wraith-like spirit created in the Shadow Realm from the violent death of a shadow fey or evil fey.

entries.name: Rift Walkers
entries: Many deathwisps remain among the shadows, but a few enter the natural world through planar rifts and gates or by walking along the shadowy roads between the worlds. Retaining only a trace of their former personality and knowledge, their lost kindness has been replaced with malice.

entries.name: Devour Breath
entries: A deathwisp feasts on the breath of living things, and it invariably seeks to devour animals and solitary, intelligent prey. It is quite intelligent and avoids fights against greater numbers.

name: Decahedrooze
entries: When Dr. Stein left his lab at short notice (following a pitchfork-wielding-mob related event), he left an entire pool of his patent-pending Mut-x exposed to the elements. Things fell into it; those things had brains, and those brains, their memories, and the sum of their intelligence fused with gelatinous cubes into biomantic polyhedroozes.

entries.name: Empathetic
entries: When a biomantic polyhedrooze forms, it begins absorbing the latent psychic energy of its environs. Creatures with strong psyches that are nearby in either space or time influence the nascent sentience of the polyhedrooze. A long-destroyed lich might impart its madness and hate into the ooze, whilst a colony of highly-charismatic mice might lend the goopey mass a penchant for cheese.

entries.name: Reactive Mutations
entries: The true feat of Dr Stein's research, and a trait that the polyhedroozes embody, is that of extreme biomantic reaction to environmental stimuli. A polyhedrooze that takes damage immediately adapts its morphology to prevent further damage of that type. The larger the polyhedrooze, the more such adaptations it can sustain at any one time.

entries.name: Size Matters
entries: Bigger polyhedroozes have absorbed more brains and, so, are more clever. A polyhedrooze that reaches a critical mass might decide to split into two, with the idea of sending one of its halves in search of pastures new. Unfortunately, the decrease in intelligence that results from a split means that polyhedroozes can get confused and end up in a cycle of splitting and reforming over and over.

entries.name: Hyphans
entries: Sharing a closer genealogy with the common toadstool than with any of the humanoid races, hyphans is the term used for the alien, fungal hive mind and the creatures it animates. Found underground, hyphans line vast subterranean caverns as stationary toadstools, penetrate tremendous expanses of rock and soil as microscopic mycelia, and infect the bodies of creatures. This latter form, though the least common, permits hyphans to interact with other creatures of The Low, while also providing defensive measures in response to incursions by greedy adventurers. All such creatures are part of a single entity, the hyphan colony. Any sensation one portion of the colony experiences, the rest of the colony comes to know about soon after.

entries.name: Co-opted Assistance
entries: A hyphan hive mind typically adapts an infected creature's body into one of three archetypes: the brute, duskcap, or sporeslinger. These individuals must regularly return to the heart of their colony to be replenished and regain their vigour, lest they become decrepit, dessicated husks.

entries.name: Hyphan Brute
entries: Strong and burly creatures will be formed into brutes. Used for clearing rockfalls and to intimidate interlopers in a hyphan's domain, these large specimens' size can often act as an impediment in the tight tunnels of The Low. On the battlefield, brutes act as juggernauts, sending ranks of foes to the floor—perfect targets for their smaller cousins, the duskcaps. Their bulk and toughness allow them to fight without any sense of self preservation as they rampage through the enemy lines.

entries.name: Hyphan Duskcap
entries: Lithe, graceful, or otherwise agile creatures can expect to become duskcaps if they should find themselves overcome by a hyphan colony's grasp. Primarily information gatherers, duskcaps are adept at passing without notice, and often patrol a colony's periphery, acting as its eyes and ears.

entries.name: Brainless Senses
entries: An isolated duskcap—indeed any isolated hyphan—does not possess the ability to understand what it hears; it is the fungal hive mind that interprets those sounds. While a duskcap is within range of a colony's communication spores, this interpretation happens instantaneously. However, if a duskcap should range beyond these spores, it will record everything it hears, to be transmitted to the hive mind with unfailing accuracy upon its return.

entries.name: Hyphan Sporeslinger
entries: Innately magical creatures that get 'hyphanated' (the term used by scholars to describe the act by which a creature is overcome by a hyphan colony) will become sporeslingers. Some of these individuals may remember the spells they knew in life, but, for the most part, this connection with the Weave is co-opted to provide the colony access to charm-based magics. Sporeslingers use these beguiling enchantments to capture stray creatures and deliver them to the fungal heart where they too can be hyphanated. Without these specimens, a hive mind would have to rely on serendipity to gather new biomass. With them, it can take a more proactive approach.

entries.name: Self-preservation
entries: A hyphan hive mind is far from stupid. It understands the fragility and value of a sporeslinger. A sporeslinger possesses the ability to produce clouds of obscuring spores (from which to make its escape) and is rarely found alone. On diplomatic missions they may be accompanied by brutes, for their intimidating size. When laying a trap, a sporeslinger may stand alone in a field of barely-visible puffball toadstools, several duskcaps lying in wait in the shadows.

name: Deep Angler
entries: This enormous, predatory fish has the uncanny ability to cast an illusion around its lure to fit what its prey most responds to. A curious adventurer might see a floating chest of treasure, a swimmer in distress, or an empty boat floating on the surface—whatever gets its prey to come a bit closer for a better look. The deep angler has even been known to lunge onto the shore to swallow its prey, and then wriggle back into the water, making anything on the shoreline fair game.

{@i This large, unnerving drake's glassy black scales have purple undertones. Its features are elongated and almost alien. Black, expressionless eyes stare ahead, and a barbed stinger sits at the end of a long tail}.

entries.name: Friend to Ghouls
entries: The deep drake has made a niche for itself in subterranean realms, establishing trade with the darakhul and with other races of the underworld. The drakes' poison ensures the ghouls have replacements when their population dwindles. In return, those underlings who fail their rulers become food for the drake.

entries.name: Love Darkness
entries: Deep drakes are 12 feet long, plus a three-foot long tail, and weigh up to 1,500 pounds. Their coloration makes them ideal predators in the subterranean dark. They love life underground, and they feel a kinship with the aberrations and undead residing there. They avoid sunlight and are strictly nocturnal when on the surface.

entries.name: Few in Number
entries: A deep drake mates for life with another deep drake when two of these rare creatures meet. A hermaphroditic creature, the drake assumes a gender until it finds a mate, at which time it may change. Once every 10–20 years, the drakes reproduce, resulting in three or four three-foot long, rubbery eggs. Occasionally, subterranean undead or aberrations take these eggs to their cities to train the young drakes. A "household drake" is a great status symbol in some deep places, and surface necromancers who have heard of them are often eager to acquire one.

name: Deep Dreg Warrior

entries: Emerging from the contaminated waters is a humanoid figure with disturbing piscine mutations. Their body is covered in glittering scales of sea green, midnight purple, and deep blue. Their monstrous face has two large, bulbous eyes and a gaping, fishlike mouth filled with oddly-shaped teeth—a mixture of humanoid, shark, and other aquatic animals. Spindly, fleshy whiskers surround their fish lips. They have webbed feet and hands, and thin fins jut from their arms, legs, and face. They wear little more than ragged clothing and scraps of leather armor, and carry a brace of javelins, a spear, and a fishing net.

Dwelling in the contaminated sewers and waterways of Drakkenheim, a Deep Dreg Warrior is left with only dim memories of their former lives, their identities are fully subsumed by eldritch contamination and thralldom to the Duchess. Nevertheless, many describe their state as preferable to the lives they lived before, describing unfortunate humans as cursed landwalkers who must be "freed.".

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when {@action Study|XPHB|Studying} a Deep Dreg Warrior, learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (5+) Amphibious Mutant
entries: You know the creature is a capable swimmer and is immune to Contamination.

entries.name: (10+) Foe Catcher
entries: You are aware of the Deep Dreg Warrior's Net attack and Catch of the Day trait.

entries.name: (15+) Strong and Tough
entries: You learn the creature's strongest and weakest saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Deep Dreg Warriors attack from the water, throwing their spears and diving back under the surface as added protection against ranged retaliation. When they engage in melee, the warriors use their Net to restrain their foes, and make melee attacks (with the bonus damage from Catch of the Day) to knock them {@condition Unconscious|XPHB}.

Deep Dregs Warriors flee whenever they are outnumbered or if they are reduced below half their maximum {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. They swim to safety rather than die fighting, and prefer to fall back and retaliate after gathering reinforcements.

name: Deep Knight

entries: Towering over the other Deep Dregs is a muscle-bound warrior with a head shaped like a hammerhead shark. They carry a colossal shield made from the opalescent shell of some mollusk, and their gnarled hide is covered in algae and barnacles. A thick chain is wrapped around their wrists, attached to the massive, spiked harpoon they carry.

Champions of the Duchess, Deep Knights tower over others of their kind. They lead groups of Deep Dreg Warriors on excursions and important missions. The Duchess keeps a contingent of Deep Knights as her personal honor guard to protect her lair.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine a Deep Knight. They learn the following information based on their check result.

entries.name: (5+) Amphibious Mutant
entries: You know the creature is a capable swimmer and is immune to Contamination.

entries.name: (10+) Foe Catcher
entries: You are aware of the Deep Knight's Harpoon attack and Unwavering Sentinel trait.

entries.name: (15+) Strong and Tough
entries: You learn the creature's strongest and weakest saving throws are similar to that of a normal human.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Deep Knight is the forward assault of the Deep Dregs and uses their seashell shields to deflect attacks and their harpoons to pull enemies into close range before biting them with their shark teeth.
The Deep Knight will defend the other Deep Dregs to the death. If it is the last one standing it will attempt to flee, but as long as there are allies to protect, it will stay and fight.

name: Deep One

entries: It was a thin, stoop-shouldered man not much under six feet tall... His age was perhaps thirty-five, but the odd, deep creases in the sides of his neck made him seem older when one did not study his dull, expressionless face. He had a narrow head, bulging, watery blue eyes that seemed never to wink, a flat nose, a receding forehead and chin, and singularly undeveloped ears.
entries.from: H.P. Lovecraft, The Shadow over Innsmouth

entries: Along lonely coasts, where few live and even fewer travel, the ghastly cult of Cthulhu and his servitors takes root. The deep ones are aquatic creatures that live in undersea colonies located in the darkest depths. Within these cities, they conduct loathsome rites to their chief deities, Dagon, Mother Hydra, and Cthulhu.

entries.name: Insidious Corruptors
entries: The deep ones spy upon isolated coastal communities, keeping watch for signs of weakness or decay. If a village falls upon hard times, the deep ones make their move. They come ashore and approach the villagers peacefully, promising bountiful fishing, protection from monsters, and shelter from storms. Like a shepherd tending to wayward sheep, the deep ones tend to the humans while slowly making them wholly dependent upon their care.

entries.name: Generational Evil
entries: If the human community proves malleable, especially after culling a few dissidents, the deep ones further their corruption. In a grand ceremonial feast, they declare that the land folk have proven their worth and can now truly join with their aquatic protectors. The final step involves the deep ones marrying into prominent human clans to bind the villagers by blood. The children of these grotesque arrangements are deep one hybrids. While they are born human, they slowly and torturously transform into hybrids once they reach adulthood.

entries.name: A Slow Corruption
entries: In time, the village becomes fully integrated into deep one culture. The hybrid villagers maintain the façade of normalcy, venturing into civilization as needed or dealing with outsiders as appropriate. Meanwhile, the deep ones expand their influence to nearby settlements and lure more into their twisted cult.
{@i These fishlike folk have enormous eyes, a wide mouth, and almost no chin.}

entries.name: Elder Gods
entries: In their fully grown form, the deep ones are an ocean-dwelling race that worships elder gods such as Father Dagon and Mother Hydra, and they dwell in deep water darkness. In some areas, they intermarry with coastal humans to create human-deep one hybrids.

entries.name: Coastal Raiders
entries: The deep ones keep to themselves in isolated coastal villages and settlements in the deep ocean for long periods, and then, at the command of their patron gods, turn suddenly into strong, relentless raiders, seizing territory, slaves, and wealth all along the coasts. Some deep ones have even founded small kingdoms lasting generations in backwater reaches or distant, chilled seas.

entries.name: Demand Sacrifices
entries: They demand tolls from mariners frequently; those who do not leave tribute at certain islands or along certain straits find the fish escape their nets, or the storms shatter their hulls and drown their sailors. Some seafaring nations have found it more profitable to ally themselves with the deep ones; this is the first step in their patient plans to dominate and rule.

entries.name: Ocean Change
entries: A deep one born to a human family resembles a human child, but the person transforms into an adult deep one between the ages of 16 and 30. Such deep ones then hear the siren call of their elder god masters and oceanic cousins, which eventually supplants the love the person might feel for family and friends on land.

entries.name: Gods of the Deep Ones
entries: The deep ones are faithful servants of horrific powers inimical to all life on land. Father Dagon is a god of fertility, fish, and the strength of the deep ocean and is an evil lord of storm and waves. Mother Hydra is his consort, a goddess of immense strength and size, spawning entire schools of fish at once. She is mistress of the great kraken and toothsome krake spawn, who are her children and servitors. Both deities plot conquest through a long program of forced interbreeding and eldritch meddling with human bloodlines.

In addition, many deep ones follow Shar-Ngolyeth, a long-lost deity referred to as That Which Lurks Beneath the Waves. This kraken and her krake spawn offspring are close allies to the deep ones, but they are largely indifferent to Dagon and Hydra.

name: Deep Siren

entries: This a wretched, mutated crone has sea-green hair and blue-gray flesh, and is garbed in a gown of algae and kelp. They carry pouches filled with occult reagents, and vials filled with a strange octarine goo. Despite their appearance, as they speak their words are no less honeyed and sweet.

Spellcasters transformed by the Duchess's influence become Deep Sirens, retaining a measure of their magical abilities. These sirens will act as forward generals or confidants for the Duchess, and often a well-regarded siren will act as her personal court mage.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine a Deep Siren. They learn the following information based on their check result.

entries.name: (5+) Amphibious Mutant
entries: You know the creature is a capable swimmer and is immune to Contamination.

entries.name: (10+) Illusive Opponent
entries: You are aware of the creature's Misty Step action.

entries.name: (15+) Nimble and Enchanting
entries: You learn the Deep Siren's strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Deep Sirens are the generals and confidants to the Duchess and often serve as the eyes and ears of their mistress. They use their Illusory Appearance to walk among humanoids and observe them, planning and plotting the attacks of the Deep Dregs. Once it has gathered information, a Deep Siren returns to the Duchess, and is often sent with the Deep Dregs to storm beaches, infiltrate sewers, or take over cities on stormy nights.
The siren doesn't like being in close combat, and always attempts to use {@spell Misty Step|XPHB} to move to a more beneficial position, then unleash Storm Lash or spellcasting upon their foes.
They flee if surrounded, if outnumbered, or if they feel the battle is not going in their favor.

name: Deepdreck

entries: {@i Poisoned Subterranean Wretch}

Deepdrecks were miners long ago who found themselves far too deep beneath the earth, where they were cursed and corrupted by deforming powers. Now they tunnel and dig greedily, bloated with poisonous gases.
Astute observers have noted that these monsters occasionally bear a resemblance to missing loved ones who have long been thought dead.

entries.name: Secret
entries: The toxic essence of deepdrecks is disrupted by pleasant scents such as flowers, perfume, spices, or incense.
{@i This giant retains a look of daunting power despite its stooped bearing, tattered clothing, and pieces of slapdash armor strapped on wherever it fits.}

entries.name: Haunt Ruins
entries: The degenerate descendants of ancient titans haunt the ruins where their cities once flourished. These descendants hunt for any living thing to eat, including each other, and sometimes chase after herds of goats or other animals for miles. While they are easily distracted, they always find their way home unerringly.

entries.name: Insane and Moody
entries: Degenerate titans are prone to erratic actions and unexpected mood shifts. They are fiercely territorial creatures who worship the still-active magical devices of their cities and any surviving statuary as if the statues were gods. Their lairs are filled with items scavenged from the city. These collections are a hodge-podge of dross and delight, as the degenerate titans are not intelligent enough to discern treasure from trash.

entries.name: Primal Power
entries: Degenerate titans cannot command magical words of power like their ancestors, but they retain a connection to the natural world, allowing them to tap into the earth's latent mystic power to generate strange geomancy. These devolved misfits may have lost most of their former gifts, but what remains are primal powers that tap, without subtlety or skill, into the fundamental building blocks of the world.

items.name: Delerium Dragon Wyrmling
entries: Playful and full of wonder, Delerium Dragon Wyrmlings do not stray far from where they hatch, as they still must contend with their multidimensional existence. A wyrmling usually does not yet fully understand their transtemporal senses, and experiences memories of their adulthood and future in dreams and visions.

entries.name: Delerium
entries: In addition, characters can collect {@item crystal|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium crystals} from its body: a wyrmling has {@dice 2d4} {@item fragment|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|fragments}.

entries.name: Delerium Dragons

entries: This unearthly dragon is a crystalline horror, its body formed from angular gem-like scales pulsing with octarine light. Its form is raw delerium. Each scale is a gleaming crystal refracting light into eerie hues of purple, yellow, and green, with an unnatural sharpness that feels both fragile and impossibly durable.

The dragon's wings are translucent and webbed with glowing crystal veins that shimmer, casting kaleidoscopic patterns as it moves. Each beat causes the air to hum, vibrating with a chaotic energy that overwhelms and distorts the senses. Each step the dragon takes leaves delicate motes of crystal growing into jagged formations, tainting the landscape. Its eyes are like multifaceted gems, swirling with chaotic magic pooling within their depths. The beast's crystalline horns and talons are razor-sharp, gleaming like polished jewels, yet crackling with eldritch energy.

Inscrutable beings of the Space Between Worlds, Delerium Dragons are order from chaos incarnate. How such creatures came to be is unknown, and few know of their existence. Some propose that they emerged spontaneously, hatching from crystalline eggs with octarine shells.

A Delerium Dragon is not simply contaminated, but a unique type of gemstone dragon with an otherworldly physiology. These dragons are literally made of the crystals: their claws, bones, and scales are refracting {@item shard|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium shard}. Their flesh and organs are incomprehensible organic matter, and their blood is delerium sludge. When unleashings its breath weapon, it exhales a storm of glittering shards that explode, causing madness, mutation, and wild magic to erupt in the area.

Delerium Dragons are amongst the most powerful beings born within the Space Between Worlds. Capable of perceiving dimensions imperceptible to mortals, these dragons often seem flighty or {@condition distracted|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}, but this is because they experience layers of reality which humans cannot. They are thus strange intermediaries, able to interact with creatures on a transdimensional level. Indeed, Delerium Dragons are unstuck in time, unrestrained by the linear progression of past, present, and future. Some experience their entire lives simultaneously, whereas others live their lives non-sequentially. Most understand that even their own existences is beyond comprehension, and many contemplate the fundamental nature of existence, chaos, and the cosmos. any are nihilistic solipsists who believe that nothing actually exists except themselves, and even then many doubt their own existence, believing they are merely half-remembered dreams caught betwixt a fleeting thought. Others instead revel in their chaotic existence, seeking new forms of art and untamed creation. Powerful mages and talented bards have sought their wisdom and knowledge.

Most Delerium Dragons find the Mortal World, and mortals, rather limited and boring. Throughout history, only one emerged in the Mortal World, the mighty Amaranthyst, archmage of the Amethyst Academy—the dragon's true nature known only to the other members of the Academy Directorate.

Delerium Dragons exert their force of will over the Space Between Worlds and make their lairs realms unto themselves. hese lairs may open into a Thin Place, the yawning cavern of a normal dragon's lair instead leading to the madness of the Delerium Dragon's home. These dragons fill their lairs with treasures and secrets of mysterious significance and anachronistic origin, hoarding items which may have been valuable in the distant past, or of critical importance to the distant future. Like themselves, some of their greatest possessions may exist in a state mortals can't perceive or which are fundamentally hazardous, such as multidimensional art objects, miniature primordial black holes, degenerate matter taken from a neutron star, or magical vessels containing another universe or pocket dimension.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill History|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine a Delerium Dragon, learning the following based on the result.

entries.name: (15+) Empowered by Eldritch Magic
entries: You understand the dragon's {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances} and senses.

entries.name: (20+) Octarine Breath
entries: You recognize the effects of the Delerium Dragon's breath weapon, as well as noting its Spellcasting capabilities.

entries.name: (25+) Few Weaknesses
entries: You learn its highest and lowest saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: A Delerium Dragon views combat less as a violent encounter and more as a chance to change foes into a new form. It darts about using flight and teleportation, seldom remaining in the same place for more than a turn. Their movement makes it easy for the dragon to find the perfect place to catch many enemies with its breath weapon. Delerium Dragons love to spread {@condition contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} and cause {@table Arcane Anomalies|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Arcane Anomaly}, and delight causing monstrous transformations with their contaminated attacks.

Delerium Dragons use their Bite, Contaminated Rend, and Tail attacks to tear opponents apart in between uses of their breath weapon. When they are unable to close the distance, they mentally assault their targets with Mindfire.

entries.name: Harvestable Components (Rarity Varies)
entries: Component rarities are as follows: Wyrmling: Uncommon; Young: Rare; Adult: Very Rare; Ancient: Legendary.

entries: Aberrant Dust.

entries.name: Delerium
entries: In addition, characters can collect {@item crystal|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium crystals} from its body: a wyrmling has {@dice 2d4} {@item fragment|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|fragments}, a young dragon has {@dice 2d8} {@item shard|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|shards}, and an adult has {@dice 2d6} {@item crystal|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|crystals}. An Ancient Delerium Dragon's body has 1 {@item geode|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium geode} and {@dice 2d6} {@item crystal|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|crystals}.
Who knows how many of these twisted abominations were once our steadfast comrades, friends, and loved ones. When you see these lost souls, you must not hesitate.

Many who succumb to {@adventure contamination|DungeonsDrakkenheim|12} become grotesque mockeries of their former selves. They suffer a wretched and loathsome fate, aimlessly wandering the ruins following half-forgotten memories. Most are gripped by despair, fear, and madness which drive them to act violently, though a rare few experience lucidity and a gruesome awareness of their miserable state. Their distorted and emaciated bodies are sustained by the magic of the Haze.

name: Delerium Dreg

entries: This wretched figure has been twisted and warped by eldritch contamination. Beneath their shredded and torn clothing, you can see all manner of sores, lesions, and bulging blood vessels upon their purple-gray flesh, and their limbs and joints bend at unnatural angles. Their facial features are unnaturally warped into a permanent expression of confused agony, and an octarine glow fills their sunken eyes. Small aberrant mutations appear across their bodies: crystalline bony protrusions and small tendrils bursting forth through their skin, a yellow eyeball blinking open upon their neck, and a disturbingly elongated tongue. As they catch sight of you, they moan painfully and lunge forward.
The typical Delerium Dreg is a disheveled and piteous creature who wanders the ruins in a quasi-addled state. Most have benign mutations that confer no special traits or unique abilities.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Survival|XPHB} or {@skill Nature|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks to {@action Study|XPHB} a Delerium Dreg, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (5+) Humans Transformed
entries: You know these Aberrations are immune to further delerium {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} but otherwise have no special {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}.

entries.name: (10+) Contaminating Claws
entries: You recognize the dangers of the creature's Claw attack.

entries.name: (15+) Shambling Corruption
entries: You understand the creature's highest and lowest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Delerium Dregs are desperate and confused combatants, incapable of any complex tactics beyond lunging towards their foes to attack by the most direct means. If they see a creature who is not contaminated, they will attack on sight. However, they will band together to form small herds, shuffling through ruins, or wandering the streets together. A wounded Delerium Dreg typically responds with fury and rage, attacking whatever damaged it last without regard to its personal wellbeing. In very rare cases, a wounded Dreg may attempt to flee, especially from a much more formidable combatant.

entries: Aberration.

entries: Skull, Spine, Ribs.

entries: Claws.

entries: Hair.

entries: Skin.
