entries: Dr. Everett Freed regards you with a stern frown. He is longfaced, bald-headed, and wears thick, circular glasses that magnify his focused gaze. Beneath his bleached-white surgical apron, he is dressed in a tailored dark jacket. The coat is deceptively normal: thick and heavy, it conceals numerous pockets stuffed with vials and unusual instruments. His hands, sheathed in slightly stained rubber gloves, tightly grip a black leather doctor's bag at his side. A faint scent of formaldehyde and burnt metal clings to him.
I think we can all agree you're better off without vocal chords

Perhaps no apothecary is a more prolific creator of monsters than the Reanimator, and amongst them, Dr. Everett Freed is perhaps the most infamous. A gifted professor of anatomy and medicine at Altbruke University, Dr. Everett Freed served as a field medic and surgeon during the Westemär Civil War, where the brutality and chaos of war allowed him to clandestinely begin his experiments with the fallen or grievously wounded soldiers thrust into his care. The sights of the war caused him to see the frailty of the human form—the cries of pain and agony of the wounded collected in the fields disgusted him with their feeble, broken bodies. Deep within himself welled the desire to create a perfect soldier, a warrior who would not bend or break in battle.

During the war, one of Dr. Freed's duties included triaging casualties to determine who could be saved or recover. Unbeknownst to his commanders, Dr. Freed used his position to manipulate the diagnosis, choosing ideal specimens for his experiments, individuals who would then be listed amongst the slain and missing.

entries.name: Reanimator Minions
entries: It's possible Dr. Freed was the first to create many creatures. He is most well known as the first to create Reautomata. In the process of making his magnum opus, Freed built creatures such as the {@creature Body Snatcher|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}, {@creature Cerebrograft|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}, the {@creature Ripper|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}, and the {@creature Stitcher|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}. Freed's experiments did not stop there, and in many ways his practice ascended the body alone thanks to his collaborations with the Alienist Dr. Sina Rienks, eventually transforming himself into a {@creature Think Tank|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}.

entries.name: Mind Over Body
entries: One of Freed's infamous gambits was to remove his brain from his own body, placing it into a body double. Eventually, Freed became a Think Tank, able to remotely control brainless bodies from his hidden sanctum.

items: {@b Personality Trait:} I am always calm and composed, especially when explaining the 'necessary' cruelty of my experiments
{@b Ideal:} Progress demands sacrifice; the advancement of knowledge justifies all actions, no matter how gruesome.
{@b Bond:} I still possess the first successful reanimation I ever created: the preserved head of a beloved family member. It's both my proudest achievement and my darkest secret.

{@b Flaw:} I am obsessed with the perfection and infallibility of my creations, often dismissing any evidence of their defects, uncontrollable behavior, and horrific appearances. I never accept any failure as my fault.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Medicine|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks to {@action study|XPHB} the Reanimator, learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (10+) Protected by the Reanimated
entries: You know of his {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}, {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}, and Bodyguard {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.

entries.name: (15+) Deadly Toxins
entries: You are aware of his Touch of Death.

entries.name: (20+) Electrical Reinvigoration
entries: You learn of his Reanimate action.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Prior to combat, Freed casts {@spell False Life|XPHB} and {@spell Death Ward|XPHB} on himself, and perhaps any allies joining him in battle. He does not engage in combat without creations by his side. If Freed is caught alone, he doesn't fight; he flees. However, when supported by his loyal creations, he can be overconfident and brash, secure that his bodyguards will keep him safe from harm. Freed always remains within 10 feet of one or more creations so he can use his Bodyguard {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} reliably.

On his turn, Freed uses Electric Jolt and Necrotic Blast to hammer his foes, while directing a favored creation with Creator's Command. Should one of his minions be brought down, he uses Reanimate and immediately sends it back into the action with Creator's Command.

Freed uses Touch of Death against a particularly loathsome foe, one who harries him with dangerous abilities, or who he especially wishes to slay. All the while, he threatens his enemies by telling them his plans for their body parts once he's killed them.
The mastermind behind some of the worst things to ever find in a basement. Watch out because even your fallen allies can be enemies.

name: Dragon
entries: The dragons on Obojima come in all sizes, shapes, and demeanors. Some are playful, some are lazy, some are sagacious, and some are downright dumb. There are dragons that live high in the mountains or deep underground, and there are dragons that roam around and might take up residence in a farmer's barn or curl up under a bridge. Dragons can be animalistic and they can also be intellectual, so it's always good to know what kind of dragon you're encountering before you attempt to commune with one.

entries.name: Honored Guests
entries: Most Obojimans believe that dragons are guardians of the island, and there are many legends that tell of dragons bringing good luck, good fortune, and other supernatural boons to people and to the land. A dragon that takes up residence on a farm is afforded all the hospitality from a good scale scrubbing to home-cooked meals, and a dragon that lives within a hill overlooking a town is certain to have a shrine dedicated to it heaped with flowers, food, and other offerings.

entries.name: Ancient Elders
entries: Across Obojima, temples and shrines to dragons are one way to encounter these massive and sometimes magical beasts but it's wise to remember that not all dragons are benevolent. Some dragons guard treasure or secrets and others may even find humans somewhat delicious. Some dragons have been on Obojima for a very long time and their memories can stretch back a thousand years or more. In that time, a dragon has seen generations come and go, making human needs and lives seem as insignificant as a leaf falling on an autumn evening.
{@i This slender aquatic creature sports a powerful single finned tail and wicked jaws like a matched pair of serrated blades.}

Dragon eels are wingless, slender, underwater dragons that vary widely in color from browns and blacks to brilliant iridescent hues in mottled patterns. Though not true dragons or drakes, they are no less fearsome and powerful.

entries.name: Fond of Servants
entries: While most dragon eels are solitary and irascible, on rare instances some form pairs or small bands—and some gather humanoid servants.

entries.name: Magnetic and Lightning
entries: Dragon eels make their natural homes in twisting underwater cave systems and prefer magnetically-aligned, metallic cavern formations navigable with their refined electric sight. Some dragon eels use their constant electric auras combined with acquired alchemical reagents to electroplate portions of their golden hoard onto the walls of their dwellings.

entries.name: Pirate Fleets and Dominions
entries: Dragon eels claim large swaths of shoreline as their demesne. Although neither particularly cruel nor righteous, a dragon eel often lords over awed tribes, allowing locals to revere it as a mighty spirit. Some dragon eels use such tribes as the core of a pirate fleet or raiding parties carried on their backs. Their ability to swim through air during storms adds to their reputation as terrible thunder spirits.

entries.name: Bribable
entries: Their deceptive moniker sometimes lulls foolish sailors into a false confidence when they expect to face a simple if dangerous eel beast, but instead find themselves dealing with intelligent draconic kings of the coastal shallows. Wise sailors traveling through known dragon eel territory bring tithes and offerings to placate them.

name: Dragon Frog
entries: Dragon Frogs are formidable monsters that once roamed the island as towering behemoths whose steps left villages in shambles—in today's age, they are the domesticated workhorse of the Nakudama people. For centuries the dragon frog has been shaped by Nakudama culture and desires, which in return have changed the creature irrevocably. In the Nakudama Age, it was common for dragon frogs to grow to heights of 60 to 100 feet tall; now the average dragon frog is no larger than a donkey.

entries.name: Near Extinction
entries: During the Age of Nakudama, it became common for great warriors to hunt Dragon Frogs. In certain stories, this was also said to be a method by which one could gain knighthood from the queen. Although most records on this are lost, there is a document that has over a hundred written accounts of slain dragon frogs.
Historians believe it was also during this time when the monarchy began to tame them.
{@i The dragon-headed leaves of these oak trees sometimes rustle despite a lack of wind, betraying a hint that they're more than they seem.}

entries.name: Gifts among Dragons
entries: These magnificent trees are imbued with some characteristics of their draconic masters. While most groves consist of only one type of dragonleaf tree, dragons sometimes make gifts of them to cement a pact or as a show of fealty. The dragon giving the tree relinquishes command of the plant as part of the deal. This accounts for mixed groves belonging to especially powerful dragon lords.

entries.name: Silent Guardians
entries: Dragonleaf trees use fairly simple tactics to deter potential intruders into their masters' lairs. They remain motionless or allow the breeze to jostle their leaves to appear inconspicuous. Once enough intruders enter the grove, the trees fire razor sharp leaves or rain elemental energies upon the intruders, adjusting their position to make better use of their weapons.

entries.name: Long Memories
entries: Dragonleaf trees live up to 1,000 years. They stand 15 feet tall and weigh 3,000 pounds, but ancient specimens can reach heights of 45 feet. Growing a new dragonleaf tree requires a cutting from an existing tree at least 50 years old, which the tree's draconic master imbues with power, sacrificing the use of its breath weapon for a month. While this time barely registers on a dragon's whole lifespan, it still carefully considers the creation of a new tree, for fear that others might discover its temporary weakness.

entries.name: Dragonleaf Trees in Midgard
entries: The finest druidic minds in the Mharoti Empire created these trees for the draconic lords of the land. Once the druids had shown the dragons the secret of the tree's creation, they were slain so that the secret would not spread. A handful of human and kobold gardeners know how to tend them and make them thrive, but little more.

name: Dragonling

entries: I did mein best to downplay ze greed tendencies but zese adorable drakes just kan't help zemselves. If you need ein hot töddy or kold beer in a giffy, chuck von a gold or silver koin und vatch it get to vurk!

Like a dragon, but a little less greedy and a little more pliant, dragonlings are Humperdink's attempt at retaining a dragon's useful characteristics and limiting the more... tyrannical ones. Able to shift its makeup depending on the metals to which it is exposed, the dragonling is an adaptable, if distractable, companion.
If any of the dragonling's traits or actions require a saving throw, it is always against the dragonling's save DC, as calculated below.

entries.name: Save DC
entries.text: 8 + the tamer's proficiency bonus + the dragonling's Constitution modifier

entries.name: Monster Trainer
entries: In addition to the improvements you can normally give your companions, you can choose to grant the dragonling the following improvements using your Monster Trainer feature:

entries.name: Growth I
Prerequisite:
entries: Become a tamer's companion.

entries.name: Type
entries: Passive (companion).

The dragonling's size increases to Small and its Hit Die size increases to a d6 (its hit point maximum consequently increases by 1 for each of its Hit Dice). The damage die of its Bite attack increases to a d8. The dragonling gains this improvement when it becomes a companion; it doesn't cost an improvement.

entries.name: Harden I
Prerequisite:
entries: 3rd-level tamer.

entries.name: Type
entries: Passive (companion).
The dragonling gains a +2 bonus to its AC while it isn't wearing armour.

entries.name: Breath Weapon I
Prerequisite:
entries: 5th-level tamer.

entries.name: Type
entries: Active (action).

As an action, the dragonling can unleash a torrent of elemental energy. Each creature in an area must make a saving throw, taking 17 ({@damage 5d6}) damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The area, damage type, and saving throw depend on the dragonling's affinity (see its Metallic Character trait):

After the dragonling uses this action, it can't do so again until its tamer finishes a short or long rest. When the dragonling's tamer reaches 9th level in the tamer class, this action's damage increases to 24 ({@damage 7d6}).

entries.name: Multiattack
Prerequisite:
entries: 5th-level tamer.

entries.name: Type
entries: Active (action).
As an action, the dragonling can make two Bite attacks.

entries.name: Growth II
Prerequisite:
entries: 5th-level tamer, Growth I.

entries.name: Type
entries: Passive (companion).

The dragonling's size increases to Medium and its Hit Die size increases to a d8 (its hit point maximum consequently increases by 1 for each of its Hit Dice). The damage die of its Bite attack increases from a d8 to a d10.

entries.name: Blindsight
Prerequisite:
entries: 9th-level tamer.

entries.name: Type
entries: Passive (companion).
The dragonling gains blindsight to a range of 15 feet.

entries.name: Harden II
Prerequisite:
entries: 9th-level tamer, Harden I.

entries.name: Type
entries: Passive (companion).
The dragonling gains a +2 bonus to its AC while it isn't wearing armour. This improvement is in addition to the bonus from Harden I.

entries.name: Breath Weapon II
Prerequisite:
entries: 13th-level tamer, Breath Weapon I.

entries.name: Type
entries: Active (action).

The damage of the dragonling's Breath Weapon action increases to 31 ({@damage 9d6}), the area of the cones increases to 30 feet, and the length of the line increases to 90 feet. The dragonling gains a +1 bonus to the save DC of this action. When the dragonling's tamer reaches 17th level in the tamer class, the Breath Weapon's damage increases to 42 ({@damage 12d6}).

entries.name: Growth III
Prerequisite:
entries: 13th-level tamer, Growth II.

entries.name: Type
entries: Passive (companion).

The dragonling's size increases to Large and its Hit Die size increases to a d10 (its hit point maximum consequently increases by 1 for each of its Hit Dice). The damage die of its Bite attack increases from a d10 to 2d6.

entries.name: Wing Attack
Prerequisite:
entries: 17th-level tamer.

entries.name: Type
entries: Active (action).

As an action, the dragonling can beat its wings. Each creature within 10 feet of the dragonling must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC = 8 + the tamer's proficiency bonus + the dragonling's Strength modifier) or take bludgeoning damage and be knocked prone. The damage equals 4d6 plus the dragonling's Strength modifier. Creatures larger than the dragonling automatically succeed on this saving throw. The dragonling can then fly up to half its flying speed.

name: Drakkenheim Sewer Gator

entries: Surfacing from the rancid sewer waters is a terrible alligator nearly fifty feet long. A jagged ridge of delerium runs along its back, ending in a fell crown atop its head as pallid skin frames its octarine glowing eyes. A thick, purple tentacle-like tongue undulates out of its tooth-filled maw. Strong and sturdy legs support its scarred body, attesting to countless battles in the ruins.

Some creatures seem less affected by contamination, or perhaps are just lucky to only grow in size and ferocity. Reptiles are speculated to be more resistant to uncontrollable mutations than other creatures. The occasional gator making its way up the {@link Drann River} was always a problem, but now, stories of vicious lizards are becoming more bizarre and horrifying.

Rumors speak of a massive gator living in the sewers, with sightings in the Drann River or echoes of its growls heard from sewer grates. None who came close enough to verify its existence have yet survived. Some report half-submerged forms passing through sewer entrances, sometimes mistaking them for large turtles. Others tell of a large beast rumbling through the pipes under their feet. In the taverns of Emberwood, the creature has earned the nickname "the Gray Queen" due to her pale skin and delerium crown. Others have called it by other names: the Devil of the Drann or the Greater Gator. Some have suggested that multiple giant gators live in the dirty waters.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Animal Handling|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Nature|XPHB}) checks to study a Drakkenheim Sewer Gator, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (5+) Fearless Aquatic Predator!
entries: You learn the Drakkenheim Sewer Gator's condition {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities} and Swim speed.

entries.name: (10+) Watch out for its bite!
entries: You are aware of the creature's Crushing Bite and Death Roll actions.

entries.name: (15+) Get it out of the water!
entries: You know of the creature's Contaminated Regeneration trait.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Drakkenheim Sewer Gator is primarily aquatic, haunting the sewer system or the Drann River. These monstrosities lunge from the waters to grab prey, dragging it beneath the surface. Once a target is in its jaws, the gator Death Rolls until its victim stops moving. It is a cunning hunter, knowing how to disappear below murky waters, but it can be provoked to chase its prey. Out of the water it is vulnerable and flees if reduced below half its Hit Points.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Monstrosity.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Monster Blood, Contaminated Ichor.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Eyes, Heart, Brain, Guts, Flesh.

entries.name: Bones:
entries: Skull, Ribs, Spine.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Teeth.

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Skin.

name: Drakkenhob

entries: {@i Dragon Disguised as a Festival Horse}

The drakkenhob is a draconic monster with a sinister disguise, presenting itself as an actor wearing a horse costume, such as a mounted knight or a festively clad rider. Its draconic head resembles a decorated or armored horse's head, and its sharp teeth fit together to appear like blunt, harmless decorations. The drakkenhob uses this benign guise to get close to its prey, which are typically within crowds near festivals or parades, before it summons its similarly garbed hunting hounds and strikes. Its breath is a blood-curdling wave of terror that makes lesser victims drop dead from fright alone.

entries.name: Secret
entries: Unable to resist revelry and merriment, drakkenhob are driven away by payment offered in gold or alcohol.
{@i These winged snakes are coastal beasts and sometimes confused with true dragons or wyverns. They are neither, but quite deadly in their own right.}

entries.name: Searing Acid and Dissolving Gaze
entries: The gaze of these winged snakes can paralyze and dissolve their victims. Drakon fangs do not deliver venom; volatile acid constantly burbles up from a drakon's stomach and enhances its attacks. A caustic drool clings to creatures they bite, and drakons can also belch clouds of searing vapor. Their lairs reek with acidic vapors and droplets of searing liquid.

entries.name: Coastal Beasts
entries: Drakons lair along warm, largely uninhabited coasts, where they explore the shores and the coastal shelf, spending as much time above the waves as under them. Fortunately, they rarely travel far inland.

name: Dread Skeljaskra
entries: Once every few generations, a skeljaskra hibernates in a place suffused by magic. Over many years, it grows into a threat to entire settlements. Such horrors are known as dread skeljaskra.

name: Dream Eater

entries: {@i Devourer of Nightmares}

Dream eaters are horrors that feed  on the dreams, sense of identity, and some say the very souls of other creatures. Dream eaters have the bodies and wings of great owls, while their beaks are filled with blunt, humanlike teeth and hide long snaking tongues. Their feathers are drab colors on the exterior, but their wings display a dazzling cascade of rainbow hues on the undersides when unfurled.

These colors flow and shift, mesmerizing the dream eater's prey and leaving them helpless. A creature whose dreams are devoured is left in a listless, near-blank state. Without help, their victims waste away.

entries.name: Secret
entries: Dream eaters are confused by the intricate patterns on moth wings, and it disrupts their own colorful hypnosis.
{@i This tattered skeletal humanoid resembles a monster from a nightmare with vestigial skeletal wings with a few feathers, small horns, sharp teeth, and cloven hooves.}

entries.name: Drawn to Sin
entries: Dream eaters are dedicated to lust, gluttony, and greed. They make their lairs in casinos, brothels, thieves' dens, and other locations where gambling, food, and other pleasures are readily available. Sometimes dream eaters work together to create such a place, especially near large towns or cities. Some band together to create traveling shows, offering all the oddities, whimsies, and flights of fantasy customary for such entertainers.

entries.name: Devouring Hopes
entries: Dream eaters lure people into their lairs, enticing them with promises of pleasure or wealth. Of course, they make sure the odds are stacked in their favor. Eventually, their victims are left with nothing. Worse than the loss of physical treasures, dream eaters leave their victims stripped of hopes and aspirations. Dream eaters feed on emotions, leaving helpless thralls willing to sell their souls for their vices.

name: Dream Whisperer
entries: Those learned individuals with aspirations of greatness, but who have fallen to fate's twisted ironies and been afflicted by a {@spell Curse of Lost Sentiment|GrimHollowPG24}, may emerge from such trials as a Dream Whisperer. Now a deformed, hunched creature covered in contorted arms, the Dream Whisperer uses its many hands to grasp and shred the hopes, dreams, thoughts, and memories of its victims.

Though animalistic in behavior, Dream Whisperers often reside within larger settlements, cities, and the like, where they can spread their influence and remain undetected for long periods of time. Preferring to attack at night, Dream Whisperers often sneak into unsuspecting targets' homes through windows and otherwise inaccessible openings, since their many arms allow them to scale otherwise impossible surfaces. Once inside, their arms serve a second function— to physically tear treasured memories from their victims and replace them with feelings of paranoia and doubt.

Fighting a Dream Whisperer is a dangerous task. Brave heroes have been driven mad by the Dream Whisperer's aberrant attacks. Comrades-in-arms have been compelled to turn on each other, and the weakest minds snap, leaving a drooling mess in the creature's wake. With each stolen memory, the Dream Whisperer seeks to slake its unquenchable thirst for its lost cognition.

entries.caption: Lost Memories
outro: A {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell reverses this effect and restores the victim's memory.
rows: The target becomes deeply suspicious of a character or NPC of the GM's choice. They gain the following flaw: "I know they are seeking to betray me. I have to act first—it's me or them!"
The target forgets all memories of a loved one of the GM's choice. The next time the target sees them, it's as if they are meeting them for the first time.
The target becomes stricken with doubt and gains the following flaw: "The world is out to get me, and I can't win. I may as well give up now."
The target forgets how to speak in one language known, decided by the GM.
The target forgets the location of something important to them, of the GM's choice. It may be the location of a goal, their home settlement, or a hidden treasure.
The target loses an inconsequential memory such as what they ate a few nights ago or the name of an unimportant NPC.

name: Dreamholder
entries: Natives of the Anomalies, dreamholders often find routes through to the Astral Plane and, from this staging post, parasitise creatures who astrally project, hitching a ride on their psyches back into the home plane. There, they flit between the minds of sleeping creatures, distorting each dreamer's narrative and feasting on their fear, joy, and distress. An incorporeal version of the floating eye tyrant, the dreamholder can unleash a devastating array of eye beams at lucid dreamers who threaten to expel them from their mind.

entries.name: Fear of Ejection
entries: Rarely does a dreamholder take physical form on the Material Plane. Instead, a dreamholder traverses the world through a dreamscape, an ephemeral plane created by the psyches of sleeping creatures. If this dreamscape ever disappears, such as if all creatures within range of the dreamholder's influence awaken, the dreamholder is ejected back to the Astral Plane, a place it loathes due to the absence of its favourite snack: sleeping beings. For this reason, dreamholders are commonly found in densely populated areas, places with a mix of diurnal and nocturnal beings, or wherever sleeping creatures can be reliably preyed upon.

The dreamholder is a clever and resourceful aberration. Should its continued existence in the dreams of creatures on the Material Plane be threatened, it chooses one of two tactics. If it believes itself more powerful than its foe, it will immediately attempt to annihilate the threatening creature's psyche and render their body a comatose shell. Alternatively, a dreamholder might bargain with its assailant, delivering secrets to them nightly until such a time as it can destroy this erstwhile ally.

entries.name: Balanced Diet
entries: Dreamholders feed on the gamut of emotions that a creature can experience. For a properly balanced diet, a dreamholder needs to consume anger, disgust, fear, happiness, sadness, and surprise. A dreamholder that can keep a group of humanoids experiencing all these emotions simultaneously is a contented dreamholder indeed.

entries.name: Inconsistent Incorporeality
entries: The dreamholder maintains its incorporeal form through psionics. Its mastery of this technique is absolute; even the most well-placed blow with a magical weapon passes through thin air, the dreamholder dissolving the instant before contact is made. The dreamholder abhors loud noises and psychic attacks, all of which interfere with its focus, causing it to become momentarily corporeal and susceptible to physical blows.

entries.name: Dream Stasis & Bridging
entries: Dreamholders possess the unique ability to bridge the dreams of sleeping creatures, a feature they use to slip from a soon-towake mind into that of one that has recently drifted off. Indeed, one of the symptoms of dreamholder parasitisation is the increased frequency of shared dreams between individuals in a community (and the social awkwardness that soon follows). Powerful dreamholders can exert such influence over a sleeping creature that the dreamer enters a 'dream stasis', a paralytic state from which it can't wake of its own volition. A clever dreamholder learns to release these captured sleepers just before they waste away entirely, knowing full well that they must return to sleep eventually.

entries.name: Dream Lair
entries: Combining these two abilities of stasis and bridging, a dreamholder can create a tangled web of interconnecting landscapes, scenarios, and protagonists, a veritable feast of corrupted dreams. Time dilates and constricts at the dreamholder's whim, and respite is rarely attainable. In this varied, restless landscape, physical prowess means little; the dreamholder is the ruler, and those that are weak of mind seldom emerge.

Drella Swoop is a cheery sera luma able to make conversation with people from all walks of life. She is a con artist who left Alderheart after burning all of her bridges there, and has decided to join the hunters of Reya's Watch in the hopes of swindling them out of some of their more lucrative trophies.
{@i A drowned woman floating in the water, her long hair drifting around her, suddenly rises! Her hair strikes out like dozens of watery snakes.}

entries.name: Raging Romantics
entries: Drowned maidens are piteous, but terrifying, undead. They are created when a woman dies in water due to a doomed romance, often from unrequited love or drowned by a philandering partner. Either way, the drowned maiden awakens from death, seeking vengeance. Even as she dishes out retribution, a drowned maiden anguishes over her tragic fate.

entries.name: Beckoning for Help
entries: The maiden lurks in the silent depths where she died—usually deserted docks, bridges, or coastal cliffs. She waits to pull the living to the same watery grave in which she is now condemned. Using her ability to disguise herself as a living person, she silently beckons victims from afar, acting as if in danger of drowning. When a victim is within range, the maiden uses her hair to pull her victim close enough to drain its strength with a magical kiss. Victims soon weaken and drown. The victim's final vision is the drowned maiden's tearful lament over the loss of life.

entries.name: Death to Betrayers
entries: Desperate individuals may bargain with drowned maidens. Sometimes maidens release pleading victims who promise to return to her lair with the person who caused the maiden's death. Embracing and drowning her betrayer releases the maiden from undeath.

name: Drowned Raider Vaettir
entries: {@i Rotting Waterlogged Warrior}
{@color Brown liquid drips off the corpse of a waterlogged warrior and with it, the stench of decay and mold.|006abe}

Drowned raider vaettir are like others of their kind—restless undead warriors who defend their belongings and burial places. They are called drowned raiders, however, because their burial sites have been flooded or otherwise contaminated with sea water, which alters their forms over time. A drowned raider vaettir has rotten, corrupted flesh that is falling off its skeleton, and it drips liquid constantly. It can regurgitate a stream of rotten, flesh-stripping seawater from its mouth.

While vaettir often defend their burial sites and possessions with a persistent fury, drowned raider vaettir tend to be more chaotic and unpredictable due to the disruption of their lairs and their bodies.

Sometimes, the flooding of a burial site pulls the vaettir's belongings out of their resting place and deposits them in distant places, drawn by the sea's currents. The drowned raider is drawn to these far-flung objects and will hunt them down in an attempt to restore itself to rest.

name: Druid of the Sanguine Rite

entries: This ancient druid is adorned in skulls and bones hanging off its thick gray cloak. They carry a staff of bone drenched in animal blood, with dried blood painted on their face and clothes. Their features are skeletal in nature, their skin stretched tightly over them. They appear ancient, their eyes sunken and black, their teeth yellowed with age and neglect. The druid whispers in forgotten tongues as they perform blood sacrif ices and draw on primal magics.

These druids are older than even the vampire families. The few that remain are not descendants of any vampiric bloodline; they are the ancient blood druids who performed the rituals that created Vladimir von Drakken. Few of these druids still remain and those who do are reclusive and hidden. Their ancient blood rituals instilled in them a cursed eternal life, and those still roaming the world have transformed into something half alive. Not the same as a vampire, and not shackled by the vampires' weaknesses, these druids are bound to darkness to replenish them and use blood to fuel their rituals and magic. Their powers are a tightly guarded secret that few have witnessed.

Some of these dark druids saw Vladimir as a prophet, a destiny fulfilled. The Druids of the Sanguine Rite saw Vladimir as a vessel for their dark magic, a powerful being that would usher in an age where they could practice their rituals openly and grow their power. Others live eternally in deep regret of transforming Vladimir, feeling that in doing so they cursed themselves to an eternity of hiding in the darkness.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Religion|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when taking the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine a Druid of the Sanguine Rite, learning the following based on the result.

entries.name: (10+) Unrelenting Unlife
entries: You recognize the creature's Regeneration trait.

entries.name: (15+) Bloody Renewal
entries: You learn of the creature's Bloodthorn Whip attack and Plasma Absorption trait

entries.name: (20+) Unnaturally Aware
entries: You know their highest and lowest ability scores

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The druid of the blood rites uses dark magic to twist the lifeforce of other creatures. The druid uses its bloodthorn whip to inflict a series of open wounds upon its foes, and then feeds on their lifeforce by pulling it through their wounds using plasma absorption.
When not directly engaged in combat, the druids attempt to charm a group of foes and convince them to partake in their blood rituals, using their life force as sacrifice to empower one of their own.
If the druids are directly confronted with greater numbers, or their health is below half, they attempt to flee.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Undead.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Monster Blood.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Eyes, Heart, Brain, Guts, Flesh.

entries.name: Bones:
entries: Skull, Spine, Ribs.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Teeth, Claws.

entries.name: Hair:
entries: Hair

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Skin.

entries.name: Dust:
entries: Undead Dust.

{@note This Hydra lives in {@book Mooren Lake|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Mooren Lake} and has gained intelligence by living for so long in the {@item residuum|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}-infused waters. It has an Intelligence score of 12 (+1), can speak {@language Common}, and commands a tribe of {@creature lizardfolk}.}
{@note See {@book Unfriendly Waters|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Unfriendly Waters (mid-level)}, a mid-level adventure hook, for more information.}

Du'ulora are spirits of fury that feed on anger and inspire rage in mortals. A du'ulora is a maelstrom of eyes and wings, bound together by flesh that seems like solidified shadow. It can extend up to three tentacles from this dark mass. A du'ulora can turn a victim's anger into manifested heat; in battle, it grapples its victims and burns them with their own fury.

entries.name: Manipulating Fury
entries: While they feed on anger and hatred, du'ulora rarely act rashly. They are cunning and calculating strategists who excel at inspiring fury in others and turning it against them. In battle this can cause their victims to lower their guard and even to strike their own allies in heedless rage. As servants of the Dreaming Dark, the du'ulora craft dreams that stir buried anger and incite hatred; they excel at igniting feuds and inspiring vendettas. So where a tsucora agent of the Dreaming Dark manipulates peoples' fears and a hashalaq employs seduction, the du'ulora excel at inciting violence.

entries.name: The Fists of Dal Quor
entries: The du'ulora are martial champions of the quori. They thrive on conflict and love to personally crush their enemies. While they enjoy fighting in the vanguard, the du'ulora are also skilled strategists. In Dal Quor , the du'ulora command squads of tsucora and lesser quori. In Riedra, military commanders are typically Inspired bound to du'ulora spirits.

entries.name: Rage Against The Darkness
entries: The du'ulora bound to the kalashtar serve the light, but they still manipulate fury. Du'ulora kalashtar learn to harness and channel their own aggression, and are often Fighters or Barbarians; others are dispassionate Monks, who provoke rage in their enemies while never allowing it to distract them from their goals.

entries.name: Quori
entries: The quori are the spirits that rule Dal Quor , the Region of Dreams. Quori are immortal, but they can be slain; when a quori dies, its essence returns to the Dreaming Dark, where it is reconstituted as a new spirit. Quori spirits are bound to emotions, and they feed on those emotions and excel at manipulating them in mortals. The tsucora thrive on fear, the hashalaq manipulate pleasure, the du'ulora are driven by anger, and the kalaraq consume pride and ambition. These are the most common quori, but there are many others; the spiteful tsoreva and the domineering usvapna have already been mentioned in previous editions.

The quori are the creations of il-Lashtavar, the malevolent force that shapes Dal Quor. Cruelty is a part of their nature. However, when a quori is reborn, there is a microscopic chance that it will be touched by il-Yannah, the incarnation of light that will one day replace the Dreaming Dark. It's possible for a quori to carry this seed of light and never embrace it. The kalaraq Taratai was the first to rally those quori who could sense the light, teaching them to push back the darkness and embrace il-Yannah. These rebels are the spirits who are now bound to the kalashtar. They are still quori—tsucora, hashalaq, du'ulora, kalaraq—and they are still tied to the emotion associated with their quori type. But they are driven by their vision of the light that is to come rather than the darkness of the present. Taratai's rebels fled Dal Quor long ago, and there have surely been new quori touched by il-Yannah since then. But today, the Dreaming Dark are constantly policing their own ranks and searching for such "corrupted" spirits. Any that are found will be destroyed, so their spirits can be reborn as proper servants of il-Lashtavar.

All quori have powerful psionic abilities. DMs could choose to represent this by granting each quori {@book Eberron: Rising from the Last War|ERLW} telepathy with a range of 120 feet. If a quori has any Inspired hosts, as do all that interact with the Material Plane , it would also speak the Riedran language.

entries.name: Quori: Fiends Or Aberrations
entries: Quori aren't biological creatures. They're immortal spirits, fragments of nightmare spawned by il-Lashtavar. They don't sleep, and they dine only on the emotions of mortals. They are known for their ability to possess other mortals, a reflection of their fundamentally spiritual nature. All of these make them quite different from creatures such as beholders or mind flayers—monsters that are deeply alien, but that are still formed of flesh and blood.

The choice to classify quori as Aberrations in fifth edition reflects the idea that "aberration" is a broad category including any entity that is fundamentally alien; and certainly, the quori have no place in the natural world. However, this has a number of concrete mechanical effects. Many effects that target evil spirits only affect Fiends and Undead. As Aberrations, quori can't be detected by a Paladin's Divine Sense or banished to Dal Quor with {@spell Divine Word|XPHB}. The {@spell Hallow|XPHB} and {@spell Forbiddance|XPHB} spells don't protect against them. This was an intentional decision that renders quori immune to many of the tools that can be deployed against devils or demons. However, as a DM, you can choose to make quori Fiends instead of Aberrations if you want these spells and effects to be effective against them. Or you could compromise by leaving quori as Aberrations, but say that Clerics and Paladins devoted to the Path of Light can affect quori with any spell or class feature that affects Fiends. This keeps quori as mysterious and alien, and gives the Path of Light a unique role in battling them.
{@i The black horse strides out of the shadows with its nostrils huffing steam. Its rider, swathed in black leather, raises its arm to reveal not a lantern but its own severed, grinning head.}

Though it appears to be a headless rider astride a black horse, the dullahan is a single creature. The fey spirit takes the shape of a horse rider holding its own head aloft like a lantern, or (more rarely) the form of an ogre cradling its head in one arm.

entries.name: Harbingers of Death
entries: Hailing from the darkest of fey courts, the dullahan are macabre creatures that walk hand in hand with death. They sometimes serve powerful fey lords and ladies, riding far and wide in the capacity of a herald, bard, or ambassador. More often than not they carry doom to a wretch who roused their lord's ire.
{@i The sand surges and shifts, a sinkhole opens, and sandy tendrils reach out.}

entries.name: Enormous Forms
entries: Though most commonly seen as dunes, a dune mimic can take the form of a date palm grove, a riverbank, an enormous boulder, or other large shapes in the landscape.

entries.name: A King's Guardians
entries: Dune mimics were created by a forgotten king as guardians for his desert tomb. Somewhere, dozens of them guard vast wealth.

entries.name: Spread by Spores
entries: Although not intended to reproduce, they began producing spores spontaneously and replicating themselves. Now they are spread across the deserts. Luckily for the other inhabitants, dune mimics reproduce just once per century

name: Durheim Guide
entries: When Durheim monks have honed their soul to the point where the Walking the Liminal Path is the next stage of their destiny, they begin their journey as Guides. Along the Path, they travel across the land and dutifully seek out struggling spirits. When they feel the time is right, they return to record their experiences. As the main body of the Monastery's membership, Guides are often someone's first introduction to the Order.

name: Durheim Initiate
entries: Those who have only recently begun to follow the teachings of Attiskin are referred to as initiates. These individuals have begun to open their eyes to the wonders and dangers of the Ethereal, but they are only fledglings. Some of these inexperienced monks feel the call to Walk the Liminal Path earlier than is typical—these brave souls are destined to accomplish greatness or fall to tragedy.

name: Durheim Leader
entries: Within the walls and courtyards of Durheim Monastery, the Leader serves as spiritual and secular advisor. In this role, they give lectures and interpretations of Lightseer Attiskin's teachings and philosophies, and ensure that both the living and the dead can walk their respective paths safely.

Black-tailed squirrels called dusktails are found across Humblewood. Dusktails are swift, agile, and intelligent. Dusktails can eat just about anything, and are adept at sneaking into seed stores where they can quickly deplete food supplies if given the chance.

{@i This striking woman with obvious fey features and skin the color of slate sits in the shade of an ancient, vine-wrapped tree. Clothed in vines and leaves, she is almost indistinguishable from the tree.}

entries.name: Creeper Vine Spirits
entries: Duskthorn dryads are spirits tied to thorn-bearing creeper vines. They seek out dead trees as homes for their vines. They can travel through trees to escape their foes but must stay near their vines.

entries.name: Grove Guardians
entries: Duskthorn dryads use their vines and the plants in their glades to defend themselves. They often call on the aid of forest animals and children of the briar. Occasionally, a circle of duskthorn dryads work together to call on the aid of an enormously strong vine troll skeleton to protect their grove.

entries.name: Duskthorn Dryads in Midgard
entries: These dryads are commonly found near the ruins of Thorn, in the Arbonesse Forest, and in the Shadow Realms. They are close friends to the darker fey and are thought by some to be created from ordinary dryads drawn into the corruption of the Shadow Realm. Certainly, their mastery of the shadowy Umbral language shows their close ties to this darker world.

{@i A ragged creature emerges from the sand. Its spindly frame is encased in a hodge-podge of armor scraps and rusted weapons. A long, hooked nose protrudes over a wide mouth filled with sharp teeth}.

Dust goblins vary greatly in size and appearance, although they are universally scrawny, bony, and lanky. They seem to suffer from malnutrition even when in perfect health, a perception reinforced by the way their bellies distend after they've gorged themselves on flesh. Their skin is always dry and cracked, ranging from dusky gray to dark green in color.

entries.name: Rule the Wastelands
entries: Dust goblins are twisted creatures, tainted by many generations of life in a blasted wasteland. After a magical war devastated the dust goblins' homeland, they rose to become the most dominant inhabitants. They inhabit ancient ruins and ambush travelers who stray too close to their borders.

entries.name: Twisted Minds
entries: The lingering magical energy saturating the wastes of their home, coupled with the harsh conditions in which they scratch out a living, have tainted the minds of all dust goblins. Their thinking is alien and unfathomable to most creatures. Whereas most goblins are cowardly, dust goblins don't seem to experience fear. To the contrary, they enjoy wearing skull helmets and using ghostly whistles to frighten foes. Owing to this alien mindset, dust goblins get along disturbingly well with Aberrations. The creatures often forge alliances and work together for mutual benefit, while making their unnerving mark on communal lairs.

name: Dustbunny
entries: Dustbunnies are relatively harmless, often pesky critters that live within towns and out on the plains and grasslands in deep burrows. There are many stories about dustbunnies, the most common one being a cautionary tale to keep your house or shop swept clean as it can quickly become overrun by dustbunnies. Some believe they were created by Obojima and are therefore good luck, so they allow the critters to multiply in droves, but many just think it an excuse to get out of housework. Whatever the case, most towns have their fair share of dustbunnies and live in relative harmony with them.

Curves are seldom seen in the stacked blocks and precise geometric forms of dwarven architecture. Devoid of angles and planes with no beginning and no end, circles are a mystery and hold power. Dwarven ringmages are those dwarves who have mastered the art of tapping into that power, imbuing it into metal rings and their spellcasting. Rings and circles are sacred to them, and they read omens in the cycle of seasons, the shape of flowers, and in a storm's first rain drops.

name: Dyra
entries: Fully recognizing their strengths and weaknesses, the dyra have spent centuries developing their mechanical prowess, acting as Magmarath's premier engineers. Some dyra have even developed juggernauts—metal and stone constructs that they can mold and stretch themselves around to pilot. While doing so, the dyra gains increased size and vigor from its sturdy framework, and also gains additional offensive and defensive capabilities as the juggernaut helps ground and redirect electricity.

name: Dyra Juggernaut
entries: Infernal Barbarians take power from an infusion of fiendish energy, often transfused with blood magic, that imbues them with the wrath of the Lower Planes. Many of them are coerced into contracts and deals, while others seek this power willingly, or in a desperate attempt to survive the perils of the Iron Maw Arena.
{@i This swanlike creature's feathers are made of shining metal. When it inhales, the feathers on its chest glow red hot.}
Eala are beautiful but deadly creatures native to the Plane of Shadow. They grow feathers like their Material Plane counterparts, but their feathers are made of gleaming, razor-sharp metal.

entries.name: Metallic Diet
entries: Eala plumage displays a stunning mixture of metallic colors, which vary depending on their diet. An eala uses its fire breath to melt metals with low melting points such as gold, silver, lead, copper, and bronze. The eala consumes the molten metal, some of which migrates into the creature's deadly feathers. Eala that display primarily or entirely a single color are highly prized among some nobility.

entries.name: Eala in Midgard
entries: Eala are favorites of Sarastra, the Queen of Night and Magic and a ruler of the shadow fey. She is partial to jet black eala, and all such specimens are brought to her flock at the Winter Palace. Those who bring her such birds are rewarded with a magical dagger and the title and status of "Honored Eala Catcher," or "Lord or Lady of Black Feathers" for those who bring her several.

{@i This terrible creature resembles an imposing knight wearing baroque plate armor made of calcified resin. Its helm is a blank gray oval without eye slots or mouthpiece, and one of its arms ends in a slavering, fanged mouth.}

Eaters of dust can consume just about anything with their horrible maw-arms, but they prefer the flesh and souls of mortals. This ability to sustain themselves on almost anything, even on dust and soil, earned them their current name, given by the fiends that employ them, after their original name was long forgotten. A typical eater of dust is 7 feet tall and weighs more than 350 pounds. While an eater of dust cannot speak, it can telepathically communicate.

entries.name: Mercenary Companies
entries: Eaters of dust—or {@i yakat-shi} as they are sometimes called in ancient planar texts—roam the lower planes selling their services to arch-devils, demon lords, and other fiendish rulers for the chance to sample new flavors and morsels. Eaters of dust feel only contempt for most other life forms. They attack and eat their non-eater allies at the first sign of weakness. Because of this, eaters of dust often operate in small, deadly units of eaters led by a powerful leader, styled the {@i yakat-norog}.

entries.name: Armor Shell
entries: While many sages confuse eaters of dust for some obscure variety of fiend, they are aberrations escaped from a far-flung dimension of madness and nightmares. Indeed, their armor is not armor at all, but a secreted resin that hardens into a shell as strong as steel. When cracked, it exudes a nacreous blood, and the resulting scar resembles mother-of-pearl. Some old eaters are covered in intricate networks of shimmering scars.

entries.name: {@book Ebon Syndicate|GrimHollowCG24|13|Ebon Syndicate}

entries: The night is our kingdom.

If behind every unexplained success lies an undiscovered crime, then the Ebon Syndicate's successes are as innumerable as their crimes. The syndicate's tendrils stretch out from the seedy shadows into every aspect of urban life in Etharis, and often beyond.

They are the beggar on the corner inconspicuously eavesdropping on nobles' conversations. They are the thief cutting a purse string. They are the traceless spy planting evidence before the militia raid. They are the hooded assassin coming for you in the dark alley, and the smiling waiter serving you poisoned wine should you escape that alley. They have the thing you want, and the thing you need, and their eyes on the thing you hold most dear.

The syndicate primarily operates in Etharis's biggest and richest cities, where targets and opportunities are most plentiful. Lesser organizations and freelance operatives soon find themselves facing a deadly offer: stop, join, pay, or find yourselves bleeding in a gutter. The latter is not an idle threat, but a quickly fulfilled promise—those who step on the Syndicate's toes or try to take their territory are mercilessly dispatched.

Etharis's other major factions may look down upon the syndicate's activities, but they know enough to respect its capabilities. Even groups like the Augustine Company and the Watchers that publicly claim to oppose the syndicate have been known to take {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} of its unparallelled spy network.
The syndicate pursues every kind of under-the-table opportunity. From petty crime to organized drug smuggling, extortion, and assassination — if it needs to be done outside the law, they get it done.

entries.name: Agents
entries: The unknowing agents of the Syndicate are many. A wash maid with access to everyone from soldiers to nobles is a perfect scout for a den of thieves. A duke's steward with a gambling problem may divulge the an important delegate's arrival, enabling a road ambush that can't be traced. A gang of street thugs tipped off to a rich dandy's passage won't know that their attack forced the victim's influential father promt a military reinforcement, leaving a distant outpost ripe for the taking. Such are the webs the Syndicate spins.

entries.name: The Shadow Academy
entries: For the chosen few identified to join as full members of the Syndicate, there is the Shadow Academy. The academy is not a school or training ground; there are no stern masked instructors preaching rules, and there is no graduation to a fancy moth mask. The Shadow Academy is itself a tenet, a concept of how agents are trained.

The core philosophy of the academy is of hands-on training: "Every lesson is an action; every action is a test." Passage through the Shadow Academy is typically overseen by the member who vouched for the recruit. Trust is paramount. If you're not willing to vouch for those you bring in, then they do not deserve anyone else's time.

Recruits are expected to bring some level of craft to the Syndicate, but more importantly, the right mindset. Once a recruit is brought in, they are mentored by different specialists, learning tasks on the job, before being passed on to the next. The recruit's performance is discussed by the leadership when they change mentors.

Promising recruits who fail at certain tasks are given chances to excel in other areas. Recruits that fail repeatedly, or who embarrass the Syndicate, tend to disappear. Many are killed, but some—if the knowledge they have poses little danger—may be released and watched or relocated. While there are no "instructors" per se, the Syndicate encourages skilled members to pass their knowledge on. In exchange, they get a skilled new member for their own crew.

entries.name: Specialists
entries: The Syndicate is not a military organization and has no official ranks other than Grayman. Members are referred to by name or alias, and often by their specialties, often using local slang. For example, spies might be called "ears," "listeners," or "flies," while assassins could be "blades," "blackmoths," or "fins." Slang varies widely across the continent.

entries.name: Elite Assassins
entries: The Syndicate's most skilled assassins concoct specialized compounds for each mission. They can make their target spasm in pain, suffocate in silence, or simply fall unconscious, allowing the agent to wisk them away or stage the murder as desired. Their smoke bombs help them escape or turn an unexpected fight in their favour.

entries.name: Local Enforcers
entries: Street-level agents deliver overt official messages. Thugs and brutes with some manners and basic business sense can beat both into a target when the need arises. In addition to common weapons, Syndicate enforcers favor fighting chains or "chain-knuckles" that give them the choice to strangle or bind their opponents. These have the benefit of being less conspicuous than a blade.
{@i An evil wind swirls out of the desert, parching those it touches and whispering evil plans.}

entries.name: Bitter Exiles
entries: Desert and plains tribes often exile their criminals to wander as outcasts. A banished criminal who dies of thirst sometimes rises as an edimmu, a hateful undead that blames all sentient living beings for its fate.

entries.name: Rise Again
entries: Unless its body is found and given a proper burial, an edimmu is nearly impossible to destroy. Edimmus rarely venture more than a mile from their remains, but they sometimes follow prey they have cursed to seal the creature's fate. Once that creature is slain, they return to the site of their demise.

{@i The grotesque beast has the muscular tail, bulbous head, and rubbery, slime-covered flesh of an eel. Its torso and webbed paws resemble those of a misshapen canine, while needle-sharp teeth fill its menacing jaws.}

entries.name: Hounds of the River Fey
entries: Ferocious aquatic fey, these amphibious menaces often serve lake trolls, lorelei, green hags, and other watery fey and giants. Predatory beasts as dangerous on land as they are in the water, the have a capricious cruelty. Few creatures beyond the fey appreciate eel hounds' lithe power and cruel grace, instead noting only their grotesque form and unnerving savagery.

entries.name: Slippery Ambushers
entries: Eel hounds are ambush predators, hiding among the muck and algae of riverbanks, bursting out as a pack. Possessed of a low cunning, they prepare ambushes by vomiting their slippery spittle where land animals come to drink or along game trails. Then they surge from the water to snatch the off-balance prey. They surround targets, latching on with their powerful jaws, and then drag non-aquatic prey into the depths to drown or force aquatic prey onto land to suffocate.

entries.name: Fey Water Hounds
entries: Eel hounds understand Sylvan, and those dwelling near humans or other races pick up a few words in other tongues.

name: Effulgent Cnidarian

entries: A translucent bulbous mass floats through the air gently, throbbing neon colors radiating across its skin like a cosmic nebula or an eldritch borealis. A mass of thin strands dangle down from the creature, pulsating with bioluminescent light. The tendrils move and glide about, gently groping and grabbing at objects as it passes by. The whole creature glows, illuminating the darkened city streets around it. A distant chorus of ethereal hums and tones fill the air.

Drakkenheim glows at night. The bizarre alien color palette of the cosmic borealis caused by the Haze and the {@item crystal|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium crystals} is a sight to behold. Yet, within the drab nighttime landscape, one can also spot orbs of strange hypnotic light bobbing and swaying between the tall towers and ruined buildings. Upon closer inspection, these wispy lights appear to be a sort of aerial jellyfish, whose semi-translucent skin shifts in kaleidoscopic colors.

These strange jellyfish creatures light up the Inner City of Drakkenheim at night, like bizarre night lights that float through the city. Their nature and what exactly created them remains a mystery. Jellyfish were not a common creature found in the Drann River, and so Academy researchers have speculated that these creatures emerged from rifts between the Mortal World and the Space Between Worlds, or that they are the core of arcane energies coalescing into a sentient wisp before transforming into a body made of delerium that illuminates the city in the twilight of dusk. They gently hum in dissonant notes, giving an eerie presence to the ruins at night.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks to {@action Study|XPHB} an Effulgent Cnidarian, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (5+) Aberrant Resistance
entries: You recognize the monster's {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities} and {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}.

entries.name: (10+) Hypnotic Color Change
entries: You learn of the monster's Hallucinogenic Bioluminescence trait.

entries.name: (15+) Weak but Aware
entries: You are aware of the monster's strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Effulgent Cnidarians are not predatorial—they only want to bask in the glow of {@item crystal|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium crystals}, feeding slowly on the arcane energies they emit. They are, however, protective of their food sources. If creatures venture into an area of heavy delerium crystallization, they are sure to find a few Cnidarians bobbing about. The Cnidarian prefers to use its Hallucinogenic Bioluminescence to dissuade threats from engaging, instead hoping to cause its enemies to kill one another. The Cnidarians feed on creatures under its hypnosis, absorbing their essence through its tendrils. If attacked, it uses its Reflexive Flash and attempts to move away from its threats, often floating straight up as quickly as it can and out of the reach of danger.
Cnidarians do not stay around to fight. If all targets have avoided its charm and are actively attacking it, it abandons its food source to seek other safer areas.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Aberration.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Contaminated Ichor, Goopy Ooze.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Glands.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Tentacles.

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Skin.

entries.name: Dust:
entries: Aberrant Dust.
In the search for glowing rocks beware the mind jellyfish.

name: Eikthyrnir
entries: {@i Thorny Stag Horror}

{@color The creature's pelt resembles that of a deer, but denser and shaggy, like that of a bear. Its antlers are disproportionately large and curved into long, wickedly sharp points above eyes that burn with uncanny fire. Thorny brambles have pushed through the beast's skin from within, wrapping around its body and antlers like climbing ivy.|006abe}

Eikthyrnir are enormous stag-like horrors formed when stags consume World Tree acorns that have been corrupted by evil energies. They stalk the branches of the World Trees, occasionally reaching mortal planes, where they spread horror and carnage.

name: Einar Tromma
entries: Trollkin leader of a college

{@i A line of stout, bearded warriors with golden auras stand ready, adorned in chain mail and carrying battle axes and oaken shields. Their badges and symbols are all different, and no two have the same braided pattern in their beards.}

The einherjar are great warriors chosen by the valkyries. They eat and drink their fill of boar and mead each night, then spend their days preparing for Ragnarok. Some of this is combat training, and other portions are raids against the giants fighting the gods. Regardless of how often they are slain, the einherjar reappear each morning in Odin's hall, leaving them without fear of death.

entries.name: Defenders of the Mortal World
entries: Occasionally, ravenfolk guide a troop of einherjar against some of Loki's minions on the Material Plane. These raids are often small battles that further delay the inevitable rise of the world serpent and its many evil spawn. They fight against giants, demons, lindwurms, and other evil creatures, but the einherjar themselves are not exactly saintly. They can drink and carouse with the loudest and most boastful of humanoids. Though otherworldly and servants of Odin, einherjar are very humanlike, if somewhat larger than life.

entries.name: Fear Dragons
entries: The einherjar are superstitiously fearful of dragons and dragonkin, the distant progeny of the world serpent.

entries.name: Never Speak to the Living
entries: In theory, the einherjar are forbidden from speaking with the living: they must pass their words through a valkyrie, ratatosk, ravenfolk, or one of the other races allied with Odin. In practice, this rule is often flouted, though if Loki's servants notice it, they can dismiss any einherjar back to Valhalla for a day.

name: Eira Mosjøen
entries: Local villain

name: Eirik Ellefsen
entries: Bard and leader of Skaldholm

items.name: Elder Dragon Frog
entries: Most Nakudama would say that elder dragon frogs haven't existed in centuries. However, it doesn't stop the myth and rumor that some are still alive on the island today—hiding from the mighty forces of the long-since dissolved Nakudama armies. Little to no proof has been offered as to where these creatures are hiding, but some academics believe that there is some legitimacy to these claims.

name: Elder Lava Wurm
entries: Occasionally, a lava wurm will live long enough and grow their vestigial wings large enough to become an elder. These creatures are an order of magnitude more dangerous than the young wurms, as their small but now functional wings allow them to more readily and swiftly follow their prey through molten rock and the open air. With their sheer bulk and love for fine granite, elder lava wurms are an infrequent but greatly feared invader of Heavensteppe, usually requiring many Steel Hawk lives to drive away.
{@i A large dragon with black scales and shadowy wings emerges from the darkness. Its red eyes glare bright as coals, and it speaks in a deep monotone.}

entries.name: Solitary Lairs
entries: They haunt dark and lonely places, such as deep caves, dense forests, shadowy ruins, and many wild locations in the Plane of Shadow. They are long-lived for drakes, often reaching 250 years of age, and mate rarely, abandoning their eggs shortly before hatching.

entries.name: Fade Into Shadows
entries: An elder shadow drake naturally fades from view in areas of dim light or darkness, becoming invisible until it attacks or is bathed in sunlight.

name: Elder Thing

entries: They represented some ridged barrel-shaped object with thin horizontal arms radiating spoke-like from a central ring and with vertical knobs or bulbs projecting from the head and base of the barrel. Each of these knobs was the hub of a system of five long, flat, triangularly tapering arms arranged around it like the arms of a starfish.
entries.from: H.P. Lovecraft, Dreams in the Witch House

entries: The bizarre elder things predate all other known forms of life, or so sages believe. Ancient ruins, archaeological evidence, and even entreaties to the gods seem to indicate that the elder things existed in the universe even before the gods arose.

entries.name: Ancient Remnants
entries: In their heyday, the elder things dug deep into the lore around the Cthulhu Mythos. They crafted the first shoggoths and used them to erect great, cyclopean cities. They warred against the mi-go and the star-spawn of Cthulhu for dominance over the primordial world, and were eventually defeated when the shoggoths grew too cunning and overthrew them.

entries.name: Scattered Remnants
entries: A few elder things remain, though they are scattered and isolated. Now and again a mortal sage or spellcaster may come into contact with one. They can offer strange insights to those who learn their bizarre, piping, whistling language.

entries.name: Slumbering Threats
entries: In some cold corners of the world, ancient ruins built by the elder things remain undisturbed. These creatures slumber there, having plunged into a hibernation in the ancient days in order to outlast the threats they faced. When outsiders uncover these ruins, the elder things awaken and set to work. Driven by a scientific approach to the world, they may catch, study, and dissect any humanoids they encounter. They use their magic and cunning to cultivate worship and obedience, turning neighboring creatures into cultists to help them achieve their inscrutable aims.

One of the finest professors in the Amethyst Academy, Eldrick Runeweaver has personally instructed a generation of talented arcane spellcasters. He is the foremost living expert on abjuration magic, but is also highly regarded within the Academy as a dedicated administrator and calculating leader. If Eldrick Runeweaver successfully retakes the Inscrutable Tower, he will likely take up the vacant spot in the Academy Directorate and assume the mantle of Archmage of Drakkenheim.

Eldrick Runeweaver is a towering and broad-shouldered man in his mid-sixties. His amber eyes glow softly behind his circular glasses, and he has a square-cut, greying black beard. He wears nine rings of silver, gold, and electrum: one on each finger except his left thumb. He wears flowing purple garb with golden embroidery, and carries an obsidian staff tipped with a delerium crystal.

items.name: Personality Trait
items.entry: I carefully calculate my every action, and I speak using a few well-chosen words. I'm a teacher at heart, so I often phrase my responses in the form of a pointed question.

items.name: Ideal
items.entry: I will seek out more information whenever I encounter an unknown situation or problem. Through reason and logic, the facts always bear out the truth of the matter.

items.name: Bond
items.entry: I hold a position of responsibility and authority within the Amethyst Academy, and it is my duty to protect the Academy's interests, carry out its agenda, and keep its many secrets.

items.name: Flaw
items.entry: I care deeply for my students, but tend to overlook their faults and failures. I've had several wayward apprentices over the years, and I've often had to cover up their mistakes.

entries: Eldrick Runeweaver has a cat familiar, and travels with an iron golem bodyguard and a homunculus servant. He most often communicates via sending, telepathic bond, and project image spells, or by sending his simulacrum instead. Eldrick always has a contingency spell in place, and has a clone kept in a distant stronghold with extra equipment should the unthinkable occur.

name: Eldritch Cataclysm

entries: A swirling vortex of dark clouds, debris, and icy shards moves in like an eldritch storm. Crackling octarine lightning fills the air, the ground rumbles and shakes with the might of the unnatural weather phenomenon, but this is no ordinary storm. Within the dark clouds appears a snarling face, its eyes and mouth like pools of octarine light. The creature is the weather itself, warped and infused by the Haze of Drakkenheim into an arcane and twisted form of life, filled with the uncaring and unbridled anger of a storm.

Drakkenheim was always known for its lousy weather; miserable rainy days were commonplace even before the city was ravaged by the falling stars. Now, the city is frequently wracked by violent and otherworldly weather conditions. The ever-present mists of the Haze occasionally give way to contaminated acid rain, flashing bolts of arcane lightning, and piercing hailstones filled with {@item shard|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium shards}. Most adventurers know it's best to avoid venturing into the ruins altogether on such days, but in the erratic conditions of the ruins, the weather can shift dramatically at a moment's notice.

During the fiercest octarine thunderstorms, the powerful energies converge into a maelstrom of lesser elemental forces, fusing into a sentient storm known as an Eldritch Cataclysm. Its manifestation is marked by a swirling vortex of dark clouds, debris, and icy shards, all illuminated by the ominous glow of octarine lightning. These raging elementals are driven by pure destructive impulse, and their presence calls forth a host of other Contaminated Elementals to join them in a cacophony of annihilation. {@creature Entropic Flame|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Entropic Flames} and {@creature Living Deep Haze|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Living Deep Hazes} are readily drawn to Eldritch Cataclysms, but their presence compels even normally docile Contaminated Elementals such as {@creature Walking Delerium Geode|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} and {@creature Animated Delerium Sludge|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} to rise up and destroy.

Fascinated by the destructive power of these elemental creatures, mages of the Amethyst Academy have studied these phenomena surrounding the emergence of an Eldritch Cataclysm. Corroborating reports from Hooded Lantern scouts indicate that the locus for these storms appears to be the swirling vortex of raw magical energies which overhang the Crater itself.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they {@action Study|XPHB} an Eldritch Cataclysm, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (15+) Amalgamation of Energies
entries: You learn the creature's {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}, as well as its Air Form trait.

entries.name: (20+) An Octarine Storm
entries: You recognize its Chain Lightning, Meteor Strike, Quake, and Icy Bolt actions.

entries.name: (25+) Exceedingly Resilient
entries: You are aware of its strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Eldritch Cataclysms rule the skies, and never willingly descend to the ground. Instead, it rains down lightning, meteors, and icy blasts from above. The temperamental nature of these elementals means they delight in attacking with a variety of elements, and seldom use the same action two rounds in a row. They enjoy using their Meteor Strike on targets they've {@condition Frozen|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} with Icy Bolt, and delight in using their Cyclonic Storm to blow away weapons and equipment dropped by targets of their Chain Lightning.

These enraged creatures revel in destruction but have little conception that anything could actually pose a threat to them. When confronted with a foe able to withstand their onslaught, they treat it as a personal affront, and furiously focus their subsequent attacks upon them occasionally to the exclusion of all else. Despite this single-minded strategy, an Eldritch Cataclysm can recognize when a creature is resistant or immune to its elemental attacks and tries to use only the most effective powers against its chosen target.

name: Eldritch Crawler

entries: Amidst a web of fractured realities and glimpsed timelines sits an arachnid creature with twisted features. Its elongated form writhes and shivers as it clambers across its broken glass mosaic of possibilities. Its fanged maw gnashes and chomps. Within its movements one can make out faint resounding reverberations of possible movements and reactions that did not occur, as if with every step the creature takes, an infinite ghost of possible movements it may have taken glimmer and fade.

These strange arachnid-like creatures seem to weave together partial realities, parallel dimensions, and alternate timelines like a spider spinning its web. They have features that resemble that of a large spider, but their twisted forms, elongated torsos, fanged maws, and spiny hides give them an otherworldly guise that makes them hard to distinguish as anything from this plane of existence.

Those who have faced one have commented on the broken sense of reality that occurs when attempting to attack an Eldritch Crawler. In response Eldritch Crawlers shift realities, and whether the attack hits or misses, a glimpse through time and space shows all possible outcomes of the attack at once. Even when an Eldritch Crawlers is defeated, it's debatable if they are truly dead, or if it was simply observed in a single timeline in which it was killed—the monster may still exist in every other possible reality. This could mean Eldritch Crawlers transcend human concepts of time and space and can't actually be killed, only removed from one instance of time and space amongst an infinite sea of them.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill History|XPHB} or {@skill Nature|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine an Eldritch Crawler, learning the following based on the result.

entries.name: (5+) Uncontainable
entries: You know the creature's {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: (10+) Escape Reality
entries: You are aware of the creature's Void Walker {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: (15+) Dull and Diffident
entries: You recognize the creature's highest and lowest ability scores.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Eldritch Crawlers weave together fractured timelines, and slip in and out of the Space Between Worlds with ease. They create their own Thin Places and travel through them back and forth as needed. When under attack, Eldritch Crawlers bend and alter the realities they exist in to shift to one where they are more likely to survive. They teleport around the battlefield and vanish into the Space Between Worlds as they need to, using Void Walker and their Fractured Reality Reaction, only to reemerge and attack their prey with Contaminated Venom.

name: Eldritch Dreg

entries: The scrawny, twig-thin creature shuffles out of the shadows, seeming unstable on its feet, and disproportionately weighted by its massive, throbbing cranium that pulses with octarine energy. Suddenly, the creature lifts off the ground and a shimmering field surrounds it. Its hollow eyes begin to glow with contaminated energy as it whips its head towards you, a pulsing psychic energy emanating from its gaze.

Eldritch Dregs have a warped and twisted psyche. Contaminated energy collects in their brain, causing it to swell to a massive size while granting the Dreg arcane powers which it can barely comprehend—or control. Through this strange mutation, the Eldritch Dreg has lost most of its muscle tissue. They struggle to hold themselves upright when shuffling on their feet but can Levitate into the air when needed. Spellcasters who succumb to eldritch {@condition contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} are particularly likely to become Eldritch Dregs, especially those who have dabbled with contaminated spells.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Survival|XPHB} or {@skill Nature|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks to {@action Study|XPHB} an Eldritch Dreg, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (5+) Haze Bound
entries: You know this Aberration has {@sense Truesight|XPHB}.

entries.name: (10+) Psychic Powers
entries: You are aware of its Hazewarp Hex {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and Psychic Blast actions.

entries.name: (15+) Cunning Being
entries: You learn the Eldritch Dreg's highest and lowest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: An Eldritch Dreg curses its chosen target with Hazewarp Hex, and then hammers it with its Psychic Blast. It uses {@spell Levitate|XPHB} to keep itself out of melee by hovering above the battlefield and it will unleash its Synaptic Shock if its enemies are close to one another. If brought to less than half its Hit Points, it attempts to flee.
