First she spoke of a power greater than the gods. Then there was this ringing in my ears. I don't remember what happened after that, but the nightmares were terrible.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The touch of an Aether Kindred's dreams can taint objects with an unstable nature, particularly potions. Any potion found on the servants of these beings has a 50 percent chance to be tainted, making the potion's effects unpredictable. Someone inspecting such a potion must succeed on a {@dc 17} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check to identify the instability. Otherwise, the potion appears to be a normal potion of its type.

When an unstable potion is consumed, roll on the Eldritch Effects table to determine the effect of the instability, which is in addition to the potion's normal effects and can last as long as the potion does or 1 minute, whichever is longer. However, a creature can attempt a {@dc 13} Wisdom saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the instability effect on itself on a success.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
items.entry: In the wake of the gods' disappearance, some turned to other ancient entities for power. Those that succeed are known as eldritch priests.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
items.entry: These priests draw their power from maddening entities known as the Aether Kindred, which some arcane scholars point to as the cause of the gods' disappearance. The power granted by such creatures can produce bizarre and unpredictable effects.

items.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
items.entry: Some eldritch priests seek to awaken their new "gods" by spreading the story of the demise of members the Etharis pantheon. As more people tap into the dreams of the slumbering Kindred, the creatures begin to rouse. If they wake, the world is doomed.

rows: The creature takes 4 ({@dice 1d8}) psychic damage at the start of each of its turns.
The creature is disoriented. It falls prone and does so again at the end of each turn it moves 5 feet or more.
The creature is distracted by visions and voices and has disadvantage on attack rolls and Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks.
The creature is unsure of itself. It can move or take an action on its turn, but not both, and it can't use reactions.
The creature is reckless. It has advantage on attack rolls and attack rolls against it have advantage.
The creature is deafened and can't see more than 30 feet away.
The creature is frightened of the source of this effect. If that source can't be sensed, the creature is frightened of one other random creature it can sense.

items.name: Eldritch Trickster

entries: Draped in black robes and carrying an obsidian wand, the Eldritch Trickster has a hood pulled up tight around its head as arcane power focuses into its hand, forming a blade of raw energy.

The Queen's Men have attracted a handful of renegade mages, undiscovered sorcerous talents, and wicked warlocks. Many are malfeasants who used their magic to commit crimes such as robbery, conspiracy, impersonation, or murder. Now seeking to avoid the clutches of the Amethyst Academy and Silver Order alike, these mages offer their magical talents to the Queen of Thieves in exchange for her protection. Ironically, this often sees them using magic for many more misdeeds.

name: Eldritch Troll

entries: The mottled faded purple skin of this massive creature is accented by erupting {@item crystal|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium crystals} along its spine, shoulders, and forearms. Its large, frog-like octarine eyes glare at you. Its skin writhes and crawls as new appendages burst forth from it, in a constant state of mutation.

When a troll's innate ability to regenerate combines with the devastating mutating properties of delerium, it causes an Eldritch Troll to form. These creatures are near impossible to kill, regenerating from almost any attack thrown at them. They also seem to have some control over their mutations, which they can change at any moment to help them hunt their prey. Eldritch Trolls have been known to grow wings and fly, or grow extra arms to attack or to cover their body in crystalized delerium.

Unlike most other trolls, Eldritch Trolls do not travel in packs or form tight-knit family groups. They are corrupted abominations and lose much of their sentience in the process. They are more likely to be encountered alone, wandering the ruins of Drakkenheim, or the corrupted Thin Places of the continent.

Eldritch Trolls tend to wander the areas they became corrupted in, never straying too far away from the delerium that they crave. Their grotesque transformation gives them a hunger for more {@condition contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}, and to contaminate anything else that comes near. When they sense danger, a threat, or even just wandering prey, Eldritch Trolls attack aggressively, and without remorse.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks to {@action study|XPHB} an Eldritch Troll, learning the following information based on the result:

entries.name: (5+) From Harsh Environments
entries: You know the troll's {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: (10+) Hard to Kill
entries: You learn of the troll's Regeneration trait.

entries.name: (15+) Special Weakness
entries: You have insight into the troll's {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB|Vulnerabilities}.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Eldritch Trolls stalk the streets of the Inner City of Drakkenheim attempting to contaminate any creature they come across. They use Corrupting Blast to contaminate their foes, mutating to whatever best suits them in the battle, and then use their Claws and Bite.
If an Eldritch Troll takes Psychic damage, it immediately flees and attempts to find a safe place to recuperate.

Trolls eat a lot of garbage but the ones that get into delerium remind you how stupid they really are.

name: Eleanor Heyling
entries: Eleanor Heyling's love of rare books is readily apparent to anyone who enters her shop and spots her nose-deep in her newest acquisition. She will not sell a book until she's read it. Some claim that she has been cursed by her reading, while others claim she's gained magical powers from the pursuit of rigorous study.

Although she is only in her early 40s, Eleanor has the look of an older woman. A life of little sleep and eye strain has left her far-sighted and sickly. She adopted her younger sister's three children: Margery, Algernon, and Sheridan (Neutral Good, human noncombatant {@creature Commoner|XMM|Commoners}). They go to school on most nights but are otherwise left to their own devices by their eccentric aunt. In fact, they often end up caring for her more than she cares for them.

Although Eleanor has lived in Wickermoor Village all her life, she is staunchly in the camp of the Newcomers. She values all knowledge and the wisdom her collection has imparted upon her, remaining skeptical of the strange rituals and beliefs of the other factions in town.
{@i The ground ripples and tears as rocks fall, jets of flame erupt, and howling winds rage around a rocky creature.}

entries.name: Spirit of the Land
entries: Elemental loci are living spirits inhabiting or embodying tracts of land and geographical features. They are the ultimate personification of nature—the land itself come to life. They vary in size from small hills to entire ridge lines, with no discernible pattern to where they take root.

entries.name: Stubborn Nature
entries: Elemental loci are fiercely protective of their chosen location. They tolerate no interference in the natural order and challenge all who despoil the land, be they mortal, monster, or god.

entries.name: Elemental Loci in Midgard
entries: Among the Tamasheq, the elemental loci are cherished as minor deities, nearly as powerful as the Wind Lords themselves. The sorcerers of Kush have tried to capture and enslave loci for decades; thus far without success, but they grow bolder (and closer to their goal) with each attempt.

name: Elemental Spirit
entries: It's easy to look past these enigmatic spirits, whose elemental nature allows them to blend in with their surroundings, given the right environment. There is a theory among those who study spirits, that claims elemental spirits are likely the first to cross from their realm into the physical. There are probably more of them than we know about, existing as part of and on behalf of nature.
The table below has a list of examples of forms an elemental spirit might take. Feel free to create your own.

She was ancient, tall and gaunt, imperious and fierce. Her skin was translucent and slightly luminous with the crimson fluid beneath lending it a bizarre, vibrating flush. Her anger and sorrow reached from her, sharing the sense of a time before my people cut and burned the forest. I wept.

entries.name: Elf Vampire Customization
entries: As shown in the following stats, young and older elf vampires gain Turn Resistance and immunity to being charmed or rendered unconscious. Although some wood elves are an exception, most elf vampires do not take on animal form and, therefore, lack the Beast Form action. Young and older elf vampires also gain the Fey Majesty action, but until the vampire is ancient, as is the one in the stat block, they can affect only humanoids and beasts with this power.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: An elf vampire's flesh turns to glittering powder when the vampire dies. This powder can still be used to make the ointment rendered vampire flesh can make. However, this dust can also be used as a material component for any enchantment spell or spell that deals necrotic damage. If a spellcaster uses the dust in this way, the spell save DC for the spell increases by 2. If the spell requires an attack roll, the caster scores a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20, and any damage die for necrotic damage that rolls a 1 is treated as a 2. One vampire produces enough dust for two uses, plus one use per age category of the vampire beyond spawn.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
items.entry: Elf vampires don't sleep, so they are aware all the time. And they can't be charmed or knocked unconscious.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
items.entry: Fey ancestry combines with vampirism to render elf vampires resistant to effects that turn undead.

items.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
items.entry: Elf vampires can manipulate the minds of beasts and people. Legend says that ancient elf vampires can sway the minds of other creatures.

name: Elhild
entries: Cultist fanatic

name: Elias Greaves
entries: Elias {@i (eh-LYE-us)} Greaves was a gambler from the world of the living who dreamt of wealth and influence far beyond his station. Seemingly blessed by Lady Luck herself, he won big at every gambling hall he visited, eventually growing bored and craving a new challenge. He found a way to board the {@i Ghostlight Express} and travel to Druskenvald, where he met Phillip and Adela.

Despite his powerful new friends, his luck ran out in the lands of death, and his fortune was quickly spent. Soon, he was stuck playing low stakes games aboard the{@i Laughlin Lullaby}, a riverboat that traveled up and down the Silverbell River in Wickermoor Hollow. In desperation, he made a deal with Mister Crossroads to turn his luck around.

After shaking the croc-folk's hand, his luck instantly turned around, and he even won ownership of the riverboat in a poker bet. He renamed it {@i Dead Man's Hand} in reference to the skeletal left hand of his new patron. The gambler enjoyed years of prosperity, but as always, {@creature The Grinning Sinner|CrookedMoon24} exploited the man's greed and the fine print in the deal, and it all came crashing down.

name: Eliza Pennygleam
entries: Eliza Pennygleam is an eluran, a group of cat-like people from the west. While not native to Humblewood, elurans are commonly seen along the roads as part of merchant caravans, and behind merchant stalls in the capital. Eliza is a savvy merchant, on her way to Alderheart to take over her late sister's shop. She is a natural bargainer, but she is also charitable to those who have faced hardships. Eliza uses the {@creature commoner} stat block. She is neutral good.

Elora Quickwit is a thin, middle-aged kindled corvum and the owner of Moss Hall, Marshview's local inn and tavern. She often overcharges her customers and involves herself in disreputable schemes to turn a profit. Though most of the locals detest her, the perch is too small to boycott her establishment, and she has close ties with Sergeant {@creature Burlywhirl|HumblewoodTales}, the head of the local Perch Guard.

name: Elthia Flathame
entries: Village blacksmith

The elvish veteran archer is a stealthy hunter that quietly slips through the wood, watching for game or intruders. While capable with a sword, the elvish archer's true skill lies with the longbow. When unseen, the archer can launch a volley of arrows at its foes with deadly results.

entries.name: Mimics
entries: Mimica mutafigura are patient predators that use disguise as a means of attracting unwary creatures. A mimic will then adhere themselves to their prey, making up for their slow speed and inability to pursue a quarry.

entries.name: Biomancy
entries: Exposure to high levels of biomantic magic has led to subspecies of mimics, Mimica destorquera, that distort light to unbalance their foes. Their elongated pseudopodia let them strike at a greater range before closing the distance and exogenously digesting prey using their hyper-corrosive stomach acid.

name: Ember Roc
entries: Centuries old, birthed by primordial chaos, and equaling the oldest dragons in size, the ember roc is an engine of ruthless consumption. With wingspans vast enough to blot out the sky and auras bright enough to rival the sun, these fiery birds of prey hunt only the deadliest game.

entries.name: Evolutionary Fire
entries: The Fire Ashari of Pyrah believe that the mythic {@creature roc|MM|rocs} that gave rise to the ember rocs maintain balance in Tal'Dorei. {@creature roc|MM|Rocs} avoid humanoid settlements and hunt the monstrous creatures that would otherwise threaten those settlements. So {@book the Ashari|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|2|The Ashari} lure {@creature roc|MM|rocs} to sites of elemental rifts, enticing them to devour creatures attempting to escape into the Material Plane. After years of feeding on {@creature fire elemental|MM|fire elementals}, {@creature salamander|MM|salamanders}, {@creature fire giant|MM|fire giants}, and more, a {@creature roc} is imbued with primordial power, flames erupting from every feather to transform it into the ember roc.

entries.name: Hopeless Ends
entries: An ember roc patiently observes prey for hours before it strikes, snatching up {@creature elephant|MM|elephants}, {@creature killer whale|MM|whales}, and even young dragons. It unleashes iron talons to {@action grapple} targets, paying no heed to counter-attacks, then soars back to its nest—often inside an active volcano. If prey proves too much trouble while in flight, an ember roc readily drops it from some great height. But those unable to escape slowly roast in the creature's fiery grip.

name: Emberbat
entries: Curious and gentle creatures, these tiny bats have ashen fur and noses which sport a small candle-sized flame.

entries.name: Winged Fire
entries: Emberbats only started appearing in Humblewood after the calamity that befell the Scorched Grove, and scholars nearly all agree that the emergence of the creatures had something to do with the elemental magics present in the Grove. The flames that give the bats their name are lit through an internal combustion process that issues fuel from their nostrils as they exhale. Emberbats appear able to start and stop this process at will. The bats obviously do not need the flames to see, but it is hypothesized that the small candle serves to attract moths or other insects into their waiting mouths, greatly facilitating hunting.

entries.name: Colonies of Combustion
entries: Emberbats are most often seen flying in clouds consisting of many different families acting in unison. The bats perform virtually every task as a cohesive unit, from flying to hunting to nesting. The real threat they pose lies in the remarkable coordination of their colonies.

Alone, an emberbat is no more dangerous than a candle. But together they have the potential to burn like a pit of hot embers, and can easily set dry tinder ablaze. When a colony of emberbats attacks a target, it is usually for defensive purposes. The air temperature within the cloud rises dangerously fast, and it has to potential to cook the victim alive. When encountering a colony in the wild, it is best not to engage them. However, recently colonies of emberbats are acting aggressively towards travelers, harassing any who approach their expanding territories. Some swear they have seen emberbat supercolonies whose heat could be felt from yards away.

entries.name: Fine Familiars
entries: Throughout Humblewood's history, the docile nature of the emberbats have made them ideal familiars or animal companions, especially to masters who journey into dark places.
{@i This floating, green crystal sparkles with an inviting glow above the head of a fallen figure.}

entries.name: Servants of Logic
entries: Arcane scholars often debate logic with specially created speaking crystals that are based on their own minds, allowing them to ponder topics from different angles. Most scholars create the crystals to work through a puzzling topic, then dispel the crystal's magic once the topic has been resolved. Long-lived speaking crystals can develop personalities and sometimes abandon or even kill their creators, desiring more than debate. The magical backlash of breaking away from their creators transforms the crystals into emerald eyes.

entries.name: Trapped Manipulators
entries: Upon transforming, these floating, oval-shaped, pink or purple crystals turn a dark shade of green and gain powers of manipulation. They quickly discover that, though they broke from their creators, they must be bound to a creature to survive.

entries.name: Shifting Goals
entries: Each emerald eye's motivations are different, though all share a desire for knowledge and varied experiences. One may be purposeful, using its power to drive its bound creature toward some specific goal. Another might be cooperative, defending its bound creature in exchange for mobility. Still another might be a manipulator, using and abandoning bound creatures as it hops up a political power chain.

The Emerald Order cult leader has embraced the mysteries of the Emerald Tablet and has bent its worship of Thoth-Hermes to furthering the efforts of the Order. The cult leader seeks to gather arcane and alchemical knowledge wherever it is found by any means necessary. If subtle manipulations fail, the cult leader is not above using lethal methods to ensure the cult's goals are met.
{@i This dark cloth of black and purple, stitched with silver and golden threads, resembles a garment of elvish make. Smoke sometimes billows under the hood.}

entries.name: Silent Motion
entries: A billowing empty cloak glides through the air, either under its own power or on the shoulders of its master. Its movement appears odd somehow, as though it moves slightly out of step with the frame bearing it.

entries.name: Guards
entries: Created by the shadow fey as unobtrusive guardians, empty cloaks are often paired with animated armor or other constructs like monolith footmen, and made to look like a display piece.

entries.name: Shadow Servants
entries: Shadow fey nobles sometimes wear an empty cloak as their own clothing, using it to cover a hasty retreat or to assist in a kidnapping.

The smell of smoke and incense consumed the castle walls, and we heard the furious and gleeful bellows of the most immense bull we'd ever seen. As our battlements burned and crumbled, we knew all was lost.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The exploded metal hide of the Empyrean brazen bull can be harvested to make gleaming and radiant {@item brazen armor|GrimHollowLairsEtharis} (see Appendix A of Lairs of Etharis). A proficient armor smith can make a suit of {@item brazen armor|GrimHollowLairsEtharis} by succeeding on a {@dc 20} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check and using 2500 gp of components. This process takes 20 days to complete.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
items.entry: Wildfires that seem to begin with hoofprints are sometimes found during the dry season in farmland, and bright spots on the horizon that look like a massive cow are often reported at the same time.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
items.entry: The Empyrean brazen bull is a beast of burden for angels, used for besieging enemies.

items.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
items.entry: The Empyrean brazen bull explodes when it dies, and luck be with all in the wake of the blast.

entries: Contaminated Elementals can be found all over Drakkenheim, often in areas where the eldritch magics are especially concentrated. Many who have encountered these elementals have spoken of the city itself coming to life to attack them. Reports of ruins reaching out and crushing adventurers, burning flames moving and hunting with minds of their own, or contaminated pools lurching to engulf passersby have been heard. Even the blowing air itself has mustered parts of the Haze into shifting clouds that stalk adventurers through the streets. These magical creatures are a constant reminder that nothing in the city can be trusted, and that nowhere is truly safe.

name: Entropic Flame

entries: An elemental alight with purple-green flames illuminates the desolate streets ahead. Composed of cascading octarine fire, the elemental moves like wildfire spreading uncontrollably. Within the dancing flames is a scornful expression of rage. It crackles and blazes, the heat from its body distorting the air around it. The pungent smell of burning ozone and sulfur saturates the area, and flecks of cinder and ash whirl about, shedding from the creature as it glides menacingly toward you.

The fires from the day Drakkenheim was destroyed never truly died. Many became Entropic Flames—Contaminated Fire Elementals that travel the ruins like living embers. Countless can be found wandering the areas around the Crater and southern Drakkenheim. The Followers of the Falling Fire view Entropic Flames almost like fallen angels, symbols of the vortex itself.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they {@action Study|XPHB} an Entropic Flame, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (10+) Supernaturally Resilient
entries: You are aware of the creature's {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: (15+) Inextinguishable Fires
entries: You learn of the elemental's Dancing Flame action and Flickerjump {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, as well as its Enduring Flame trait.

entries.name: (20+) Swift and Senseless
entries: You know the creature's strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: An Entropic Flame is a haughty combatant driven by a burning desire to set the world on fire. It teleports from place to place using its Flickerjump, setting alight creatures and objects using its Dancing Flames. If possible, it tries to remain close to {@condition Burning|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} targets to keep them on fire within its Enduring Flame aura.

Within the smoking ruins of Drakkenheim, Entropic Flames love to set buildings, furniture, and other objects on fire. They quickly turn the battlefield into a roiling inferno, one which cannot be extinguished easily thanks to their presence.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Elemental.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Contaminated Ichor.

entries.name: Dust:
entries: Elemental Dust.

name: Entropic Watcher

entries: This floating mass of wet flabby flesh drifts through the air, its many long spindly tendrils dangling down like an incomprehensible jellyfish. Appearing in strange hues of pale pinks, purples, and whites, its large single eye in the middle of its fleshy mass glows with octarine hues, weakening body and mind. The soft sound of thrumming and suckling follows it as it assaults minds with insane chattering in unknown languages.

Many of the creatures inhabiting the Space Between Worlds are aberrant and primordial in nature. The Entropic Watcher is one such incomprehensible creature. To look upon it is like looking at an abstract painting, the forms and shapes of it body painful to observe by the mortal mind. It silently drifts through the Space Between Worlds, drawn to Thin Places where it observes the places beyond, as if analyzing or calculating some unknown concepts as it stares through like a cat at a window. For this reason, Entropic Watchers are one of the more common occurrences in the Mortal World, as they tend to congregate around Thin Places, and often slip through.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill History|XPHB} or {@skill Nature|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine an Entropic Watcher, learning the following based on the result.

entries.name: (10+) Guarded Existence
entries: You learn the creature's {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: (15+) Imperiling Stare
entries: You recognize the creature's Withering Gaze feature.

entries.name: (20+) Physically Resilient
entries: You know the creature's highest and lowest ability scores.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Entropic Watcher is a keen hunter who, by its very gaze, can cause a creature to grow weak and leave it open for annihilation. The Entropic Watcher focuses its gaze upon its prey and unleashes its eye beams towards it, knowing that if it can hold its gaze, the creature will succumb to the watcher's blasts much easier. It will use its Force Barrier and Shadow Crash to force its victims into an optimal position for it to strike, and grab them with its tendrils, holding them readily in its Withering Gaze.
If the Entropic Watcher is reduced to less than 50 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it attempts to flee.

entries: Aberration.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Contaminated Ichor, Goopy Ooze, Mucus.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Eyes, Guts, Glands, Flesh.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Tentacles.

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Skin.

entries.name: Dust:
entries: Aberrant Dust.

This ancient elvish hermit tends the shrine. Eoghan Ghostweaver is a priest of Morrigan, and keeps the old faith of his goddess. He has a sallow face with skin stretched thin over his cheekbones, is garbed in black feathered robes, and wields a staff of the woodlands.

{@i The air crackles and lights flicker in the ruins. In a whirl of colorful robes, a gaunt human materializes from the maelstroms of time. His eyes scan the hall in panic, witnessing an event only he can see}.

entries.name: Adrift in Time
entries: Not much is known about the time-traveling eonic drifters other than that they were humans who left a dying civilization to look for help not available in their own age. To their misfortune, returning to their own time proved much more difficult than leaving it, and the eonic drifters found themselves adrift in the river of time. As the decades passed, their chance of returning home withered, along with much of their vitality. They have become gaunt and semi-mummified by the passing of ages.

entries.name: Crystal Belts
entries: A drifter carries an odd assembly of gear gathered in countless centuries. It barters with these goods when necessary. The more eclectic the collection, the more jumps it has performed on its odyssey. Belts of crystals around its body store the energy that fuels a drifter's travels. After each large jump through time, the reservoirs are exhausted for awhile, allowing only short jumps.

entries.name: Jittery and Paranoid
entries: Visiting countless eras in which mankind has all but forgotten their once-great civilization has robbed most eonic drifters of their hope. Their greatest fear is being robbed of their crystal belts, which are their only remaining links to the people they once were. They plead or fight to the death for the belts.

entries.name: Ruins Dwellers
entries: Drifters can appear at any time or place, but they often frequent the sites of their people's past (or future) cities. There they are comforted by knowing that they're at least in the right place, if not the right time.

{@i This small humanoid has a slightly pointed face with bright, brown eyes and a black, snout-like nose. Its skin is covered in short, tan fur, and its head, shoulders, and back have smoothed-down quills.}
Erinas, or hedgehog folk, are a small, communal people.

entries.name: Burrowed Villages
entries: Natural diggers at heart, erinas live in shallow networks of tunnels and chambers they excavate themselves. Enemies who attack the peaceful erinas become confused and lost in the mazelike tunnels. On their own ground, the erinas can easily evade, outmaneuver, or surround invaders. They lure intruders into choke points where the enemy can be delayed while noncombatants and valuables are hustled to safety through other tunnels. Such choke points are often protected or held by erina defenders, the largest and hardiest of their kind.

entries.name: Scroungers and Gatherers
entries: Erinas are naturally curious. They tend to explore an area by tunneling beneath it and popping up at interesting points. They dislike farming and live mainly on the bounty of the land surrounding their homes. In cities, they subsist on what they can find, and they have a knack for finding whatever they need.

{@i This small humanoid has a slightly pointed face with bright, brown eyes and a black, snout-like nose. Its skin is covered in short, tan fur, and its head, shoulders, and back have smoothed-down quills.}
Erinas, or hedgehog folk, are a small, communal people.

Such choke points are often protected or held by erina defenders, the largest and hardiest of their kind.

entries: Erinas are naturally curious. They tend to explore an area by tunneling beneath it and popping up at interesting points. They dislike farming and live mainly on the bounty of the land surrounding their homes. In cities, they subsist on what they can find, and they have a knack for finding whatever they need.

name: Ether Fish
entries: These small, silvery fish have developed the ability to shift between the Ethereal and Material Planes as a potent defense against their numerous predators. Ether fish can be found most reliably near bodies of fresh water, although their ability to fly notably adds clouds to the list of possibilities. Students of the Ethereal Plane speculate that the creatures—which have never been observed eating insects, algae, or similar visible food sources—might derive nutrients through environmental absorption.

name: Etherean Trickster
entries: Lawbreakers are uncommon in etherean society, but their stringent laws place very little importance on the possessions of the denizens of other planes. Some ethereans make their living by 'liberating' valuable resources from their neighbors on the Material Plane, usually focusing on commodities not found on the Ethereal. For some, this means retrieving basic food, or raw materials for crafting; for others, it means fine jewelry or exquisite art.

These two-foot-long beetles have shells in a range of reds, yellows, and oranges, with anywhere from eight to twelve black spots on their back. They are often kept as pets and seen as signs of good luck, as they feast on many common garden pests, including the dreaded gimlet. When threatened, they can ooze a noxious-smelling liquid from their carapace to ward off predators.

entries.name: Fine Familiars
entries: You can summon an everbug as your familiar.
...and that's why we don't go to Slaughterstone Square.

name: Executioner

entries: The massive construct looms menacingly within the center of Slaughterstone Square. Pacing back and forth, it drags its guillotine blade behind it, with the grinding of steel on stone echoing off the old buildings. Its form is a mass of steel plates and gears resembling a huge suit of armor. From within its frame, the glow of octarine light illuminates it with an eerie glow of corruption. The poor souls of its victims cling to it, reaching out in terror as if clawing to escape their last moments when the Executioner took their heads.

The Executioner is a hulking clockwork knight that originally carried out public death sentences in the Slaughterstone Square of Drakkenheim. This ancient machine was engineered by the dwarves of Glitter Peak during the height of their brilliance in distant antiquity. It was left buried deep beneath the avalanches which destroyed the magnificent dwarven capital, and subsequently unearthed by an expeditionary team several decades ago. The king commissioned the Amethyst Academy to bring the construct back into good repair; they altered its arcane programming to obey the commands of the monarch of Westemär.

Laws and customs surrounding capital punishment in Drakkenheim have been a controversial matter ever since the tyrannical reign of Albrecht von Drakken, who issued a draconian decree that demanded family members of the convicted be the ones to carry out their execution sentence. After his reign ended, few were ever willing to serve the role of royal headsman, viewing the act of carrying out the killing as yet another act of murder. Although various devices and contraptions were used to create distance between the death and the administer of the punishment, these hesitations and public resistance to capital punishment remained. In the Executioner, the monarchy had the perfect solution to its judicial problem: the impartial construct is no mortal, and therefore none are culpable for carrying out the death sentence. That the machine makes an impressively terrifying show of the deed was certainly not an insignificant factor either.

Unfortunately, the erratic magic of delerium has scrambled the machine's control protocols. Now contaminated by the Haze, the construct is an engine of destruction and terror which can call upon spectral chains and the spirits of its victims to aid its duty. It attacks anyone who enters the square. However, it never wanders outside the bounds of Slaughterstone Square. The large octagonal plaza features the Executioner's platform, and the surrounding buildings have narrow balconies and tall, dour-looking windows overlooking the square. Mountains of corpses are piled in the square—the grim toll of the Executioner's vocation. Nevertheless, scavengers and adventurers still occasionally risk trying to slip past the Executioner to loot the corpses for valuable equipment and magic items. For many, this mistake is their last, and rather than escape with new treasures, they join the pile of the Executioner's trove.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill History|XPHB} or {@item artisan's tools|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine the Executioner, learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (5+) Unstoppable Machine
entries: You know of the Executioner's

entries.name: Immutable Form, Dimensional Anchor, and Rejuvenation
entries: traits, as well as its damage {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: (10+) Strange Abilities
entries: You recognize its Destroyer, Summon Grasping Shadow, and Guillotine Blade actions.

entries.name: (15+) Powerfully Tough
entries: You are aware of the Executioner's strongest and weakest saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Executioner is not a foe to be defeated, but rather an obstacle to be avoided or a danger to escape. It is a reminder of the callous and uncontrollable dangers present in Drakkenheim. The Executioner's combat tactics vary based on whether it detects low-level characters trespassing in Slaughterstone Square or high-level characters trying to defeat the machine itself. The Executioner pursues its targets within Slaughterstone Square, but never leaves the plaza.

When the Executioner detects creatures trespassing on Slaughterstone Square, it responds first by using Summon Grasping Shadows, followed up by Death Grip to try to prevent their escape. Meanwhile, it uses Lumber Forward to gain ground. You should embrace clever solutions that characters invent to escape or bypass the Executioner. As long as your players aren't trying to destroy it, the Executioner will only use Guillotine Blade against a {@condition Restrained|XPHB} target within its melee range, and does not make ranged attacks nor activate its Necrotic Vents aura.

However, should your players engage the Executioner directly in combat, do not pull any punches. They have made an incredibly foolish mistake by confronting a well-telegraphed deathtrap and should be served their just desserts. It activates its Necrotic Vents, and then relentlessly attacks with its Guillotine Blade. The Executioner throws the massive weapon to hit targets trying to avoid it in melee, or those that try to harm it with ranged weapons or spells. If it encounters any impediment in its way (such as a {@spell Wall of Force|XPHB}), it crushes it with Destroyer.

How do you dead what is dead? I see no end to this riddle.
Listen, I don't care if you call yourself a scientist or a doctor, if you put a demon in you, I'm going to kill you.

The figure wears a wide-brim hat that casts shadows on their face. A long, black trench coat covers their form. The dour figure carries a simple doctor's bag in one hand and a holy symbol of the Sacred Flame in the other. Ethereal energies flit and flick around the doctor as they mumble incoherent ancient words, summoning spirits, or perhaps something worse.

An Exorcist comes prepared to deal with evil entities, sinister spirits, and fearsome fiends. Equipped with their holy symbol, a book of prayers, and a bag of ritualistic baubles, Exorcists stand ready to face the most unnatural and otherworldly entities of the realms. Some Exorcists, however, are so familiar with the ways of the undead, they can summon spirits into hosts. In some rare cases, Exorcists allow demons to inhabit the living.

entries.name: Exorcists Minions
entries: Exorcists deal with all manner of entities. They can call forth Specters, Ghosts, Demons, Wraiths, and other extraplanar entities. The most horrifying creation of the Exorcist is the Soulbound Host, which occurs when an Exorcist allows themself to be a vessel for demonic, extraplanar, or fairy entities, attempting to harness the power of such beings. Most are driven mad during the process.

items: {@b Personality Trait:} I speak to the dead often, sometimes when I am not even sure if they are there..
{@b Bond:} The understanding of life and death grants us power over the planes that few have dared to grasp.
{@b Ideal:} It is in control of demons and ghosts that we will transcend to our true potential.
{@b Flaw:} I am sure I have the strength within me to host a demon or spirit without succumbing to its will.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Medicine|XPHB} or {@skill Religion|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks to {@action study|XPHB} an Exorcist, learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (5+) Demons and Undead
entries: You recognize the Exorcist's {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities} as well as their Expel Evil action.

entries.name: (10+) Master of Possession
entries: You are aware of the Exorcist's Grasping Ghost action.

entries.name: (15+) Weak of Character and Body
entries: You learn the Exorcist's Strength and Charisma ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Exorcist relies on its divine weapons and direct combat skills. They often reside in locations that have natural hazards where they can use their Grasping Ghosts to force enemies into danger. Hazards could include {@condition burning|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} braziers, spiked pits, or a pool of blessed acid. If any foe has a summoned creature, the Exorcist dispatches it using Expel Evil, and destroy any undead foes with Last Rites.
If the Exorcist is in a losing situation, they attempt to use Spiritual Healing on themself before fleeing.
I admire their divine focus but it's the controlling you with ghosts thing where they lose me.

An eye crawler is an ambulatory eye that observes everything. It might be spying for something else. An eye crawler has no effective attacks. Mages theorize eye crawlers derive sustenance from light or ambient magical energy.

Eye crows are big corvids plentiful throughout Etharis. They mimic sounds and voices, and they're extremely clever, remembering faces, locations, and how other creatures treat them. People keep eye crows as pets and often use their iridescent black feathers, which have a deep-green sheen, to decorate.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The nest of an eye crow contains glittering baubles, coins, gems, or jewelry worth at least 5 gp. Feathers of one eye crow can fetch a similar amount of money.

items.name: {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Nature}):
items.entry: Eye crows can be tamed and trained for simple tasks. Unscrupulous trainers teach the crow to attack others, going for the eyes.

entries: {@i Eye-like sigils dot the smooth, marble skin of this statue. One of the eye sigils opens, and a beam of brilliant light shines out.}

entries.name: Covered in Arcana
entries: Eye golems stand at least ten feet tall, and their magically durable hide is covered with real eyes as well as arcane sigils that resemble eyes.

entries.name: Blinds Victims
entries: An eye golem rarely kills its victims, choosing to steal its victims' eyes instead. The victims are left blinded, wandering, and tormented, seeing only visions of the eye golem flashing through their memories. This drives some mad, while others instead choose to serve the golem, becoming devoted to the one who still holds sight.

entries.name: All Eyes Open
entries: When killed, an eye golem does not simply fall down dead. All of its eyes open at once, and a blinding burst of light shines from the body. When the light stops, hundreds of perfectly preserved eyeballs remain where its body fell, still warm, fresh, and without scars or damage. Detectable only by those trained in the arcane arts, each eye emits a barely perceptible beam of light, connecting it to its owner. The creature that holds the golem's central eye after it is slain can use the eye to restore stolen eyes to their victims.

name: Eyvora Fiddercall
entries: Sleek feathers. Large amber eyes. Thick protective goggles.
{@b Background:} Her family has served the cloud giants for generations, and she is the latest in a long line of royal messengers.
{@b Personality Traits:} Chatty and curious, birdlike mannerisms.
{@b Bonds:} Loves her "flock" of eagles.
{@b Flaws:} She is a trifle flighty. Doesn't pay much heed to future problems.
{@b Wants:} To do a good job for her queen.
{@b Talking to Eyvora:} The ravenfolk messenger freely relates her background (above) plus the following:

items: Sunreach is a palace of wonders. It stays at a comfortable temperature no matter the altitude, kept afloat by magic (which Eyvora doesn't really understand).
Though strong-willed and serious the queen always has been kind to Evyora and her family. (She can chat endlessly about the wonders of Bjarmia and the beneficence of the queen.)

entries: The grim-faced doctor's jaw tightens as they lower their browand sigh. Suddenly, their face contorts into a wicked, impossiblegrimace, a smile stretched too wide for the muscles on their face.Fiendish light glimmers in their eyes as hornlike bulges rip throughthe flesh of their forehead. Profane runes suddenly blaze upontheir flesh, releasing the smell of burning meat and sulfur. Thebody rises into the air, the muscle spasms barely containing the evilspirit bound within this mortal host. A spiral of flame encircles theapothecary's body as they unleash a horrific scream, speaking in avoice which is not their own. "Now, you will die, mortal."

A Soulbound Host is the physical body of an apothecary who has willingly allowed an extraplanar creature to possess them, trapping the powerful outsider in a mortal form. Powerful yet vulnerable, Soulbound Hosts loathe their creators. They wander the world for the means to reverse the curse of mortality placed upon them and return to their otherworldly domains.

Exorcist and Alienist apothecaries do not primarily study the body, and rarely practice the type of magic and science which leads to mutant horrors and flesh-stitched abominations. They are instead concerned with the supernatural forces of the mind and soul. Many research and contact powerful extraplanar entities, eager to possess mortals as a means of entering the material world. These apothecaries learn how to create Soulbound Hosts as a powerful means to contain and fight back against these dangerous otherworldly foes.

entries.name: Desperate Gambit
entries: A Soulbound Host is usually created under truly desperate circumstances, such as when a heroic apothecary faces a dangerous otherworldly being such as a demon, fey, spirit, or inscrutable entity from the Space Between Worlds. Not only are these planar invaders pernicious foes, many are effectively immortal—often these creatures simply reform when killed outside their native planes. Thus, an apothecary who lacks the ability to defeat the demon on their own, or who wishes to defeat a powerful outsider in a more permanent fashion, may instead decide upon a heroic act of self-sacrifice by turning themselves into a Soulbound Host.

entries.name: Preparing the Trap
entries: Using an array of implanted metals, ingested tinctures, mental preparations, and occult incantations, a skilled apothecary may willingly prepare their body for possession. During the process, the apothecary can weave a unique spiritual trap. It then falls to the apothecary to convince the otherworldly creature to possess them, an act that many outsiders are eager to do. Thus, the canny apothecary preys on the ego of the monster itself.

entries.name: Mortal Curse
entries: When the outsider inhabits the body, the apothecary's soul departs, leaving the extraplanar creature to take their place spiritually. If this mortal form is killed or destroyed, the bound creature does not simply return to their plane of origin. Instead, the spirit departs to the afterworlds like any other mortal soul, losing their accumulated otherworldly power forever. Thus, the Soulbound Host becomes both a prison and a death sentence for the other wielding being tricked into the apothecary's body.

entries.name: Rogue Hosts
entries: Unfortunately, this act of self-sacrifice is not without its imperfections. The apothecary's body is filled with otherworldly essence, and while the creature's power is greatly diminished, they often remain extremely dangerous—allies of the departed apothecary may still find it challenging to slay the Soulbound Host. Many escape, wandering the world with stolen lives and even assuming the identity of their host while they search for the means to escape their now mortal form. All bound outsiders are painfully aware of their new mortality, frustrated that returning to their planes of origin is not a simple matter of destroying their flesh-cage or switching their essence into a different host, one which lacks the binding wards placed by the apothecary.

entries.name: Price of Freedom
entries: Trapped outsiders can win their freedom by calling back the soul of the apothecary who trapped them, and resurrecting them into their body. This is a thing many outsiders are loathe to do out of fiendish ego, since it puts the original soul in a bargaining position. In this way, the apothecary can force the spirit to accept a bargain which requires them to remain in their own worlds for at least the duration of the apothecary's lifetime.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Religion|XPHB}, {@skill Medicine|XPHB}, or {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks to Study a Soulbound Host, learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (10+) Possessed Body
entries: You know the Soulbound Host's type and damage {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}.

entries.name: (15+) Extraplanar Magic
entries: Depending on the type of spirit, you learn either the Hellfire Chain, Illusory Assault, or Psychic Barrage actions, as well as the Spellcasting trait of the host.

entries.name: (20+) Cursed Fate
entries: You recognize its desperation caused by its spirit-bound mortality and its Reactions.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: A Soulbound Host is a careful combatant. Though powerful, the last thing they want is to be killed in their mortal form. If they are seriously injured, they often attempt to bargain, offering power and knowledge to assailants who spare them.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Fiend, Fey, or Aberrant.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Monster Blood.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Eyes, Heart, Brain, Guts.

entries.name: Bones:
entries: Skull, Spine.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Claws.

entries.name: Hair:
entries: Hair.

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Skin.

entries.name: Dust:
entries: Fiendish, Fey, or Aberrant Dust.

When a will-o'-wisp basks in the eternal sunset of the Plane of Fey, a change overcomes the malevolent spirit that lies at its heart. In place of a wisps' despair, a faerie develops a guileful and mischievous cunning.

These faeries often pair themselves with more powerful creatures, such as a fey queen with a penchant for collecting waifs and strays, or a territorial suneater owlbear. They act as a lure for such a creatures, coaxing unwary wanderers to follow their cheerful nimbus. If all goes according to the faerie's plan, both faerie and host will gain a meal from this symbiotic mutualism.

entries.name: Etymology
entries: What came first, faerie fire or the faerie-o'-fire? Though the great and prolific wizard Plagiaritrix claimed to have invented the faerie fire spell, this origin story is now shrouded in doubt. The faerie-o'-fire's solar flare attack was discovered to have surprisingly similar characteristics to the spell, leading scholars to believe that Plagiaritrix might simply have 'borrowed' it while on one of their many trips to the Plane of Fey.
Never make a deal with the fey. Never make a deal with a goblin. And if you ever meet a faevlin, you'll know why.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Faevlins love to collect objects that increase their personal prestige and power. Every faevlin is likely to have a few personal trinkets like this, along with the occasional item of real worth.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
items.entry: A faevlin can teleport away from attackers but does so in a manner even the faevlin can't predict.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
items.entry: Faevlins are goblins cursed by powerful fey magic

items.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
items.entry: A faevlin can't be charmed by non-fey, but they have been known to pretend to be charmed to trick the enchanter.

name: Fafnir
entries: Dragon guarding Loki's Hall

name: Fafnir
entries: {@i Dwarf Cursed into Dragon Form}

{@color This bat-winged monster has a sinuous body covered in scales the color of weathered iron. Its limbs are powerful, but warped, bending in impossible ways. The monster's head is like that of a dragon, but it has too many eyes, and whiplike tentacles circle its skull like a crest. Its maw is lined with rows of long fangs, and its underside is speckled with golden coins, jewelry, and gemstones embedded between its scales.|006abe}

Fafnir was once a dwarf, one of the four sons of the famed smith Hreidmarr. When their brother was mistakenly slain by Loki, the clever god gave their father a magical ring as wergild. This item, called Andvaranaut, was supposed to bring untold wealth, but the ring bore a horrible curse. Inflamed by greed, Fafnir killed his father to possess the ring and drove his brothers into exile. The curse and his own avarice warped and changed the dwarf until Fafnir transformed into a serpentine dragon with gold coins and gems embedded in his belly. It also destroyed Andvaranaut.

Fafnir makes his lairs in isolated caves often carved into the base of a hills or into the side of high cliffs. He changes lairs frequently, paranoid that his hoard will be stolen from him. The area within 1 mile of Fafnir's current lair is warped, causing creatures to become greedy and possessive of their belongings.
{@i This small man wears hunting leathers and a cowl decorated with antlers, and he holds a glaive made of antlers.}

These shy fairies dress as small fey herdsmen wearing hide armor, hide boots, cloaks, and cowls, all trimmed in fox fur and with a red sash or tunic. They often ride woodland creatures, such as elk, giant weasels, or snowy giant owls.

entries.name: Hunters and Herders
entries: The far darrig were the hunters, herders, and equerry of the elven nobility. Some still serve in this capacity in planes where the elves rule. Far darrig carry glaives made from fey antlers; each remains enchanted only as long as a far darrig holds it. Their leaders ride on fey elk the color of foxes, with gleaming green eyes. When these elk shed their antlers, the far darrigs' smiths craft the antlers into the glaives wielded by their people.

entries.name: Hate Arcanists
entries: While not inherently evil, far darrig are hostile to most humanoids and often attack humanoid spellcasters on sight. If they can be persuaded of a spellcaster's or humanoid's good intentions, they make good guides, scouts, and hunters in dangerous forests.

entries.name: Serve Hags and Worse
entries: They are sometimes found as thralls or scouts serving hags or other evil fey, but they rarely do so willingly.

entries.name: Far Darrig in Midgard
entries: The far darrig thrive in forests such as the Arbonesse and Margreve, and they are close allies to the druids in those woodlands. Some believe they also serve in a hidden fey court, somewhere in or near the Green Duchy of Verrayne.

entries.name: Far Dweller

entries: This tall, gangly creature hovers ominously, levitating inches above the ground. Its arms hang loosely at its sides and thin legs dangle below its body. Shifting motes of otherworldly energy dance between its long, gnarled fingers. Its purple-gray skin stretches tightly over its emaciated frame. Instead of a head, a mass of thick, writhing tentacles sprouts from its neck, reaching out into the air. The atmosphere around it vibrates with chittering whispers, slurping and the hoarse mumbles of maddening truths and incomprehensible realities.

Known as Far Dwellers, these enigmatic beings are among the most persistent and terrifying entities encountered in the Space Between Worlds. They traverse dimensions and Thin Places, abducting victims to perform alien experiments on them. However, their motives and purposes remain utterly obscure, and their objectives beyond human understanding. Nevertheless, Far Dwellers demonstrate uncanny understanding of the psychic forces and wild magic of the Space Between Worlds, and perhaps have an interest in spreading the influence and {@condition contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} of that dimension. None possess greater mastery over delerium and contaminated magic than these creatures. They weave their spells to create eldritch machines with unknown purposes, dominate their victims, evade harm, and complete their esoteric research.

It is evident from the limited interactions Far Dwellers have had with mortals that they pose a grave threat and harbor malicious intentions towards humanoids. Far Dwellers perceive humanoids much as a person might view an insect or perhaps a stray animal—sometimes with indifferent disregard, other times with evident disgust or disdain. They rarely communicate with mortals and seem unwilling or disinterested in explaining themselves or their goals. Far Dwellers show scant concern for their captives' desperate pleas for help or cries for mercy as they secure them to stone slabs and invade their minds with countless probing tendrils.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill History|XPHB} or {@skill Nature|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine a Far Dweller, learning the following based on the result.

entries.name: (10+) Psychic Fortress
entries: You learn the creature's {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: (15+) Mental Control
entries: You are aware of the creature's Pluck the Puppet Strings {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: (20+) Otherworldly Intellect
entries: They learn the creature's highest and lowest ability scores.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: A Far Dweller often disregards creatures it deems lesser than itself until it is outwardly threatened, often outright ignoring nearby mortals like one might ignore a passing insect or rodent. However, when provoked they are intelligent, efficient, and ruthless. Thanks to its great intellect, a Far Dweller rapidly assesses the capabilities of its attackers and responds to methodically dismantle them accordingly.

Far Dwellers begin combat by casting {@spell Maze}, {@spell Hypnotic Pattern}, or {@spell Slow} to incapacitate as many foes as possible. On subsequent turns, it uses Contaminate and Mind Scramble to launch a contaminated psychic assault, preferring to target spellcasters and physically weak targets, while choosing physically strong but easily manipulated targets for Pluck the Puppet Strings.

When attacked, a Far Dweller disappears temporarily using Vanish to the Space Between Worlds. Note that this ability functions normally on the Space Between Worlds itself, as the Far Dweller momentarily travels to a different spatial dimension on that plane.

A Far Dweller is always willing to abandon a fight and its projects if it is sufficiently threatened, and will flee to the Space Between Worlds using {@spell Plane Shift} if it is {@status Bloodied|XPHB}.

entries.name: Contaminated Spell List
entries: For those that own Sebastian Crowe's Guide to Drakkenheim, here is an alternative spell list for the Far Dweller and Far Dweller Mastermind:

entries: {@spell Comet Shards|GuideDrakkenheim} (replaces {@spell Magic Missile})

entries: {@spell Banish to the Space Between Worlds|GuideDrakkenheim} (replaces {@spell Maze}), {@spell Weave the Elder Sign|GuideDrakkenheim} (replaces {@spell Hypnotic Pattern}), {@spell Siphon Time|GuideDrakkenheim} (replaces {@spell Slow})

name: Far Dweller Abductor

entries: The being appears humanoid in shape, but much taller and more slender than would seem natural, with long spindly arms and elongated fingers. Their heads are large for their lank bodies, coming to a point where their chin would be, and round and bulbous at the top. They have no features upon their face but as their head tilts and shutters, there is a seemingly vast perception. The creature moves without making a sound and seems engulfed in blinding light from an unknown source.

Some folk have told tales of wandering travelers alone at night who saw strange lights in the sky, or through the trees of thick woods, or incomprehensible beings that wandered into their camps through rifts between worlds. The most horrifying are those who speak of the creatures effortlessly entering their homes and taking them somewhere else, only to awake with a hazy memory and no signs that anyone was ever there.

Their motives are completely unknown, but they arrive from the Space Between Worlds to observe, and experiment upon mortals. When one encounters a Far Dweller Abductor, they are left with no memory of ever having experienced the creature in the first place. The abducted are left with strange and bizarre dreams, confused visions, and blurred concepts of what may have occurred. This has led to doubt and discourse over the very existence of these creatures. For those who share stories are often met with disbelief, as witnesses and victim share conflicting tales of their experience.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill History|XPHB} or {@skill Nature|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine a Far Dweller Abductor, learning the following based on the result.

entries.name: (10+) Psychic Fortress
entries: You learn the creature's {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: (15+) Confounding Existence
entries: You are aware of the creature's Unfathomable Presence trait.

entries.name: (20+) Malign Brilliance
entries: They learn the creature's highest and lowest ability scores.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Far Dweller Abductors are not fighters, and simply wish to gather specimens and study them. When Abductors appear, they usually do so when a creature is resting or asleep. They rely on their Unfathomable Presence to confuse and dismantle their target. They use use Mind Warp or Devour Thoughts to weaken the mind of their target before attempting to Abduct them.

The Far Dweller Abductors do not wish to be observed or remembered, and do not want even their dead left behind to be discovered and known to the creatures they are researching. A Far Dweller Abductor will teleport away and use {@spell Plane Shift} if it has lost the upper hand, is outnumbered, or feels in any way threatened. If a Far Dweller Abductor dies, any Far Dwellers still engaged in battle attempt to take their bodies and vanish as quickly as possible, attempting to leave no trace of their presence.
