items.name: Far Dweller Mastermind

entries: Draped in ancient robes and carrying a {@item staff|XPHB} made of otherworldly material, the creature observes you with cold disregard. It holds out a hand, bending the very fabric of time and space around it. It hovers above the ground, its head a mass of writhing tentacles, and its gangly pale body pulsing with octarine energy.
Especially ancient and terrible, these powerful Far Dwellers have wandered existence for untold eons.
Sometimes you have to improvise. for example, when a sword doesn't work, try throwing a javelin. if that doesnt work I am out of ideas.
{@i Violet radiance surrounds this large pale centipede. Its flesh is translucent, and its jaws are crystalline.}

entries.name: Destiny Destroyers
entries: Fate eaters infest remote areas of the planes, where they consume the threads of Fate itself. The beings in charge of Fate view them as vermin. Sometimes those beings engage particularly canny planar travelers either to hunt fate eaters or to help repair the damage they've done. This can be a deadly job, as the fate eaters consider the destiny of a mortal to be the tastiest of delicacies, rich in savory possibilities.

entries.name: Planar Gossips
entries: Fate eaters can and do trade information about various dooms, fates, and outcomes, but one must have something rich in destiny to trade—or at least, juicy gossip about gods and demons.

entries.name: Visionary Flesh
entries: Eating the properly prepared flesh of a fate eater grants the eater insight into the fate of another being.
{@i This well-dressed figure appears elven, save for its featureless face and taloned hands.}

Known as a fiarsídhe among themselves, fear smiths are servants of shadow fey courts and other, similar dark fey courts. While its mouth is closed, a fear smith's face is featureless save for rows of deep wrinkles. Opening the large mouth in the center of its face reveals long needlelike teeth surrounding a single, massive eye.

entries.name: Icy-Cold Eyes
entries: Fear smiths often serve as torturers or are dispatched to demoralize the court's enemies. Their stare stops enemies cold, making it easy for heavily-armed warriors to trap and finish a foe.

entries.name: Devour Fear
entries: Fear smiths feed off strong emotions, and their favorite meal is terror. The fey prefer prolonging the death of victims, and, when free to indulge, a fear smith stalks its victim for days before attacking, hinting at its presence to build dread.

entries.name: Hoods and Masks
entries: Fear smiths favor fine clothing and high fashion, donning hooded cloaks or masks when discretion is required. Eerily well-mannered and respectful, fear smiths enjoy feigning civility and playing the part of nobility, speaking genteelly but with a thick, unidentifiable accent.

Fell wraiths appear as crooked wanderers, roaming among ancient ruins, wrapped in cloaks hiding their spectral features. Their flesh is almost transparent, and their eyes seem to glow like embers. If encountered in the hours of twilight, they may pass as Men, as they can speak, even if with an unusual hissing voice and strange accents. Fell Wraiths carry old weapons, relics from an age of strife that they employ to deadly effectiveness.

entries.name: Wraiths
entries: It is said that many who fought in the wars against Angmar fell victim to the Black Shadow, a terrible illness spread by the Nazgûl. Many did not perish, and were slowly consumed by it instead.

Wraiths are creatures that once were living beings but whose lives were consumed by sorcery or by another evil power. They are now undead, and live in both the living world and the wraith-world. Wraiths maintain a physical shape, albeit partially faded and thus resistant to harm.{@i "Begone, if you be not deathless! For living or dark undead, I will smite you, if you touch him."}

entries.name: Undead
entries: Many horrors haunt the lonely lands of old Arnor, in the shadow of the darker woods and under the still waters of rotting marshes. Some say those shades are what remains of the ill-will of Evil Men and proud Elves, others that they are spirits out of Angmar, sent to infest barren hills and lonely barrows; others more blame dark sorcery and evil curses.
{@i A darkly foreboding intelligence glows behind this automaton's eyes, and its joints seep hissing green vapors.}

entries.name: Spectral Constructs
entries: Fellforged are the castoffs of gearforged and clockworks production, given foul sentience when the construct bodies attract specters yearning to feel the corporeal world. The clockwork bodies trap the specters, but it gives them physical form. The specters twist the bodies to their own use, sometimes going so far as to destroy the body to harm the living. On rare occasions, other ghostly undead choose to inhabit such constructs, using the constructs as tools to enact their will in the living world at the cost of many of their natural abilities and defenses.

entries.name: Soldiers for Vampires
entries: Fellforged often seek out greater undead as their masters. Vampires and liches are favorite leaders, but mummies and darakhul also make suitable commanders.

entries.name: Grave Speech
entries: The fellforged's voice is echoing and sepulchral, unnerving most living creatures.

entries.name: Fellforged in Midgard
entries: Dwarves of Grisal canton create fellforged to fight against undead haunts and spirits and melt them down afterwards, destroying wraiths, ghosts, and other incorporeal undead. The fellforged are also sometimes created by the Emerald Order and other cults seeking to give their evil masters a body and a shape with which to rule.

name: Fenrikyn
entries: {@i Howling Fangs and Chains}
{@color This massive, warped canine has frothing jaws and chains that wrap around its body, obeying its every whim.|006abe}

Fenrikyn are warped worgs and winter wolves, altered by the influence of Fenris, the Great Wolf. Fenrikyn roam the cold forests and the hills of the Northlands, devouring all that they encounter. Generally solitary, fenrikyn have been known to gather into small packs or to take over a pack of wolves or worgs. Though they despise most living things, they reserve their greatest enmity for good-aligned canines and followers of the god Tyr.

name: Fenris
entries: The Great Wolf

name: Ferryman

entries: {@i Cursed Undead Boatman}

Ferrymen are Undead created through the use of curses and jinxcraft and are doomed to ply the waters where they were raised. They pole through the bayous and rivers, and even across land on a wave of swamp water, in coffin boats. They can focus the malice of their curse through the light of their lantern poles, jinxing enemies or those who try to force a ride without payment.

entries.name: Secret
entries: Paying a ferryman 3 copper coins lifts any curse the creature placed on the payer, and it entitles one to a single unnerving but safe ride in the ferryman's coffin boat.

name: Festerhulk

entries: {@i Fungal Undead Giant}

Festerhulks are dead giants whose corpses are infested with fungus engorged by the magic of decay. This fungus has consumed and replaced much of the giant's flesh and now animates the corpse. The heads of these giants are often completely overtaken by repulsive mushrooms and other fungal growths. The spores given off by their infestation can spread to victims killed by festerhulks, giving rise to further Undead.

entries.name: Secret
entries: Festerhulks shrink from sunlight, which harms the fungus that animates them.

name: Festus Battlechef
entries: A veteran of both cuisine and combat, the battlechef is a devout warrior and an exemplary cook. Renowned for their magical prowess and strength of will, a battlechef goes where their deity and culinary sense of purpose lead. They are found most often behind the bar, within the bustling kitchen, slicing through enemies, or providing much-needed succor to those in need.

{@i Taut dead skin, adorned entirely with tattooed fish scales, covers this woman's face and hands. She wears scaled armor, sea green like verdigris on copper, and wields a sword swirling with arcane energies. Her pale eyes stare, unblinking}.

entries.name: Undead Warlock Vassals
entries: Ancient and powerful beings across the multiverse grant magical knowledge to mortals through dangerous pacts. Those bound to these pacts become warlocks, but the will and force of their patron is borne by more than just those who strike bargains for sorcerous power. A fext is a former warlock who has become wholly dedicated to their patron—mind, body, and soul—and functions as enforcer, bodyguard, and assassin. They are powerful undead slaves to the will of their otherworldly patron.

entries.name: Linked to a Master
entries: Each fext is a unique servant of their patron and exhibits the physical traits of its master. The eyes of every fext are tied directly to their patron's mind, who can see what the fext sees at any time. The fext also possesses a telepathic link to its patron. The process a warlock undergoes to become a fext is horrendous. The warlock is emptied of whatever morality and humanity he or she had as wine from a jug, and the patron imbues the empty vessel with its corruption and unearthly will. Whatever life the fext led before is completely gone. They exist only to serve.

entries.name: Outdoing Rivals
entries: Scholars have debated about how many fext a patron can command. The more powerful and well-established have at least 100, while others have only a handful. Where there is more than one fext, however, they maneuver amongst themselves to curry favor with their powerful patron. Each fext is bound to obey commands, but they attempt to carry out the commands to the detriment of their competitors. Scheming is common and rampant among them, and each fext tries to work without the aid of other fext as much as possible.
{@i Dark, bark-like rust encrusts the trunk of this metal tree, and its dull metallic leaves rustle with the sound of sharp metal.}

entries.name: Cold Iron Trees
entries: These ferrous constructs are cold-forged in a process taking several years, as bits of rust and other oxidation are cultivated one layer at a time into bark and branches. In this way, the artificers create massive, twisted trunks resembling real, gnarled trees. Green-tinged leaves of beaten cold iron are welded in place by the master craftsmen, and trained warmages bring the construct to life through intense magical rituals rumored to take a full turn of seasons.

entries.name: Fey Destroyers
entries: The feyward tree unswervingly obeys the commands of its creators, guarding key points of entry across fey rivers and streams, abandoned sacred groves deep in the forest, suspected faerie rings, or possible elf encampments. Many are released deep in elvish woods with orders to attack any fey on sight. These trees are rarely, if ever, heard from again. Whether they leave a bloody trail of flayed elves in their wake or some fey counter-measure neutralizes them is unknown.

entries.name: Growing Numbers
entries: Each year, the feywardens order the construction and release of a handful of feyward trees, trusting in the destructive nature of the constructs. The feywardens leave nothing to chance, flooding fey forests with the constructs over decades.
{@i What appears to be a mated pair of birds changes into two bestial celestials that move in perfect harmony.}
Fidele angels form from souls so devoted to each other that their love transcends death.

entries.name: Friends to Lovers
entries: Fideles are charged with exhorting mortals to respect the bonds of partnership. They assist lovers facing obstacles and punish the enemies of love. Where there is a conflict between two cultures' laws in love, they prefer the result that keeps lovers together.

entries.name: Quiet Diplomats
entries: They prefer diplomacy to force and, despite the urgency of love, they've been known to live secretly among mortals for years or decades while waging quiet campaigns against social mores and cultural norms that keep love from achieving its full potential.

name: Field Giant
entries: Field Giants are large and docile nature spirits known for crafting the winds that roll across the western foothills of the island. They're enthralled with how the gentle breezes interact with the world around them—Which is why they're often spotted gazing off in the distance. Because of this, locals have made a habit of placing pinwheels out on clotheslines to encourage the wind-making spirit to dry their garments.

entries.name: Not Predator, Not Prey
entries: These giant spirits have grown to become one with the environment, yet they seem to take nothing from it. Unlike most creatures on Obojima, they need not sleep, or eat.

name: Fiendish Handler
entries: Handlers are a case study in misdirection Due to their imposing presence, musculature, and distinctly fiendish glare, they are often mistaken for a pygmy raksha's shapeshifting disguise. This is entirely intentional; the handler's sole job is to protect its fiendish master.

entries.name: Deals With Devils
entries: Who says crime doesn't pay? Stronger, more lethal, and more hardy than even a master-at-arms, handlers have traded their soul for infernal power. Sure, they're little more than a glorified cat carrier, but gosh, wouldn't it feel good to be that powerful? What are you going to do with your soul anyway...?

The grim-faced doctor's jaw tightens as they lower their browand sigh. Suddenly, their face contorts into a wicked, impossiblegrimace, a smile stretched too wide for the muscles on their face.Fiendish light glimmers in their eyes as hornlike bulges rip throughthe flesh of their forehead. Profane runes suddenly blaze upontheir flesh, releasing the smell of burning meat and sulfur. Thebody rises into the air, the muscle spasms barely containing the evilspirit bound within this mortal host. A spiral of flame encircles theapothecary's body as they unleash a horrific scream, speaking in avoice which is not their own. "Now, you will die, mortal."

A Soulbound Host is the physical body of an apothecary who has willingly allowed an extraplanar creature to possess them, trapping the powerful outsider in a mortal form. Powerful yet vulnerable, Soulbound Hosts loathe their creators. They wander the world for the means to reverse the curse of mortality placed upon them and return to their otherworldly domains.

Exorcist and Alienist apothecaries do not primarily study the body, and rarely practice the type of magic and science which leads to mutant horrors and flesh-stitched abominations. They are instead concerned with the supernatural forces of the mind and soul. Many research and contact powerful extraplanar entities, eager to possess mortals as a means of entering the material world. These apothecaries learn how to create Soulbound Hosts as a powerful means to contain and fight back against these dangerous otherworldly foes.

entries.name: Desperate Gambit
entries: A Soulbound Host is usually created under truly desperate circumstances, such as when a heroic apothecary faces a dangerous otherworldly being such as a demon, fey, spirit, or inscrutable entity from the Space Between Worlds. Not only are these planar invaders pernicious foes, many are effectively immortal—often these creatures simply reform when killed outside their native planes. Thus, an apothecary who lacks the ability to defeat the demon on their own, or who wishes to defeat a powerful outsider in a more permanent fashion, may instead decide upon a heroic act of self-sacrifice by turning themselves into a Soulbound Host.

entries.name: Preparing the Trap
entries: Using an array of implanted metals, ingested tinctures, mental preparations, and occult incantations, a skilled apothecary may willingly prepare their body for possession. During the process, the apothecary can weave a unique spiritual trap. It then falls to the apothecary to convince the otherworldly creature to possess them, an act that many outsiders are eager to do. Thus, the canny apothecary preys on the ego of the monster itself.

entries.name: Mortal Curse
entries: When the outsider inhabits the body, the apothecary's soul departs, leaving the extraplanar creature to take their place spiritually. If this mortal form is killed or destroyed, the bound creature does not simply return to their plane of origin. Instead, the spirit departs to the afterworlds like any other mortal soul, losing their accumulated otherworldly power forever. Thus, the Soulbound Host becomes both a prison and a death sentence for the other wielding being tricked into the apothecary's body.

entries.name: Rogue Hosts
entries: Unfortunately, this act of self-sacrifice is not without its imperfections. The apothecary's body is filled with otherworldly essence, and while the creature's power is greatly diminished, they often remain extremely dangerous—allies of the departed apothecary may still find it challenging to slay the Soulbound Host. Many escape, wandering the world with stolen lives and even assuming the identity of their host while they search for the means to escape their now mortal form. All bound outsiders are painfully aware of their new mortality, frustrated that returning to their planes of origin is not a simple matter of destroying their flesh-cage or switching their essence into a different host, one which lacks the binding wards placed by the apothecary.

entries.name: Price of Freedom
entries: Trapped outsiders can win their freedom by calling back the soul of the apothecary who trapped them, and resurrecting them into their body. This is a thing many outsiders are loathe to do out of fiendish ego, since it puts the original soul in a bargaining position. In this way, the apothecary can force the spirit to accept a bargain which requires them to remain in their own worlds for at least the duration of the apothecary's lifetime.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Religion|XPHB}, {@skill Medicine|XPHB}, or {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks to Study a Soulbound Host, learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (10+) Possessed Body
entries: You know the Soulbound Host's type and damage {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}.

entries.name: (15+) Extraplanar Magic
entries: Depending on the type of spirit, you learn either the Hellfire Chain, Illusory Assault, or Psychic Barrage actions, as well as the Spellcasting trait of the host.

entries.name: (20+) Cursed Fate
entries: You recognize its desperation caused by its spirit-bound mortality and its Reactions.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: A Soulbound Host is a careful combatant. Though powerful, the last thing they want is to be killed in their mortal form. If they are seriously injured, they often attempt to bargain, offering power and knowledge to assailants who spare them.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Fiend, Fey, or Aberrant.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Monster Blood.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Eyes, Heart, Brain, Guts.

entries.name: Bones:
entries: Skull, Spine.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Claws.

entries.name: Hair:
entries: Hair.

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Skin.

entries.name: Dust:
entries: Fiendish, Fey, or Aberrant Dust.

name: Figory Figgins
entries: A slender, blond-furred jerbeen with an affable nature and an unfortunate reputation. Figory has been studying for two years at the Avium, but anxiety about the professors expectations and the complicated schedule needed for featherless students to navigate campus have held him back a full year compared to other students. He has been bullied by his classmates at the Avium, and his recent encounter with the cobblefright has left him deeply unnerved. He desperately wants someone to believe his story and take action against the creature lurking around campus. Figory uses the {@creature commoner} stat block, adjusted with the racial traits of a jerbeen. He is neutral.

name: Filthy Jasper
entries: Filthy Jasper is an abominable Monstrosity, weasel-like but disturbingly human in his features, with unsettling hands that mimic those of a man. Formed from {@creature Vessla Browntooth|CrookedMoon24|Vessla Browntooth's} nightmarish magic, Filthy Jasper obeys her every whim and leads the swarming weasels through the Crooked House and Wickermoor Village.

As wicked as his creator, Filthy Jasper revels in human suffering, particularly that of children. An eager collector of humanoid teeth for Vessla's rituals, he savors the act of tearing them from skulls with his own hands.
[he/him]

name: Finneas Trout
entries: Finneas Trout enthusiastically teaches the children of the area their letters and numbers, or other more esoteric subjects for the children whose parents value such things. A bookish young man, he wears spectacles under a mop of unkempt brown hair, and his physical features are unimposing. Finneas has a reverence of "book learning" that is seen as admirable to some and silly to others.

He came to Wickermoor Village recently from the city of Baskerton (see chapter 1), and he keeps a room at the Green Queen Inn, paid for by the town and the parents of his more affluent students, who receive additional tutoring.

Finneas falls into the camp of the Newcomers, hoping that the pure light of reason can drive away the darkness of superstition. He has also found a source of brightness in his romantic affection for the chandler, {@creature Oswick Frey|CrookedMoon24} (see area V17).

name: Finulf One-hand
entries: Early thirties. Blue eyes. Long blond hair, full mustache, and short beard. Blade scar on right cheek. Wears patched leather armor over green tunic, black pants. A cloak with a white fur trim. Sword and dagger on his belt. Missing left hand capped with metal cuff.
{@b Found Initially In:} Down the Wolf's Barrow. Also appears in Attack on Birgkrona.
{@b Background:} Leader of the Fangs of Vanagandr, a mercenary company.
{@b Personality Traits:} Direct, never gives up, has a hundred stories that start "This reminds me of the time . . ."
{@b Bonds:} Members of the Fangs. Fighting the good fight.
{@b Flaws:} Is a bit "glass-half-empty," cheerfully points out problems in gory detail.
{@b Wants:} When they first meet, to keep the stolen Uror's Shears from the hands of the Cult of Ragnarok. Later, to defeat the cult once and for all.
{@i This proud bird struts like a peacock, made all the more majestic by its flaming fan of feathers, which shift through the color spectrum.}

entries.name: Guides and Helpers
entries: Firebirds are welcome sights to those in need of warmth and safety. They primarily work at night or in underground areas, where their talents are most needed. Friendly to all creatures, they become aggressive only upon witnessing obviously evil acts. Firebirds enjoy working with good adventuring parties, providing light and healing, though their wanderlust prevents them from staying for long.

entries.name: Redeemers
entries: Firebirds enjoy acting as reformers. They search for creatures they perceive as potential "light bringers," and they grant boons to such creatures, magically coaxing the creatures into performing good deeds in the hope such acts redeem the creatures.

entries.name: Magical Feathers
entries: Firebird feathers are prized throughout the mortal world, and occasionally, the creatures bestow feathers upon those they favor. Firebirds also seed hidden locations with specialized feathers, which burst into full-grown firebirds after a year. Firebirds live over 100 years.
{@i Wisps of black smoke and spots of bright flame coalesce into a vaguely humanoid shape.}

entries.name: Elemental Echoes
entries: When a fire elemental meets its destruction in a particularly humiliating fashion, particularly by humanoids, while summoned away from its home plane, its remains transform into a firegeist. Malevolent and resentful, they exist for revenge.

entries.name: Indiscriminate Arsonists
entries: Firegeists are not adept at telling one humanoid from another, and they are satisfied with burning any similar creature, providing the creature is flammable.

entries.name: Brighter Light, Darker Smoke
entries: A firegeist can shine brightly or be primarily smoky and dark, as it wishes. It always sheds a little light.

These foot-and-a-half-long wasps are a seasonal pest around Alderheart, drawn to the tree in the summer months by the blooming of giant orchids known as witherhearts. They are named for their red-orange coloration, as well as for the burning pain caused by their venom. Firelances are easily provoked and quick to sting. Firelances possess a potent venom that is coveted by assassins for both its availability and its lethality.

entries.name: Firelance Poison
entries: The venom of the firelance can be brewed into a potent poison that has the following statistics:

name: Fish Folk
entries: Fish folk are fish-like humanoid creatures who live under the Shallows in grottoes and caves. They are generally unpleasant and enjoy marauding along the coastline in their makeshift boats. To many Obojiman's they are considered the Howlers of the sea. While the overall number of fish folk is small, they are pesky, persistent, and opportunists. When they raid villages, they usually do so with a dozen or fewer bandits, and often when the villagers expect it least.

entries.name: Fish Folk in General
entries: Most fish folk live in the Shallows and are divided into two kingdoms, those under the rule of the Lionfish King and deepsea fishfolk under the rule of Venomous Rex. Almost all deepsea fish folk are tainted by the Corruption and afflicted by its horrific, skeletonizing effects making them desperate and oftentimes unwell.

entries.name: Villains and Cutthroats
entries: Both kingdoms of fish folk are pirates and bullies, demanding tribute from all who roam their waters. These threats are often hollow, but will do the trick, as most islanders would rather pay to end a fish folk interaction than to save a few gold.

name: Fitch Talltree
entries: Fitch is not quite thirty, though his wild beard and fierce eyes make him appear older. Like his father before him, he holds the protection of Archet and its people as a sacred duty, and would gladly lay down his life to protect anyone in the tiny community. He blames himself for the untimely death of his father nearly ten years ago, when the two were hunting a brutal Stone-Troll from the Weather Hills that his father had nearly bested in combat previously. Not only was Fitch unable to aid his father in defeating the Troll, but the elder Talltree died saving his son from a particularly grievous blow from the Troll's massive stone club. To this day, Fitch seeks to alleviate his guilt over the death of his father, but fears facing the Troll alone. He is torn between this personal quest to avenge his father, and carrying out his promise to protect the people of Archet.

name: Fjord Troll
entries: {@i Canny, Regenerating Fisherfolk}
{@color What looks like a troll with slimy skin and webbed fingers is pulling up a net full of fish onto a boat. It spots you and grins maliciously.|006abe}

Fjord trolls dwell on the coastlines of the Northern fjords and fish for sustenance in boats of their own making. They are at home in water and possess a fatty layer beneath their skin that helps protect them from the near-freezing temperatures. Webbing between their fingers and toes aid them in swimming. Despite their ease in the water, fjord trolls often fish from canoes constructed of wood and hide, which they row using their long arms and webbed hands instead of oars or paddles. Those same hands end in hooked and barbed claws that secrete a paralytic poison. This makes them effective at capturing fish and other creatures of the coast. They also have a special craw that they can fill with ice cold water and spit at their enemies.

{@i This obese, bell-shaped giant is blemished by ulcers, enlarged veins, and fungal rashes. Though it stumbles about on a pair of short, calloused legs, it moves its weight with dangerous potential.}

entries.name: Great Girth
entries: Whether as a result of a centuries-past curse or a gradual adaptation to an easygoing existence, the flab giant is gigantic in width rather than height and almost comical in its simple life. Too obese to effectively grasp weapons in its chubby fingers, a flab giant uses its great mass to deadly effect, overrunning or grabbing opponents and then sitting on them to crush them to death. Its bulk and hardiness allow it to tolerate the blows of struggling victims until they are fully crushed.

entries.name: Efficient Foragers
entries: Flab giants are the least active of giant types, spending most of their waking hours resting, napping, and sleeping, and only devote a short period each day to listlessly shuffling about, scrounging for food. Because a flab giant can eat practically anything, it doesn't have to roam far to find enough food to sustain its bulk, and only devote a short period each day to listlessly shuffling about, scrounging for food. Because a flab giant can eat practically anything, it doesn't have to roam far to find enough food to sustain its bulk, and it is rarely found far from its crude lair

entries.name: Knotted Skins
entries: Flab giants wear only scraps of clothing made of loosely knotted skins, leaving most of their stretch-marked and discolored skin exposed. Favored pelts include bear and human. A flab giant stands eight to ten feet tall and weighs 2,000 to 2,500 pounds.

{@i The dragon bears black scales, more charred than naturally colored. Cracks between the scales glow a dull red, until the dragon rears its head and roars. Red embers become bright orange flames as the creature lights up from tail to maw}.Flame dragons are capricious creatures, fascinated by dark emotions and destructive passions. The dragons of eternal fire are proud and jealous, quick to anger, and utterly unforgiving. They bring total ruin to entire civilizations for trivial reasons, but their true motivation is the fun to be had. These burning serpents treat rage, deceit, and despair as toys for their amusement. "May you be the fire's plaything" is a curse often used by the foolish.

entries.name: Taunting Others
entries: The hot-blooded creatures tease their victims like cats, seeing the world and all within it as their rightful prey. Young flame dragons are less subtle than their elders. Wyrmlings may force a woman to watch her family die or ruin a beautiful face for pleasure—direct and evil. As the dragon matures, this natural sadism develops into a desire for more complicated sport. Aging dragons of fire use politics, murder, and magic in elaborate schemes only their ilk can appreciate. Many create plots so intricate and layered that they lack a true resolution, creating only endless manipulation. A hero might foil an assassination only to see the king thus saved become a despot. She might defeat the vizier whispering lies in the ruler's ear only to discover he was a pawn in a vast conspiracy. Dark ambitions, poisoned daggers, and old vendettas build such momentum that one scheme begins each time another ends. Often, even killing the draconic mastermind cannot extinguish the fires it started.

entries.name: Malevolent Purpose
entries: The results of a flame dragon's schemes are secondary to the enjoyment it derives from pursuing a nebulous and ever-changing goal. Some flame dragons spend centuries torturing a family line for nothing more than trespassing on the dragon's land. Others plot eternal curses after twisting poorly chosen words into dire insults. The vengeance itself is secondary to an excuse for hate, plot, and ruin. Flame dragons relish such opportunities for revenge. Each is a delightful hobby. Any disruption in their game kindles a terrible rage, and in these rare moments of defeat, their anger can be catastrophic. Entire cities burn.

entries.name: Fond of Souvenirs
entries: Flame dragons are as materialistic and territorial as other true dragons. Each pursues an individual obsession it fixates upon with mad devotion to fill its hoard. Some corrupt innocence, others push nations to war, but they always collect a memento for each victory, petty or grand. One might collect scorched skulls, while another saves the melted treasures of toppled empires. When not out sowing discord, the ancient flame dragons enjoy contemplating their hoards. Every piece reminds them of their own majesty and genius.

entries.name: Vengeful Brethren
entries: Nothing is safe from a flame dragon's scheming and narcissism. They crave absolute attention and constant reassurance. Anyone who humiliates a flame dragon would be wiser to kill it. Its survival ensures the dragon's undivided attention for generations. Wiser still, is to remove all trace of involvement in a flame dragon's death. All burning serpents see the murder of one of their kin as the gravest insult.

items.name: Flamekeeper

entries: Dressed in white and gold robes adorned with the holy symbols of the Sacred Flame, the Flamekeeper recites prayers and holds a burning candle. Warding off evil and healing its allies, it stands as a protective beacon to the Knights of the Silver Order.

Every monastery, chapel, cathedral, and shrine to the Sacred Flame is watched over by a Flamekeeper. These white-robed women guided by their faith are known throughout the nations to aid the downtrodden, protect the innocent, and perform religious ceremonies of many types. Occasionally, Flamekeepers will join Silver Order knights on holy expeditions, or as envoys for the Sacred Flame, joining battlefields and wars as protectors, healers, and symbols of the faith.
I'll show you who should be keeping the flame! It's me, with my awesome sword.

entries.name: Flaming Skeleton
entries: The skeletal remains of many of those who opposed {@book Thordak the Cinder King|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|1|Thordak, the Cinder King} are said to be forever imbued with the primordial power of his fire breath. Areas scarred by the red dragon's power, including {@book Thordak's Crater|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|7. Thordak's Crater} in {@book Emon's|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Emon, the City of Fellowship} {@book Cloudtop District|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Cloudtop District}, the {@book Ashen Gorge|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Ashen Gorge} in the {@book Stormcrest Mountains|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Stormcrest Mountains}, and {@book Serpent's Head|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Serpent's Head} in the {@book Cliffkeep Mountains|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Cliffkeep Mountains}, are rife with flaming skeletons. These undead react to the raw power of the Elemental Planes, and are filled with an unquenchable desire to spread flames far and wide until nothing is left untouched by fire.

items.altText: A half-orc warrior in the foreground with her mouth open in a battle cry, brandishing a blade at a host of flaming skeletons approaching from blackened trees.

name: Flea
entries: Cultist ally

name: Fleshcrafter
entries: Only the most reckless necromancers pursue the ancient, malevolent art of fleshcrafting. To them, the only perfection in life or undeath is that which they bestow. While they are immensely dangerous mages on their own, their power grows exponentially when acting in concert with their {@creature flesh golem|MM} creations.

name: Fleshcrawler
entries: {@i Crawling Flesh that Wears a Face}

{@color This creature resembles a humanoid-shaped collection of partially formed body parts, including muscles, bones, organs, ligaments, and facial features. Countless small pseudopods squirm from every part of its body, occasionally falling off and writhing as if still alive.|006abe}

Horrific nightmares that somehow escaped from the sealed land of Hyperborea, fleshcrawlers seek to reproduce and spread their infestation across the world while causing as much pain and destruction as possible.

Their attacks temporarily warp the physical form of the target, twisting flesh and bone painfully. These attacks also renders the victim potentially vulnerable to infestation by the flesh-like webs that they spawn.

Once a host is infected, the fleshcrawler controls that creature's actions like a puppeteer. Over the course of a few days, the host grows weaker as it is consumed from within, until nothing remains of the original form but its skin. This becomes a cocoon for a new fleshcrawler, which emerges in its fully grown form.

Fleshcrawlers are typically encountered alone or in small groups, though some keep a clutch of newly infected humanoids nearby. Thanks to its limited telepathy, the fleshcrawler can sense the presence of others of its kind and rarely competes for prey or new hosts.

name: Fleshdobbin

entries: {@i Flesh-Crafted Amalgam of Knight and Horse}

Fleshdobbins are abominations created when a horse and its rider are horrifically melded through fleshcrafting magic. Their limbs stretch and deform, though afterward, their bodies resist further transformation.

Fitted with saddles and bearing savage weaponry, these monsters may look like riderless horses from a distance, but each leg culminates in oddly human-looking gnarled hands with fingers ending in wicked claws. Their voices are the comingled shrieks of human and horse.

entries.name: Secret
entries: Affixing a bridle to a fleshdobbin causes the instincts of the horse within the amalgam to take over, becoming a loyal steed once more.

name: Flintclaw
entries: These lithe, fiendish felines actively stalk the shadowed alleyways of Magmarath in search of prey. In this way, they are very similar to predatory cats found on the Material Plane. Particularly renowned for their ferocity, flintclaws are protected by their dense black iron skeletons, and rend flesh like butter using their white-hot metal claws. They are also frequently utilized in the Iron Maw Arena as motivation for races and other timed events, to such a degree that mortal challengers are often nicknamed 'flintclaw fodder'.

name: Flora Spirit
entries: Spirits of this variety can resemble all kinds of foliage. They get a form as they enter the Physical Realm, growing into it as though they were actual flora. They might be mistaken for a plant or mushroom at a cursory glance, but anyone paying attention will notice that they have arms, legs, and expressive little faces.

Flora spirits tend to see the plants or fungus that resemble them as kindred, and they are most often found tending the places where they appeared. However, some leave their familiar soil, venturing forth to roam the island.
The table below has a list of examples of forms a flora spirit might take. Feel free to create your own.

{@i This mass of fused corpses resembles a butterfly with wings of skin, limbs of bone, and a head formed of several different skulls. The dark magic that formed this abomination swirls around it hungrily.}

entries.name: Bound by Necromancy
entries: Flutterfleshes are created in terrible necromantic rituals. Cultists gather in the name of a dark god, powerful lich, or crazed madman, and forever bind themselves body and soul into a single evil being. Flutterfleshes take recently severed limbs and fuse these new pieces to themselves in accordance with some unknowable aesthetic.

entries.name: Dilemma of Flesh
entries: The most horrifying thing about a flutterflesh, however, is its devious nature. A flutterflesh offers its prey the choice to either die or lose a limb. If it accepts the limb, the flutterflesh then leaves the victim alone. One can always tell where a flutterflesh resides because so many of the locals are missing appendages.

name: Flying Beast Spirit
entries: Unlike their land-bound counterparts, flying spirits tend to keep a degree of distance from settlements, while not altogether rejecting them. People are fascinating, and flying spirits prefer to watch from a distance. It's not uncommon for a person to claim they are being watched by the same owl or followed by the same chicken every day. When the time is right, the spirit will reveal itself to their chosen person.
The table below has a list of examples of forms a flying beast spirit might take. Feel free to create your own.

name: Flying Book
entries: Little can be said about the flying book that is not readily apparent. Though it is indistinguishable from an arcanist's spellbook while motionless, this animated arcane tome can flutter through the air at a moment's notice, using its cover as rudimentary wings. Flying books are playful, and enjoy the sensation of being written in.

name: Flying Magnetite Weapon
entries: Crafted from highly magnetic magnetite, these animated armours and weapons share the common property of being immobilised by heat The animated suit of plate armour is capable of conjuring bolts of arcanomagnetic force that can knock a creature off its feet.

name: Flying Polyp

entries: A horrible elder race of half polypous, utterly alien entities... They were only partly material and had the power of aerial motion, despite the absence of wings... Suggestions of a monstrous plasticity and of temporary lapses of visibility... singular whistling noises and colossal foot-prints made up of five circular toe marks seemed also to be associated with them.
entries.from: H.P. Lovecraft, The Shadow Out of Time

entries: Almost nothing is known of the dreaded flying polyp. The details of their culture, the motivations behind their actions, and even the name they use to refer to themselves are complete mysteries.

entries.name: Abandoned Domains
entries: The flying polyps once gathered in great cities. They constructed vaults deep within the earth. Stone wells bored through the rock and dirt allowed the polyps access to their strongholds. When they departed the world, they sealed these wells with stone caps. Only a patient climber, or a creature capable of flight, can navigate the long, deep wells to reach the polyp ruins below.

entries.name: Masters of the Air
entries: While flying polyps are powerful combatants, their most potent attacks is their ability to control the weather. When three or more of these creatures gather, they can conjure howling wind storms that scour an entire region of life. It takes an hour for three or more polyps working together to create a storm. When they finish their ritual, a terrible storm rips through the area in a 5-mile radius around the ritual site. The storm lasts for an hour and flattens all buildings that lack fortifications. Creatures caught in the open take 1d4 Bludgeoning damage per minute until they find shelter.
{@i This person has goatlike legs, small horns partially hidden beneath a hood, and a mouth full of rows of serrated teeth. Its clothes are a mixture of heavy leathers and bright silks.}

entries.name: Dimensional Merchants
entries: The folk of Leng are interplanar merchants and avid slavers, trading silks, rubies, and the magic-infused stones of Leng for humanoid slaves. They sail between worlds in peculiar ships with split, lateen-rigged masts and rigging that howls like the damned in high winds. They are said to befriend Void dragons, heralds of darkness, and other servants of the Void.

entries.name: A High Plateau
entries: Leng is a forbidding plateau surrounded by hills and peaks. Its cities are places which some claim have fallen into ruin, and which others claim to have visited in living memory.

entries.name: Love of Nets
entries: When in combat, the folk of Leng use nets woven from silk taken from their enemies, the spiders of Leng.

entries.name: Followers of the Falling Fire
entries: The Followers of the Falling Fire are a religious sect who believe the meteor signaled a celestial prophecy. These fanatics consider delerium a holy sacrament. Called to pilgrimage by the prescient testament of their leader, {@creature Lucretia Mathias|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}, zealous masses of devout commonfolk now journey to the Crater's Edge to take their place in a divine plan.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Falling Fire pilgrims give up their possessions and wealth and often carry very little on them. For the most part, common Falling Fire devotees are not equipped to fight. Most members try to avoid combat. Preferring a peaceful approach, they are more reactionary in their tactics and hope most situations do not come to bloodshed. However, Drakkenheim is a dangerous city, and monsters and bandits have attempted to thwart the efforts of the devout worshippers often. Pilgrims have been known to take up clubs, daggers, and any mundane weapons they can find to defend themselves, and often groups of traveling pilgrims are accompanied by armored zealots and spellcasting divine leaders who are ready to protect their flock.
There comes a time in every man's life where he wants more. Delerium in your chest is the wrong way.
A cowardly bandit, ready to rob a defenceless victim, but capable of ambushing a lonely companion with the help of others.

entries.name: Ruffians
entries: Local robbers, cut-throats, brigands and other assorted criminals fall within this category of potential adversaries. Such foes can be encountered on the lonely roads of Eriador, but they are met as likely in a dark alley in Bree.{@i "Where d'you think you're going?" said one, the largest and most evil-looking of the crew}.

entries.name: Evil Men
entries: Cruel individuals like brigands, marauders and slavers prowling the Lone-lands of Middle-earth fall within this category. Their malicious will notwithstanding, Evil Men are not servitors of Sauron, and they can end up opposing the Player- heroes for reasons not dependent on an allegiance with the Dark Lord.
{@i A relatively diminutive giant stalks beneath the forest's dark canopy, large spear in hand.}

entries.name: Painted Skin
entries: Roughly the size and shape of an ogre, the forest marauder is covered in paint or colored mud. An exaggerated brow ridge juts out over close-set eyes, and corded muscle stands out all over the giant.

entries.name: Keep to the Wilderness
entries: Cruel and savage when encountered, the forest marauders' demeanor has worked against them, and they have nearly been driven to extinction in places where they can be easily tracked. They have since learned to raid far from their hidden homes, leading to sightings in unexpected places.

entries.name: Orc Friends
entries: Forest marauders get along well with orcs and goblins, who appreciate their brute strength and their skill at night raids.

name: Forest Prowler

entries: "Did you see that? Was it just the wind in the leaves, or has a prowler come calling..."

Forest prowlers feature prominently throughout folktales in Humblewood, notably as monsters in frightful stories. These cat-like beasts have the unique ability to grow leaves and moss on their spotted fur, allowing them to camouflage perfectly within the forest canopy.

entries.name: Fable and Folklore
entries: One of the reasons forest prowlers have attained such mythic status is due to their elusive nature. They are adept at moving unseen through the canopy where they hunt, and their skills as ambush predators means that few who see them live to tell the tale. In some communities the killing of a forest prowler is considered a rite of passage among beast hunters. The large fangs seen adorning the necks of Humblewood's greatest hunters and warriors, and cloaks made from prowler fur, are trophies that showcase one's prowess and skill.

entries.name: Fierce Hunter
entries: Forest prowlers are apex predators. They can claim virtually any prey they desire, but usually target deer, elk, and other large herbivores. Prowlers use their powerful bodies and gripping claws to drag their kill up into their tree nests, where it can be consumed at their leisure. These felines are known to travel long and winding paths through the forest, residing in temporary shelters throughout the seasons. Although nomadic, the prowlers are quite territorial of whatever area they currently inhabit. Relatively passive in the winter, they are most active in the spring and summer during peak hunting and breeding seasons.

entries.name: Forge Guardian
entries: Just as {@book dwarves|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|4|dwarves} created the earliest golems, the {@deity The All-Hammer|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|All-Hammer} fashioned forge guardians to guard the divine furnaces and hearths that designed the first {@book dwarves|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|4|dwarves}. Shaped from extravagant marble and fused with adamantine, crafted with impeccable detail and care, these rare and massive constructs exemplify the highest form of artistry that every Exandrian blacksmith, forgemaster, and artisan spends a life-time hoping to achieve.

entries.name: Divine Spark
entries: A faceless, tireless being of immense strength, a forge golem is gifted life by a single shard from the {@deity The All-Hammer|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|All-Hammer's} own divine spark, lovingly kept safe inside a ring of arcane flame and ancient sigils. The {@deity The All-Hammer|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|All-Hammer's} divinity is akin to a volcano inside the golem, turning the construct's blood into lava. Fire no longer harms the construct, but instead heals it.

entries.name: Sacred purpose
entries: Where it looms over a divine forge, a forge guardian's appendages end in a stretched set of hooked forceps and a rune-adorned blade. The golem can assist a blacksmith in creating new golems, or it can trample, bludgeon, push, and knock down any who threaten this sacred process of creation.

Forge golems also serve as opponents for any wishing to engage in the {@deity The All-Hammer|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|All-Hammer's} trial of worthiness. A golem's attacks blind prospective heroes, who must then earn back their vision by risking a deadly counterattack.

items.altText: A gigantic, metallic humanoid construct stands chained to a stone cavern wall. A fiery hot red glows through the cracks of its silver body.

name: Formless Spawn

entries: When the men of K'n-Yan went down into N'Kai's black abyss... they found living things... amorphous lumps of viscous black slime... They did not pause for detailed observations, and those who escaped alive sealed the passage.
entries.from: H.P. Lovecraft and Zealia Bishop, The Mound

entries: These black, protean beings change shape in an instant, from toad-like lumps to elongated things with hundreds of rudimentary legs. They ooze through small cracks or enlarge to block entire passages.

entries.name: Alarmingly Intelligent
entries: Despite their ooze-like form, formless spawn are cunning, malevolent entities spawned by the Cthulhu Mythos. They lurk in forgotten shrines and ruins, guarding ritual relics and reacting swiftly to any intrusion.

entries.name: Relentless Guardians
entries: Formless spawn often guard sacred Mythos objects. If an intruder steals such a relic, the spawn relentlessly tracks them to reclaim it, never stopping until the object is recovered.

name: Fossegrim
entries: {@i Cavorting Fey Musicians}

{@color This small being is attired in a fur-lined vest and pointed cap. It has greenish skin, a long nose, and twinkling black eyes. It smiles mischievously and pulls a fiddle from behind its back.|006abe}

Mysterious water fey that are mystically linked to waterfalls and streams, fossegrim resemble gnome-sized creatures with vaguely troll-like features, including pale green skin and bulbous noses. Fossegrim can also disguise themselves as attractive humanoids of the species most prevalent in the region to lure humanoids into heedless revelry.

Every fossegrim owns a musical instrument, such as a fiddle, lyre, or shawm, which it can play to weave powerful, enchanted melodies. While a fossegrim's musical instrument doesn't display any magical properties in the hands of others, some fossegrim have been known to teach talented humans and elves some of their tricks in exchange for companionship or food.

name: Fractal Lepidoptera

entries: Fluttering in midair is a cavalcade of color, of rushing energy and indecipherable movement, a tessellating fractal impossible to follow with your eyes. With a rush, it brushes past you, tossing you as a leaf on the wind. As you crash to the ground, your confused mind grapples with the creature's unfathomable form. A perpetually unfolding butterfly of vibrant color is the best your mind can interpret from the nonsensical imagery you see.
I keep waking from a dream thinking I am a butterfly that dreams they are Pluto. {@spell Polymorph} screws with your head, man.

To look upon a lepidoptera confounds the mind, as its essence extends into multiple dimensions and the patterns of its form tessellate and refract. Once mesmerized by the spiral of its wings, one is lost in the unformed realms of infinity of the Space Between Worlds. The lepidoptera is simultaneously present in both the known world and the world beyond, bridging the borders between, confounding all on both sides of the divide.

Fractal lepidoptera emerge in Thin Places, or in areas where the northern and southern lights flutter across the sky. These places are a chrysalis to the lepidoptera in which it waits until its pattern infiltrates a realm so it can take flight. Slowly it extends the range of its pattern until all around it exists within the lines of its fractal. And yet it is not truly malevolent. The lepidoptera merely is, living and growing in more dimensions than humans can comprehend. In the dance of its motif and the flutter of a butterfly's wing, mortal lives are set in motion on a path outside of their own will.

The presence of a lepidoptera is recognizable when creatures start behaving repetitively and against their nature. A conspiracy of ravens sings together in syncopated rhythm; streams flow in unnatural direct paths up and down hills; children speak in haikus; hunting animals perpetually circle their prey that has long since died of hunger.

entries.name: Lair effect
entries: Fractal Lepidoptera transform reality around them, manifesting the following effect:

entries.name: Quantum Entanglement
entries: Creatures taking a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} within 1 mile of the lepidoptera must succeed on a {@dc 17} Charisma saving throw or gain a pattern effect. Creatures can repeat the saving throw at the end of each {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} once they are outside the range of Quantum Entanglement. Casting {@spell Lesser Restoration} or similar spells of higher level on an affected creature can remove the pattern effect.

entries.caption: Fractal Lepidoptera Patterns
rows: Something unseen hampers you. You gain the {@condition Staggered|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} condition.
On each of your turns, you can only walk in straight lines in the direction of either north, south, east, or west.
Your hands start to flutter uncontrollably. You gain the {@condition Clumsy|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} condition.
You can only speak in haikus, rhyming couplets, or iambic pentameter.
You float an inch above the ground. Your walking {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is unchanged and {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} does not affect you.
You gain the ability to see polarized light and the ultraviolet spectrum. You see {@condition invisible} objects and creatures, and you can see into the Ethereal Plane.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine a lepidoptera, learning the following based on the result.

entries.name: (5+) Mothlike Features
entries: You recognize its Phototaxis trait.

entries.name: (10+) Chaotic Patterns
entries: You learn the lepidoptera's Quantum Entanglement and Tessellation features.

entries.name: (15+) Multidimensional
entries: You know of the creature's Multidimensional Presence and Incomprehensible Vision features.

entries.name: (20+) Creature of Energy
entries: You are aware of its {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB|Vulnerabilities} and Energy Form trait.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The lepidoptera flies through creatures while making Fractal Wing attacks, scattering foes with its Energy Form trait. If at least one enemy is {@condition Staggered|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}, it targets them with Tessellation. The lepidoptera uses Criss Cross to protect itself from attacks on the border Ethereal Plane.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Elemental.

entries.name: Dust:
entries: Elemental Dust.

entries.name: Getting lost in the Border Ethereal Plane
entries: When encountering a Fractal Lepidoptera, characters can get stranded in the Border Ethereal Plane. This has the potential to derail a campaign. Here are a few suggestions on how to run this scenario instead:

items: When the lepidoptera dies, the fabric of reality temporarily weakens and everyone can safely return to the Prime Material Plane.

Immediately after the lepidoptera dies, the party needs to succeed in a skill challenge to traverse the veil between the planes. Each character can contribute to the skill challenge by suggesting actions that they take to help find the veil, withstand the pull of the Ethereal Plane, and open a gate.
The group succeeds if they make 4 successful DC 15 skill checks before 3 failures.
The characters must harvest the animus of the lepidoptera and craft a {@item fractal key|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}.

entries: A wise me once thought to myself, the longer you can go without getting hit, the better. that's free advice for you.
{@i This slight creature resembles a goblin, but its blue skin and the icicles hanging from the tip of its long nose speak to the chilling truth.}

The fraughashar are a race of short, tricky, cruel fey who inhabit cold mountainous regions. Fraughashar have light blue skin, short pointed ears, and needlelike teeth. Delighting in mayhem, they always seem to have devilish grins on their faces.

entries.name: Sacred Rivers
entries: The fraughashar view cold rivers and river gorges as sacred places in which their wicked god Fraugh dwells, and they likewise revere the snowy peaks where the Snow Queen holds sway. They are fiercely protective of their territory, and their easy mobility over frozen and rocky terrain lets them make short work of intruders.

entries.name: Chilling Tales
entries: The origin of the strange and deadly fraughashar is unclear. Some druidic legends claim the fraughashar were born out of a winter so cold and cruel that the spirits of the river itself froze. Bardic tales claim that the fraughashar are a tribe of corrupted goblins, and that they were permanently disfigured during a botched attempt at summoning an ice devil. Whatever the truth of their beginnings, the fraughashar are cruel and merciless. They kill anyone who enters their land.

name: Fray Merridan
entries: Fray is a dashing red-furred vulpin with sharp eyes and a quick wit. A highly skilled swordswoman, she was left without a home when forest fires spreading from the Scorched Grove burned her village. She saw joining the bandits as an opportunity to use her skills to provide for herself and those she cares for. She is astute and talented, but also competitive and unwilling to forget even the smallest slight against her. Fray uses the {@creature vulpin captain|HumblewoodCampaignSetting} stat block.

entries.name: {@book Company of Free Swords|GrimHollowCG24|13|Company of Free Swords}

entries: Blood and Honor, Strength in Steel

The Company of Free Swords is the pre-eminent mercenary organization on the continent, with branches in most major cities. The company takes all manner of contracts—from ridding a village of a monster, to protecting a town from bandit raids, to sending hundreds to fight a full-fledged war for a well-paying lord.

The company has a code of honor and an elite reputation they make sure to spread. Despite the name, its services do not come for free. If you want the best loyalty money can buy, a company known for slaying daemon lords and sending aether kindred into the void, then you want the Company of Free Swords, and you better be ready to pay.

Despite their love for coin, the Free Swords are not unscrupulous. The company's honor, its soldiers' well-being, and the outright refusal to commit atrocities are core principles. While individual branches may at times be swayed by coin to stray from their code, the Free Swords are known to "discipline" their own, so none take that chance lightly.
Skill and honor are the main qualifications for joining the Free Swords, and they have attracted warriors, priests, druids, rogues, spies, and monster hunters into their ranks.

entries.name: Agents
entries: Historically, new recruits into the Swords—regardless of their training or military service—spend at least a year in regimented training. The action they see is plenty dangerous, but only under strict veteran oversight. The training is as much to ensure their combat prowess as it is to instill the Company mindset and tenets.

Since Yrsa's unorthodox yet well-documented ascension, there have been more exceptions made for those with proven records and skills. This has been met with decidedly mixed feelings among the veterans.

entries.name: Ranks and Pay
entries: The Free Swords embrace their "simple soldier" mindset and avoid a complex hierarchy. A recruit who's completed their first-year training and initial engagements becomes a Free Sword — the typical foot soldier of the company. All Free Swords of the same rank are paid the same share.

After at least five years and having proven themselves, one becomes either a Veteran or a Specialist, gaining a bigger share than a regular Free Sword. Specialists are Veterans with unique skills. These include sappers who use engineering, alchemy, or magic to affect the battlefield, battlemages who are field-level combatants that bring powerful spell support, and infiltrators who are skilled in stealth, poison, and neutralization of individual targets. Other specialists — including several types of ranged combatants — also exist. Specialists must be proven in their area and receive a higher coin share than a Veteran. Finally, those who lead are promoted to Captains. Captains get the highest share of the coin.
Although there is no combat rank higher than Captain, there is a leadership hierarchy among the different chapters, which determines rank among the Captains.

In the field, a Captain can lead as few as one other Sword and as many as several hundred. For large battles, temporary military-style designations are given to different Captains to create the necessary hierarchies. This allows the company to field units of dramatically different sizes.

entries.name: Equipment and Visual Identity
entries: Free Swords are always proficient with the sword and {@item Shield|XPHB}, and many choose to carry these tried-and-true implements into battle. The company itself does not mandate equipment and encourages its members to take pride in the procurement and maintenance of the best weapons of war for themselves.

In times of mass battle, the Free Swords don their distinctive red and gold "Double Lion" tabards or those provided by their employer. Otherwise, the mercenaries are allowed to wear what they want. All are issued a sturdy double lion brooch, which they wear with pride, except in cases of espionage or other subterfuge.

While the company rarely provides more than the very basics of equipment, they do have access to some of the best merchants and artisans across Etharis, including many who set up permanently on-site at company locations. After all, where better to get a good price for weapons of war than amongst well-paid mercenaries for whom such things could mean the difference between life and death?

entries.name: Experienced Leaders
entries: Veterans of the Company of Free Swords are formidable foes on the battlefield. They are well equipped and combine the tactics of a well-oiled military machine with individual flare.

entries.name: {@book Company of Free Swords|GrimHollowCG24|13|Company of Free Swords}

entries: Blood and Honor, Strength in Steel

The Company of Free Swords is the pre-eminent mercenary organization on the continent, with branches in most major cities. The company takes all manner of contracts—from ridding a village of a monster, to protecting a town from bandit raids, to sending hundreds to fight a full-fledged war for a well-paying lord.

The company has a code of honor and an elite reputation they make sure to spread. Despite the name, its services do not come for free. If you want the best loyalty money can buy, a company known for slaying daemon lords and sending aether kindred into the void, then you want the Company of Free Swords, and you better be ready to pay.

Despite their love for coin, the Free Swords are not unscrupulous. The company's honor, its soldiers' well-being, and the outright refusal to commit atrocities are core principles. While individual branches may at times be swayed by coin to stray from their code, the Free Swords are known to "discipline" their own, so none take that chance lightly.
Skill and honor are the main qualifications for joining the Free Swords, and they have attracted warriors, priests, druids, rogues, spies, and monster hunters into their ranks.

entries.name: Agents
entries: Historically, new recruits into the Swords—regardless of their training or military service—spend at least a year in regimented training. The action they see is plenty dangerous, but only under strict veteran oversight. The training is as much to ensure their combat prowess as it is to instill the Company mindset and tenets.

Since Yrsa's unorthodox yet well-documented ascension, there have been more exceptions made for those with proven records and skills. This has been met with decidedly mixed feelings among the veterans.

entries.name: Ranks and Pay
entries: The Free Swords embrace their "simple soldier" mindset and avoid a complex hierarchy. A recruit who's completed their first-year training and initial engagements becomes a Free Sword — the typical foot soldier of the company. All Free Swords of the same rank are paid the same share.

After at least five years and having proven themselves, one becomes either a Veteran or a Specialist, gaining a bigger share than a regular Free Sword. Specialists are Veterans with unique skills. These include sappers who use engineering, alchemy, or magic to affect the battlefield, battlemages who are field-level combatants that bring powerful spell support, and infiltrators who are skilled in stealth, poison, and neutralization of individual targets. Other specialists — including several types of ranged combatants — also exist. Specialists must be proven in their area and receive a higher coin share than a Veteran. Finally, those who lead are promoted to Captains. Captains get the highest share of the coin.
Although there is no combat rank higher than Captain, there is a leadership hierarchy among the different chapters, which determines rank among the Captains.

name: Frenzied Dreg

entries: This muscular Dreg bounds on all fours towards you, its hands and feet are stretched out with almost talon-like claws, its hanging open mouth foams and drips, its eyes mad with a frenzied bloodlust.

The Frenzied Dreg is a faster, more muscular cousin to its shambling brethren. It hunts the streets of Drakkenheim, actively seeking out prey. It lurks in dark ruins, even occasionally taking to the sewers, or clambering up the sides of buildings. When a group of Frenzied Dregs find other lesser Dregs, they herd them into the streets and use them as a trap, luring adventurers to engage with them and waiting to strike

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Survival|XPHB} or {@skill Nature|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check to {@action Study|XPHB} a Frenzied Dreg, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (5+) Transformed Human
entries: You recognize the creature is an aberration that has a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} thanks to its claws.

entries.name: (10+) Fast and Dangerous
entries: You learn of the creature's Claws attack and Bounding Leap {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: (15+) Dangerous Hunter
entries: You recognize the Frenzied Dreg's highest and lowest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Leaping into the midst of combat, Frenzied Dregs chase down their foes and unleash a flurry of claws. Frenzied Dregs howl in fury as they bound upon their targets. So loud are their screams and screeches that it often attracts other Dregs and monsters to the area. Frenzied Dregs rarely flee; they pursue their enemies through Drakkenheim up to the edges of the Haze.

A variant that is as hungry for prey as it looks. Runs as fast as a Caspian heading towards a buffet.

name: Friar Olaf
entries: As a young monk, Friar Olaf of the Silver Bells was the leader of the monastery before Renathyr took it over and became his second convert thereafter. In its early years, the cloister was called Silverbell Monastery, for it overlooks the Silverbell River in the valley below, and it was dedicated to the Patient Lady. There, Olaf and his monks tended to the infirm and to outcasts, but he longed in his heart for glory. He demanded payment from his charges and commissioned a great silver bell for the monastery inscribed with his name so that he would be remembered forever.
Renathyr's arrival stoked Olaf's hunger for reverence and immortality. It was simple to urge Olaf onward from stipends of coin to sacrifices of blood.

name: Fright
entries: Hauntings can usually be attributed to the usual spectral suspects: ghosts, specters, shadows, and poltergeists. But benign hauntings, where the restless spirit merely play tricks on the living, is usually caused by a fright. These spirits are usually the artifacts of children or entertainers, clinging to the afterlife for company and a semblance of affection, and are as such preoccupied with fun. They never willingly harm others when they haunt a house, and will serve any master that conjures them, if only for the sake of inclusion.

A retired mistral raptor hunter, Frond is the owner and sole employee of Frond's Fineries, the general store in Reya's Watch. She has aspirations of earning enough coin to move her shop to Alderheart.

{@i "They took the sled dogs first, and later the seal-skinner set to guard them. We'd hear a confused, muffled cry in the wind and then we'd find them—a raven harvest, cold and stiff on the ice. Next time, we hid ourselves and watched, and we saw them floating through the air like kites. A wisp of blowing snow that never dispersed, a billowing, snowflake sail moving with sinister purpose. The 'cloak of death' our guide called it."}

Whipped through the air by snowstorms and resembling a spider's web dangling with delicate ice crystals, these silently gliding, beautiful killers are semi-sentient plants adapted to the merciless cold of the north.

entries.name: Cloak of Death
entries: Flat nodes shaped like large snowflakes connect the frostveil's netlike body and trailing tails of transparent fibers. Gossamer tendrils stream behind and between the flying snowflakes, ready to grab and entangle any warm-blooded creature the frostveil detects.

entries.name: Seek Warmth
entries: Each starlike node contains crude sensory organs, able to detect warmth as meager as a living creature's breath and steer the gliding web toward it.

entries.name: Spirit Spores
entries: Northern shamans say the dance of the frostveils is beautiful when lit by the northern lights and a powerful omen. With great care, shamans sometimes harvest frostveils for their frozen spore-shards, which grant potent visions of the spirit world when melted on the tongue.

name: Fungal Trolling

entries: Resembling a large purple and white mushroom, Fungal Trollings throb and ooze with overcharged energy. They appear ready to burst as their grim little expressions whine and wail.

Fungal Trollings are grown from the strange concoctions of Troll Hags. A {@creature Troll Hag|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} can grow hundreds of these creatures in their gardens within a very short amount of time. However, the trollings are prone to bursting if they get too excited. Only a small few ever grow to adulthood, becoming {@creature HUmongous Fungus Troll|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Humongous Fungus Trolls}.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check to {@action study|XPHB} a Fungal Trolling, learning the following information based on the result:

entries.name: (5+) From Harsh Environments
entries: You know the troll's Spore Slam action.

entries.name: (10+) Explosive Death
entries: You learn of its Death Burst trait.

entries.name: (15+) Special Weakness
entries: You have insight into the troll's {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB|Vulnerabilities}.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Fungal Trollings emerge from patches of mushrooms and run screaming towards their enemies, lashing out with their tiny tendrils. When hit hard enough, they explode in a puff of spores that can weaken their enemies.

I know how big they can get. So cut em down when they're small. Just hold your breath.

Slimes are magical oozes with strange properties. Slimes provide an important role in many ecosystems across Humblewood, as their bodies can digest just about anything. The bodies of slimes are also sought after for use in potion making.

entries.name: Fungusfeaster
entries: These silvery-grey slimes feast on the fungus found in Alderheart's roots. Though they are a pest to threadgrass farmers in large numbers, they help keep harmful varieties of fungus at bay.

We've been led to believe that vampires and werewolves are natural enemies. Convenient that two fearsome creatures would be so opposed to the other. Never did we imagine, nor prepare, for a time when they might unite.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Someone who has proficiency with alchemist's supplies can use 1 pint of blood from a fzeg and mix it with silver and other reagents worth 50 gp to create a {@item lycanthropy antidote|GrimHollowLairsEtharis} (see Appendix A of Lairs of Etharis). A slain fzeg has 10 ({@dice 1d4 + 2}) usable pints of blood. The blood of a fzeglaich can be used, but it takes five times as much blood and twice as long to brew. Creating the antidote takes 4 hours of work and a successful {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}) check.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
items.entry: A fzeg is a mix of werewolf and vampire but has fewer weaknesses. The creature is resistant to nonmagical attacks.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
items.entry: With its bite, a fzeg can drain life force and curse a person with werewolf lycanthropy. Someone who dies from a fzeg's bite becomes a fzeglaich, a creature like the fzeg and loyal to it.

items.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
items.entry: A fzeg can transform into humanoid form. It's natural form, however, is that of a wolf-human hybrid. This vampiric monster isn't vulnerable to sunlight, but radiant damage prevents it from regenerating.

entries.name: GM Advice
entries: An ambitious DM could imagine a fzeg at the lead of a force including other werewolf-undead hybrids. Combined with a ghoul or ghast, the creature would paralyze, or combined with a wight, it would drain the life and lower the maximum hit points of a target. Similarly, other kinds of lycanthropes could become undead and wield hybrid powers.
