name: He Who Laughs Last

entries: The bloated demon lord descends, his wings unfurling like a curtain falling at the end of a tragedy. Holding a skull in one clawed hand, he is garbed in black-and-white checkered patterns, featuring a great belt of skulls and a frilled doublet made from finger bones. The skin upon his leering face has peeled away, revealing a mask-like goat skull beneath which frowns on one side and grins on the other. His appearance is almost like that of a great, macabre clown. His bellowing laughter resounds in your ears, stirs the blood, shakes the bones, and chills the soul.

He Who Laughs Last is a primordial demon of death and decay. Profoundly nihilistic yet strangely mirthful, this archfiend revels in the drama and theatrics of mortal existence, seeing life itself as a cosmic joke. To him, each moment is merely a meaningless scene in the grand tragicomedy of the universe. His spiteful laugh echoes through the corridors of time and space. Legend tells it will be the final sound at the end of all things — when the curtain falls on existence itself. He Who Laughs Last believes this to be his perverse destiny, and this purported knowledge fuels his interactions with mortals, who he regards as powerless pawns in the great play of life and death.

any undead creatures are believed to be his designs, mocking curses the demon lord has lain upon humanity for his own sick entertainment. Given his mastery over such dark magic, He Who Laughs Last is often sought by necromancers, warlocks, and other arcane practitioners alike as an instructor or patron. Furthermore, He Who Laughs Last often makes eldritch pacts offering power, knowledge, and the promise of escape from mortality. In particular, the demon lord is believed to know the blasphemous rituals required to transform a mortal spellcaster into an abhorrent lich. Rather than bargain for the souls of his petitioners, however, He Who Laughs Last demands they collect the souls of others instead. He cares not for the method, only that the quota is fulfilled. The demon lord hungers for mortal souls not for the power they contain — although that is certainly a factor — but because he enjoys keeping soul-puppets to entertain himself by replaying the tragedies of their lives.

Еhe Theatre of the Danse Macabre is the domain of He Who Laughs Last. Located in the dark pits of the abyss, this fiendish citadel resembles a great theatre-in-the-round made from bone and blood. There, the collected souls of He Who Laughs Last are bound eternally among the shadowy players and audience members, where they must continually perform tragic stories and watch the dark circus play out.

Although the demon lord's followers are a common target for Knights of the Silver Order, the fiend himself has a particular enmity amongst worshippers of the Old God Morrigan, the goddess of death and magic. He Who Laughs Last often appears to desperate penitents and heretical priests of the Old God, occasionally even impersonating the deity to trick and deceive her devoted followers into creating undead creatures and participating in his schemes.

entries.name: Roleplaying Traits
entries: Adventurers who interact with He Who Laughs Last must endure his mocking laughter and jeering comments, as he remarks on the futility of their actions, the dramatic irony of their mistakes, and the meaninglessness of their quests. In doing so, He Who Laughs Last carefully offers an escape or solution—if the adventurers will offer him service in exchange, one that is almost certain to have unforeseen consequences.

entries.name: Personality Traits
entries: In conversation, I cannot contain my dark mirth, which manifests from a low chuckle to a belly-bursting guffaw. Most of all, I love the moment when mortals realize the cost of their terrible mistakes and poor decisions.

entries.name: Ideal
entries: Mortals fear death. I play upon that fear, and with it I can catch the conscience of any soul.

entries.name: Bond
entries: I harvest of souls at life's curtain call, binding them to my cast of players in my Theatre of the Danse Macabre.

entries.name: Flaw
entries: I oft direct the play too long, delighting in extending the final act. My patience is as deep as the grave, allowing me to savor each move in the mortal game, though sometimes to the detriment of a timely demise.

He Who Laughs Last loves nothing more than when mortal heroes attempt to outmaneuver him. As befitting his name, there is almost always some unfortunate upset or surprise twist the demon has in store. Even when he is seemingly defeated, he is always sure to remind his foes who will have the last laugh.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Arcana|XPHB} or {@skill History|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Religion|XPHB}) checks when they take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine He Who Laughs Last, learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (20+) Powerful Demonlord.
entries: You are aware of his {@sense Truesight|XPHB} and telepathy, his {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}, and his Epic

entries.name: Resistance.
entries: You also know this eldritch entity is beyond life and death and can reform years later if killed.

entries.name: (25+) Killing Aura.
entries: You know of his Mortal Coil aura, and his spellcasting Epic Actions.

entries.name: (30+) Powerful Presence.
entries: You know his highest and lowest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: He Who Laughs Last approaches battle lazily, as his mere presence causes mortals to die in short order from his Mortal Coil aura. Nevertheless, he casually ends lives using Sleep No More, Dusty Death, and Out Brief Candle, trapping another foe in a Cage of Sorrows so they must bear witness to the death around them before they expire to his Mortal Coil.

He Who Laughs Last does not fear his own destruction, confident that he will reappear if his corporeal form is destroyed. He is certain of his fate to watch the end of the universe, and even when slain his echoing laughter remains as a grim reminder of his power.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Fiend.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Monster Blood.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Heart, Eyes.

entries.name: Bones:
entries: Skull, Spine, Ribs.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Teeth, Claws.

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Skin, Wing Membranes.

name: Hedge Bard
entries: Recognized for being excellent diplomats and mediators, hedges are less well known for their love of music. Those who turn their natural charm towards the talent of entertaining can find great success. Some of the most gifted performers are blessed with magical talents. While most hedges use these powers for good, others choose a more sinister path, using their bardic talents to cheat, dupe, or steal from common folk.

Not every graduate of the Amethyst Academy remains a part of the institution. A few depart to find their own way in life, quietly using their magical talents pursuing their own interests. So long as they keep the edicts and laws, they may practice magic undisturbed.

name: Hedge Witch
entries: Many who apply to study at the Avium are turned away by the prestigious institution. Spurred by their desire for knowledge, rejected candidates sometimes start on a path to become self-taught masters of arcana. Notably in tune with the magic of the forest, hedges pursuing an individualistic path often leverage their connection to these natural forces to make pacts with powerful fey or elemental beings, learning secrets inaccessible to traditional students.

Hedy is a venerable mistral raptor who takes pride in her career in the Perch Guard. She is calm, composed, and unbending in her principles. Although she is still disciplined, the sternness of her youth has been long since eroded by time and good-humored company, and she spends her off-hours at the Rose Hip teahouse, catching up with her old friend Christophe and enjoying hid delicious tea.

name: Hekja No-Curl
entries: Lanky sailor with a surprising bald head. Yellow eyes and lupine features. Always scowling. Hide armor. Handaxe and seax dagger on her belt.
{@b Found Initially In:} Ogre's Run. Also appears in The Redspear Trail.
{@b Background:} First mate on Sly Raven; later second in command of the longship Stokkvari.
{@b Personality Traits:} Grim and brooding, dark sense of humor.
{@b Bonds:} Owes a life-bond to Kosktup for saving her life.
{@b Flaws:} She is a descriptive pessimist, providing "helpful" worst-case-possibilities.
{@b Wants:} To save her captain and support him in his crazy adventures.

name: Helpful Hand

entries: Skittering out from the shadows is a grotesque parody of a hand, desiccated and skeletal, its bony fingers clicking against the floor. The creature moves with an unsettling agility, crawling up walls and across ceilings with ease. As you watch, its sharp, talon-like digits flex and twitch, ready to jab or latch onto its next victim.

Every apothecary could use an extra set of hands. Overstretched apothecaries use Helping Hands in a variety of ways: fetching tools and ingredients, taking notes, sending messages, holding open ribcages, and assigning them to suturing or administering concoctions to a patient.

entries.name: Player Character Familiars
entries: Subject to GM approval, an apothecary with the Laboratory Assistant esoteric theory can create a Helpful Hand or Speaking Skull to serve them using the {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} spell. A familiar created in this manner always acts in combat immediately after its creator's turn. It can use its special attacks in its stat block only if the apothecary uses a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on their turn to command the familiar to take one of those actions.

name: Hemonculus

entries: {@i Sanguine Servitor (Fresh blood and gem dust)}

Hemonculus are servitors created by a blood magic ritual that binds a fiendish spirit into a blood-formed body. For the cost of a small sacrifice in blood (the creator's own or otherwise), the creatures serve as spies and assist in procuring further blood for magical use.

name: Hennrik
entries: Kosktup's first mate

name: Henrika Langerkvist
entries: Headwoman of Hvalfell
{@i The giant has bruised, purple skin and wart-like blood blisters that deform its features. It wears cowled robes, and its staff is ebony and mithral embedded with precious stones.}
As powerful sorcerers and blood mages, heralds of blood are without peer. They enjoy enslaving ogres and giants whenever possible, though they make do with lesser slaves when they must.

entries.name: Dark Prophets
entries: Their stirring speeches proclaim that the end times are fast approaching and that all must prepare for a bloody reckoning. Their charismatic preaching serves various elder earthly gods, who demand blood sacrifices, and dark druid orders devoted to hunting and murdering innocents. They have the power to grant strength, lust, and vitality—or to wither those who cross them.

entries.name: Blood Magic Vortexes
entries: Beneath their giant-like veneer, heralds of blood are swirling vortexes of blood, bone, and raw magical power. They feed on ley line magic and the black blood of the earth as much as on flesh and blood.

name: Herald of Calamity
entries: The tragic individuals who become Heralds of Calamity were afflicted by the Fates themselves, or so the story goes. As recipients of a {@spell Curse of Ill-Fated Fortune|GrimHollowPG24}, Heralds of Calamity bring tragedy upon all who linger in their presence.

Legends say these foul beings hunt unseen, lurking near vital locations such as a village well, bridge, or other communal site where they can inflict many casualties before survivors think to abandon the place.

When seen, Heralds of Calamity appear as incorporeal skeletal figures, though they are invisible except under the light of the moon. Unlike other curse monsters, Heralds of Calamity are not physically formidable, nor do they wield tremendous arcane power.

Many monster hunters, however, have fallen believing that a Herald of Calamity would be an easy challenge. Expert archers have misfired, fatally wounding companions. Seasoned adventurers have slipped on trivial obstacles and received debilitating injuries.
Regardless of the circumstance, all who have engaged a Herald of Calamity have the same advice: Rely on the maxim that if something can possibly go wrong, it will.
{@i A tall and beautiful fiend, this creature resembles a dark-haired fey wearing a cloak and armor glittering with dark light.}
Heralds of darkness speak in fluid tones and sing with the voices of angels, but their hearts are foul and treacherous.

entries.name: Vision of Evil
entries: Heralds of darkness can take on another appearance entirely, disappearing into insubstantial shadows and unveiling an evil majestic form that leaves those who see it shaken and weak—and often blind. Speaking of this form is difficult, but poets and bards trying to describe it have said it resembles an apocalyptic horror built of chained souls and the slow death of innocents carried along in a glacial river, rushing to an inevitable doom.

entries.name: Sword and Cloak
entries: The black sword and star-scattered cloak of a herald of darkness are part of its magical substance and cannot be parted from it. Some believe the cloak and blade are true visions of its body, and that the smiling face and pleasing form are entirely illusory.

entries.name: Corruptors of the Fey
entries: Heralds of darkness are companions and sometimes masters to the shadow fey. They seek to draw many others into their orbit with wild promises of great power, debauchery, and other delights. They are rivals to the heralds of blood and bitter foes to all angels of light.

name: Herald of Fools

entries: {@i Leader of Fiendish Revels}

Heralds of fools lead troupes of fiendish revelers in service to the enigmatic Lord of Fools, a clown or jester entity who is a curious mix of levity and cruelty (though always with a sense of irony). The heralds are agile and graceful, every movement a dance, spinning their banner poles in intricate displays that can swiftly turn from entertainment to death.

entries.name: Secret
entries: Heralds of fools are wonderful dancers, and they must never stop dancing, or they quickly perish.

name: Hexahedrooze
entries: When Dr. Stein left his lab at short notice (following a pitchfork-wielding-mob related event), he left an entire pool of his patent-pending Mut-x exposed to the elements. Things fell into it; those things had brains, and those brains, their memories, and the sum of their intelligence fused with gelatinous cubes into biomantic polyhedroozes.

entries.name: Empathetic
entries: When a biomantic polyhedrooze forms, it begins absorbing the latent psychic energy of its environs. Creatures with strong psyches that are nearby in either space or time influence the nascent sentience of the polyhedrooze. A long-destroyed lich might impart its madness and hate into the ooze, whilst a colony of highly-charismatic mice might lend the goopey mass a penchant for cheese.

entries.name: Reactive Mutations
entries: The true feat of Dr Stein's research, and a trait that the polyhedroozes embody, is that of extreme biomantic reaction to environmental stimuli. A polyhedrooze that takes damage immediately adapts its morphology to prevent further damage of that type. The larger the polyhedrooze, the more such adaptations it can sustain at any one time.

entries.name: Size Matters
entries: Bigger polyhedroozes have absorbed more brains and, so, are more clever. A polyhedrooze that reaches a critical mass might decide to split into two, with the idea of sending one of its halves in search of pastures new. Unfortunately, the decrease in intelligence that results from a split means that polyhedroozes can get confused and end up in a cycle of splitting and reforming over and over.

items.name: High Flamekeeper Ophelia Reed

entries: A stout woman in her late forties with rich brown skin stands invitingly before you. Her warm smile is framed by rounded features and braided hair. She wears the flowing gold and white robes of a Flamekeeper of the Sacred Flame. She carries a silvered staff and a censer with a {@spell Continual Flame|XPHB} spell cast upon it.

Ophelia Reed is one of the most renowned Flamekeepers in the Silver Order. She has been granted charge overseeing the efforts in Drakkenheim to ensure the Sacred Flame is represented, and the goals of the church and Divine Matriarch are kept during such trying times.

entries.name: Personality Traits
entries: I attentively listen to others and respond from a place of warmth and kindness.

entries.name: Ideal
entries: I will always seek the right remedy for any ailment or problem, offering my patient guidance to those who ask for it.

entries.name: Bond
entries: I have taken a vow of poverty and devoted my life to the service of the Sacred Flame.

entries.name: Flaw
entries: Darkness is all-consuming once it has taken root. For some, death is the only salvation.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Ophelia is a powerful divine figure and is often accompanied by many Silver Order paladins and cavaliers. In combat she often defaults to buffing her allies more so than attacking directly, but will use her spiritual weapon liberally against foes who threaten her. If she can end an encounter using {@spell Banishment|XPHB} or {@spell Dispel Magic|XPHB}, she will opt for that. Otherwise she relies on {@spell Bless|XPHB}, {@spell Guidance|XPHB}, and {@spell Healing Word|XPHB} to keep her allies in the fight.
She will flee if her paladin knights demand her to, or if most of them have been slain or she is left alone in a threatening situation.

entries.name: {@book Watchers of the Faithful|GrimHollowCG24|13|Watchers of the Faithful}

entries: Though the gods no longer grace the heavens, the Arch Seraphs still guide the way.

Born in the fires of the Gods' End, the Watchers of the Faithful rose to prominence first in Castinella as part of its theocratic government. Priests, paladins, chaplains, and other clergy rallied to the remaining Arch Seraphs to hold the fabric of society together. Throwing their faith behind the Arch Seraphs, the major churches reformed into a large organization dedicated to preserving the old faiths in a new form.

This young faction is utterly devoted to Sagrado Valieda's Eternal Dogma: revere the Arch Seraphs, follow their laws as handed down by the Divine Speaker, and destroy all that is unholy and evil in their sight through any means necessary. Where the Arcanist Inquisition is militant in rooting out corruption, the Watchers instead pursue Valieda's mandate to fight for the Arch Seraphs with fiery words. Swords are well and good in defense of the faith, but the real battle is in the hearts and minds of the faithful.

Through preaching and persuasion, the Watchers seek to make the change in the world that they believe the Arch Seraphs desire. Edicts declaring heresy inflame the Inquisition to hunt for monsters or tainted spellcasters. A public proclamation that a government is straying from the true path causes citizens to rise up and force change. Decrees are issued creating new ecclesiastical rules that the faithful embrace over secular laws issued by less religious rulers. Slowly but surely, the Watchers guide the world to a better place.

entries.name: Agents
entries: The Watchers of the Faithful are not soldiers. While they may have some have martial training, their members are priests, spies, and evangelists. Watchers fight with words and not blades. They spur faithful populations to turn against those they deem heretical. They are not single heroes, but rather the voice behind the zealous mob. The most common missionaries are Watchful Priests who combine divine spells with an almost magical command of oratory to enflame crowds.

name: Highland Wolf
entries: Large packs of wolves hunt across the highlands, rarely choosing to interact with humans. When food becomes scarce or when travelers become separated from their groups, these thickly furred canines become a deadly threat.
More dangerous than a common brigand, a Highway Robber is used to a life in the Wild, and has learned how to deal with armed victims.

entries.name: Ruffians
entries: Local robbers, cut-throats, brigands and other assorted criminals fall within this category of potential adversaries. Such foes can be encountered on the lonely roads of Eriador, but they are met as likely in a dark alley in Bree.{@i "Where d'you think you're going?" said one, the largest and most evil-looking of the crew}.

entries.name: Evil Men
entries: Cruel individuals like brigands, marauders and slavers prowling the Lone-lands of Middle-earth fall within this category. Their malicious will notwithstanding, Evil Men are not servitors of Sauron, and they can end up opposing the Player- heroes for reasons not dependent on an allegiance with the Dark Lord.

name: Hilda Brom
entries: While farms throughout the hollow feed the people, hunting for wild game is invaluable—and profitable—for times when crops fail. Hilda Brom is renowned as one of the most skilled hunters and trappers. She seems wild and unsocial to people she first meets, but her personality shines for those she knows and trusts. If a criminal escapes justice, the mayor and constable call upon her to hunt a different caliber of prey.

Hilda is a Follower of the Old Ways, finding special kinship with and reverence for the Green Queen. She has seen too much in the grim and sometimes haunted wilds to ignore the grasp of the spirit world on the land. If the characters ever get into trouble elsewhere in Wickermoor Hollow, Hilda might show up to lend a hand.

name: Hill Dragon
entries: Hill dragons are notoriously aggressive and territorial—Which paired with their long hunting treks throughout the Gale Fields, has earned them a "flee on sight" command by the Courier brigade. They often accumulate a layer of sod, dirt, and debris on their backs, which bonds with their clay-like bodies. This hallmark grassy coat of the hill dragon is not just an outcome of their life sleeping in the fields but also perfect ambush camouflage when hunting the fast and elusive Sheep Dragon.

entries.name: Eggs
entries: Looking like pumpkin-sized acorns, hill dragon eggs can remain dormant in the ground for a year or more before they hatch. Hill dragon eggs are usually buried out of sight, but certain flowers like to grow around burial pits giving their positions away, and egg-hunting hogs can be trained to sniff them out.
Not known for powerful maternal instincts, hill dragons lay their eggs in clutches all across the plains, dales, and rolling hills of Obojima.
{@i A pile of gold, jewelry, and weapons rises on its own like a tidal wave of riches, with a cold and determined face.}

entries.name: Dragon Fears Made Real
entries: Hoard golems were born from the paranoia of dragons. Despite their great physical and intellectual power, dragons are always suspicious of any creature willing to work for them. The first hoard golem was created when a dragon realized that there could be no guardian more trustworthy with its hoard than the hoard itself. Since then, the secret of hoard golem construction has emerged, and rich nobles have followed suit, enchanting their wealth to defend itself from thieves.

entries.name: Patient Homebodies
entries: As constructs, hoard golems are mindless, lying in wait for anyone other than their creator to come within striking distance. In the case of evil dragons, this may include the wyrmlings of dragon parents looking to establish dominance in the family. Hoard golems fight to the death, but they rarely leave the rooms they inhabit for fear that clever treasure hunters might trick the hoard into walking itself right out of the owner's den.

entries.name: Silent and Wealthy
entries: Hoard golems cannot speak. A hoard golem is 25 feet tall and weighs 20,000 pounds. A hoard golem's body is composed of items—copper, silver, gold, works of art, armor, weapons, and magical items—worth at least 5,000 gp

name: Hofgir
entries: Guard of the gatehouse tower

name: Holly Aster
entries: Holly Aster spends most of her time in the kitchen, either preparing the ingredients for the night's baking or fussing by the ovens. Her ruddy complexion is exacerbated by the heat of the ovens, and her straight pale hair is held back with pins while she works.

Holly comes from a long line of bakers living in Wickermoor Hollow, with her mother and her grandmother both filling the role of the bread-maker for the town. Both her mother and her grandmother died on their 35th birthdays of unknown causes, and Holly is just weeks away from hitting that milestone.

Holly is a dedicated Follower of the Old Ways, and she shares a curse with her mother and grandmother: she and her progeny are doomed to die on their 35th birthdays until the Crooked Queen returns. Holly knows this, and she has a terrible dilemma: join the cult of the Crooked Queen and help usher in the return of Kehlenn or die. How she chooses to act on that is left up to you.

items.name: Hooded Lantern Apothecary

entries: Hooded Lantern Apothecaries are the Lanterns' field medics. Called Apothecaries, they are distinct from other Hooded Lanterns, often wearing a white tunic with a simple green Hooded Lanterns insignia. They have a leather hood and typically carry a large doctor bag and a bandelier of vials for various ailments or poisons. They carry several medical instruments on their belt.

Apothecaries are trained field medics who support the Hooded Lanterns in battle with helping their wounded stay in the fight, and saving severely injured soldiers, pulling them to safety or administering emergency procedures in the midst of battle. Although an apothecary will rarely move beyond the Support Regiments, they are some of the most renowned and respected Hooded Lanterns. Every field medic has the stories of many Lanterns who would have been dead if it wasn't for their bravery in the face of the horrors of Drakkenheim.
Having an apothecary around can help if you've had a bad day. Of course, a good sword can prevent a bad day from ever happening.

items.name: Hooded Lantern Scout

entries: This lightly-armored urban scout is armed with a grapple gun, flare gun, shortsword, and longbow. They wear tight and simple garb to help them with mobility, with patches of boiled leather to protect critical areas. A simple green cloak and hood signify their allegiance to the Lanterns.

The forward patrols of the Watch Regiment, scouts are members of the Hooded Lanterns who are not yet ready for the intense field work of the Vanguard, but have proven themselves capable of navigating the ruins and remaining hidden in the streets. They operate as the eyes and ears of the Hooded Lanterns, keeping reports on the monster groups moving through the city. Not only will scouts be on constant patrols within a few blocks of secured Hooded Lantern bases, but also often move ahead of Vanguard Regiments to report any problems ahead of important missions. Scouts use their flare guns to signal issues ahead, calling in the more heavily armed Vanguard to deal with the issue.
Very reliable are the scouts of the Hooded Lanterns however with great eyes come weak abdomens.

items.name: Hooded Lantern Trapper

entries: This Hooded Lantern field agent wears a green tunic emblazoned with the symbol of the Hooded Lanterns, and a belt heavy with hanging tools, satchels of powders, and vials of liquids. Their large backpack is loaded with rope, animal traps, containers, small wooden kegs and boxes, and all sorts of gear for building and setting traps in the field. The Trapper wears thick leather boots and gloves, heavy worker goggles, and a dirt smeared face with wild hair.

The Hooded Lantern Trapper is one of the field operatives of the Support Regiment. Their job is twofold: they are both a hunter who keeps the Lanterns fed with fresh meats, berries, and foraged goods from the woods outside of Drakkenheim, as well as lays traps and ambushes for special operations inside the city walls. Trappers are well equipped with various tools and alchemical ingredients for building advanced traps for dismantling groups of monsters and helping give the Vanguard Regiments the advantage.
The Hooded Lanterns traps can be as deadly to monsters as I am, but I require less preparation.

items.name: Hooded Lantern Veteran

entries: These Hooded Lanterns are garbed in dark and rustic armor whose colors match and blend with the city ruins of Drakkenheim. They wear cloaks of deep green and carry well-made precision longbows. They wear masks that cover their nose and mouths to limit the sound of their breathing, and are equipped with grapple guns to scale walls quickly.

Rooftop snipers are members of the Vanguard Regiment and are exceptionally skilled at pinpoint accuracy with bows. They tend to stick to high vantage points and are a key part of any Hooded Lantern ambush. Rooftop snipers often travel in a group and will locate their enemies, find multiple vantage points to surround them, and wait for the opportune moment to strike. Often accompanied by scouts and other ground forces, one may suspect they know the number of Hooded Lanterns they are facing, and rarely account for the unseen snipers above them.
I've never had a bad day in Drakkenheim, except the first day, and maybe one more.

entries.name: Hooded Lanterns
entries: The Hooded Lanterns are an irregular military force drawn from remnants of the old Drakkenheim City

Watch and veterans of the Westemär Civil War, led by the grim Lord Commander Elias Drexel. They wish to drive out the monsters and outlaws who infest their nation's capital, find an heir to the throne, and restore the realm of Westemär.

The Hooded Lanterns are divided into three regiments which occupy the city and the areas surrounding it. New recruits joining the Lanterns are often first put into the Support Regiment. They make up the chefs, apothecaries, scribes, and maintenance workers at every Hooded Lantern fortification. Many of those positions are held by folk who will never move beyond the Support Regiment, and their job is valuable to the foundations of the Hooded Lanterns.

The Watch Regiment defend the walls and gates of any Lantern-controlled location. Oftentimes, if the Vanguards manage to gain a new foothold in the city, a group of Hooded Lanterns Watch are sent to hold the new position and ensure it remains in the Hooded Lanterns' hands. They also often operate as scouts in the field. Not specifically aiming for tactical engagement or large-scale battles, but they are the eyes and ears of the Lanterns throughout the city and occasionally clean up wandering monsters from the streets near their bases.

The Vanguard Regiment are the front line of the Hooded Lanterns. They are skilled combatants, who know their way around the ruins of the city and can find vantage points, plan ambushes, secure positions, and dispose of monster dens and other enemies. Vanguards are often soldiers who have proven themselves as reliable and talented Watch or Support Regiment and aim to prove themselves further in the city.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Hooded Lanterns rarely go into a fight without a plan. They set up ambushes, tailoring an encounter to put them at an advantage. They know their territory and can navigate the ruins of the city with relative ease compared to most adventurers who journey into Drakkenheim. They travel in well-equipped groups, and often carry tools to alert other nearby scouting parties if they need help.

The Hooded Lanterns are skilled archers. They often occupy rooftops and ruined towers. If they expect combat to occur, they position soldiers with bows in any nearby vantage points with a clear view of their allies down on the streets. They place scouts in ruined buildings to keep eyes on the streets and run for aid if a combat breaks out. The Lanterns lay traps and ambushes before their enemies have entered the area. Hooded Lanterns are often incredibly prepared and use the ruins as camouflage for their attack.
{@i Resembling a cave cricket the size of a dog, this beast's black, chitinous thorax is topped by a translucent digestive sac. Half-digested eyeballs of various sizes and colors float in the sac.}

entries.name: Leaping Claws
entries: Insectoid killing machines with a penchant for consuming their victim's eyes, the bloodthirsty horakhs travel in small packs and make lightning-fast attacks against the weak or vulnerable. Their powerful rear legs enable enormous bounding leaps, while the sharp hooks at the end of their powerful claws help them to climb and latch onto prey. Heads dominated by scooped mandibles can shoot forward like pistons, shearing meat from bone.

entries.name: Leaping Screech
entries: When attacking, a horakh leaps from its hiding spots while making a deafening screech. Horakhs are highly mobile on the battlefield. If threatened, horakhs return to the shadows to attack from a more advantageous position.

entries.name: Herd the Blinded
entries: After blinding their prey, horakhs often herd the blind like sheep until they are ready to consume their prey and sometimes even use the blinded prey as bait to capture other creatures. Many an explorer has been ambushed, blinded, and condemned to death in the bowels of the earth by these predators.

An imposing pronghorn cervan, Horns is {@creature Elora Quickwit|HumblewoodTales|Elora Quickwit's} bouncer and her personal guard at Moss Hall. He is an avid tea drinker and always has a cup ready while he works.

entries.name: The Dreamers
entries: Found exclusively in dreamscapes, dreamers are the psyches of sentient creatures blocked from re-entering their corporeal form. The longer a psyche spends in a dreamholder's twisted realm, the more corrupted it becomes, losing the virtues, values, and empathy it once held dear.

entries.name: Damage
entries: The mind is a magnificent thing, capable of adapting to new realities, and parsing the stimuli in the best way it knows how. This, however, is the dreamers' weakness; while a blade doesn't technically exist in a dreamscape, the mind interprets the damage the blade should cause, creating internal psychic trauma in the host's corporeal body.

entries.name: Horror
entries: A sleepwalker becomes a horror when its mind is finally broken. In constant fear, a horror attacks with unprovoked ferocity. It does not trust kind words, for the dreamholder has tricked it too many times. Only creatures in possession of truly powerful restorative magic can bring back some semblance of sanity to these psyches. Even then, should the mind be restored to its body, it would likely not be recognisable.
If you see fast movement in the trees, run. It might not be enough, but it could be all you can do.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The reaction of most folks who have encountered a horror flit is, "Burn it with fire!" But a handful of naturalists seek out these creatures for a variety of purposes, paying handsomely for samples. Bounties for these creatures in urban areas range from 10 to 100 gp.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
items.entry: A horror flit has no eyes, but they sense their prey by means of vibrations in the air or in the water. They breed by infesting the flesh of their prey.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
items.entry: The largest of these creatures, called "breeders" by most, can spit out swarms of their young, especially when the breeder instinctively feels it might die. The creature normally reproduces more slowly, vomiting a new swarm every few days.

name: Hospital Horror

entries: {@i Mutated Experiment}

Hospital horrors were once people, but now they are repulsive mockeries created through surgical  and magical alteration. They have no memory of  their past lives, existing only within a chemically induced rage. Often, they are conditioned by the use of specific command phrases that allow them  to be controlled.

entries.name: Secret
entries: Hospital horrors have spent much of their existence being prodded with needles, so being pierced frays what few wits they retain.

Chosen for its ferocity and malicious intelligence, a Hound of Sauron is a minion of the Dark Lord, a servant sent on a precise errand, be it the gathering of forces for a coming war, the hunt for a specific individual, or spying on an area. Hidden behind the shape of an ordinary Warg, a Hound of Sauron conceals much greater powers.

entries.name: Werewolves
entries: It is suspected by the most learned among the Wise that the cruellest packs of Wargs might be led by the foulest of creatures: trusted servants of the Dark Lord returned from the Ancient World to serve him once again. Devouring spirits trapped in wolf-form, they hate the very soil they walk upon, and desire only to defile and ruin in an attempt to quench the dreadful hunger that consumes their mortal bodies.{@i "Listen, Hound of Sauron!" he cried. "Gandalf is here. Fly, if you value your foul skin! I will shrivel you from tail to snout, if you come within this ring."}

entries.name: Wolves of the Wild
entries: By the time of Bilbo's adventures, Wargs and Werewolves could be encountered at night in the eastern vales close to the Misty Mountains, where they prowl in search of prey. Years later, packs of Wolves have crossed the Hithaeglir, and can be found across Eriador.
All Wolves share a prodigious agility that prevents their enemies from keeping a distance in combat.
{@i This enormous black hound pants in the moonlight, wisps of steam rising from its muzzle, as it follows its elvish master.}

entries.name: Fey Bloodhounds
entries: Hounds of the night are bred by the shadow fey for use as hunting companions and guardians, and they excel at both tasks. Far more intelligent than other hounds, they are difficult to evade once they are on a quarry's trail, because they can think their way past problems that would throw their lesser kin off the trail. Their shadow fey masters claim that hounds of the night can smell a shadow on running water and can sniff out a ghost passing through a wall.

entries.name: Cousins to Winter
entries: Somewhere in their early existence as a breed, some enterprising hunter interbred them with winter wolves. Every trace of their white fur is long gone, but the cold breath of those dread canines remains.

entries.name: Dimensional Stepping
entries: Hounds of night excel at distracting prey while some of their pack teleport away to achieve some larger goal, such as dragging off a treasure or overwhelming a spellcaster in the back ranks.

name: Houndmaster Jaeger
entries: Sigmund Jaeger served Father Renathyr as a squire during Renathyr's time as a knight, raising hunting dogs to track down men and monsters alike.

When the knight founded the Crimson Faith, Jaeger was the first Renathyr sought and the first to convert. The houndmaster had a loving family once, but—like Renathyr—he abandoned them, tempted by the promises of the Crimson Rose. He took only his hounds with him, which he turned into batlike hybrids using blood magic. Now a prior of the Crimson Monastery, Jaeger rears and trains the {@creature Bat Hound|CrookedMoon24|Bat Hounds} and {@creature Warhorse|XMM|Warhorses} used to track down the faithless.
When the clock stops, your time has run out.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: When the sand from the widow's hourglass is mixed with wine, it creates an elixir that when consumed prevents the creature from aging for {@dice 2d6 + 10} years. There is enough sand in the hourglass to create an elixir for two creatures. A creature cannot benefit from the sand of an hourglass widow more than once. The sand can be sold for 5,000 gp.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
items.entry: Hourglass widows are undead who can control time to act more than once a round.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
items.entry: Hourglass widows are resistant to cold, force, lightning, and necrotic. They are immune to poison and nonmagical attacks.

items.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
items.entry: Inexplicably, an hourglass widow can affect those trapped in a time stop, imprisonment, or other stasis effect.

name: House of Horror

entries: {@i Cursed House Brought to Malevolent Life}

Houses of horror are living houses, often angry or bitter due to the circumstances of their awakening. They were once mundane buildings or dwellings where powerful magics of life and death took place and infused the stones and timber.

Houses of horror jealously covet the true life that its former inhabitants enjoyed, or they carry echoes of the suffering that bodies and souls experienced within them. The houses vent this fury on any who enter, tormenting and terrifying trespassers. The souls of those who die inside are trapped, waiting to be unleashed upon future victims.

entries.name: Secret
entries: While not haunted houses in the traditional sense, houses of horror can have their consciousness quelled by the same exorcism or purification rituals that put unquiet spirits to rest or drive out possessing spirits.

name: Howie Butterman
entries: Howie Butterman is short and wiry, and his brown hair sticks out from his uniform cap. While he doesn't look imposing, he is quick and deadly in a fight.

Deputy Howie presents himself as the more affable of the law-enforcement duo. His friendly demeanor and helpful attitude make him more suitable than the constable at dealing with the public. He plays "good cop" to {@creature Doris Squire|CrookedMoon24|Constable Doris's} "bad cop" when dealing with lawbreakers.

In reality, Deputy Howie is a fervent cult member who works behind the scenes to bring about the return of the Crooked Queen. He uses his position of authority to move events very subtly toward her return. The arrival of {@creature Phillip Druskenvald|CrookedMoon24|Phillip} and {@creature Adela Druskenvald|CrookedMoon24|Adela} triggers him and the other servants of the Crooked Queen to put their plans into action (see chapter 8).

name: Howler Yipper
entries: Howlers are monsters, and if there's one thing in all of Obojima that gives villagers the most grief and worry, it's howlers. They're responsible for more raids on farmhouses, stolen livestock, and pillaged wagons than any other creature on Obojima.

Howlers are fairly large, hyena-like humanoids that live in endlessly squabbling packs led by the most crafty or the most combative among them. Most of the howler population live in burrows and dens throughout the Gale Fields, but there are small gangs that live in the wildernesses all across Obojima.

entries.name: Howler Worldview
entries: Howlers generally see the rest of the world as resources to be taken or a toy to be played with. They have little empathy, which is why they don't see an issue with taking something they want, even if that means robbing and stealing to get it. Their main desires are food, territory, and trophies to impress their pack and their leader, known as "snarlers". Howlers sleep when their snarler does, and even then it's only for a few hours a day, so they are almost always active in seeking whatever will get them more favor and status within the group.
A howler clan can be a mix of scheming, toadying, raucous, and indifferent, with brief bursts of showboating from their snarler to establish dominance.

entries.name: Rogue Howler
entries: Not every howler belongs to a pack, and these "rogue" howlers are among the most aggressive and dangerous and are often the ones that cause concern among villages.

entries.name: Public Enemy
entries: Most Obojimans know of howlers and it is one of the reasons why villagers take at least some instruction from the sword schools or resident fighters so that they can defend their crops, livestock, and merchandise. Despite the warnings, there are always those who believe howlers are misunderstood and just need a hug, but more often than not, they come back from their missions of mercy missing teeth or not at all.

entries.name: Howler Yipper
entries: Howler Yippers are the bottom of the pecking order in a howler pack making them both craven and surly. Yippers spend their limited brain power bullying, stealing, and generally messing around. Most yippers work hard to curry favor with their superiors by bringing offerings and heaps of flattery, but it is in their nature to do acts of mischief and destruction, so they inevitably incur wrath and punishment from their elders.

entries.name: Howler Snarlers
entries: Howler Snarlers are often the leaders of howler packs due to their great strength and keen intellect but they are also the ones most susceptible to flattery and greed. A snarler's day is spent showing the clan just how much of a snarler they are—bossing other howlers around, making big barking sounds, and leading raids to get food and loot.
A snarler's life is usually short, often ending in betrayal at the hands of the next snarler or failure of a grandiose stunt.

entries.name: Howler Stalkers
entries: Although howlers are pack monsters, some howlers shy away from the clan, preferring to lurk in the scrublands or in the darkness where they can move unseen and more easily ambush prey. These howler stalkers are the ones that you don't hear barking a mile away and that you don't see coming. While the pack as a whole can take down large game once every several outings, the stalkers may not take down a massive beast, but they never return empty-handed.

Snarlers and stalkers have a tenuous relationship within howler clans, and it's often a threat for snarlers to have more than a handful of stalkers in a pack as snarlers always like to know where their enemies are coming from.

{@i The giant stands braced in the midst of powerful wind. With a baleful stare, he shakes his fist and bellows a war cry. The cry becomes an avian shriek, and the giant's form melts into that of a massive bird whose wings blot out the sky}.
A giant with divine blood in his veins, Hraesvelgr the Corpse Swallower is powerfully muscled. His skin is a pale bronze, his eyes are violet, and his hair is the color of storm clouds.

entries.name: Roc Form
entries: When he takes his alternate form, Hraesvelgr becomes a tremendous roc, with massive wings that stir the wind across the sky. His eyes remain the same violet and these roc-form feathers match the color of his hair, sparkling with specks of color here and there, like jewels set in steel.

entries.name: Birth of the Wind
entries: Hraesvelgr dwells on the fringe of the world itself. From atop the peak of his home, he creates the wind and sends it across the globe. As befits a creature of such primal power, Hraesvelgr doesn't take kindly to intruders. He gluts himself on the bodies of fools who test his might in search of the fabled riches in his home.

entries.name: Hraesvelgr's Lair
entries: Hraesvelgr's lair is a windswept crag of gray stone at the edge of the world. At the highest pinnacle rests a massive cottage hewn from the mountainside. A great nest made from the splintered trunks of immense trees rests on the flat roof of the cottage, and the wind constantly howls.
The magic our wizard used just bounced off the gigantic creature, and as our fighter slashed at it with her sword, the creature's blood spawned even more monsters.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: A central spike growing from the hraptnon can be fashioned into a spear or lance by a proficient weaponsmith succeeding on a {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check. This takes 10 days of work and 1000 gp of components. The spear or lance acts as a+3 weapon that does an additional 7 ({@dice 2d6}) force damage on a successful hit. This magical weapon can affect the hraptnon, unlike other magical weapons.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
items.entry: The hraptnon lives in the Stillborn Forest, and it has never been seen outside of the forest bounds.

items.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
items.entry: No magical spells or weapons can hurt the hraptnon, and its blood can spawn creatures known as xakalonus.

items.name: {@dc 25} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
items.entry: The hraptnon cannot be permanently killed unless its heart, which rests in a magical pool in a grove at the center of the Stillborn Forest, is found and destroyed. This heart, known as the Stillborn Heart, could be sold to a sage for a large sum of gold.

entries.name: GM Advice
entries: The hraptnon is a great example of a "puzzle monster," a beast that cannot be defeated until its secrets are revealed. Puzzle monsters can be a great deal of fun, especially to challenge extremely powerful parties. Just when the players think they've scored a potentially easy victory, they find that the threat remains.

The key to maximizing the impact of puzzle monsters like the hraptnon is to make sure not to reveal too much information too soon. Make the characters puzzle out the reality behind the monster, using resources and taking time to do so. When they are finally able to fully defeat the creature, their victory will be all the sweeter.

name: Hrefna
entries: Ambitious cultist leader

name: Hugo
entries: Hugo is Matron Lethica's ward, bodyguard, and the ultimate proof of her alchemical ambitions. Born of a cursed fomorian bloodline, Hugo's immense strength was overwhelmed by debilitating pain and horrific visions so severe that they harmed those around him and threatened to end his own life. His suffering drove him to Lethica during the earliest days of the hospital, where she promised comfort and relief through her alchemy. She kept her word—quieting the agony of his curse—but at the cost of turning him into a mutated servant entirely dependent on her.

{@i This gray-skinned dog-like creature seems pathetically eager to please but fantastically skittish, its ears alerting at every nearby sound, and its large oval eyes following anything that passes by.}

entries.name: Emotional Giant
entries: A hulking whelp is a tightly wound ball of emotion, extremely defensive of its personal space and terrified of the world around it. When it feels its personal space is violated, or its fragile concentration is broken, the small, quivery fey grows into a muscled beast of giant proportions.

entries.name: Calm Friend
entries: When its emotions are under control, a hulking whelp is friendly and even helpful, although this has more to do with its guilt over past actions than a true desire to help others. In its calm form, a hulking whelp is just over three feet tall at the shoulder and weighs 50 pounds. Unleashed, it is 20 feet tall and 4,000 pounds.

name: Humongous Fungus Troll

entries: Fungus Trolls are most prominently found in the Trogrowth Forest of Caspia but are also known to inhabit prominent wetlands and swamps within the continent. They are one of the most problematic troll groups known in the world. Their ability to produce new trolls en masse is staggering. Not only do the hags who tend to fungal gardens create hundreds of them at a time, but the Fungus Trolls can grow to such massive sizes, that their lumbering presence shakes the very trees of the swamps they inhabit. These massive fungal monstrosities rain down spores that grow into {@creature Fungal Trolling|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Fungal Trollings}. These networks of Fungus Trolls travel together. When you see one Humongous Fungus Troll barreling towards you, be warned that there are likely more following.

{@b {@i Swampland Protectors.}} Humongous Fungus Trolls stand as the guardians of their swamps. They do not cater to trespassers of any kind. Loyal to their Troll Hag mothers, they defend their fungal farms and wander the swamps spreading their spores as they go.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks to {@action Study|XPHB} a Humongous Fungus Troll, learning the following information based on the result:

entries.name: (5+) From Harsh Environments
entries: You know the troll's Spore Slam and Grasping Tendrils Actions.

entries.name: (10+) Hard to Kill
entries: You learn of the troll's Regeneration trait.

entries.name: (15+) Special Weakness
entries: You have insight into the troll's {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB|Vulnerabilities}.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Humongous Fungus Trolls remain motionless and observe trespassers to see if they are a threat. If combat is initiated, the Humongous Fungus Troll uses its Grasping Tendrils to pull victims towards it, then use its Entangling Mycelia to entangle as many creatures as possible within its Rotting Aura.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Giant.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Monster Blood.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Eyes, Heart, Guts, Flesh..

entries.name: Bones:
entries: Skull, Spine, Ribs.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Tentacles, Spores.

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Bark.

entries.name: Dust:
entries: Elemental  Dust.
The only time I ever felt like a pincushion. Incredible speed and furiosity, if they weren't a machine-corpse enemy I'd be impressed.

{@i A toothless mouth adorns the headless shoulders of this oversized, four-armed, doughy humanoid. Colors and half-formed phantasmal shapes appear and vanish around it, to the creature's obvious delight.}

entries.name: Creative Chaos
entries: Wise yet child-like creatures of chaos, hunduns are four-armed, headless humanoids that embody spontaneous creation and the confusion that precedes enlightenment. Taking delight in creation of all kinds, they bring change to the staid and stagnant, spin revelation from confusion, and inspire moments of great creation—from works of art to new nations and faiths, and even the formation of planets and planes.

entries.name: Nonsense Speech
entries: Although not mindless, hunduns rarely seem to act out of conscious thought; however, their actions seem wise and are usually benevolent. They communicate only in nonsense words but have no trouble communicating among themselves or acting in coordination with other celestials.

entries.name: Flesh of Creation
entries: Hundun blood is a powerful catalyst, and their spittle is a potent drug. Each hundun's heart is an Egg of Worlds—an artifact that can give birth to new concepts, powers, or even worlds. Obviously, the hundun must die for its heart to be used this way, but this is a sacrifice one might make willingly under the right circumstances.

name: Hunter Hulk

entries: A hunched and bloated form lurches out of the shadows. It has two massive tentacle arms that end in large talon-like hooks. The creature's head has two large octarine eyes, yet where a mouth should be there is only a fleshy surface. Instead, the creature has a massive snarling maw in its gut with jagged bone teeth and a large purple tongue. It squeals hungrily as its arms flail towards you, ready to pull you into its open mouth. But suddenly, it vanishes before your eyes, yet you can still hear its hungry squeals.

Hunter Hulks lurk the streets in a constant state of hunger. Unlike other dregs, these seek out prey to eat, yet their appetites never seem to falter. Even more horrifying is the way a Hunter Hulk has adapted to the hunt: they can turn Invisible using a natural camouflage that has mutated their skin. These stealthy Haze Hulks wait in the shadows for their prey to draw closer, only to pounce out and scoop them up for a snack.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Survival|XPHB} or {@skill Nature|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check to {@action Study|XPHB} a Hunter Hulk, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (10+) Stealthy Assassin
entries: You know of its Invisibility trait.

entries.name: (15+) Hooked Arms
entries: You learn of the Hulk's Lashing Tendrils attack and Reel {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: (20+) Strong and Tough
entries: You are aware of the Hulk's highest and lowest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Hunter Hulks hide in the ruins of Drakkenheim, often Invisible, attempting to get the drop on their prey. Once the Hulk's target is in a prime position, it lunges out and whips its arms around them, pulling in the unfortunate target. The Hunter Hulk then devours them with its Belly Maw. If the creature breaks free, or if the Hunter Hulk is being too heavily damaged, it turns Invisible again and slinks back into the shadows. However, the Hunter Hulk will not so easily give up on its prey, and it may stalk the target and their party for a time, looking for a better moment to strike again. Sometimes it launches another ambush almost immediately, other times it will stalk them for several hours.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Aberration.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Monster Blood, Contaminated Ichor.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Eyes, Heart, Brain, Guts, Flesh.

entries.name: Bones:
entries: Skull, Spine, Ribs.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Tentacles, Teeth.

entries.name: Hair:
entries: Hair.

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Skin.

entries.name: Dust:
entries: Aberrant Dust.

name: Hunting Horror

entries: And in the air about him were great viperine creatures, which had curiously distorted heads, and grotesquely great clawed appendages, supporting themselves with ease by the aid of black rubbery wings of singularly monstrous dimensions.
entries.from: August Derleth, The Lurker at the Threshold

entries: Hunting horrors serve Nyarlathotep's bidding across the cosmos, and even into the unknown outer realms. Cultists who venerate the Crawling Chaos sometimes contact these creatures, receiving dictates, omens, and secrets in the profane rituals dedicated to the Stalker Among the Stars.

entries.name: Relentless Pursuers
entries: As their name implies, these otherworldly terrors hunt. Spellcasters who bind them use them as assassins, bat-winged killers who hunt with inhuman intensity. Once a hunting horror is directed toward a target, the horror stalks its quarry until it's slain or the horror is destroyed. Their bite corrupts and necrotizes flesh from within in moments.

entries.name: Sinister Truths
entries: As servitors of Nyarlathotep, hunting horrors rarely share their motivations or goals. They are loyal only to their master and serve mortals only when it benefits the Crawling Chaos.

entries.name: Creatures of the Night
entries: Hunting horrors loathe bright light, especially sunlight. They are active only at night, and by day dwell within cavernous lairs.

name: Hyphan

entries: A helpful fungal friend, the hyphan's climbing ability makes it especially useful for dusting those hard-to-reach corners. It's also very good at stopping bar fights; it has a real calming presence. I just have to remember to put him in the basement when we want to really let loose and break some furniture.

Always keen to offer aid, hyphans make excellent support companions, both on the battlefield and emotionally. Able to calm intense emotions, charm aggressors, and disappear into the earth, they are experts in de-escalation and can aid a party's escape by lacing large areas with necrotising puffballs.
If any of the hyphan's traits or actions require a saving throw, it is always against the hyphan's save DC, as calculated below.

entries.name: Save DC
entries.text: 8 + the tamer's proficiency bonus + the hyphan's Constitution modifier

entries.name: Monster Trainer
entries: In addition to the improvements you can normally give your companions, you can choose to grant the hyphan the following improvements using your Monster Trainer feature:

entries.name: Helpful
Prerequisite:
entries: Become a tamer's companion.

entries.name: Type
entries: Active (bonus action).
As a bonus action, the hyphan takes the Help action. The hyphan gains this improvement when it becomes a companion; it doesn't cost an improvement.

entries.name: Detritivore
Prerequisite:
entries: 3rd-level tamer.

entries.name: Type
entries: Active (action).

As an action, the hyphan can drain one Small or larger corpse within its reach, regaining hit points equal to twice its tamer's level. Once the hyphan has used this action, it can't do so again until its tamer finishes a long rest. A corpse can be drained by this or similar abilities only once.

entries.name: Growth
Prerequisite:
entries: 5th-level tamer.

entries.name: Type
entries: Passive (companion).

The hyphan's size increases to Small, its Hit Die size increases to a d6 (its hit point maximum consequently increases by 1 for each of its Hit Dice), and the damage of its Poison Spray increases to 2d12.

entries.name: Hallucispores
Prerequisite:
entries: 5th-level tamer.

entries.name: Type
entries: Active (reaction).

As a reaction when the hyphan takes damage, it can jettison out a cloud of spores. Each creature within 10 feet of it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by the hyphan until the end of its next turn. The hyphan has a number of uses of this ability equal to its Constitution modifier (minimum 1) and regains all expended uses when its tamer finishes a long rest.

entries.name: Puffballs I
Prerequisite:
entries: 5th-level tamer.

entries.name: Type
entries: Active (action).

As an action, the hyphan can cause two 10-foot squares of dirt, rock, or wood it can see within 60 feet of it to sprout tiny puffball mushrooms, which last for 1 hour or until the hyphan dismisses them as an action. The squares must be contiguous with one another. When a creature enters the area, the 10-foot square of puffballs explodes, disappearing into a cloud of spores. Each non-hyphan creature in the area or within 5 feet of the area must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 13 ({@damage 2d12}) necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. After the hyphan uses this action, it can't do so again until the tamer finishes a short or long rest. When the hyphan's tamer reaches 9th level in the tamer class, the hyphan can create one additional 10-foot square of puffballs (three total), and the damage increases to 19 ({@damage 3d12}).

entries.name: Damp Dark Dweller
Prerequisite:
entries: 9th-level tamer, Detritivore.

entries.name: Type
entries: Passive (companion & tamer).

The hyphan has immunity to necrotic damage. In addition, while the hyphan is summoned, its tamer has darkvision out to a range of 60 feet. If its tamer already has darkvision, the range is increased by 30 feet.

entries.name: Fungal Fruits
Prerequisite:
entries: 9th-level tamer.

entries.name: Type
entries: Active (1 minute).

Over the course of a minute, the hyphan can grow a random assortment of mushrooms on its body. Each time it does this, roll a d4 twice and consult the options below to determine which two mushrooms grow. 1-Bloomshroom. As an action, a creature can eat this mushroom, regaining 2d4 + 2 hit points and gaining advantage on all Constitution saving throws for 1 minute. 2-Boomshroom. As an action, a creature can throw this volatile mushroom at a point it can see within 60 feet of it, where it explodes in a 10-foot-radius sphere of flames. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 14 ({@damage 4d6}) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The fire ignites flammable objects in the area that aren't being worn or carried. 3-Doomshroom. As an action, a creature can throw this dusky mushroom at a point it can see within 60 feet of it, where it explodes in a 10-foot-radius sphere of purple spores. Each creature in the area must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or become afflicted by the bane spell for 1 minute (concentration not required). An affected creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. 4-Gloomshroom. As an action, a creature can eat this mushroom. For the next hour, it gains darkvision out to a range of 60 feet. If it already has darkvision, the range of this vision is increased by 30 feet. The mushrooms last until the hyphan's tamer next finishes a long rest, but lose all magical effects 10 minutes after they are plucked. You can pluck a mushroom as part of the action to use it. After the hyphan uses this trait, it can't do so again until its tamer finishes a long rest.

entries.name: Multihelp
Prerequisite:
entries: 13th-level tamer, Helpful.

entries.name: Type
entries: Active (action).

When the hyphan takes the Disengage action, it can take the Help action up to three times on that turn as part of the same action. After it uses this action, it can't do so again until its tamer finishes a short or long rest.

entries.name: Puffballs II
Prerequisite:
entries: 13th-level tamer, Puffballs I.

entries.name: Type
entries: Active (action).

When the hyphan uses its Puffballs action, it can create an additional 10-foot square of puffball mushrooms, for a total of four 10-foot squares. The damage they deal increases to 26 ({@damage 4d12}). The hyphan gains a +1 bonus to the save DC of this action. When the hyphan's tamer reaches 17th level in the tamer class, the hyphan can create one additional 10-foot square of puffballs (five total), and the damage increases to 32 ({@damage 5d12}).

entries.name: Mycelial Reconstitution
Prerequisite:
entries: 17th-level tamer.

entries.name: Type
entries: Active (action).
As an action, the hyphan can dissolve into mycelia, ending the grappled and restrained conditions on it and reappearing in an unoccupied space on the ground it can see within 30 feet of it.

entries.name: Hyphans
entries: Sharing a closer genealogy with the common toadstool than with any of the humanoid races, hyphans is the term used for the alien, fungal hive mind and the creatures it animates. Found underground, hyphans line vast subterranean caverns as stationary toadstools, penetrate tremendous expanses of rock and soil as microscopic mycelia, and infect the bodies of creatures. This latter form, though the least common, permits hyphans to interact with other creatures of The Low, while also providing defensive measures in response to incursions by greedy adventurers. All such creatures are part of a single entity, the hyphan colony. Any sensation one portion of the colony experiences, the rest of the colony comes to know about soon after.

entries.name: Co-opted Assistance
entries: A hyphan hive mind typically adapts an infected creature's body into one of three archetypes: the brute, duskcap, or sporeslinger. These individuals must regularly return to the heart of their colony to be replenished and regain their vigour, lest they become decrepit, dessicated husks.

entries.name: Hyphan Brute
entries: Strong and burly creatures will be formed into brutes. Used for clearing rockfalls and to intimidate interlopers in a hyphan's domain, these large specimens' size can often act as an impediment in the tight tunnels of The Low. On the battlefield, brutes act as juggernauts, sending ranks of foes to the floor—perfect targets for their smaller cousins, the duskcaps. Their bulk and toughness allow them to fight without any sense of self preservation as they rampage through the enemy lines.

entries.name: Hyphans
entries: Sharing a closer genealogy with the common toadstool than with any of the humanoid races, hyphans is the term used for the alien, fungal hive mind and the creatures it animates. Found underground, hyphans line vast subterranean caverns as stationary toadstools, penetrate tremendous expanses of rock and soil as microscopic mycelia, and infect the bodies of creatures. This latter form, though the least common, permits hyphans to interact with other creatures of The Low, while also providing defensive measures in response to incursions by greedy adventurers. All such creatures are part of a single entity, the hyphan colony. Any sensation one portion of the colony experiences, the rest of the colony comes to know about soon after.

entries: A hyphan hive mind typically adapts an infected creature's body into one of three archetypes: the brute, duskcap, or sporeslinger. These individuals must regularly return to the heart of their colony to be replenished and regain their vigour, lest they become decrepit, dessicated husks.

entries.name: Hyphan Duskcap
entries: Lithe, graceful, or otherwise agile creatures can expect to become duskcaps if they should find themselves overcome by a hyphan colony's grasp. Primarily information gatherers, duskcaps are adept at passing without notice, and often patrol a colony's periphery, acting as its eyes and ears.

entries.name: Brainless Senses
entries: An isolated duskcap—indeed any isolated hyphan—does not possess the ability to understand what it hears; it is the fungal hive mind that interprets those sounds. While a duskcap is within range of a colony's communication spores, this interpretation happens instantaneously. However, if a duskcap should range beyond these spores, it will record everything it hears, to be transmitted to the hive mind with unfailing accuracy upon its return.

entries.name: Hyphans
entries: Sharing a closer genealogy with the common toadstool than with any of the humanoid races, hyphans is the term used for the alien, fungal hive mind and the creatures it animates. Found underground, hyphans line vast subterranean caverns as stationary toadstools, penetrate tremendous expanses of rock and soil as microscopic mycelia, and infect the bodies of creatures. This latter form, though the least common, permits hyphans to interact with other creatures of The Low, while also providing defensive measures in response to incursions by greedy adventurers. All such creatures are part of a single entity, the hyphan colony. Any sensation one portion of the colony experiences, the rest of the colony comes to know about soon after.

entries.name: Co-opted Assistance
entries: A hyphan hive mind typically adapts an infected creature's body into one of three archetypes: the brute, duskcap, or sporeslinger. These individuals must regularly return to the heart of their colony to be replenished and regain their vigour, lest they become decrepit, dessicated husks.

entries.name: Hyphan Sporeslinger
entries: Innately magical creatures that get 'hyphanated' (the term used by scholars to describe the act by which a creature is overcome by a hyphan colony) will become sporeslingers. Some of these individuals may remember the spells they knew in life, but, for the most part, this connection with the Weave is co-opted to provide the colony access to charm-based magics. Sporeslingers use these beguiling enchantments to capture stray creatures and deliver them to the fungal heart where they too can be hyphanated. Without these specimens, a hive mind would have to rely on serendipity to gather new biomass. With them, it can take a more proactive approach.

entries.name: Self-preservation
entries: A hyphan hive mind is far from stupid. It understands the fragility and value of a sporeslinger. A sporeslinger possesses the ability to produce clouds of obscuring spores (from which to make its escape) and is rarely found alone. On diplomatic missions they may be accompanied by brutes, for their intimidating size. When laying a trap, a sporeslinger may stand alone in a field of barely-visible puffball toadstools, several duskcaps lying in wait in the shadows.
Strange new life germinates in the Haze. These multicoloured flowers emit a hallucination-inducing pollen and overflow with contaminated nectar. They are often fatally mistaken for an eldritch lily.

name: Hypnotic Eldritch Blossom

entries: The multi-colored petals of this large lotus-like flower gently open. Light dances across its leaves and shimmering blossom in strange hypnotic rhythm. The colors seem to shift as it moves, at times creating unimaginable colors. As you gaze at it, maddening patterns fill your mind, and a wave of confusion sweeps over you, making it impossible to tell if your glance was for but a moment or a lifetime.

Queen's Park Garden was one of the most visited locations in the city prior to the meteor. Although the park existed since the city's founding, it was Helena von Kessel II, the mother of the late Ulrich IV, who ordered its redesign into the brilliance it grew to be. This redesign added tiered gardens, topiary masterpieces, cobblestone walkways, tranquil streams, and quaint waterfalls. The Queen's Park Gardens included an astounding assortment of flowers, many of which were exotic to Westemär. Even the wooded groves bustled with wildlife and an unrivaled selection of trees and bushes. With the contamination of Drakkenheim, the beauty of the gardens have become horrific feasting grounds for carnivorous plants, sentient trees, and strangling vines, and its flowers are now a constant threat to any who enter.

Hypnotic Eldritch Blossoms are one of many plants warped by mutation. They emit a hallucination-inducing pollen and overflow with contaminated nectar. They are often fatally mistaken for eldritch lilies, a magical plant sought for its contamination resistive properties. These flowers mimick lilies to lure prey close enough to be hypnotized. They often grow in hazardous environments such as near delerium encrusted growths, contaminated water, or delerium sludge. Once entranced by the pollen's influence, creatures move closer to be contaminated until transformed into a monsters.

Apothecaries who have studied the strange blossoms suspect they may be part of a network that "speaks" to delerium in a manner we could never understand. The flowers may be seeking to corrupt the living, changing them into more suitable creatures that can further the spread of contamination.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Nature|XPHB}) checks when they {@action Study|XPHB} a Hypnotic Eldritch Blossom, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (5+) Slow Moving Plant.
entries: You're aware of the plants movement, {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}, and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: (10+) Enchanted Blossoms.
entries: You learn of its Hypnotic Pollen action and Spell Reflection Reaction.

entries.name: (15+) Tough and Unthinking.
entries: You recognize the blossom's strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: These plants typically grow in places protected from easy access, such as a pool of contaminated water, and they weaponize their environment against threats. The blossom attempts to contaminate victims with its nectar and uses the surroundings to amplify the danger of contamination. The flower is not agile enough to escape attacks, and relies on its Hypnotic Pollen to keep itself alive. Hypnotized victims view the flower as an impossibly beautiful object and are lured into any nearby hazards.

entries: Plant.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Contaminated Ichor, Sap.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Flowers.

entries.name: Bones:
entries: Stem.
