Humanoids who dwell in the Shadow Realm sometimes pursue the path of a shadow knight to better serve their liege lords. Blessed by the shadow fey, these glorified bruisers are dark reflections of the cavaliers who protect the mortal world.

entries.name: Dark Arms
entries: Knights of shadow carry shadow fey forged swords and shields imbued with potent magic. Merely touching the surface of these armaments is enough to drain warmth and vitality.

entries.name: Sensory Training
entries: Every knight of shadows is trained to fight in magically dark conditions, so they are equipped to deal with the many light‑manipulating creatures who haunt the Shadow Realm. They combine their talents for blind fighting with their magical control of darkness to get the drop on unsuspecting foes.

Knight-Captain Theodore Marshal is a man in his prime. He is athletic and tall with boldly sculpted features, bronzed skin, and unkempt sandy brown hair. Unshaven stubble has grown into a beard over the criss-cross of scars on his face. A leather patch covers his right eye. He wears gleaming silver plate armour etched with golden trim, and carries a shimmering sword and a broad shield engraved with the symbol of the Sacred Flame.

items.name: Personality Trait
items.entry: I act with determined calm and respect. Little rouses my anger, instead I respond with disappointment when others incite my ire.

items.name: Ideal
items.entry: I believe that good-hearted people can set aside their differences to work together.

items.name: Bond
items.entry: I am willing to lay down my life for a just and righteous cause.

items.name: Flaw
items.entry: I will never give up on my comrades. I do not trade lives.

items.name: Knight-Captain Theodore Marshal

entries: Theodore Marshal is athletic and tall with boldly sculpted features, bronzed skin, and unkempt sandy brown hair. Unshaven stubble has grown into a beard over the criss-cross of scars on his face. A leather eye patch covers his right eye. He wears gleaming silver plate armor etched with golden trim, and carries a shimmering sword a broad shield engraved with the symbol of the Sacred Flame.

Knight-Captain Theodore Marshal is a decorated veteran of the Silver Order. Hand-picked by the Divine Matriarch to lead their mission to Drakkenheim, the valiant knight possesses a level-headed and clear-eyed faith. He would never ask his soldiers to undertake a task he would not brave himself, and prefers to lead from the front lines.

entries.name: Personality Trait
entries: Honorable. I treat all matters with great honor and respect, and I standing up for what I believe. I expect others to act similarly, respecting any who match my ideals and honor.

entries.name: Ideal
entries: Tradition. I uphold the traditions of the Sacred Flame and the Silver Order. I take pride in my standing within the Order and the responsibilities that befall my position.

entries.name: Bond
entries: I will willing to lay down my life to reclaim the lost relics in Drakkenheim and sanctify the cathedral. I know that there is no cost too great if it means purging the world of the filth of this blighted city.

entries.name: Flaw
entries: I trust those of my order and faith, and I believe whatever commands come from my superiors. I hestiate to trust those who do not swear to my faith, as there can be no other way that to follow its teachings.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Honorable to a fault, Theodore Marshal will always entertain parley and accept surrender, even if he doesn't expect the same from his foes. If it comes to blows, Theodore Marshal charges into battle and strikes hard with his warhammer, setting his enemies alight with {@spell Searing Smite}. Well aware of the dangers of spellcasters and monsters, he uses call the sacred flame to blind them so he can engage in melee with impunity.

entries.name: Knights of the Silver Order

entries: The Silver Order is an elite church-sanctioned regiment of paladins and ordained knights oath-sworn to combat supernatural evils, otherworldly incursions, and dark magic. As faithful devotees of the Sacred Flame, they believe delerium is a dangerous and contaminating blight. Led by the valiant Knight-Captain Theodore Marshal, the knights have been dispatched to eradicate Drakkenheim's corruption at its source.

The Silver Order are a well-known military organization hailing from the nation of Elyria in the southwest of the continent. Loyal to the Church of the Sacred Flame, the Silver Order are a well-known military organization they operate as a church-sanctioned military whose stated purpose is to protect the world from evil magical intrusions, to keep otherworldly threats at bay, and to protect the people against dark magic and abuses of power from mageborn. Many believe the Silver Order are a strict organization who upholds the letter of the law within the Edicts of Lumen, a legal document that dictates the balance of power between the church, the mages, and the royalty.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: What the Silver Order lacks in subtlety they make up for with sheer force. They are a military organization, and their soldiers are well trained and work together as a team. When they tackle problems, they do so in a uniform fashion, knowing when to rely on one another, complete tasks and make pushes in unison. The Silver Order has simple call signs, hand signals, commands, and strategies that they can rely on in the field.
Silver Order knights and paladins should work as a cohesive unit who know their strengths and how to protect their weaknesses.

Any Silver Order regiment is accompanied by at least one paladin or Flamekeeper, and usually at least one of each. Larger organized military missions will see griffon riders as well as entire units of paladins and several Flamekeepers or Pyre Priests. This means that no Silver Order unit is without moderate healing, protective buffs, and often forms of divination and holy battle magic. When push comes to shove, the order's divine spellcasters tend to have a few Fireballs and Flamestrikes amongst their options.
{@i This slight, reptilian humanoid is bedecked with ceramic flasks and glass vials. An acrid reek follows in its wake.}

Kobold alchemists are usually smelled before they are seen, thanks to the apothecary's store of chemicals and poisons they carry. Alchemists often sport mottled and discolored scales and skin, caused by the caustic nature of their obsessions. They raid alchemy shops and magical laboratories to gather more material to fuel their alchemical experiments.

entries.name: Dangerous Assets
entries: Alchemists can be a great boon to their clan, but at a cost. Not only do the alchemists require rare, expensive, and often dangerous substances to ply their trade, they tend to be a little unhinged. Their experiments yield powerful weapons and defensive concoctions that can save many kobold lives, but the destruction caused by an experiment gone awry can be devastating for the alchemist's neighbors.

{@i This small, draconic humanoid struts as though it were ten feet tall. It wears the gilded skull of a small dragon as a helmet, and its beady eyes gleam out through the skull's sockets. It hefts its spear and shield and lets out a blood-curdling shriek, signaling the attack}.

While most kobolds are scuttling scavengers or pathetic sycophants, a few carry a spark of draconic nobility that can't be ignored. These few forge their tribes into forces to be reckoned with, rising to the rank of chieftain. A kobold chieftain stands proud, clad in war gear of fine quality and good repair. Their weapons are tended by the tribe's tinkerers, particularly evident in their springspike shields.

entries.name: Living Legend
entries: A kobold chieftain is more than a leader, it is a symbol of the tribe's greatness. The strongest, most cunning, most ruthless of a kobold tribe embodies their connection to the revered dragons. When a chieftain sounds the call to battle, the kobolds meld into a fearless, deadly force.

entries.name: Kobold Constructs
entries: While some kobolds are blessed with sorcery bequeathed to them by their draconic origins, others possess the ability to believe so fervently that their beliefs manifest. Baron Bodrum has seized upon this untapped form of magic to improve the profits on his 'Buddy Bots' line of automatons. Kobold belief has cut costs by over sixty percent, and designs are in the works for constructs that contain no magical components. Of course, the Kobold Resources department is under strict orders to keep this under wraps lest it make the kobolds begin to doubt their work.

entries.name: Paradox of Gullibility
entries: This brings us to a paradox. Kobolds are pretty gullible, and will believe almost anything if enough big words and shinies are used. But, if enough of them start believing a lie, the lie can come true. Who's the gullible one then!? On returning from a month in the cramped kobold caves, Dr. Doolots posited that this belief-manifest is a defence mechanism evolved in response to other creatures' desire to abuse kobold gullibility.

entries.name: Kobold Mech
entries: Barrels, pots, pans, a temperamental arcanomechanical core, and your grandma's retainer are all key ingredients of a kobold mech. Some say they've even seen one that used a kitchen sink. With legs capable of burrowing, javelin-dynamite-missiles for, presumably, mining, and fiery boosters, few things can escape this hunk of lubricated junk.

{@i This kobold is bedecked in satchels, pouches, sacks, and bandoliers. All of these are bursting with tools, bits of scrap, wire, cogs, and twine. Impossibly large eyes blink through the lenses of its goggles}.

Some kobolds hatch a bit cleverer than their counterparts. These sharp-witted creatures feel driven to fiddle with the world, and those that don't meet an early demise through accident or violence often take up tinkering. Trapsmiths make a kobold lair into a deadly gauntlet of hidden pain.

entries.name: Improvisers
entries: Trapsmiths are adept at improvising on-the-fly. They can use whatever spare parts are at hand to create simple thieves' tools or construct makeshift traps to fling at foes.

entries.name: Shifting Peril
entries: Trapsmiths aren't warriors and avoid direct confrontation with enemies that aren't mired in traps or engaged with other foes. If the trapsmith senses that invaders in its lair are likely to get past its traps, it tries to hide or escape. A trapsmith delights in laying traps and snares behind invaders, along tunnels and paths they've already cleared and believe to be safe, then luring them back through its handiwork.

entries.name: Kobold Constructs
entries: While some kobolds are blessed with sorcery bequeathed to them by their draconic origins, others possess the ability to believe so fervently that their beliefs manifest. Baron Bodrum has seized upon this untapped form of magic to improve the profits on his 'Buddy Bots' line of automatons. Kobold belief has cut costs by over sixty percent, and designs are in the works for constructs that contain no magical components. Of course, the Kobold Resources department is under strict orders to keep this under wraps lest it make the kobolds begin to doubt their work.

entries.name: Paradox of Gullibility
entries: This brings us to a paradox. Kobolds are pretty gullible, and will believe almost anything if enough big words and shinies are used. But, if enough of them start believing a lie, the lie can come true. Who's the gullible one then!? On returning from a month in the cramped kobold caves, Dr. Doolots posited that this belief-manifest is a defence mechanism evolved in response to other creatures' desire to abuse kobold gullibility.

entries.name: Koboldzilla
entries: This machine should not function. Every rivet, bolt, and staple that holds the koboldzilla together is brimming with belief. The metal ignores its maximum shearing load, the wood forgets that it should spontaneously combust, and gravity forms an anomaly around its ridiculously armoured carapace.

entries.name: Burgeoning Sentience
entries: Before it becomes godlike, the koboldzilla is aware. It causes armour plating to come loose in the nick of time to protect its kobold pilots, and its growing causes objects for miles around to begin working again with the most rudimentary percussive maintenance. With the belief that only martyrdom can bequest, the koboldzilla is a hair's breadth from apotheosis.

name: Kolmurag
entries: Cultist occupant of cold storage
{@i This large pterodactyl has emergent feathers and a long, beaklike jaw.}

entries.name: Boat Breaker
entries: The kongamato's name means "breaker of boats," and, as that implies, it delights in systematically destroying the small vessels of those who come too close to its perch. No one knows what motivates this form of attack, although some sages suppose that the kongamato mistakes canoes for large prey like hippopotamuses or crocodiles.

entries.name: Spoken in Whispers
entries: For some tribes, kongamatos present a terrible threat, and the villagers speak only in whispers about them, fearing that mention of the beasts could attract their wrath. In some cases, evil priests and cultists summon these beasts as their servitors and use them to terrify villagers.

entries.name: Maneaters
entries: Kongamatos that have eaten human flesh develop a preference for it. These maneaters perform nightly raids on small towns, snatching locals in their claws and flying away.
{@i The fiendish hulk bears features taken from a nightmare scorpion, with three stinging tails and four limbs. It wields a massive scythe.}

entries.name: Shaped by Arbeyach
entries: These fiends sprang from the dark imagination of Hell's Prince of Swarms, Arbeyach, who twisted them into being from lemures and scorpions. Arbeyach shaped the koralk to be annihilators in battle and to gather souls from the fallen, bypassing typical soul collection methods to feed his war machine more quickly. They are sometimes called "harvester devils."

entries.name: Transforming Poison
entries: Poison from the koralk's stingers liquefies the victim's insides in an agonizing transformation. The creature swells as its organs, muscles, and skeleton rapidly break down and reform, transforming the creature into a lemure in a burst of fiendish goo. The new lemure is subject to the will of more powerful devils, and its fate from that moment on is the same as any lemure's. The koralk's poison can work this transformation on demons, giving Arbeyach's armies a unique edge.

entries.name: Infernal Mounts
entries: A koralk is strong enough for many devils to ride. They prefer only powerful devils as riders, but they obey their superiors and carry even the lowest of devils into battle if directed. Arbeyach often rides an especially large specimen into battle, called the Grand Annihilator by his devilish troops.

name: Kosktup Farleap
entries: Small squirrelfolk. Red-brown fur. Eyes the color of acorns. Cocky grin. Plain but serviceable leather armor over a teal shirt. Gold earrings in one tufted ear. Matching rapier and dagger hanging from his belt.
{@b Found Initially In:} Ogre's Run. Also appears in Among the Norns, The Redspear Trail, and others.
{@b Background:} Courageous swashbuckler, longship captain, squirrelfolk.
{@b Personality Traits:} Daring, cocky, and charming in equal measure.
{@b Bonds:} This longship dream—oh, and stopping the Cult of Ragnarok.
{@b Flaws:} Hides his idealism and dedication behind vanity and playful indifference.

{@b Wants:} To fulfill his dream of building and owning the greatest longship in the North, but when they first meet him, he'd settle for getting away from the ogres and perhaps a nice bath. Ultimately, he wants to keep his ship and crew alive and whole, which means stopping the end of the world.

{@i This oddly colored cat appears at first to be a powerful panther of some kind. Its wide mouth pulls into something like a human grin, and its knowing eyes hint at intelligence beyond that of a typical jungle cat.}
Enemies of elves and blink dogs, kot bayuns are magical hunting cats gifted with eloquent speech and cunning abilities.

entries.name: Speaking Fey Cats
entries: These brutal and temperamental creatures get along well with cruel-minded fey. Gentler fey rightfully find the creatures to be a menace. A kot bayun measures six feet long and weighs over 200 pounds. They are long-lived, and some stories record the same kot bayun in a region for over 400 years.

entries.name: Sing to Sleep
entries: In addition to their stealthy natures and physical prowess, kot bayun have the ability to put prey to sleep with song. They carefully stalk victims for a time, learning the victim's strengths and weaknesses before making their attack. They lie in wait until their prey is vulnerable and then begin their song. Those resisting the call to slumber are always the kot bayun's first victims as the predator launches from cover and attempts to disembowel its prey. In forests with a thick canopy, a kot bayun stealthily creeps among tree limbs, tracking the movement of its prey below.

entries.name: Healing Poetry
entries: If discovered by intelligent prey, a kot bayun opens with a parley instead of claws. In rare cases, a kot bayun finds something in its prey it likes, and cold predation turns to a lukewarm association. Befriending a kot bayun has benefits, as the creature's poems, tales, and sagas have healing power. A kot bayun tells its stories in the form of strange epics and poetry, ranging from simple rhyming folk poems to complex sonnets, and it heals listeners only at the end of the poem.

name: Kraghammer Goat-Knight
entries: The sheer cliff faces and winding mountainside roads of the {@book Cliffkeep Mountains|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Cliffkeep Mountains} are nearly impossible to traverse by normal means with any speed. The Peakclimber Knights of {@book Kraghammer|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Kraghammer}—commonly known as the {@creature Kraghammer Goat-Knight|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|goat-knights}—are the enforcers of peace and justice across the mountain range. They trust their {@creature Goat-Knight Steed|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|giant goat steeds} to master the harsh mountain slopes, and many travelers lost within the {@book Cliffkeep Mountains|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Cliffkeep Mountains} have been saved by a {@creature Kraghammer Goat-Knight|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|goat-knight} who led them to safety along the more traversable mountain paths.

These knights serve the {@deity The All-Hammer|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|All-Hammer} and sometimes find themselves at odds while enforcing the laws of {@book Kraghammer|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Kraghammer} and upholding the edicts of their god.

entries.name: Mounted Combatant
entries: Any spell the {@creature Kraghammer Goat-Knight|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|goat-knight} casts with a range of self also targets the goat.

When a {@creature Goat-Knight Steed|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} drops to 0 hit points, it disappears, leaving behind no physical form. The {@creature Kraghammer Goat-Knight|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|goat-knight} can also dismiss the steed at any time as an action, causing it to disappear. In either case, the same steed is summoned when the {@creature Kraghammer Goat-Knight|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|goat-knight} casts {@spell find steed}.

images.altText: A dwarf with long, braided brown beard and clad in full plate armor, sits atop a large, wiry-haired mountain goat.

entries: {@i This twisted, beast looks like the unholy union of squid and spider. Its shell-covered core has six small rubbery legs, peculiar antennae, and six tentacles around a squid's enormous beak.}

entries.name: Demonic Crossbreeds
entries: Some believe krake spawn are demonic crossbreeds created by the aboleth, fusing kraken blood with demonic souls. Others say that krake spawn are the horrible creation of a long-forgotten meddling god, summoned to the mortal world by deep ones. Certainly, krake spawn respond to summoning magic, and spellcasters summon krake spawn through blood sacrifices to work evil in the world. However, they do so at considerable peril: unlike demons and devils, krake spawn are seldom bound by pacts of any kind.

entries.name: Outwit Humans
entries: Though enormous and carrying an armored green shell on their six spindly legs, krake spawn are surprisingly quick and agile. Worse, they have a malicious and bloodthirsty intellect. A krake spawn is considerably smarter than most humans, who often mistake them for dumb beasts—an error that can often prove fatal.

entries.name: Iceberg Fortresses
entries: Krake spawn live in remote, icy regions, where they fashion elaborate iceberg fortresses. These fortresses are stocked with frozen creatures (an emergency food supply), the krake spawn's treasure and library, slaves or prisoners of many races, and a hellish nest filled with the krake spawn's offspring.

name: Krall, the Scavenger King
entries: Krall is an imposing mapach, standing nearly 6 feet tall with a solid build and matted fur that is missing in patches. He was close friends with Benna, although he didn't share her altruism and instead believed that those who couldn't carry their weight should be left behind. He expects complete loyalty from his followers, and favors hit-and-run tactics. He and his troops exact tolls on poorly-defended caravans for passage along the roads, which many pay to avoid his wrath. Krall uses the {@creature mapach brute|HumblewoodCampaignSetting} stat block.

This nightmare was conjured from Arrevis' mortal fear of the Amaranthine {@deity Kren|Amaranthine|HumblewoodCampaignSetting}, whose wrath he now dreads after breaking ties with the devotees. It takes the shape of a ferocious shadowy fox with two tails and glistening fangs.

name: Kristoff Gruber
entries: Being a small community, there is little here for outsiders. Briar Public House was opened to provide a drinking spot for locals, but it also offers food and lodging for travelers and merchants who find their way into the small village. Briar Public House is owned and operated by {@creature Kristoff Gruber|CrookedMoon24} (Neutral Good, human {@creature Commoner|XMM}), a portly, gruff man whose sour disposition belies his caring nature.

name: Kronen

entries: In the shadow of the ruins, a pale, gaunt human appears. Their peculiar black cordlike hair shimmers strangely. With a bizarre gat they they stride forward revealing a monstrous form. Six skitterin legs hold up its sprawling torso resembling the thorax and abodme of a massive cockroach. Its chitinous shell gleams with a sickly sheen a pair of long twitching antennae sprout from its head, and it arms end in clawed, human-like hands. Small oculi dot its forhea surrounding large compound eyes. Opening its mouth reveals no a tongue, but horrific mandibles. Countless small cockroaches dar among weeping holes covering its torso

Drakkenheim's citizens were struck with panic and terror the day the city fell. While many tried to flee amidst the chaos, a few sought safety, barricading themselves in whatever shelter they could find. They hid in cellars, closets, outhouses, tunnels, and other seemingly secure places in a desperate attempt to survive. When the flames died down and the Haze took hold, a few chose to wait out the eerie mists. Who can say if they would have fared better had they attempted escape?

Isolated and alone, most tried surviving on contaminated water and subsisting on vermin creeping into their shelters. These fools did not realize the Haze could permeate their hiding places. Worse, the insects and rodents they consumed began to feed on them. Gradually exposed to contamination, the survivors metamorphosed into loathsome, vermin-like monstrosities befitting their wretched dwellings. Most knew that something had changed but they had little sense for how much time has passed.

Many of these unfortunates remain in their hiding places, confined within nightmarish conditions. Indeed, many are trapped within their shelters due to flooded passages, fallen rubble, or collapsing ruins. When discovered within deep cellars and sealed passages, they respond with panicked and confused violence. Explorers seeking to unearth treasure and lost relics within the city quickly learn to carefully inspect dig sites for hollows or buried chambers where a "Kronen" may dwell.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Nature|XPHB}) checks when they {@action Study|XPHB} a Hypnotic Eldritch Blossom, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (5+) Infected Vermin.
entries: You are aware of the creature's Infestation Reaction.

entries.name: (10+) Speed and Dread.
entries: You learn of the creature's Loathsome Presence action and Scuttle Bonus Action.

entries.name: (15+) Broken Personality.
entries: You understand the creature's strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: A Kronen is usually agitated and alarmed when encountered, and its first instinct in combat is to find a new hiding place or flee deeper into its lair. It uses its Loathsome Presence while clawing at any in the way of its escape using Scuttle, reflexively spreading roaches to attackers via its Infestation Reaction.

If it escapes, a Kronen is eventually drawn to return to its old hiding place. Should characters remain there, the Kronen will furiously attack to reclaim its shelter but won't pursue charac ters who leave it alone in its hideout.

entries: Monster Blood, Contaminated Ichor

entries: Eyes, Guts, Flesh.

entries: Claws.

entries: Carapace.

entries: Aberrant Dust.

name: Krusgr Ironcap
entries: Fire giant warlord

name: Kruug
entries: Guard of northeastern wall

name: Kvasir
entries: Divine spirit

name: Lady Elwen - Fell Wraith

entries: Once a valorous Dúnadan noble lady, but when her city fell, she survived, only to be slowly consumed by grief and by the curse of the Chief of the Ringwraiths—Lady Elwen is now a Fell Wraith, bound to roam the ruins of her castle.

As a Fell Wraith, she appears as a crooked hag, wrapped in tatters hiding her spectral features. Her flesh is almost transparent, and her eyes glow like embers. Thin strands of white hair escape her hood.
Why have you come? There's nothing here, only death. Leave this place, or join me in my torment!
She is armed with a pitted sword, the weapon she used to defend her city and fortress.

name: Lady Feluciana, Legendary Medusa Sorceress
entries: Legends vary in their accounts of Lady Feluciana, and whether she is the oldest medusa or simply the most powerful of her kin. Like all medusas, the Lady is said to have been cursed due to her obsession with beauty and cruelty, but unlike other tales of such curses, nearly all accounts of Lady Feluciana state that she most certainly deserved hers. With many years to foment plans and practice her magic, the Lady is now a truly legendary sorceress and a terror to behold. Her followers are typically those that hunger for magical knowledge and power over other humanoids in their lives.

One of the most organized collections of warlocks, the Sorceress's followers focus mostly upon the study of potent and forbidden magics. In this, their patron seems to behave unpredictably, as the Lady's worshippers seem utterly unable to determine precisely what behaviors she constitutes as ideal. Some scholars speculate that she enjoys seeing occasional in-fighting and squabbling, perhaps viewing it as a necessary or helpful means of weeding out the unworthy and identifying the truly gifted. Regardless, those cunning and cutthroat enough to survive the metaphorical snake pit are worth keeping a very careful and close eye on.

Like many other Medusas, Lady Feluciana employs liberal use of terrain and her petrifying gaze to devastating effect. However, it should be noted that in stark contrast to typical Medusas, the Sorceress seems to have unlocked a more potent form of petrification magic, allowing her to petrify those she concentrates upon even if they avert their gaze. She is also exceptionally crafty, and reports indicate that her entire lair is covered in enchanted mirrors so she cannot be taken by surprise. However, it should be quite obvious that all information about the Lady is hearsay, given that not a single individual in recorded history has visited her lair and lived to tell the tale.

entries.name: Reflection's Doom
entries: Those foolish enough to encounter the Legendary Sorceress within her lair on a mist-enshrouded and uncharted island typically realize their folly long after the point of no return. Coated in mirrors that cannot be broken except by powerful magic or at the Lady's command, Reflection's Doom is home to poisonous albino snakes and is the final resting place of countless would-be heroes and marooned sailors.

name: Lagertha Giantblooded
entries: Gray-blue skin. Ice eyes. White, braided hair. Old battle scars on her face.
{@b Background:} A member of the Apostles of Inexorable Ruin.
{@b Personality Traits:} Appears smug and confident. Well-hidden ruthlessness and cruelty.
{@b Bonds:} Fanatically loyal to Thyrin the Black and his cause.
{@b Flaws:} Can't resist being scornful.
{@b Wants:} To fool the giants into turning against the characters and to murder any disloyal to the Blood Reckoning.
{@b Other Notes:} Disguised as a paladin of Thor, Deception +5
{@b Talking to Lagertha:} Among other details, the giantkin "false paladin" gives the following evidence for her accusation:

items: The characters aided the known criminal Finulf One-Hand, even though they knew he was a thief who'd stolen an important relic from a temple of Wotan in Wolfheim (in {@i Down the Wolf Barrow}).
After slaughtering a remote outpost, the characters freed a heretical ratatosk, leaving a trail of destruction across the Haamu Hills (in {@i Ogre's Run}).
Aided by a disreputable ratatosk, the characters consorted with fell entities near the lair of Nidhogg, the creature gnawing at the roots of Yggdrasil (in {@i Among the Norns}).
The characters prevented the villagers of Hvalfell from fleeing a force of ogres and trolls because they needed time to finish building a longship (in {@i Assault on Hvalfell}).

While participating in a bardic competition in Skaldholm, the characters organized the murder of a prominent bard to gain influence over the {@creature Eirik Ellefsen|NorthlandsSagas|Master of Thyles} (in {@i Trials of the Lost Skald}).

name: Lake Dredger

entries: {@i Undead Aquatic Monster}

Lake dredgers are Undead water behemoths, such as whales, giant fish, or dinosaurs. These creatures are reanimated through the deep, primal fear of the unknown horrors that lurk in the murky depths. They dwell in the beds of lakes, rivers, or oceans, dredging up the detritus to replenish their ever-rotting mass.

They also add to their decaying bulk by feeding on living creatures, especially drawn to those who exhibit fear of the deep. Once prey is devoured, it is impaled on its cracked ribs until the waterlogged flesh becomes one with the beast's.

entries.name: Secret
entries: Lake dredgers exist because of the fear of the unknown, and their essence is undone in the presence of a captured or crafted depiction of themselves, such as a drawing or carving.

{@i This large, lanky creature has arms too long for its body. Its hands are webbed and equipped with wicked claws. Its skin is covered in dull green scales and embedded with stones, and limp hair like scraggly seaweed hangs across its long-nosed face}.

Water-dwelling cousins of the more common trolls, lake trolls are both stronger and slightly more intelligent, but thankfully less common. Accompanied by a reek of old, rotting fish, these slimy creatures live beneath the surface of lakes, ponds, rivers, and sometimes even ocean coves.

entries.name: Violently Territorial
entries: A lake troll is savage in the defense of its claimed expanse of territory; any encroachment into the creature's water is met with sudden violence from the depths. Fishermen are the most vulnerable to these attacks, especially when they explore new bodies of water.

entries.name: Cruel Cunning
entries: Even seasoned soldiers are wise enough to fear the claws of a lake troll; a person with no weapon facing the creature is doomed. Lake trolls delight in splintering wood and twisting metal with their talons and in shrugging off the deadliest of blows with their tough hide. They often prioritize wielders of grand weapons because they delight in the horror brought on by dulling their prey's weapons with a few strokes of their powerful claws. Lake trolls are cunning ambushers. They make use of the water to cover their attack and to protect themselves from the flames of would-be troll hunters.

entries.name: Hard to Kill
entries: A lake troll's regeneration is shut down only by cold and fire damage at nearly the same time, making them tricky to fight and exceedingly difficult to kill. Many adventurers have been shocked or slain when a lake troll they presumed was burned to death suddenly leapt back into the fray. Because they're reclusive and so very lethal, these creatures are poorly understood by most scholars.

name: Lambent Dreg

entries: The creature glows with a pallid, soft light. At times it gives off-hues of purples, oranges, and greens, but on occasion the color seems wholly indescribable. Its mouth hangs wide open, that same glow emerging brighter from its gullet, and its eyes shine like two lanterns as it surveys the area around it, drawn to the contaminating energies around it.

Lambent Dregs have become so contaminated that they glow like delerium. They are drawn to the contaminated crystals, gathering around them in groups. Studying these strange glowing Dregs, it has become clear that they become more hostile towards already contaminated creatures. Something about contamination motivates them to chase, attacking anyone suffering from mutations or sickness caused by exposure in the ruins.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Survival|XPHB} or {@skill Nature|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check to {@action Study|XPHB} a Lambent Dreg, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (5+) Drawn to Contamination
entries: You are aware of the Dreg's Arcane Hunger trait.

entries.name: (10+) Urge to Contaminate
entries: You know of the Lambent Dreg's Octarine Beam and Wave of Contamination attacks.

entries.name: (15+) Smart and Cunning
entries: You learn of the Lambent Dreg's highest and lowest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Lambent Dregs tends to gather around delerium clusters throughout the city, often appearing in groups in highly contaminated areas. Creatures who have {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} levels are prime targets for Lambent Dregs. The Dregs chase them down, avoiding non-contaminated targets when possible.

If threatened, Lambent Dregs run into the middle of a group of enemies and expel their Wave of Contamination, attempting to render their foes into a state of {@condition contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}, allowing the Dreg to easily engage with them.
Lambent Dregs flee if outnumbered and in a losing situation.

entries: Claws.

entries: Hair.

entries.name: Dust:
entries: Aberrant Dust.

The creature is cloaked in dark rags that hang off their hunched form, two massive lanterns dangling from fleshy protrusions off their back. Their arms and legs are gangly and long, as though they walk on stilts as they lumber forward on all fours. Their face is expressionless and pale, with hollow black pools for eyes. As their mouth opens, their jaw unhinges to reveal a gaping maw filled with spiked, hooked teeth. The creature's screech is harrowing as lamps glow brighter and motes of arcane energy flit about them.

Before the cataclysm that claimed Drakkenheim, lamplighters would traverse the city's streets at dusk, ensuring all the lanterns along the main thoroughfares were lit. Once, those lanterns were guiding lights to those making their way home at the end of the day. Now, the contamination that spreads through Drakkenheim has transformed the former lamplighters into twisted abominations. Their forms have merged with the lanterns they once kept lit, letting them lure creatures in the ruins toward their comforting lights—then devour those creatures while they bask in the glow.

In their contaminated madness, lamplighters view other creatures as pests desiring to put out their lanterns, and so they have resolved to snuff out those creatures instead. One can sometimes hear the muttering and wailing of the lamplighters echoing these delusions, as they cry out, "Keep the lights!" or "Must not let the darkness in ..."

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Lamplighters hide in dark, ruined buildings or small hovels during the day, emerging only at dusk. They patrol through the night, magically lighting the ruined lanterns of the city to ensure that the main roads are well illuminated.

From a distance, a lamplighter appears as a softly glowing light that bobs as it moves through the ruins. The creature uses their Lantern Beams action to either fend off creatures from a distance, or to lure unsuspecting prey in toward them. When a creature is close enough, the lamplighter uses their ravening maw to attack and devour them.

A lamplighter reduced to below a quarter of their {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} usually attempts to flee into the ruins to recover. These creatures are territorial to the streets they worked in life, and they will return to that territory once healed, continuing to protect their precious lights against intruders.

Because lamplighters are inherently drawn to the dark places of Drakkenheim, characters can often avoid them by sticking to areas already illuminated by lantern light. At the same time, lamplighters can be drawn to specific locations by snuffing out the lights in the area along a main road, compelling the creatures to come and reignite their lanterns.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: A character proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB} has advantage on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine a Lamplighter. They learn the following information based on their check result:

items.name: 10 or higher
items.entry: This check result reveals the lamplighter's resistances.

items.name: 15 or higher
items.entry: This check result reveals the creature's Lantern Beams feature and its multiple options.

items.name: 20 or higher
items.entry: This check result reveals the creature's highest (Str, Dex) and lowest (Int, Cha) ability scores and saving throws.

entries: {@i This cat-sized drake with a waxy appearance and a glow emanating from its belly can hover in midair, filling a small area with a warm glow.}

The lantern dragonette is named for its belly, which glows with a warm light. The beast's yellow, waxy scales darken with age, though the dragonettes rarely live more than 50 years. They weigh from 5 to 10 pounds and are 18 inches long.

entries.name: Eat Candle Wax
entries: The dragonette devours four ounces of candle wax each day, plus four more ounces if it has made its belly glow. A lantern dragonette's unusual diet leads it to lair in libraries, abbeys, and other places of study. Even though the dragonettes eat candles essential for study during dark hours, they still provide light and protect their adopted homes. Residents and caretakers consider them good luck and enjoy conversing with them.

entries.name: Telepathic Chatterbox
entries: This gregarious dragonette prefers to speak with its companions but uses telepathy if necessary; the creature hisses when surprised or displeased. It loves nothing more than discussing magic and history with an intelligent and informed individual.

entries.name: Adventurous Companions
entries: Occasionally, a dragonette wishing to learn more about the world finds a spellcaster or adventuring party to travel with, purely for the sake of learning or to acquire new sources of knowledge. Most parties enjoy the traveling light source and the abilities these companions bring to bear. A lantern dragonette avoids combat and uses its abilities only to escape or to defend its lair, family, and friends.

entries.name: Diligent Parents
entries: A mated pair produces one clutch of two to five eggs every five years. One parent raises the young dragonettes until they mature, typically in a year, while the other scours the area for candle wax to feed the hungry hatchlings.

name: Last Memory

entries: Seared into brick and cobblestone is the ashen silhouette of a human form. Not a trace of their body remains, the blackened stone capturing the last imprint of their existence, the moment they were incinerated by the meteor's eldritch fire. Inexplicably, the silhouette animates into distorted shapes, as distant screams and echoing anguished whimpers fill your ears.

These disembodied undead were formed the moment the meteor struck Drakkenheim. In a flash, those close to the impact were reduced to ash, but eldritch forces unleashed by the explosion trapped the memories of those it obliterated. Captured forever in that moment as silhouettes, a Last Memory is not a ghost or specter. They are not metaphysically connected to a living creature or its spirit—that creature is gone, annihilated body and soul by the eldritch fires which consumed them. Instead, these undead are pain, suffering, and misery given form in a gruesome instant. These spirits cannot be reasoned with nor spoken to, and cannot be aided or soothed. They are incapable of existing outside the singular event of their destruction, desiring only to force that moment into the minds of others, causing them to experience their anguish over and over again.

Even if the mere physicality of a Last Memory is destroyed, its lingering agony causes them to reappear, their endless torment a gravestone marking one lost to the meteor. Last Memories destroyed in the ruins of Drakkenheim return days later, emerging in a sorrowful chorus of screams that echo through the city.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Arcana|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Religion|XPHB}) checks to {@action Study|XPHB} a Last Memory, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (5+) Deathless Memory.
entries: You know the creature's monster type, {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}, and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: (10+) Painful Recall.
entries: You are aware of the creature's Anguish action.

entries.name: (15+) Weak Undead.
entries: You learn the creature's ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Last Memories can move along the ground or up walls, often hiding as shadows on the ground. They have even followed prey, appearing as a strange movement in one's peripheral vision, or a shifting shadow from an unknown source.

When they reveal themselves, Last Memories cry out in anguish, causing those nearby to suffer visions of their last moments, inducing emotional trauma to any who succumb to it. They grasp those nearby, terrorizing them with waves of sorrow. Last Memories seem to embody the raw emotions of their death, using those emotions as weapons against the living. They do not flee, for they do not cherish their existence. Their only purpose is to spread the fear and the pain of their own death before fading away, only to reappear days later to relive their agony.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Undead.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Ectoplasm, Contaminated Ichor.

entries.name: Dust:
entries: Undead Dust.

name: Lava Wurm
entries: Found most often burrowing through the igneous rock of dormant, active, or extinct volcanoes, the lava wurm is a ferocious draconic creature that lives off the rock they tunnel through. Although highly dangerous, the movements of lava wurms are followed as closely as possible by smiths who value them as natural smelters of the volcanic rock. The wurm can expel the undigested, molten metal from their gullet when threatened or expel it as the highly sought-after slag leavings.
{@i This furred humanoid glides silently through the canopy of trees, gripping a blowgun. It observes visitors cautiously with two intelligent, bulbous eyes.}

entries.name: Jungle Rulers
entries: These small, squirrel-like humanoids live in reclusive societies deep in the jungle. They are omnivorous gliders, subsisting on fruits and roots, insects and larvae, bird and snake eggs, and birds and small mammals. They sometimes barter with other humanoids for metal and forged items, but they prefer to rely on the forest for most of their needs.

entries.name: Greyfur Elders
entries: Greyfurs are the eldest and most revered lemurfolk, as much as 80 years old. Their age can be estimated by the graying of their fur, but they don't track the years. Greyfurs are cunning individuals and command the arcane arts, though they rarely pursue the art of necromancy—a strong taboo prohibits them from interacting with the dead. A typical lemurfolk stands 2 feet tall and weighs 30 pounds.
The smoky, fiery form hisses and shrieks in a cacophony of anger and confusion. There's something almost holy in the sound.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The severed head of a lenchtahg is a potent magic object. To the right buyer—a necromancer, a daemon cultist, an evil alchemist, and the like—a lenchtahg head is worth 750 gp. The servants of the Arch Daemon Malikir guard the secrets of binding a lenchtahg, but hags and other wicked creatures with magical skills possess knowledge to convert a lenchtahg head into a construct with similar unholy power.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
items.entry: Radiant damage heals a lenchtahg, which still has the flesh of a Seraph.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
items.entry: Dowsing a Lenchtahg with a lot of water or any holy water can temporarily weaken it.

items.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
items.entry: The lenchtahg's head must be consecrated in a holy ceremony or otherwise rid of its evil to avoid the lenchtahg's rejuvenation. But those with the right knowledge can use the head to craft a magical servitor.

entries.name: GM Advice
entries: Those who use lenchtahg as troops in battle will use radiant magic to damage foes while at the same time healing the lenchtahg. This greatly heightens the strength of these monsters.

Lendarick is a powerful mage graduate of the Avium, and his quest to improve the lives of the poor folk of the Roots caused him to change into a horrible slime monster known as the {@creature Slime King|HumblewoodTales}. Before his transformation, Lendarick was a sable luma with silky, red-brown feathers and a black mask-like streak across his eyes. He wore robes of blue silk. Lendarick was commonly seen scribbling in a beautifully bound notebook, and was rarely without a fresh cup of rose tea, taken with two sugars. Soft-spoken and good-natured, he was never a burden to others and always tried to help those less fortunate. Unfortunately, his ambitions to help led to his transformation.

Transformed by the Haze, Lenore is a mockery of her former self and abhorrently reacts to her own appearance. She dimly remembers seeking shelter in her grotto, but has no recollection of how she escaped the castle.

items.name: Personality Trait
items.entry: I speak softly in a perpetual daydream, rhapsodically imagining myself to be in a tragic fairytale while casting others in fictional roles.

items.name: Ideal
items.entry: The world is a mirror held up to my own glorious reflection.

items.name: Bond
items.entry: I obsessively crave beauty, decadence, and relish in art of all kinds, and especially love my garden and my lilies. They are all I have left.

items.name: Flaw
items.entry: I fly into an enraged fury at the sight of my own likeness or the names of my lost family members.

entries: Any character proficient in
{@skill History}

can instantly recognize Lenore despite her mutations. Before her transformation, Lenore was extraordinarily vain and narcissistic, though was uncharacteristically kind and gentle to her servants. She wore outrageously ornamented gowns, hats, makeup, and jewelry, including a famous golden necklace set with eleven emeralds. She loved her children only as extensions of herself, and absolutely despised her husband.

name: Lenore von Kessel

entries: The Haze transformed Queen Lenore into a monster. She stands six feet tall, clad in a once-opulent green dress adorned with gold filigree, now muddied and tattered. She wears an astonishing but tarnished golden necklace set with eleven emeralds. Her long, thin limbs and chalky skin are cracked and rigid like stone, and her hair is a writhing mass of thick, wet, tendrils, each ending in a toothy maw.

An emotionless porcelain mask obscures her face and a light shawl hides mutated hair. Her eyes are empty voids, swirling with magic and an occasional octarine glow. When the meteor fell, chaos quickly spread. Castle Drakken went to high alert, gathering the von Kessels to be escorted out of the city to safety. Queen Lenore was the first to be told to evacuate. She resisted, believing there was no safer place than the castle. But as screams erupted from the city and the Haze flowed from the South Ward, she finally agreed. Her handmaidens gathered her finest dresses, jewelry, and possessions, then used a secret passage to reach the sewers. They were wisked away by a royal boat on a private waterway to the Queen's Park Gardens but no further.

On arrival, the {@condition contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} had already reached the gardens. Terror and confusion were everywhere. After seeing a guard grotesquely transformed by the Haze, she fled with her retinue to a garden grotto, confusing familiarity with safety. They hid for some time, all becoming disfigured by the Haze. The Queen, afraid of her own reflection, had a mask fashioned to hide her features. She still resides within, waiting for her guards to return and say the danger is past. She is gripped by delusions that aside from her facial scarring, she has made it through the cataclysm unscathed.

This couldn't be more wrong. Her mind is broken and she clings to her delusionional view of reality. Anyone suggesting otherwise falls victim to her horrible gaze. She is a monster stalking the gardens, and like Drakkenheim's other horrors, she is dangerous and best left alone.

Before her transformation, the Queen was a strikingly tall and sharp-featured Caspian woman, with pale skin and vibrant orange hair. She married Ulrich IV to cement an alliance between House von Kessel and House Jones of Caspia, but refused to be a political pawn, asserting all of the royal privileges befitting a Queen. She was extraordinarily vain, hopelessly narcissistic, and frequently inebriated. She wore outrageously ornamented clothes, makeup, and jewelry, including a famous golden necklace set with eleven emeralds. She hosted parties and attended many social events where she delighted in her vassals' gossip, though was kind to her servants. She loved her children only as extensions of herself, and absolutely despised her husband.

items.name: Personality Trait
entries: I speak softly imagining myself to be in a tragic fairytale while casting others in fictional roles.

items.name: Ideal
entries: The world is a mirror held to my glorious reflection.

items.name: Bond
entries: I obsessively crave beauty, decadence, and relish all art. I especially love my garden and my lilies. They are all I have left.

items.name: Flaw
entries: I fly into an enraged fury at the sight of my own likeness or the names of my lost family members.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill History|XPHB} or {@skill Insight|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check to {@action Study|XPHB} Queen Lenore, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (10+) Mutated Queen of Drakkenheim
entries: You recognize she is an Aberration.

entries.name: (15+) Deadly Gaze
entries: You learn of her Radiant Gaze ability.

entries.name: (20+) Formidable Foe
entries: You understand her highest and lowest saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Lenore does not often outright engage in combat, throwing Dregs and her handmaidens at enemies who threaten her. She prefers to stay behind her minions where she is safe, relying on her Radiant Gaze to slowly disable and contaminate her foes..
If forced into melee, she uses her Tentacle Hair to attack and will take the first opportunity to escape if she can.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Aberration.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Monster Blood, Contaminated Ichor.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Eyes, Heart, Brain, Guts, Flesh.

entries.name: Bones:
entries: Skull, Spine, Ribs.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Tentacles.

entries.name: Hair:
entries: Hair.

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Skin.

entries.name: Dust:
entries: Aberrant Dust.

entries.name: Trophy:
entries: Lenore von Kessel's Porcelain Mask.
{@i This strange man is covered in bark and root-like growths and wears loose scraps of clothing. The hair and beard that frame his piercing green eyes writhe like living vines.}

entries.name: Expanding the Wild
entries: Solitary leshy tend plants and animals in groves around great forests, and they are the self-proclaimed protectors of the forest outskirts. Leshy have little patience for interlopers and often kill, abduct, or frighten off trailblazers and guides. They sabotage cultivated land, wipe out trails, and cultivate weed walls and thickets to keep civilization at bay. They transplant dangerous plant creatures to discourage new settlements, and some wrangle rabid animals to the same purpose.

entries.name: Ax Thieves
entries: Leshy prefer trickery to combat, leading intruders astray by mimicking animal and humanoid sounds. If challenged, they do everything in their power to scare intruders away, but they never hesitate to fight to the death in service to the forest if necessary. Leshy hate metal, especially axes, and they go out of their way to steal metal items and lead those who use them astray.

entries.name: Accept Bribes
entries: With careful courting and appropriate gifts, it is possible to gain a leshy's capricious assistance. This can be risky, because leshy love mischief. Still, a leshy's help is sometimes essential to a group traversing ancient woodlands.

name: Lesser Aboleth Broodmother
entries: Aboleth broodmothers weave a rich genetic tapestry with the ecosystem in which they settle. A broodmother's influence over its domain can be so absolute as to create a sort of hive mind out of the creatures it bends to its will.

entries.name: Alternate Evolution
entries: A broodmother does not evolve via the mechanisms proposed by many famous zoologists, such as Charlotte Darloss and Jane Lemarck, but rather assimilates the adaptations that other species develop through natural selection. After ingesting an organism, special enzymes within a broodmother's gastric tract extract useful genes and mutations, apportioning them to the relevant organs in the broodmother's form. One of those adaptations was a failsafe: a means of storing its memories, gathering biomass, and reforming itself.

entries.name: Aboleth Broodmother
entries: Due to the plethora of adaptations a broodmother has assimilated, it only vaguely resembles the form it had when it first arrived on the Material Plane. What still remains is its indelible memory and its desire to entrance living things.
Don't go to the temple. Something sinister has claimed it. Seek shelter elsewhere.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: An avarice seraph's metal-tipped feathers can be sold. Those of the lesser seraph are worth 250 gp, while those of the seraph are worth 1,000 gp.

Someone who has proficiency with alchemist's supplies can melt the metal on the feathers of an avarice seraph and use some feathers as fletching to make one arrow of celestial slaying for a lesser seraph, or four such arrows from the seraph. Making one arrow takes 7 days of work, reagents worth 1,000 gp, and a successful {@dc 17} Intelligence or Wisdom check.

The saliva of a gluttony seraph functions as antitoxin—three doses can be collected from a lesser seraph, while ten can be gathered from a seraph. Someone who has proficiency with alchemist's supplies or an herbalism kit can mix two doses of this saliva with reagents worth 50 gp and brew the mixture for 4 hours. The resulting elixir affects the imbiber as a protection from poison spell, curing a random poison in the drinker's system.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
items.entry: The disavowed are seraphs fallen to evil. Each still retains a measure of its celestial power.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
items.entry: From their celestial heritage, disavowed retain magic resistance and resistance to nonmagical attacks, as well as immunity to being charmed, exhausted, and frightened. Even in a fallen state, the seraph imparts magic and radiant damage to its attacks. Gluttony seraphs are also immune to poison.

items.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
items.entry: Avarice seraphs can rouse the greed in any creature. Huge gluttony seraphs can swallow and digest people, although their lesser kin can't.

name: Lesser Brood Chrysalis
entries: Aboleth broodmothers weave a rich genetic tapestry with the ecosystem in which they settle. A broodmother's influence over its domain can be so absolute as to create a sort of hive mind out of the creatures it bends to its will.

entries: A broodmother does not evolve via the mechanisms proposed by many famous zoologists, such as Charlotte Darloss and Jane Lemarck, but rather assimilates the adaptations that other species develop through natural selection. After ingesting an organism, special enzymes within a broodmother's gastric tract extract useful genes and mutations, apportioning them to the relevant organs in the broodmother's form. One of those adaptations was a failsafe: a means of storing its memories, gathering biomass, and reforming itself.

entries.name: Broodmother Chrysalis
entries: The broodmother's chrysalis is its failsafe. After gathering a sufficient volume of biomass within the huddle of charmed creatures, the broodlings encapsulate the huddle, creating a hard, sticky casing that protects the internal workings. In this temporary transitional state, the aboleth is almost unkillable. It metabolises the constituent creatures at an astonishing rate, almost immediately repairing any wounds it may sustain.

entries.name: Killable Chrysalis
entries: If you wish to run this monster as something that can be killed (in place of a transitional state), remove both the Regenerative and Transitional State traits.

name: Lesser Demon
entries: For those still new to the art of summoning, a fumbled attempt to conjure forth an entity of great power often results in the appearance of a lesser demon in its place. These beings are lowly, vexing creatures, eager to sow discord wherever they have been called.

entries.name: Vile and Malicious
entries: While there are all manner of devils and demons that seek to terrorize the good folk of the world, others are more off-putting and disgusting—an embarrassing blunder for the fledgling witch or wizard whose invocation went awry. Although not particularly powerful, lesser demons can still pose a serious threat to inexperienced conjurors and unsuspecting civilians.
Don't go to the temple. Something sinister has claimed it. Seek shelter elsewhere.

entries: {@i This winged fiend looks like something that has stepped out of a nightmare. Its elongated head is dominated by a mouth filled with razor-sharp teeth, and its spindly arms and legs end in long vicious talons. Where the moonlight catches it, its body appears almost transparent}.

These nightmarish creatures are smaller, weaker versions of the lunar devil, lazy and boastful fiends that draw strength from the light of the moon. Lesser lunar devils are often found serving their more powerful brethren, sent as advance scouts to spy on a druid circle their master intends to subvert, or to identify the werewolf pack leader that must be removed before the lunar devil can seize control of the pack.

entries.name: Lunar Devils in Midgard
entries: Unlike most devils, these fiends are uncommon in the Eleven Hells, rarely found outside of Sa-Mozan, the City of Silences, in the Third Hell of Qes-al-Marit, home of Alquam, Demon Lord of Night. Lesser lunar devils are much more widespread in the Shadow Realm. At any one time, a dozen or so of the creatures roost atop the Tower of the Moon where the Moonlit King once dwelt in exile, and hundreds of them flitter about his new skyborne palace, partially taking the role that shadow goblins perform in other courts. The Moonlit King dispatches the devils on bizarre missions across the plane and to Midgard, rewarding those that please him, by promoting them to full-fledged lunar devils, and demoting others to lesser status, seemingly on a whim.
