entries.name: Veiled Lady
entries: Hyphan colonies have an entirely alien system of ethics compared to other races of The Low. They have no concept of 'murder' or 'theft'; everything is simply 'useful' or 'waste'. This simplified outlook on life often brings hyphan colonies into conflict with other races.

Some colonies employ a plan of rapid relocation, moving themselves to new locations as soon as their existence is discovered. Others act hyper-aggresively, consuming any creature the moment it steps within their borders. Some colonies, in particular those that are in close proximity to other races, have developed a humanoid-like persona to interact with those peoples: a veiled lady.
The landscape of hyphan foreign policy is constantly changing as strategies that result in extermination fail to propogate, and colonies develop new, unique schemes.

entries.name: Appearance
entries: In the dim light of an underground cavern, a veiled lady appears as a huge, gowned silhouette, faintly feminine in shape. Closer inspection reveals a hollow where one might expect a cranium, and skin formed of constantly shifting threads of ultra-fine mycelia. A veiled lady appears to drift across the floor, gliding up unclimbable walls and squeezing through minute gaps without apparent effort.
{@i The humming of servos, ticking of gears, and petite discharges of steam precede the library's diminutive custodian.}
Library automatons are small constructs created to fulfill organizational responsibilities of huge libraries.

entries.name: Eyes of the Past
entries: Each automaton includes a single humanoid eyeball mounted at the end of an articulated appendage. These eyes are typically donations from the library's ailing scholars, allow them to continue serving the repositories of knowledge that were their life's work.

entries.name: Telekinetic
entries: The automatons can move and manipulate written materials telekinetically, and they can store such works in an extradimensional space within their bodies. The library automaton tirelessly pores through tomes, translates ancient texts, catalogs the institution's volumes, fetches texts for visitors, and occasionally rids the vast halls of uninvited pests.

entries.name: Scholarly Familiars
entries: Many spellcasters have discovered library automatons make particularly effective caretakers for their spellbooks and scrolls while on adventure.

entries.name: Library Automaton Familiars
entries: The library automaton's scholarly nature leads some of them to serve spellcasters and learn more of the world. Such automatons have the following trait.

entries.name: Familiar
entries: The library automaton can serve another creature as a familiar, forming a magic, telepathic bond with that willing companion. While the two are bonded, the companion can sense what the automaton senses as long as they are within 1 mile of each other. While the automaton is within 10 feet of its companion, the companion has resistance to psychic damage. At any time and for any reason, the automaton can end its service as a familiar, ending the telepathic bond.
{@i Half bone, half purple fire, this deathly hound releases an eerie howl that echoes with the voices of the damned.}

entries.name: Fiery Bones
entries: Bright white skulls with a heavy jaw and thick, robust skeletal bodies define the ferocious lich hounds. Their eyes burn green or blue, and their tongues resemble black fire. Fueled by necromantic power, these creatures are loyal servants of undead high priests or liches.

entries.name: Echoing Howls
entries: Even on their own, lich hounds are relentless hunters, pursuing their prey with powerful senses and a keen ability to find the living wherever the creatures may hide. Lich hound howls fade into and out of normal hearing, with strangely shifted pitch and echoes.

entries.name: Murdered Celestials
entries: The dark process of creating a lich hound involves a perverse ritual of first summoning a celestial canine and binding it to the Material Plane. The hound's future master then murders the trapped beast. Only then can the creature be animated in all its unholy glory. Houndlike celestials have long been outraged by the creation of lich hounds, and every few centuries, they band together to rid the world of those practicing this particular dark magic. Inevitably some knowledge survives this purge, leaving lich hounds a constant, painful reality for the celestials.
Running away from a troll is smart. Running away from a troll that casts spells is wishful thinking.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Someone who has proficiency with jeweler's tools or woodcarver's tools can fashion the skull of a lich troll into a ring of regeneration. Doing so takes materials worth 5,000 gp, 10 days of work, and a successful {@dc 15} Intelligence or Wisdom check. Somebody must also cast greater restoration on the ring each day during the process. If the ring's wearer dies while wearing the ring, the soul of the lich has a 25 percent chance to take over the corpse and use it as a new body. But if the ring is created entirely in the area of a hallow spell with the everlasting rest effect, the tie to the lich's soul is broken

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
items.entry: The lich troll is remnants of early attempts of powerful spellcasters to transfer their souls into trolls.

items.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
items.entry: The lich troll is immune to poison and resistant to necrotic damage. It regenerates and can be killed only by acid, fire, or radiant damage

items.name: Lieutenant Petra & Captain Ansom Lang

entries: Petra Lang is a fit and nimble teenager with long black hair, a narrow, pointed chin, and bold features. She wears the Lanterns' hooded green cloak and light {@item studded leather armor|XPHB} with a lieutenant's insignia on her shoulder pauldron.

Ansom Lang is an athletic teenager with long black hair and a short neat beard, angular jaw, and rugged features. He is garbed in a hooded green cloak and {@item studded leather armor|XPHB} of the Hooded Lanterns that prominently displays a captain's insignia on his shoulder

Petra, the youngest of the two, has spent most of her life training under the Hooded Lanterns. She prides herself on her marksmanship and scavenging, and knows she is looked up to by many of the soldiers. She is a proud and friendly commander who the troops are happy to follow.
Ansom plans to become the Lord Commander once Elias retires. He is a stern commander who leads by example, displaying incredible discipline and unwavering loyalty to his adopted father

entries.name: Personality Trait
entries: I see the value in those willing to risk their lives in the ruins. I have great insight and trust in my own judgment of character.

entries.name: Ideal
entries: The right path is often the harder path, but it is always one worth walking.

entries.name: Bond
entries: I was adopted by Elias Drexel, who raised and trained me. I don't want to let him down.

entries.name: Flaw
entries: I am too open and trusting of people who claim to be on the same side as me, and I put a lot of weight in counting on people who I assume are able to handle themselves.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Petra is a skilled archer and skirmisher. She prefers to keep her foes at range to gain a vantage point over them in combat. She is a cunning scout who is more likely to set up an ambush than attack directly. When pinned down, she tries to move out of melee into a more advantageous position. If she is low on options, she attempts to escape.

Ansom is a skilled swordsman who prefers to engage his foes in melee combat. He typically starts combat from a good vantage point by attacking with his bow and then moving closer to unleash a flurry of sword attacks. He is a confident and aggressive, and has pushed the Hooded Lanterns through many decisive victories over the horrors of Drakkenheim.
Ansom has enough sense to know when a combat encounter is threatening to cost the lives of his unit, and will fall back or retreat if his instincts tell him it is the better move.
Nothing like family to keep you honest. That and a sword that makes you tell the truth.

name: Lightning Giant
entries: {@i Wayward Children of Storms}

{@color Standing more than twice as tall as a human, this gray-skinned giant has pure white eyes and hands that crackle with tendrils of electricity. A bolt of lightning coalesces in the giant's hands into a staff of glowing blue-white energy that it wields with fearsome intent.|006abe}

Lightning giants dwell in large, windy caves and storm-struck keeps in mountainous terrain, raising giant goats and keeping dire wolves as pets. They are muscular and humanlike in appearance, with hair constantly blown as if by a gale, and eyes and skin crackling with electricity.

Northlanders sometimes refer to these giants as the children of Thor, a fact the Thunder God is quick to refute. They believe that the first lightning giant resulted from a union between Thor and a particularly attractive hill giant maiden. These tales do not amuse lightning giants, and they take umbrage with anyone who spouts them. The shield-maidens of Sif hold particular hatred for these giants, viewing their mere existence as a slight upon their patron goddess.

While they don't share the same habitat as storm giants, lightning giants revere them for their greater prowess and size, and defer to them whenever they meet. Storm giants don't view lightning giants quite as favorably, viewing them as overly clingy.

name: Lightning Panther
entries: Known as the best ambush hunters of the sky, lightning panthers can travel at great speeds in the form of a lightning bolt before striking with the force and intensity of their namesake. Many hunters have fallen prey to these mighty beasts, but those that can return with the corpse of a lightning panther are celebrated, often incorporating lightning into their clothing and crafts.
{@i This goblin-like creature bears one large, strange eye in the middle of its face. It wears dark and dirty rags, and its spindly claws and arms match its hunched torso.}

entries.name: Ferocious Attitude
entries: Likhos are scrappy fighters. They weaken foes from afar with their magical gaze, then rush forward, shredding the victims with their claws. Once a likho has leapt onto a creature, it shreds flesh using the claws on both its hands and feet.

entries.name: Jeers and Insults
entries: A likho uses its limited telepathy to taunt and jeer at its target from a distance during the hunt. A likho enjoys stalking intelligent humanoids and tormenting them from hiding until discovered or when it grows tired of the hunt.

entries.name: Organ Eaters
entries: Likhos thrive when they drain away luck and aptitude. Once the likho immobilizes a creature, it gnaws at the creature's abdomen with its jagged teeth, devouring the organs of its still-living prey. A likho consumes only a humanoid's organs and leaves the rest of the body behind.

name: Liminal Herald

entries: The amorphous form of the Liminal Herald quivers and ripples as it drifts through the air. Its many spider-like eyes glowing with incomprehensible colors, its flesh changing shape and color in dizzying displays. It whispers in the minds of those who approach it, telling them great truths of unknown worlds, and announcing the coming of its nameless masters.

Liminal Heralds are the scouts and messengers of unknown ancient entities that exist in the furthest reaches of the Space Between Worlds. Whatever the purpose is, their galactic information gathering remains a mystery. Liminal Heralds uncover unfathomable truths and whispered echoes of shattered realities as they seek out realms to beckon the coming of their masters.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill History|XPHB} or {@skill Nature|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine a Liminal Herald, learning the following based on the result.

entries.name: (10+) Guarded Existence
entries: You learn the creature's {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: (15+) Psychic Retribution
entries: You know of the creature's Reflect Pain {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.

entries.name: (20+) Weak but Perceptive
entries: They learn the creature's highest and lowest ability scores.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Liminal Herald is a contaminated entity from the deepest corners of the Space Between Worlds. It undoes creatures atom by atom with its Eldritch Beams. It targets the intellect of other creatures with its Mind Scramble, especially spellcasters {@status Concentration|XPHB|Concentrating} on spells. The Liminal Herald harnesses the very fabric of magic itself and uses that force against mortals who would attempt to dabble in it.

When targeted by an attack, the Liminal Herald bends space and time around it using its Reflect Pain feature, causing the creature who attacked it to take on a mental payload of pain felt by the creature.
If it is reduced below half its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, the Liminal Herald attempts to flee.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Aberration.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Contaminated Ichor, Goopy Ooze, Mucus.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Eyes, Guts, Glands, Flesh.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Tentacles.

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Skin.

entries.name: Dust:
entries: Aberrant Dust.
Some mage waves his hands, a portal opens and this thing eats him. Now I gotta kill you because that was my ride home!
{@i Coiling like a living corkscrew and moving with a scraping hiss, this serpentine creature skates nimbly across ice on long curving claws, maw agape and stinking of a hundred graves.}

entries.name: Swift and Smooth as Ice
entries: Lindwurms have long bodies and crocodilian jaws, but they skitter overland on spindly limbs. Their talons are long and curved, acting as skates or short skis when moving over ice. Few things are swifter on the ice.

entries.name: Sea Hunters
entries: In the wild, lindwurms hunt in groups, looking for breaching whales, seals, or incautious fishermen. They enjoy surrounding and surprising foes. With their considerable cunning, they may skate by their prey at speed, snapping a bite as they pass or snatching up prey with their constricting tails.

My great grandfather spoke of the lindwyrm terrorizing the countryside and devouring whole villages. But it's been so long since anyone has seen the beast, it's likely the creature is long dead. Thank Miklas!

entries.name: Salvage
entries: A dose of {@item lindwyrm venom|GrimHollowLairsEtharis} (see Appendix A of {@adventure Lairs of Etharis|GrimHollowLairsEtharis|21}) can be harvested by someone proficient with a poisoner's kit and succeeds on a {@dc 18} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check, but this must be done within 1 hour of the lindwyrm's death. If the check fails by 5 or more, the harvester instead poisons themselves. This injury poison is worth 1,000 gp.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
items.entry: Lindwyrms sleep for 100 years and when they waken are devastating to communities in its hunting area.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
items.entry: Lindwyrms have a poisonous bite and may swallow creatures they bite.

items.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
items.entry: Lindwyrms can sense vibrations in the ground from as far away as 120 ft.

entries.name: GM Advice
entries: One exciting adventure seed could find a powerful enemy of the adventurers looking to waken and control a lindwyrm. Whether that plot succeeds or not is up to you, but a three-way battle between involving a lindwyrm and other foes should be memorable as the action ebbs and flows.

name: Lion's Blume
entries: Lion's blume is a most peculiar and troublesome plant, feared by beekeepers yet sought after by brewers. Its golden-hued petals are charming to the eye, but at the very heart of this plant lies a gaping maw, ready to snap shut upon any unfortunate bee (or beekeeper) that strays too near. Beekeepers often speak ill of the lion's blume, calling it a weed, for it decimates their hives with alarming efficiency.

entries.name: Pride and Prejudice
entries: The flower grows in clusters, known as "prides," scattered across the windy moors of the Coastal Highlands. Each pride has its own family, or lineage, and it is quite common to find them in silent battle, their roots entwined in a fierce competition, each trying to choke the life from neighboring prides. Because of this natural competition, being kind to one lion's blume plant may incur the jealous wrath from its nearby neighbors.

entries.name: Dangerous but Useful
entries: Despite its ill reputation, brewers hold the lion's blume in high regard. Its milky sap is prized for concocting rare and curious beverages, while the sharp, tooth-like structures within the flower are often harvested for other uses. Thus, though many may curse its presence, there are those who wander the moors in search of the elusive lion's blume, ever mindful of its significant bite.

name: Lionfish King
entries: The Lionfish King is proud, temperamental, and dangerous, yet not wholly beyond the reach of reason. His bristling mane of spines often betrays his mood—whether fair or foul. The Lionfish King's whims are like the weather and his cares range from himself, to the Corruption, to finding a royal bride, and back to himself again. For more on the Lionfish King, see "Domain of the Lionfish King" in the Locations chapter.
{@i The curtain of rippling colors assumes a humanoid form. Its kaleidoscope body shifts and glitters with mesmeric patterns.}

Sometimes known as "light elves" because they assume a vaguely elvish shape, these enigmatic elementals make their home at the edge of the world, where reality bends and physical laws unravel. Liosalfars' mutable bodies are composed entirely of shifting colors. Among themselves, they communicate through flashing patterns and hues, but they talk to others in an echoing, choral tone that seems to emanate from everywhere and nowhere around them.

entries.name: Servants of Fate
entries: Their aims often seem inconsequential or simply baffling, but they've also sundered mountains and toppled kingdoms. Many believe liosalfars are agents of Fate, while others believe their motivations are an alien aesthetic or for their own amusement. Those who've spoken with liosalfars say they talk as if all existence was a sea of patterns and colors to be set in pleasing shapes.

entries.name: Enemies of the Ramag
entries: Liosalfars have a longstanding rivalry with the portal-making ramags, whom they despise as "corruptors of the patterns."

name: Living Biohazard

entries: This gelatinous blob drips and oozes over the ground, rolling like a slow viscous spill. At times appearing liquid, at others like a gelation, and still others it appears to take a more solid form. Its colors change and shift in alternating hues, sometimes mimicking its surroundings until the thing almost disappears from view completely.

Living Biohazards are the failed experiments of Chemists striving to perfect alchemical concoctions of far greater potency. However, there is still value in their failures. Creating slivers of sentience within chemical compounds is no small feat, and the Living Biohazard, although not perfect, has provided Chemists with a chemical defense system of sorts.

The Living Biohazard is an insatiable ooze that slides around its environment like a spilled liquid looking for creatures to dissolve. The corrosive gelatin can stick to walls and ceilings and drop down on unsuspecting creatures. It is, even in its simple-minded nature, a persistent and deadly hunter.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Medicine|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks to Study a Living Biohazard, learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (15+) Thick and Acidic
entries: You know of the Living Biohazard's Liquid Form and Hazardous Fumes traits.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Living Biohazard remains completely still until it is close enough to either drop down onto a creature or slide into position surrounding it. Its only goal is to dissolve and consume. It does not flee.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Ooze.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Contaminated Ichor, Goopy Ooze, Acidic Bile.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Guts.

name: Living City

entries: An eerie light shines within the oddly intact yet ramshackle house across the road. The door hangs ajar, gently banging open and closed as the mist and winds whip through the dark streets. As you step inside the building, the lurching floorboards creak and groan. The furnishings are bizarrely orderly, and you notice nary a speck of dust or debris accumulated in the otherwise ordinary rooms. After a moment you notice a strange glistening liquid seeping out between the timbers, and the odd reddish goo that melts between the mortar of the bricks. Suddenly, the door slams shut, the windows close and shutter, and the entire room warps and shifts. Hundreds of yellow eyes open across the walls, grin ning toothy mouths form on the ceilings and floors. Glistening barbed pseudopods reach up from the furniture, as you realize you have stepped right into the gullet of a patient predator.

Some say that the greatest threat adventurers and faction agents face in Drakkenheim is the city itself. The unstable magic of the Haze makes navigation through the city streets perilous and disorienting. It often feels like the alleys and buildings are changing position around travelers, as if Drakkenheim were slowly weaving a maze around them. Damaged buildings are filled with rubble, prone to collapse, and the perfect places for monsters to hide in ambush. Dangers and hazards abound from the transformed landscape, and tales are told of structures themselves magically transmuted into strange substances, the stone and wood becoming metals, glass, sand, or even partially made from flesh and bone, as if a twisted artist had sculpted the buildings out of macabre materials.

Just as the Haze has awakened unhinged sentience in the elements and guardian constructs of Drakkenheim, bizarre {@table Arcane Anomalies|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Arcane Anomaly} occasionally cause the furnishings and buildings of the city to awaken. Eyes, mouths, and even tendrils may appear on surfaces within. Those who brave the interior rooms and halls hear whispers in their minds as the building develops its own personality. On rare occasions, however, the internal composition of objects mutates into a metamorphic goo, imbuing the structure with the ability to change its form and composition in nearly limitless ways. When this occurs to a normal object like a table or chest of drawers, the result is a typical mimic.

A Living City emerges when this happens to an entire building. Also called manor mimics or werehouses, these deadly creatures slowly meander through the city, finding empty plots or taking the place of ruined buildings. Once they find a suitable location, they may quite literally set up shop. Due to their nature, a Living City does not create the appearance of a damaged or ruined structure, so adventurers may be naturally wary of oddly intact buildings they encounter while roaming the ruins.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they {@action Study|XPHB} a Living City, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (15+) Animated Building.
entries: You are aware of the Living City's Structural Form and No Exit traits, as well as its {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: (20+) Escape Routes.
entries: You recognize that destroying the creature's walls and doors creates exits, but these are short-lived because of its Shifting Form Epic Action.

entries.name: (25+) Slow, Smart, and Tough.
entries: You learn of the Living City's strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: A Living City takes the form of an oddly intact residence, workshop, or warehouse using its Structural Form trait, and waits for hapless creatures to wander inside. A Living City may deceive characters into entering it using its telepathy and Haunting Whispers. It suppresses its Digestive Aura and so it can take full advantage of its False Appearance trait.

Typically, a Living City shapes its body to create outer rooms that have walls bordering the edge of the Living City's space, and inner rooms deep within which do not have walls, ceilings, or floors immediately adjacent to spaces outside the Living City. The Living City will create doors, windows, or even stairs within it so that its prey can easily move from outside, to the outer rooms, and then further inside to the inner rooms. Often, the Living City might place any treasure or valuables it has collected in these inner rooms as bait.

Once a few characters have entered one of its innermost rooms, the Living City attacks and activates its Digestive Aura. When it rolls Initiative, it uses its No Exit trait to close all the doors and windows in its body, trapping characters inside. Then, it attacks them with its Grasping Tendrils, Bite, and Haunting Whispers, while using its Shifting Form Epic Action to slowly change its interior, separating the characters and cutting off their escape routes.

Should the player characters break a hole in one of its walls, the Living City uses its Shifting Form trait to plug the hole. Note that some area-of-effect attacks and spells (such as {@spell Burning Hands|XPHB}) can damage or destroy multiple sections of the Living City. However, a Living City can only take damage from one section being destroyed per turn. If characters manage to slip outside the Living City through a breached hole or exit, the Living City may use its Grasping Tendrils to pull them back in. It then tries to quickly seal them inside again with Shifting Form.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Montrosity.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Contaminated Ichor, Goopy Ooze, Acidic Bile

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Glands.

Contaminated Elementals can be found all over Drakkenheim, often in areas where the eldritch magics are especially concentrated. Many who have encountered these elementals have spoken of the city itself coming to life to attack them. Reports of ruins reaching out and crushing adventurers, burning flames moving and hunting with minds of their own, or contaminated pools lurching to engulf passersby have been heard. Even the blowing air itself has mustered parts of the Haze into shifting clouds that stalk adventurers through the streets. These magical creatures are a constant reminder that nothing in the city can be trusted, and that nowhere is truly safe.

name: Living Deep Haze

entries: The Haze enveloping you begins to churn and swirl, gradually coalescing into a dense mass of octarine fog. A ghostly visage emerges as a nebulous form takes shape, its features twisted in an eerie semblance of anguish. Flashes of contaminated energy crackle and spark inside the cloud, casting fleeting, sinister lights which mimic the movements of a tortured face. This roiling fog floats through the ruins, drifting like a specter haunted by its own turbulent essence.

True to their name, these Contaminated Air Elementals lurk within the thickest parts of the Haze, seamlessly blending in with the deadly environment. They exist to spread the contaminating mist and fog through their bodies, and delight in causing mutation and monstrous transformation.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they {@action Study|XPHB} a Living Deep Haze, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (10+) Mundane Immunity
entries: You are aware of the elemental's {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: (15+) Animate Haze
entries: You know of the creature's Fog Form and Deep Haze traits.

entries.name: (20+) Fast but Dim-Witted
entries: You understand its strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: When it encounters an uncontaminated creature, the Living Deep Haze rapidly moves into its space thanks to its Fog Form trait. It then tries to remain there as much as possible so the creature is exposed to its Deep Haze trait. The Living Deep Haze wants to transform its targets into monsters, so it uses its Slam attacks to knock them Unconscious so they can awaken to a new existence as mutant horrors.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Elemental.

entries.name: Dust:
entries: Elemental Dust.
{@i The small, rough wax sculpture of a human stands at attention, a halo of light flickering around its head from some source behind it.}

entries.name: Enchanted Wicks
entries: Living wicks are obedient wax statues brought to life by an enchanted wick that runs from the nape of their neck to their lower back. When new, a living wick looks and moves like a human. However, as the wick burns, the wax features melt, and the statue takes on a twisted, hunchbacked appearance.

entries.name: Short-Lived as a Candle
entries: Living wicks are powered by flames, and therefore they have a predetermined life cycle. They are typically reduced to formless lumps in a month, but some say a living wick's affordability more than makes up for its inevitable obsolescence. Individuals looking to quickly construct a building or fortification without the expense of paid labor or the questionable ethics of necromancy find living wicks obedient and efficient, as do those needing an army for a single battle. They are active only when their wicks are lit, and they respond only to the commands of whoever lit them. This makes it easy to transfer living wicks between owners, even those not well-versed in the use of magic.

entries.name: Explosive Ends
entries: The amount of magical energy contained within a living wick, paired with the manner in which it is released, gives them a remarkable capability for self-destruction. If their controller demands it, all living wicks can release the magic contained within their form all at once, engulfing themselves and anyone nearby in flames. This can make storing them a gamble, but many see it as an asset, especially those seeking to destroy evidence or anonymously attack their enemies.

name: Ljugar the Liar
entries: Treacherous cult captain

name: Loathsome Gag Fly

entries: This massive fly buzzes through the air, bobbing and darting with a loud buzz of its wings. Its huge eyes make up most of its round form, saliva and mucus oozing from its small mandibles. Its abdomen is slightly translucent, with a purplish green liquid sloshing around inside its bloated form. It screams in a strangely human voice that sounds like it is crying for help.

The flies grow fat in Drakkenheim. Corpses do not rot, which makes them excellent sources of food for the rats, Garmyr, and bugs of the city. Many bloated corpses are now ripe with large green maggots that feast on the dead contaminated flesh. When these maggots evolve into Loathsome Gag Flies, they buzz around areas of death in the city. Attracted to fresh corpses, or piles of dead bodies, or even following along with a group of {@creature Haze Husk|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} or {@creature Haze Wight|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} hoping to munch on bits of their flesh. The city cistern and the old well in Slaughterstone Square is a known hot spot for a large nest of Gag Flies.

The Gag Flies are bloated and overgrown flies whose acidic mucus has now formed a pouch that occupies most of their large thorax. Like all flies, they use this acidic mucus to dissolve possible food and prepare it for eating. Due to their large size, this results in a horrible experience for adventurers wandering past a group of these flies, who all vomit sprays of burning acid onto their prey and buzz down to feed on the burning targets.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Nature|XPHB}) checks to {@action Study|XPHB} a Loathsome Gag Fly, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (5+) Flying Monstrosity.
entries: You know the Gag Fly's creature type and speeds.

entries.name: (10+) Explosive Bile.
entries: You learn of the Gag Fly's Bloat Burst Reaction.

entries.name: (15+) Bestial Minded.
entries: You recognize the Gag Fly's highest and lowest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Loathsome Gag Fly is a simple-minded creature who wants to feed on flesh and lay larva on the corpses of the dead. It sprays acid on any creature that it sees nearby in an attempt to weaken it. It then lands on them and begins feeding.

Gag Flies usually attack in groups and care very little for the wellbeing of each other. As a matter of fact, when a Gag Fly is killed and explodes in a shower of acid, this usually causes other nearby flies to go into a feeding frenzy on targets sprayed in the gore, as they are drawn to any flesh dissolving in the acids of their mucus.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Monstrosity.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Monster Blood, Contaminated Ichor, Acidic Bile, Mucus.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Eyes, Guts, Glands.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Mandibles, Needles.

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Carapace.

name: Lob Frog

entries: The frog-like creature has sharp spines down its back, with mottled green and brown flesh; a large segmented mouth that bisects its face; and a large, black, soulless eye peering out from either side. Its insect-like pincers drip and gnash as it huddles close to a mound of translucent, sticky, octarine eggs throbbing and writhing with contaminated energy. It holds one of the throbbing spawn in its webbed hand, ready to hurl it directly at you.

The {@link Drann River} flows into Drakkenheim from the Kesselwald Forest to the northeast. On some of the especially quiet and warm nights, you could hear the chorus of croaking frogs from within the woods close to the river. These frogs were commonly found there, and large numbers of them would migrate down the Drann River into the northern parts of the city, especially around King's Gate. Today, the frog's migration continues, but now the contaminated waters of the Drann have caused the amphibians to bloat to horrific size, and also wildly changed their reproductive cycle.

These mutated monsters are now commonplace along the river and make crossing at any point dangerous. Their eggs do not hatch on their own but require a host body to feed on to complete the metamorphosis. For this reason, the frogs weaponize their contaminated eggs, tossing them at passing adventurers, scouts, and even other contaminated creatures, hence their moniker: "Lob" Frogs.

The Lob Frog produces hundreds of eggs and hedges its bets by throwing them at any creature it finds, hoping that a few of them have the opportunity to gestate into a newborn Lob Frog. Newly formed Lob Frogs always carry a minor element of the host. A Lob Frog formed from a Ratling may have rodent-like ears or whiskers, where one formed from a human may carry the host's eye color.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Animal Handling|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Nature|XPHB}) checks to {@action Study|XPHB} a Lob Frog, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (5+) Poisonous Skin.
entries: You recognize the Lob Frog's {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities} and Poison Skin trait.

entries.name: (10+) Hurled Eggs.
entries: You are aware of the Lob Frog's Throw Frogspawn action.

entries.name: (15+) Assured Amphibian.
entries: You know the Lob Frog's Strength and Charisma ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Lob Frogs are keen to keep their distance from predators and threats, but are constantly on the lookout for hosts for their offspring. They attempt to lob their contaminated eggs at potential threats, hoping to produce more Lob Frogs. If confronted directly, their Poison Skin acts as a defense while they use their Standing Leap to escape unfavorable situations.

If a Lob Frog has at least two or more targets with attached eggs, or if they are reduced below half Hit Points, they leap away to find somewhere safe and wet to hide. They would rather not risk their life, and simply hope to infect as many targets as possible to continue their species.

entries: Monstrosity.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Monster Blood, Contaminated Ichor, Venom.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Eyes, Heart, Brain, Guts, Glands, Flesh.

entries.name: Bones:
entries: Skull, Spine, Ribs.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Teeth.

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Skin, Webbed Membrane.

name: Longtooth
entries: Thulsamir's companion

Lord Commander Elias Drexel is a man in his early fifties. He is stocky and imposing with a furrowed brow and a grim frown on his wide and angular face. His harsh features are framed with a thick moustache, side chops, and a mane of long braided brown hair. He is garbed in chainmail armour with heavy leather gloves and boots, worn under a fur-lined dark green cloak and iron pauldrons. He wears a pinned brooch - the Lord Commander's Badge, the symbol of his office. A quiver, a longbow, and two longswords are strung on his back.

items.name: Personality Trait
items.entry: I am blunt and direct, and expect my soldiers to obey my commands and deliver results promptly. I find no humor in anything.

items.name: Ideal
items.entry: Loyalty and trust are priceless. They must be carefully given, but staunchly held. There is nothing worse than betrayal and treason.

items.name: Bond
items.entry: During the Civil War, I switched sides and killed several scions of House von Kessel who could have claimed the throne. I once believed it was for the right cause, but now I feel personally responsible for breaking the royal line. My mission in Drakkenheim is penance and redemption.

items.name: Flaw
items.entry: I'm filled with rage and conflict because of my contradictory actions and beliefs, and I don't take defeat, setbacks, or even missteps lightly.

entries: Lord Commander Elias Drexel was appointed to the office of Lord Commander before the fall of Drakkenheim, and was outside the city leading training drills when the meteor fell. Afterwards, he took part in three military expeditions to reclaim Drakkenheim, and saw firsthand their horrors. He then went on to fight in the Westemär Civil War alongside Mannfred von Kessel. However, the idea that his soldiers died for nothing in Drakkenheim festered in his mind, and made him doubt Mannfred's ability to be a good ruler. He secretly participated in a successful conspiracy to assassinate Mannfred von Kessel. Little did he know that shortly thereafter, tragedy would soon befall Cecilia von Kessel. He isn't exactly proud of his choice to betray Mannfred, and that causes him considerable guilt, regret, and internal self-loathing.

items.name: Lord Commander Elias Drexel

entries: Elias Drexel is a man in his early fifties. He is stocky and imposing with a furrowed brow and a grim frown on his wide and angular face. His harsh features are framed with a thick moustache, side chops, and mane of long braided brown hair. He is garbed in chainmail armor with heavy leather gloves and boots, worn under a fur-lined dark green cloak and iron pauldrons. He wears a pinned brooch depicting the Seal of Drakkenheim, the symbol of his office as Lord Commander. A quiver, a {@item longbow|XPHB}, and two longswords are strung on his back.

Elias Drexel was appointed to the office of Lord Commander of Westemär before the fall of Drakkenheim, and was outside the city leading training drills when the meteor fell. Afterwards, he took part in three military expeditions to reclaim Drakkenheim, and saw firsthand the city's horrors. When the expeditions failed and the nation fell into civil war, Elias Drexel found himself caught between mixed allegiances. He is haunted by the ghosts of his past mistakes and those who died under his command, and believes that his redemption will come only when Drakkenheim is reclaimed.

entries.name: Personality Trait
entries: I have great responsibilities and have no time for senseless humor. I never cease to worry about our struggling militia's desperate task to reclaim these monster infested ruins. I have no patience for anything or anyone who doesn't further the Hooded Lanterns objectives.

entries.name: Ideal
entries: Loyalty and trust are priceless. It must be carefully given, but staunchly held. There is nothing worse than betrayal and treason.

entries.name: Bond
entries: During the Civil War, I switched sides and killed several scions of House von Kessel who could have claimed the throne. I once believed it was for the right cause, but now
I feel personally responsible for breaking the royal line. My mission in Drakkenheim is penance and redemption.

entries.name: Flaw
entries: I'm filled with rage and conflict because of my contradictory actions and beliefs, and I don't take defeat, setbacks, or even missteps lightly.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Elias Drexel typically leads several {@creature Hooded Lantern Veteran|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Hooded Lantern Veterans} into battle, using his Command action to grant them additional attacks while calling in artillery strikes as often as possible. Drexel himself operates as a skirmisher, switching between melee and ranged attacks to control the flow of battle.

This horrific albino garmyr stands well over twelve feet tall. He is covered in a mass of yellowish-white mangy fur, bloodstained and scarred from countless battles, and clad in a patchwork armour of leather, chain, and bladed plate with trophies—mummified heads—hanging from his belt. A mane of bony spines and tufts of barbed grey hair jut out from his head and down his back to a long white tail braided with skulls and bone fragments. His snarling visage is filled with long, razor-sharp fangs and smouldering red eyes. The Lord of The Feast holds an oversized longbow, strung with thick sinew. A quiver on his back holds enormous arrows, some bristling with barbed snares, others connected to coils of chains around the beast's wrists, while others are tipped with delerium shards.

name: Lord of the Feast

entries: This albino Garmyr stands well over 12 feet tall, covered in yellowish-white mangy fur, bloodstained and scarred from countless battles and clad in a patchwork armor of leather, chain, and bladed plate. Mummified heads hang from his belt. A mane of bony spines and tufts of barbed hair jut from his head and run down his back to a long white tail braided with skulls and bone fragments. A snarling visage sports long, jagged fangs and smoldering red eyes. The Lord of the Feast holds an oversized longbow, stringed with thick sinew. A quiver on his back holds enormous arrows. Some bristle with barbed snares, others are connected to coils of chains around the beasts wrists, while others are tipped with {@item shard|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium shards}.

The Garmyr band together under a great warlord called the Lord of the Feast, who has grown a fearsome reputation as an expert hunter, tracker, and warrior. It seems that the Lord of the Feast enjoys hunting and killing for sport, and hanging his trophies in his grim cathedral. His favorite prey, of course, is adventurers—he revels in tracking them through the city and hanging their gear upon his trophy shelves.

The Lord of the Feast rose to power amongst the Garmyr when he emerged as a large, albino wolf amongst their pack. He was given the name Ghost due to his pale fur. Even at a young age, the Lord of the Feast was bigger than most other Garmyr. However, the creature was also cunning and smart. He knew he could best most foes with brute strength, but learned to control his insatiable hunger for bloodlust to focus on the skills needed to take down larger creatures. Through patience, a skilled hand with a bow, and using tools to modify his arrows, the Lord of the Feast began proving himself the strongest and most skilled hunter of all the Garmyr.

When the previous warlord, a gray Garmyr named Blood-Wolf, challenged Ghost to one-on-one combat, the Garmyr gathered to watch the contest. They speculated that Blood-Wolf called for the challenge out of fear of Ghost's burgeoning abilities and influence. Many Garmyr questioned Blood-Wolf challenging a pup half his age to a death match, but Blood-Wolf underestimated how powerful Ghost had already become. The match ended within seconds when three arrows penetrated Blood-Wolf 's chest. The first bound him in place, the second {@condition poisoned} him, and the third reeled him toward Ghost, who then tore his head off with his teeth. Holding up the head of Blood-Wolf, Ghost called for the Garmyr to feast on the corpse of their fallen leader. He was henceforth known as the Lord of the Feast.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine the Lord of the Feast learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (5+) Difficult to Kill
entries: You know of the creature's Regeneration ability.

entries.name: (10+) Dangerous Archer
entries: You recognize that he carries special arrows revealing his Poison Arrow, Ensnaring Arrow, and Harpoon Arrow attacks.

entries.name: (15+) Cunning Combatant
entries: You learn their strongest and weakest saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Lord of the Feast stalks the Temple Ward of Drakkenheim with his war dogs, searching for glorious kills. He seeks out the most fearsome monsters, and loves picking fights with faction agents and adventurers. When a band of plucky heroes enters his territory, the Lord of the Feast tracks and hunts them until they leave the Inner City or he has their skulls.
The Lord of the Feast uses a variety of arrows in combat:
Poison Arrow to debilitate foes, Ensnaring Arrow to stop them fleeing, and Harpoon Arrow to pull them toward him to engage in melee combat.
If the Lord of the Feast is reduced below 100 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, he attempts to escape, but regroups as soon as possible with more hunters in tow to continue the hunt.

I've been on many hunts looking for my prize, it's not often you are the one being hunted.

{@i Astride a midnight horse sits a shirtless elven huntsman. His broad chest is thickly muscled and sports tattooed knot work. Great stag antlers crest the huntsman's head, curving above his rich brown hair. The pale green glow that shines from his eyes obscures the elf 's strong features, and a massive spear twined with glowing green vines drives forward in his clenched fist}.

The baying of shadow hounds, the thundering of hoof beats, and a brassy horn note; the Wild Hunt is coming, and pity its quarry. The Lord of the Hunt is an enigma among the fey nobles. His true identity beyond title and position as master of the Wild Hunt is unknown, but he has some connection to the Black Prince of the shadow fey—while also answering to elvish druids and consorting with powerful hags and dryads.

entries.name: The Wild Hunt
entries: The Lord's court is the Wild Hunt itself, a group of huntsmen, revelers, intelligent hounds, and poor souls they sweep up in their frenzy. His home, if he has any permanent dwelling, is as mysterious as his true identity. He and his Hunt constantly move between the Plane of Shadow and the most ancient forests.

entries.name: Fey Lords and Ladies
entries: Fey are capricious, mischievous, and often dangerous beings. However, despite their chaotic reputations, they do follow a certain set of rules. These rules—widely misunderstood by outsiders—are codified and enforced by a cadre of lofty fey nobility. Befitting any courtly structure, the fey bow to lords and ladies: eldritch creatures of immense power who rule the courts.

entries.name: Heads of State
entries: The fey lords and ladies are beings of high station and prodigious personal power. Each rules over at least a great city if not an entire nation. No matter the scope of a fey noble's domain, in his or her eyes, a fey ruler's word is law. Outsiders might not understand the edicts and interdicts of a fey noble, but that's no protection against the harsh penalties that await any who break them, knowingly or otherwise.

entries.name: Vacant Thrones
entries: When a lord or lady of the fey dies, the court does not remain leaderless for long. Ambitious beings among the fey always hunger for more power and covet the stations of their superiors. After a traditional month or year of mourning, vicious power struggles winnow the weak and pave the way for the most cunning or the strongest to take the court's vacant throne.

entries.name: The Lord of the Hunt's Lair
entries: If the Lord of the Hunt has any permanent lair, it is unknown to all but his closest confidants. While the Wild Hunt is a thing of beautiful and deadly grace on the move, the Lord's encampment becomes his lair when the Hunt settles for any length of time. Tents and pavilions house the Lord and his Hunt, and great, roaring fires roast the day's kills. The hours pass with revelry, feasting, physical contests, and strong drink.
{@i Lounging on a large river rock, this breathtaking fey calls plaintively to travelers.}

entries.name: Death to Men
entries: A people born from an ancient oath to the River King, the loreleis' cruelty stems from whatever happened to their people long ago that brought about their transformation into loreleis. Now, these callous river sirens compete with one another in manipulating and destroying male travelers, using their deadly kisses to great effect.

entries.name: Beautiful Humanoids
entries: Although legends describe the lorelei as golden-haired and fair-skinned, they come in all varieties, taking on the form of their most frequent prey. While most resemble sensual humans, a lorelei's form can include elf, dwarf, and, in some recorded cases, even orc or hobgoblin.

entries.name: Ignore Women
entries: Women travelers are vexing for the lorelei. While the siren's powers affect women as readily as men, the lorelei lacks the urge to destroy them. Women traveling alone or in all-female groups may pass through a lorelei's territory safely, and they might even make peaceful contact.

items: {@creature Lorno Burrowbright|HumblewoodTales|Lorno} [he/him] and {@creature Lanelle Burrowbright|HumblewoodTales} [she/her], a pair of jerbeen siblings hail from a small village down the Talongrip Coast and have only worked for Petra for a year. Both siblings use the stat block for a {@creature jerbeen commoner|HumblewoodTales}. They are neutral good.

name: Lothrem, the Wreathed Dragon
entries: Initially a frightened and orphaned hatchling, Lothrem has grown in a curious manner. Now a full-sized and fully capable ancient dragon, their wisdom and natural magic are mighty indeed, shaping their appearance and the very weather above their hidden Warrens lair.

More in tune with nature than a typical gold dragon, Lothrem has verdant green scales, and grass and flowers grow from their back and the outside of their wings. They have elk-like antlers that wrap around their head, seeming to form a natural and regal crown. When they beat their wings, the air smells sweet like a forest glen, and bits of leaves and grass swirl about.

Unfortunately, the years of protection and isolation have not been kind to Lothrem, and for the last 500 years, they have been overcome with a bout of sadness and acute pain each day, resulting in a consistent drizzling rainfall above.
Perhaps release, even a temporary one, from this gilded cage would resolve the matter, but the Circle is unwilling to break tradition and endanger the city.
{@i This massive creature combines the torso of an ogre and the body of an elephant as it lumbers through the open plains.}

entries.name: Nomadic Families
entries: Loxodas live in small herds of two to three extended families. Several of these communities will usually cluster together, allowing members to move between groups as they get older. They have no permanent settlements, and instead loxoda families travel to new areas when they deplete the available food. Voracious omnivores, a family of loxodas will quickly strip trees bare of leaves, or hunt and cook an entire elephant.

entries.name: Often Underestimated
entries: Many people assume that loxodas are as dull witted as the ogres they resemble. This is often a fatal mistake, as the loxoda are quite intelligent. Their simple equipment and straightforward living come not from a lack of skill or knowledge, but their own isolationism and xenophobia. Their immense size and quadruped body make it difficult for them to mine metal ore, and they violently reject communications and trade with other people. The little metal they can gather is either taken from the bodies of their prey or stolen in raids on dwarven, human, or gnoll settlements.

entries.name: Vestigial Tusks
entries: All loxodas have curved tusks. While they are too small for use in even ritual combat, they are often decorated with intricate carvings or inlays or are dyed in a pattern developed by their family. Each individual also adapts the patterns with their own individual marks, often inspired by important events in their lives. Some loxodas put golden rings or jeweled bracelets stolen from humanoids onto their tusks as trophies. A loxoda matriarch may have long, dangling chains of such ornaments, indicating her high status and long life.

items: [he/him]

An aged vulpin with a prosthetic leg who was once {@creature Petra Cloudburst|HumblewoodTales|Petra's} first mate, and who now serves as the manager of The Crimson Rose. Lucas is patient, kind, and possesses an affection for The Captain, which he finds difficult to act on due to their professional relationship. He cares deeply for Petra and would do anything to help her achieve her dreams.

entries: Born Sevran Dusktalon, this notorious hitman gained the nickname "Lucky" for his uncanny ability to eliminate targets and escape unseen, even against impossible odds. What many have discounted as luck is, in fact, the result of Sevran's careful observation and keen intellect.

Lucky takes his jobs very seriously, and takes a careful, methodical approach to his work. He will devote himself to studying a target for weeks before striking, and will not accept more than one assignment at a time.

This young male dusk corvum was a former assassin employed by various criminal contacts throughout the city. He has dark, iridescent plumage with a prominent neck-ruff and amber-colored eyes. He is known to hide poisoned daggers on his person.

images.title: {@b Lucky}, 4,500 gp. Wanted For: Fraud, Extortion, Murder, Racketeering, Theft, & Smuggling

entries: Lucretia Mathias is a willowy and wizened woman with piercing eyes and pursed lips. She is in her early nineties, and keeps her greying black hair in a coiled bun beneath a linen shawl. She wears simple grey robes, and clutches a heavy leather-bound tome. A glowing golden crystal dangles from a silver chain around her neck. Her garb lightly conceals the delerium shard embedded in her heart.

items.name: Personality Trait
items.entry: I speak in proverbs and quote scripture when I speak, inspiring others to interpret my cryptic words and come to their own revelations.

items.name: Ideal
items.entry: The brightest lights shine in the darkest of places. None are beyond redemption, and all may find their inner truth and purpose by following the Falling Fire.

items.name: Bond
items.entry: I have foreseen the inevitable end of our world, but through our sacred self-sacrifice we shall set alight the Sacred Flame to bring enlightenment and salvation to the universe.

items.name: Flaw
items.entry: I only reveal the greatest truths I have seen to those I am certain can grasp them fully, and will understand them as I do.

items.name: Lucretia Mathias

entries: Lucretia Mathias is a willowy and wizened woman with piercing eyes and pursed lips. She is in her early nineties and keeps her graying black hair in a coiled bun beneath a linen shawl. Lucretia wears simple gray robes, and clutches a heavy leather-bound tome. A glowing golden crystal dangles from a silver chain around her neck. Her garb lightly conceals the delerium shard embedded in her heart.

The prophetic founder of the Followers of the Falling Fire was once a prominent Flamekeeper of the Sacred Flame. She was cast out and declared a heretic for her blasphemous insistence in the divinity of delerium.

entries.name: Personality Trait
entries: I am devout. believe intensely in my faith and will give those seeking me a chance to speak. I care deeply for those who seek me out, bringing my full wisdom and passion to bear.

entries.name: Ideal
entries: The brightest lights shine in the darkest of places.
I will find my truth through my commitment to the light.
Those who follow me will be spared when the time comes.

entries.name: Bond
entries: The Meteor. I know the meteor is an early coming of the Tarnas comet, symbolizing all I base my faith upon. Only by coming to the Crater and finding yourself within can you be purified and cleansed of all your sins.

entries.name: Flaw
entries: I only reveal the greatest truths I have seen to those I am certain can fully grasp and understand them as I do.

name: Luma Cleric of Ardea
entries: Clerics of Ardea travel the Wood on holy pilgrimages to sacred groves resplendent with life fostered by the Dawnmother. They spread Ardea's message of kindness wherever they go, taking it upon themselves to protect all life, great and small. Clerics serve the communities they pass through as healers, mediators, and occasionally as valiant defenders. Lumas who heed the call of the Amaranthine find their natural charisma and mystic talents to be of great help as they walk the cleric's path.

name: Luma Wizard
entries: It is widely believed among the birdfolk that only those with focused minds can master the subtle art of magic. For unknown reasons, perhaps their inherent connection to fate or particular manner of engaging with the world, lumas are able to tap into the mystical and magical forces with ease.
{@i A hulking figure floats in the air, a winged horror painted in mist and moonlight.}

entries.name: Corruptors of the Moon
entries: Lunar devils can be found subverting druidical orders or leading packs of werewolves. They are a lazy breed of devil and prefer lounging in the light of the moon over more vigorous activity. The only exception is an opportunity to corrupt druids and moon-worshippers, pitting them against followers of sun gods.

entries.name: Vain and Boastful
entries: Lunar devils are as vain as they are indolent. Tales the fey tell involve thwarting them by appealing to their vanity. Lunar devils frequently befriend the dark fey.

entries.name: Flying in Darkness
entries: In combat, lunar devils sometimes bring allies along, bestowing magical flight on them. The devils stay in areas of moonlight whenever they can. Lunar devils have excellent vision in total darkness, though, and are happy to use that against foes. They prefer attacking from range, allowing allies to take the brunt of any opposition.
If you find a statue in the wild with its mouth open in a scream, flee. Best case, it's an artist working out their twisted ideas. Worst case, you'll be a statue soon.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Someone who has proficiency with alchemist's supplies can take four lupilisk venom fangs, or just the two fangs of one lupilisk elder, and treat them with reagents worth 250 gp per tooth for 3 days. A successful treatment requires the alchemist to succeed on a {@dc 15} Intelligence or Wisdom check. During the treatment time, somebody must also cast lesser restoration on the fangs. After a successful treatment, someone who has proficiency with jeweler's tools can fashion the fangs, now blackened, into a necklace, creating a periapt of proof against poison. If the wearer attunes to the periapt, the amulet also provides that wearer immunity to being petrified.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
items.entry: A lupilisk's bite imparts a petrifying venom to prey. This magic toxin grows more potent as the lupilisk ages.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
items.entry: Lupilisks live in packs with an elder couple in the lead. This couple are the parents of most other pack members.

name: Lupine
entries: Werewolves, or what Kindred call the lupines, are another powerful denizen of the supernatural world. Lupines are overwhelmingly strong, terrifyingly fast, immensely resilient, and have held a frenzied level of hatred for the Kindred for as long as either side can remember. When one is not taking the shape of a human or a wolf, it stands on two legs to become a ten-foot-tall killing machine of fur, claws, and fangs who can split stone with a single slash and endure horrific amounts of damage. A single lupine is more than a match for a group of younger Kindred, and even powerful Kindred are wise to give pause before engaging unprepared.

name: Lurker in the Dark

entries: {@i Thing That Goes Bump in the Night}

Lurkers in the dark are wicked Fey creatures who prey upon the fearful, vulnerable, and alone. They resemble nightmarishly distorted people with gray skin, lank hair, and three-fingered, clawed hands. Their limbs move in impossible ways, allowing them to slip through and hide within spaces that seem far too small. They delight in stoking their victim's fears by whispering from spaces a person couldn't fit. When the terror crests, the lurkers strike, drag their victims into the dark, and vanish with them.

entries.name: Secret
entries: {@condition Frightened|XPHB} children know that lurkers in the dark can be held at bay by clutching a beloved stuffed animal.

name: Lurker on the Threshold

entries: Latching onto the Thin Places between realities, a cackling chorus of chaotic laughter in hysterical and dissonant tones tears through the minds of those who bear witness to the cosmic being. As it peers out with its three unblinking dark pools of eyes, it observes and surveys the realities as its mass of fleshy tendrils dangle from its slimy form. It ripples with black voidlike hues and splashes of deep purples and blues as if its flesh was a moving image of the cosmos.

The Lurker on the Threshold is a vile and maniacal being, drifting into our realm through Thin Places and screaming in the minds of those it witnesses. It wanders the Space Between Worlds and feeds on the raw arcane energy found in the rifts between realities, and on the shattered atoms of dead realms. It is a creature who exists on the threshold between places and non-places, between time and eternity. It exists as a personification of the roiling unfathomable nothing that is the stitches between the fabric of all things

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill History|XPHB} or {@skill Nature|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine a Lurker on the Threshold, learning the following based on the result.

entries.name: (10+) Baleful Resistance
entries: You know the creature's {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: (15+) Arcane Beams
entries: You learn the creature's Cosmic Rays attack action.

entries.name: (20+) Enduring
entries: You know the creature's highest and lowest ability scores.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Lurker on the Threshold is a creature of pure arcane energy and twisted realities. It fires Cosmic Rays at mortal creatures,warping their minds, showing truths that drive them mad, or undoes their very existence on a cellular level. It grabs creatures with its Tendrils and blasts its beams while holding them in place, undoing the creatures from the inside out, before tossing them aside and moving on to the next. The Lurker on the Threshold only flees if it is reduced to under half its Hit Points, not because of any sense of fear, but because it finds specific enemies a nuisance.

name: Lurking Dreg

entries: Draped in a dark cloak with the hood pulled up tight, the figure regards you with a cautious disposition. They pace back and forth, watching you, anticipating your actions and readying themselves for any sudden movement. From under the hood, you can make out a toothy smirk and pale flesh. Gently glowing eyes peer out from the shadows, observing you carefully and diligently.

It is not immediately obvious that a Lurking Dreg is a contaminated monster. Retaining most of their original appearance and personality, Lurking Dregs are often driven by a mad compulsion to deceive friends and loved ones into circumstances or places that will contaminate them in turn. Keen-eyed observers may be able to recognize subtle cues and signs of contamination in these creatures, such as discolored skin tones and a slight octarine glow in the eyes.

Hooded Lantern apothecaries who have examined Lurking Dreg corpses have discovered that the ruse is merely skin-deep: the creatures' innards are entirely contaminated and mutated, with almost all the internal organs rendered into unrecognizable shapes and configurations.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Insight|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check to {@action study|XPHB} a Lurking Dreg, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (10+) Something's Off
entries: You suspect this person may have been exposed to eldritch {@condition contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}.

entries.name: (15+) Hiding Something
entries: You are aware of the Lurking Dreg's Cunning {@variantrule Action|XPHB} trait.

entries.name: (20+) Not A Humanoid
entries: You realize this is a Dreg appearing to be a normal humanoid and recognize the Lurking Dreg's highest and lowest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Some Lurking Dregs hide in the shadows, waiting for an opportune moment to strike. Others pose as human and attempt to converse with prey, hoping to draw them deeper into the ruins. Lurking Dregs have been known to use stories of lost allies, trapped children, and more to lure adventurers into an ambush.

When they attack, Lurking Dregs use their Furious Ambush right away to get as many attacks in as possible. They Disengage if they can and attempt to keep their enemies at bay, possibly having other Dregs tie them up while the Lurking Dreg darts in and out.
If Lurking Dregs find themselves outnumbered at any point, they run into the shadows and {@action Hide|XPHB}, attempting to escape.

entries: Aberration.

name: Luvaar Calsson
entries: Turncoat cultist

name: Lyla Webb
entries: A native of the Drowned Crossroads born to a family of fisherfolk, Lyla {@i (LYE-luh)} Webb (Chaotic Good, human {@creature Priest|XMM}) had dreams that were much bigger than a life of catching catfish. She set off from home at a young age and eventually discovered a community in the swamp that worshipped Snake Eye Jack and held him as a beneficent spirit who made sure that luck was always on their side. She learned their ways and became a skilled jinxcraft practitioner, using her magical abilities to help the people of the bayou as well as aid her work as a trader.

Now an adult, she has become a shrewd and resourceful businesswoman who has numerous contacts throughout the Drowned Crossroads and a knack for fencing stolen goods that the rogues of the swamp bring her. Her skill in business, helpful magic, and wisdom beyond her years have made her widely respected by all the folk of the swamp, and the Bayou King has appointed her as his chief advisor and emissary.

entries.name: Mage Hunter Golem
entries: The gods cursed mortals with free will, but also blessed them with the means to survive the Primordials' wrath—the arts of magic. With magic, the people of Exandria fend off droughts, famines, volcanic flame, slashing ice, and angry earth. But knowing that the power of magic might inevitably tear Exandria apart, the gods also created the ultimate magical failsafe—antimagic.

entries.name: Hunter of Magic
entries: For many heroes who employ magic, the most terrifying nightmare is facing a hulking creature whose mere presence can strip away the power of spells and magic relics alike. Mage hunter golems are brutally efficient in their tactics, sweeping the battlefield with their disruptive antimagic, devouring spells used against them, and fitting collars to spellcasters that can leave them at the golem's mercy.

items.altText: A large, metallic construct of black armor and glowing, violet, arcane energy. One hand ends in a collar-like claw. The golem and its collar-like claw are all adorned with glowing runes.

name: Mage-Arbiter
entries: Only the most skilled, dedicated, and power-hungry Justicars advance to the rank of mage-arbiter. Known far and wide as a mage's worst nightmare made real, a mage-arbiter can swiftly and easily negate the efforts of most arcane practitioners. When their full wrath and might are brought to bear, even archmages retreat.

name: Magebreaker
entries: Perhaps the only thing truly feared by rank and file Justicars, magebreakers are uniquely trained to combat the skills and abilities of mages, Justicars, and Spelldrinkers alike. Operating outside the main command structure and only reporting to mage-arbiters, mere rumor of a magebreaker visiting an outpost of Justicars inspires fear and strict observance of the Justicar rules and regulations.

Magma elementals are native to the Para-elemental Plane of Magma, where the Plane of Earth and Plane of Fire collide. The inner inferno that sustains magma elementals constantly spews forth more material. This allows the creatures to use pieces of themselves as weaponry, hurling roiling globs of magma at individual targets or throwing a large mass of lava that explodes to damage groups of foes.

In mortal worlds, magma elementals are found in areas where strong volcanic activity is present. Eyewitnesses from inhabited areas destroyed by lava flows often sometimes report molten creatures at the vanguard of the lava, smashing and burning everything long before the lava arrives.

entries.name: Para-elementals
entries: Between the Elemental Planes of Air, Earth, Fire, and Water, which exemplify the elements that make up the multiverse, lie the Para-elemental Planes: regions where Elemental Planes collide and their elements mingle. These Para-elemental Planes are the Plane of Ash, the Plane of Ice, the Plane of Magma, and the Plane of Ooze. These planes are home to the para-elementals: ice elementals, magma elementals, mud elementals, and smoke elementals.

name: Magma Landshark
entries: Lurking inside volcanoes, subterranean magma pits, and the endless seas of flame within the Elemental Plane of Fire, magma landsharks live only to eat. These creatures are physically similar to {@creature bulette|MM|bulettes}, the common landshark of the {@book Dividing Plains|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Dividing Plains}, but are filled with churning elemental power.

This fiery, armored predator burrows and burns through solid rock and can sense the slightest movement in the ground around it. When hungry—and these creatures are always hungry—a magma landshark erupts from under the earth, oblivious to any obstruction or danger, uprooting trees, destroying roads, unleashing avalanches, and leaving sinkholes behind in its wake. Its jaws widen as it swallows prey whole, and even creatures that initially survive the attack must contend with an aura of intense heat if they can't escape.

images.altText: A black and red creature like a shark made of volcanic rock with magma coming from its spine, head, eyes, mouth, claws, and tail.

name: Magma Troll

entries: Its flesh is like molten rocks, accented by glowing veins of fire. Its eyes are two burning pools of lava. It lets out a roar that sounds like the grinding rock of an erupting volcano. Its steps leave behind pools of hot liquid magma, which drips from its hands and mouth as well.

Magma Trolls occupy the deep caverns of the earth, the vast Witherbleach desert, or the caldera of volcanoes such as the Dragon's Maw. They prefer places of sweltering heat and lava flows, and rarely leave these locations if they can help it. Naturally, the desire for food sometimes brings them out of hiding to attack mountainside communities or inhabited places near caverns and caves.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks to {@action study|XPHB} a Magma Troll, learning the following information based on the result:

entries.name: (5+) From Harsh Environments
entries: You know the troll's {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: (10+) Hard to Kill
entries: You learn of the troll's Regeneration trait.

entries.name: (15+) Special Weakness
entries: You have insight into the troll's {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB|Vulnerabilities}.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Magma Trolls hunt for food during the hottest days of summer or in places of extreme temperatures. Often accompanied by sweltering heat, they begin combat by unleashing their Sulfurous Belch before rushing in to maul foes with their claws and bites.
If a Magma Troll takes Cold damage, it immediately flees and attempts to find a safe place to recuperate.

name: Magnetite Armour
entries: Crafted from highly magnetic magnetite, these animated armours and weapons share the common property of being immobilised by heat The animated suit of plate armour is capable of conjuring bolts of arcanomagnetic force that can knock a creature off its feet.

name: Magnetite Wyrmling
entries: Matter-of-fact and down-to-earth, magnetite dragons are distant relatives of the metallic dragons, though they lack the ability to shapechange. A magnetite dragon has a bestial slant to its appearance; its short maw, narrow eyes, and stocky hind legs give it the proud and powerful cast of a rearing bull. Two wide horns—the source of its magnetic control— sweep forwards from its brow, often sporting an array of ferrous paraphernalia. Wyrmlings' scales are a dull grey, but quickly take on an iridescent red-blue sheen as they age and are exposed to sources of magic.

Of particular note are its hexofuga: the blocky shards that protrude from its back. These arcano-magnetic organs are the source of its ability to fly, its true wings being small, vestigial structures with little musculature.

entries.name: Treasure & Power
entries: Made of a keratin-magnetite composite, a magnetite wyrmling's back scales can only develop into hexofuga upon prolonged exposure to arcane fields. In fact, a magnetite dragon's growth and power is intrinsically linked to the duration and magnitude to which it has been exposed to magic. Though a magnetite wyrmling is among the weakest of all dragon wyrmlings, a fully grown individual can rival even a black dragon in power. For this reason, a magnetite dragon has no care for gold and gems; it covets only magical items and sources of arcane power: the stronger the better.

entries.name: Neutral Motives
entries: Magnetite dragons are incensed by the proliferation of order or chaos, and feel a compulsion to maintain the natural, chaotic order of the world. Persuading such a dragon to fight for good or evil is a futile affair, but the mere mention of the Plane of Fey's uncontrolled chaos, or the Clockwork Arcadia's orderly machinations, is enough to motivate evenly the most slovenly individual.

entries.name: Magical Magnetite
entries: It is an established arcano-magical fact that magnetite's properties change on exposure to strong magical fields. The usually brittle substance hardens and exhibits much stronger magnetic fields. However, the material's superconducting properties are nullified on exposure to heat. For these reasons, a magnetite dragon typically makes its home in subzero conditions and near strong sources of magic.

name: Magpie of Omens

entries: {@i Bird of Fate and Fortune (Crystal or gemstone shards)}

To those who respect the Old Ways, this bird of black and white brings tidings both fair and foul. Although the omens the magpie delivers can bring joy and grief in equal measure, they are always trustworthy.
{@i A white fin cut the surface of the water as the serpentine creature approached. Its wolfish head burst from the surface, revealing a body covered in fine, white fur.}

entries.name: Valuable Teeth and Fur
entries: A mahoru's heavy jaws are filled with triangular, serrated teeth adept at tearing flesh and sundering bone. Their white fur is prized for its warmth and waterproof qualities. Their pectoral fins feature stubby, claw-tipped paws. Mahoru is a totem beast for many northern tribes. Some make arrowheads and tooth-studded clubs with the beast's fangs.

entries.name: Iceberg Hunters
entries: Mahoru prowl northern coasts and estuaries, hunting among the fragmenting pack ice each summer. They lurk beneath the surface, catching swimmers or lurching up onto the ice to break or tilt it and send prey tumbling into the water. When necessary, they stalk beaches and riverbanks in search of carrion or unwary victims.

entries.name: Work in Pairs and Packs
entries: Mahoru work together in mated pairs to corral everything from fish and seals to larger prey like kayaking humanoids and even polar bears. They gnaw at ice bridges and the frozen surface of lakes and rivers to create fragile patches that plunge unwary victims into waiting jaws.

name: Maidenwood

entries: {@i Twitch-Warped Ambushing Tree}

Maidenwoods are creatures birthed from tree stumps by old magics, often arising from curses that turn the forest against a transgressor. They scuttle on roots like legs, and the broken trunk becomes a fierce, grinding maw. The maidenwood's tendrils blossom into lifelike figures it uses to lure its prey close.

entries.name: Secret
entries: The curse that maintains a maidenwood unravels if one is offered an apple—an ancient trick used by witches turned against them.
{@i Within a blinding wave of heat and glare walks a long-limbed, misshapen form. The creature scorches everything in its path as it strides forward.}

What most people recall most vividly from an encounter with a malakbel is the blinding light and blistering heat surrounding it. Rippling distortion obscures the creature's body, which is roughly the size and shape of an adult human.

entries.name: Demonic Messengers
