Such rat rulers might include a wererat, a rat king, an ogre, a minor demon, or an intelligent undead.

A pair of glinting yellow-purple eyes appear down the dark tunnel ahead, then another, then more. A scurrying mass of furry bodies bound up in mud-spattered cloth and greasy leather surge forward. Their rodent-like claws brandish rust-caked blades as many squeaking voices erupt into a cacophony of chittering, chirping, screeching, and finally a howl of "Kill! Kill! Kill!"

Ratlings are oversized mutated rats imbued with malevolent cunning and driven by a mad compulsion to consume and multiply. These wretched monsters suffer from a constant internal struggle between cowardly survival instincts and violent impulsive urges. Ratlings dream of eating everything, and will eat anything, but love eating people. They especially love eating babies. While they will subsist on carrion, ratlings take captives back to their lairs so they can have fresh food later. Thousands of ratlings dwell in the city. They form warring colonies that dig maze-like burrows featuring multiple entrances and tight looping passages. Successful colonies grow in number quickly, as ratlings mature in a matter of weeks when ample food and delerium are available.

name: Ratling Alchemist

entries: This ratling sports a pair of thick goggles and an impressive custom-built crossbow. The skittish rat wears a scraped-together, acid-stained leather coat and a bandolier of bubbling flasks and vials that hangs along its belt. It mixes glowing liquids that fume and sizzle, preparing to hurl a vial toward you.

All ratlings possess a wicked cunning, but a few among them are gifted with an inventive spirit, reckless curiosity, and explosive intentions. Often beginning with a fascination with fire or the strange and erratic effects of delerium, these ratlings use improvised materials, unstable ingredients, and scavenged tools to experiment and tinker, building crude devices and sometimes ingenious traps. Two out of three ratlings who attempt to become an alchemist die in their own explosions, but the one that makes it often becomes a horrible force against their foes.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: A character proficient with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} or {@item Tinker's Tools|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks to {@action Study|XPHB} a Ratling Alchemist, learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (5+) Chemical Exposure
entries: You are aware these creatures have an excellent sense of smell, {@sense Darkvision|XPHB}, are capable climbers and swimmers and its unique damage {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}.

entries.name: (10+) Inventive and Cunning
entries: You learn of the ratling's Repeating Crossbow and Delerium Bomb actions.

entries.name: (15+) Nimble but Weak
entries: You recognize the ratling's strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: A Ratling Alchemist is a ranged combatant who keeps to the backfield, where they can safely snipe their foes with their crossbow. They are happy to take pot shots when their bodyguards go down, using their Covering Fire {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.
A Ratling Alchemist doesn't care about the wellbeing or safety of their fellow ratlings, and will throw its Delerium Bomb at foes even if their allies are in the blast area.

name: Ratling Burrow Warden

entries: This burly ratling stands a head taller than their broodlings, wearing a fearless expression upon their snarling snout. Clad in scavenged bits of armor, they carry a broad, makeshift shield which may have once been a window shutter, tabletop, or part of a door. They wield a long spear topped with a vicious chunk of sharp scrap metal that appears to be coated in some kind of toxic sludge.

Ratlings look to the biggest among their number for leadership, forming posses around the largest and loudest, called Burrow Wardens. These ratlings get the privilege of bossing their comrades around, taking a larger share of food, and first pick amongst the spoils of their raids and ambushes. While Burrow Wardens might act like petty tyrants, these bullies also must constantly prove their strength and bravery lest a rival rise up to take their place. Wardens are often found at the forefront of any battle to demonstrate their might and ferocity. The smaller ratlings quite like this arrangement, as it puts their bully-bosses on the front lines during a burrow invasion. If the ratlings grow tired of one of their Burrow Wardens and want to replace them, they are in the best place to stab the big one in the back, cut them down if they're wounded, or abandon them alone against a deadly foe.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Ratling Burrow Wardens often form a tight formation during an attack, taking up their shields and poison-tipped spears to defend choke points. They especially like using their Shield Shove to push attackers into pits or other prepared traps in the burrow.

name: Ratling Guttersnipe

entries: A cloaked ratling appears from out of the shadows, a wicked blade carved from delerium in its claws. A hand crossbow hangs at their side with a quiver of poison-tipped bolts. They fire at you, then dash from the shadows, lunging to attack.

The small survive in the ruins through stealth, cunning, and a solid repertoire of under-handed tricks. Ratling Guttersnipes possess hard-won skills learned through bitter experience, and are rightfully respected and feared amongst their comrades. These grim-toothed ratlings have learned to plan careful ambushes, place deadly traps, and lure their prey into unfavorable situations. Honing their senses to a hair trigger, they are ready to kill quickly.

Guttersnipes arm themselves with choice equipment pried from the corpses of dead faction agents and explorers. These skilled thieves are bold enough to sneak outside the ruins on occasion to steal supplies, equipment, and food from faction strongholds, and even occasionally make nighttime break-ins to isolated homes and farmsteads.

The Guttersnipes observed the impact delerium had on humanoid creatures, and found inspiration for using delerium as a weapon, knowing that beyond the cut of a blade, the {@condition contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} is an even more deadly component to be dealt with. All Guttersnipes carry delerium weapons, often constructed simply by finding a sharp shard of delerium and fastening it to a makeshift hilt.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB} or {@skill Stealth|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks to {@action Study|XPHB} a Ratling Guttersnipe, learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (5+) Mutated Monstrosities
entries: You understand these creatures have an excellent sense of smell, {@sense Darkvision|XPHB}, and are capable climbers and swimmers. They are Immune to Contamination, but have no other special {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}.

entries.name: (10+) Mob Attacks
entries: You learn of the Ratling Guttersnipe's Pack Tactics trait and its Ratling Cunning.

entries.name: (15+) Nimble but Weak
entries: You know the ratling's strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Ratling Guttersnipes stick to the shadows, staying hidden as long as possible. They are likely to position themselves on rooftops or behind rubble, and often secure their locations with pit traps, flasks of oil, torches, or other devious traps when they are able. Once they notice their target is in position, Ratling Guttersnipes unload a volley of poison-tipped bolts, or unleash deadly traps. After their targets are weakened, the ratlings rushes in to surprise and stab creatures with their delerium blades, and then quickly dart back out.
As with all ratlings, if the fight turns against them, they will flee or beg for their lives.

name: Ratling Pathogenist

entries: Cloaked in a thick leather jacket and a crude, custom-made gas mask, this ratling scurries forth clutching a worn satchel brimming with poisons and potions. An acrid smell wafts off the ratling, combined with burnt hair and something putrid and rotten. Its fur is mottled, and burned away in patches across its neck, arms, and legs. Its flesh is covered in sores, blisters, and infected wounds. It rummages through its bag before producing a vial and tossing it forcefully to the ground at your feet.

Ratlings are disease-ridden creatures, and the smartest amongst them have observed the effects these diseases have on their enemies. Studying the actual causes of diseases and learning to harness them against their foes is a point of pride for a Ratling Pathogenist. These twisted doctors consider themselves amongst the most brilliant ratlings.

The Ratling Pathogenist has several disease-ridden blades, needles, syringes, and a gas mask. It's surrounded by a haze of diseased gas and acrid fumes. Even getting close to one of these highly contaminated rats is enough to make one sick.

entries: You are aware of its Plaguebringer Aura and Infection action.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Ratling Pathogenist is a cunning killer and loves to riddle its foes with diseases. The ratling will release one of its deadly infections into a creature nearby and use Rampant Sickness to spread it to anyone nearby. Metastasis causes the disease to kill its target even faster.
The pathogenist prefers to keep their distance and will attempt to scurry away if cornered or forced to fight in melee. It will also run if it is alone, or if its allies are fewer than its enemies.

entries: A pair of glinting yellow-purple eyes appear down the dark tunnel ahead, then another, then more. A scurrying mass of furry bodies bound up in mud-spattered cloth and greasy leather surges forward. Their rodent-like claws brandish rust-caked blades as many squeaking voices erupt into a cacophony of chittering, chirping, screeching, and finally a howl of "Kill! Kill! Kill!"

Representing the overwhelming mass of ratlings in Drakkenheim, these warriors have little skill and even less bravery, living a desperate life of scavenging and violence. However, a Ratling Warrior who survives and thrives may often find their own specialization or niche, becoming a {@creature Ratling Burrow Warden|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Burrow Warden}, {@creature Ratling Guttersnipe|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Guttersnipe}, or {@creature Ratling Alchemist|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Alchemist}.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks to {@action Study|XPHB} a Ratling Warrior, learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (5+) Mutated Monstrosities
entries: You are aware these creatures have an excellent sense of smell, {@sense Darkvision|XPHB}, are capable climbers and swimmers, and are Immune to Contamination.

entries.name: (10+) Mob Attacks
entries: You learn of the Ratling Warrior's Pack Tactics trait and Ratling Cunning action.

entries.name: (15+) Swift, Weak, and Cowardly
entries: You know its strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Ratlings fight together in large groups to surround and overwhelm their foes with Pack Tactics. They use whatever rusty weapons they can find, or use their teeth and claws when nothing else is available. Occasionally, ratlings carry makeshift slings and hurl anything they pick up off the ground at their enemies: rocks, bones, or even chips of delerium.

However, ratlings flee and hide using Ratling Cunning when they don't have a numerical advantage over their foes. Indeed, they won't start fights if they don't outnumber their foes at least two to one, but while they outnumber their foes three to one or more, the typical ratling warrior can become insanely brave. When ratlings overpower their foes, they may even grapple them down and take them as prisoners to eat later.

Usually an enemy unless they're given the right motivation such as not eating people.

entries.name: Ravager Slaughter Lord
entries: Some warlords of the {@book Dividing Plains|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Dividing Plains}, hungry for recognition in the single burning eye of their god, turn to the {@book Ravagers|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|4|Ravagers} in the name of blood and glory. Those few whose deeds live up to their ambitions soon find themselves leading factions of the cult—and honored by the title of Slaughter Lord. A Slaughter Lord craves combat and leads Ravager raids as often as possible. However, they are frequently forced to remain at their strongholds because of the strict regimen of alchemical treatments that grant them increased power.

A small army of shamans and alchemists attend to the Slaughter Lords to artificially enhance their strength and fury, creating concoctions to grow their muscular forms to massive size, sharpen their tactical reasoning, and bestow upon them the divine protection of the {@deity The Ruiner|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|Ruiner}. A Slaughter Lord's unnatural size is their most obvious martial advantage, enabling them to dual-wield even the largest weapons. But the {@deity The Ruiner|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|Ruiner's} blessings also grant them access to divine magic that can blind or slay enemies with a word.

It is speculated that four major arms of the {@book Ravagers|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|4|Ravagers} are each commanded by one of these terrors, but the exact number of Slaughter Lords remains unknown.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Chaotic evil.

entries.name: Ravager Stabby-Stabber
entries: Adventurers and mercenaries most often take up arms against the {@book Ravagers|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|4|Ravagers} after hearing stories of the hordes terrorizing the free peoples of the {@book Dividing Plains|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Dividing Plains}. They prepare themselves for brutal combat against even more brutal foes—and are thus unprepared for the {@book Ravagers'|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|4|Ravagers} most terrifying weapon, the stabby-stabbers. Fresh-faced warriors from {@book Emon|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Emon, the City of Fellowship} laugh at the name when they first hear it in {@book Kymal's|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Kymal} taverns, even as veteran mercenaries close their eyes and hastily bury their faces in their tankards.

Nimble Ravager warriors who show exceptional skill are brought before their Slaughter Lord and forced to drink a terrible brew the {@book Ravagers|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|4|Ravagers} call skullfire. This concoction burns away what little reasoning ability those warriors possessed, turning them into perfectly obedient, flesh-hungry monsters. In battle, stabby-stabbers swarm like rats, eviscerating enemies and bystanders alike.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Chaotic evil.

name: Ravagers
entries: The {@book Ravagers|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|4|Ravagers} are a death cult that stampedes across the {@book Dividing Plains|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Dividing Plains}, spilling blood in the name of the Betrayer God known as the {@deity The Ruiner|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|Ruiner}. Led by bloodthirsty warlords called {@creature Ravager Slaughter Lord|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|Slaughter Lords}, the cult's long-term goals are unknown, but its members are content in the short term to sow the seeds of chaos across the plains.

Such wanton, chaotic slaughter would certainly please the {@deity The Ruiner|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|Ruiner}, and the smaller settlements of the plains have learned to fear the sight of {@book Ravagers|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|4|Ravagers} on the horizon. Inside the walls of {@book Westruun|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Westruun}, however, Lord Mayor Lysandra Kallos and her councilors worry that the {@book Ravagers|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|4|Ravagers} show better organization than their bloodthirsty warlords should be capable of instilling in the cult. Who—or what—is commanding the Slaughter Lords from the shadows? And toward what end are these depraved warriors being directed?

images.altText: Two menacing individuals—one is short and emaciated, with stringy hair and a nasty grin, brandishing two small blades. The other is tall and hulking; he wears a helmet adorned with spikes and wide horns, a ragged wrap, and decorative chains across his chest. He wields a large greatsword in each hand.

entries: {@i The tree steps forward on bark-covered legs. Its head is crowned by long-stemmed, green-paddled fronds and spiked seed pods, and its dangling arms end in hooked, wooden talons.}

entries.name: Leafy Advisors
entries: Wise and long-lived like treants, ravenalas tend their coastal forest homes far from most societies. Tribal humanoids respect and venerate ravenalas and sometimes seek their advice or aid in times of great need. Ravenalas seldom interact with others unless approached.

entries.name: Prisoner's Lamentation
entries: Unlike treants, ravenalas avoid physical conflict in favor of diplomacy and compromise. If annoyed, they imprison hostile creatures within their trunks rather than killing or eating the attackers. Trapped creatures must sing their own lament as they are carried off to a distant locale away from the ravenala's home.

name: Ravencraft

entries: {@i Undead Avian Amalgamation (Silver wire)}

Ravencrafts are a grotesque fusion of feathers, sinew, and bone. Their tiny form is a contorted and twisted nightmare carelessly sewn together into the mockery of a bird. The mere presence of a ravencraft is an affront to natural death and can keep further death at bay, or they can chill the hearts of their foes with cries of torment from beyond the grave.
{@i The creature's face resembles that of a great raven or crow, and it is covered in feathers from head to toe, though without wings.}

The ravenfolk are an avian race of scoundrels, schemers, and sneaks—but they are much more than that. Long ago when Odin brokered the truce that brought peace among the gods, the wily deity magically created the ravenfolk from feathers plucked from his ravens Huginn (Thought) and Muninn (Memory). He placed this new race into the world alongside elves, dwarves, humans, and others to be his eyes and ears.

entries.name: Odin's Children
entries: To this day, the ravenfolk are Odin's agents and embody his thought and memory. They are thieves of objects, yes, but primarily, they are thieves of secrets. Their black feathers and long beaks are spotted on the road from place to place, trading information or helping to hatch plots. They are widely viewed as spies, informers, thieves, and troublemakers, but when the ravenfolk swear an oath, they abide by it. Odin grants the best of his ravenfolk magical runespears and runestaves, weapons enchanted to serve his messengers. The ravenfolk consider them special tokens meant for their use, and no one else's.

entries.name: Flightless But Bold
entries: Though they have no wings and normally cannot fly, the physiology of ravenfolk is strikingly similar to that of true avians. They stand roughly 5 feet tall and, because of their hollow bones, weigh just 95–105 pounds. Albino ravenfolk are often found in southern climates. Ravenfolk eat almost anything, but they prefer raw meat and field grains, such as corn, soy, and alfalfa. They even scavenge days-old carrion, a practice that repulses most other humanoids.

entries.name: Feather Speech
entries: The ravenfolk have two languages: a verbal language full of croaks and whistles and a language of feathers. Ravenfolk can communicate volumes without speaking a word through the dyeing, arrangement, preening, and rustling of their plumage. This language is inherent to ravenfolk, and though others may use magic to understand it, it can't be used by creatures without feathers.

entries.name: Ravenfolk in Midgard
entries: If the ravenfolk of Midgard have a homeland, it is Beldestan to the East, on a branch of Wotan's tree in the North, or a high cliff of Horus' hidden temple in the South. They have settlements in Trollheim, Vidim, Domovogrod, Zobeck, Nuria Natal, and the Dragon Empire, but none are large.

They avoid the West and the Seven Cities most of the time and are highly honored in Nuria Natal, where they serve the temples of Horus as sworn guardians, assassins, and seekers of forgotten arcana. Some are said to be members of the Emerald Order, a society devoted to arcane mysteries.

name: Ravenous Flora

entries: This massive plant writhes forward on a mass of roots and vines. Its large leaves waving back and forth surround its great floral head. Glowing hypnotic octarine petals surround a central bulb that opens into a mouth oozing with saliva nectar as a leaf-like tongue licks in anticipation. Its maw is filled with hooked, jagged teeth. The creature looks ready to swallow you whole.

Some apothecaries specialize in the study of plants. These botanist apothecaries often experiment with delerium to affect flora growth cycles. The Ravenous Flora is one unfortunate creation of these efforts. It is a plant that has grown to incredible size, gaining a primitive sentience and a desire to feed. The plant seems singly focused on its hunger, with reports often claiming that the Botanist who created the monstrosity has fallen victim to the creation's insatiable hunger.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Arcana|XPHB} or {@skill Medicine|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks to Study a Plague Carrier, learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (10+) Plant-like nature
entries: You understand the Ravenous Flora's {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities} and its Poison Ivy trait.

entries.name: (15+) Giant Maw with Toxic Pollen
entries: You learn of its Writhing Aura and Swallow.

entries.name: (20+) Large and Slow
entries: You recognize its movement speed and Dexterity saving throw.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Ravenous Flora attempts to hypnotize its prey with its Hypnotic Pollen. Because it is a slow-moving creature, it uses this to attract victims before attempting to Bite and Swallow its targets. If no targets are in range, it Spits Acid at them and does its best to move to an advantageous position.

entries: Flowers.

entries: Needles, Spores.

items.name: Ravenous Ghoul

entries: Thick poison drips from the grimy teeth and claws of these feral, unarmored ghouls. Their sunken, stark white eyes glisten as they lick their lips with a long, slimy pointed tongue, hungry for their next meal.

Ravenous Ghouls make up the brunt of the undead forces of vampires. They are vile undead creatures twisted to the will of their masters, forced to starve for months at a time to put them into a frenzy when they are unleashed upon the vampire's enemies. Their vampire masters care little for their wellbeing, and simply use them as fodder to wear down their enemies.
A spellcaster can use create undead to animate a ravenous ghoul instead of a normal ghoul.

{@i This vaguely humanoid-shaped plant boasts shimmering black and plum-colored leaves sprouting from from its head, back, and arms. The leaves are wickedly sharp and can be shaken loose to form deadly slashing clouds.}

entries.name: Roots in Shadow
entries: Razorleaves grow where the veil between the Shadow Realm and the Material Plane has thinned and darkness bleeds through into the soil. Their plant-like bodies are tinged with shadow magic but are as tangible as any other shrub or tree. Their roots are made of pure shadow and have a corrupting effect on other plants and animals around them.

entries.name: Letting the Light Out
entries: Mature razorleaves have a darkening effect on the area in which they live. Nonmagical sources of light are only half as effective in these plants' groves. There is a 50% chance that a portal to the Shadow Realm will appear wherever three or more razorleaves dwell. Sustained by the presence of the plants, the portal serves as a doorway between worlds.

name: Reality Cyst

entries: You come across a glistening mass of pustules that seem to grow  directly out of the physical structures of the city, as if the natural  wood, stone, and earth are alive. These cysts are a cancer growing  within Drakkenheim. The very air around the cyst changes, the  light refracts in incorrect patterns, and the lines and angles of its  surroundings seem to fracture in incoherent designs. To look upon  it is like looking at reality itself through a broken mirror. One  that is both present and not present at all, where your every move  and step are strained and confused. For a brief moment, you seem  to forget what you saw at all, and the landscape around you seems  unfamiliar. Have you been here before? How did you get here in  the first place? Your mind strains to grasp these questions.

The presence of delerium has caused Drakkenheim to become an epicenter for planar rifts. Commonly known as Thin Places, these tears in reality allow creatures to pass between dimensions and cause the magical qualities which define the linked plane to slowly seep into and change the Mortal World. Outside the ruins of Drakkenheim, most Thin Places are connected to the Faerie Otherworlds or the Shadowlands, but within the city, the Haze is especially prone to create pathways into the Space between Worlds.

This roiling realm of chaotic pandemonium and impossible reality floods the Mortal World with {@table Arcane Anomalies|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Arcane Anomaly} and unfathomable horrors. When rifts to the Space Between Worlds appear in Drakkenheim, it sends a rippling magic outwards from its center, affecting all creatures, plants, and even stone and wood. Thin Places in Drakkenheim are like wounds in reality, and as the wound remains, it begins to fester and infect. Like a disease, the infection begins to cause growths and cancers to form in the area around it. The Reality Cyst is one of these cancerous growths.

Those who have glimpsed a Reality Cyst have seen them vanish from sight a moment later. There are reports of adventurers lost in the ruins for days trying to navigate a city street that become completely alien and unfamiliar, only to be found by another scouting party standing perfectly still in a daze. It seems those who are affected by the Reality Cyst enter a sort of trance. They are unable to perceive the Reality Cyst and instead find themselves in a confused landscape with the very fabric of reality shifting and altering forms. Colors beyond perception bleed from walls, objects appear and disappear at random, nonsensical angles and shapes form and alter before their eyes. People might believe they are moving in one direction and find themselves moving in a completely different direction. Gravity, time, space, logic, and all other concepts are skewed and broken.

For those who have glimpsed through the veil of a Thin Place, and caught that unhinged reality of the Space Between Worlds, the state of order in the bending existence of a Reality Cyst seems strangely familiar. Its wrongness, although completely unfathomable, seems to echo the confused state of the Space Between Worlds. Those who encounter a Reality Cyst and escape Drakkenheim's walls have bordered on madness. At best they suffer severe headaches for weeks afterwards. A mind can only handle so much when the reality you interact with pushes up against the rules and concepts of your own comprehension.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Arcana|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Nature|XPHB}) checks to {@action Study|XPHB} a Reality Cyst, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (5+) Unmoving Aberration.
entries: You learn the Reality Cyst's creature type and speed.

entries.name: (10+) Draining Rejuvenation.
entries: You are aware of the creature's Feed Bonus Action

entries.name: (15+) Anomalous Influence.
entries: You recognize the cyst's ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Reality Cyst is less of a hunter than it is a disease. It feeds off the confusion of creatures trapped in its illusions. It mimics the bending realities of the Space Between Worlds and mirrors that into the minds of those who are close to it. After their target enters a trance, it drinks their mental energy and grows.

The Reality Cyst does only one thing: it feeds. It cannot move or defend itself well against attacks. It relies on creatures succumbing to its Unhinged Reality trait and devouring their minds. Once discovered, there is little the cyst can do to survive.

name: Reautomata

entries: Charging towards you with unbound fury is a lithe human clad in a hulking suit of full plate wielding a pair of oversized scimitars. As they draw closer with a snarl, it becomes clear you face no mere warrior, but a monstrous abomination of metal and flesh. The emaciated figure is not wearing the armor: the plates have been riveted and bolted into their bones. Globs of weeping, infected scar tissue pulsate where the body fights against the metal fused into muscle and sinew. It does not hold its weapons: its forelimbs have been entirely replaced with scything talon-blades. Their metal helmets are smooth and featureless save for a single ocular delerium lens, and expose the creature's sickly mouth and sharpened teeth, its breath giving off a rank chemical odor.
First created by the Reanimator Dr. Everett Freed of Altbruke University, Reautomata were designed as the ultimate shock trooper. These armored warriors feel no pain, fear, or remorse.

entries.name: Constructs of Metal and Flesh.
entries: Despite their outward appearances, Reautomata are constructs, not undead: their organic components operate more like machines than mere flesh. Such is the composition of a Reautomata that they fight on despite grievous injury, unflinching even as they are dismembered. Stopping a Reautomata necessitates mangling its body past the point of physical operation. Reautomata are ultimately brutal and decisive combatants that fight without regard for their personal well-being.

entries.name: Created in Torment.
entries: Reautomata must be skillfully made by a master Reanimator using the finest components. It is essential the work begin on both a living and fully conscious individual. Typically, most apothecaries perform the work without anesthetic, instead opting to sever the vocal cords of their victims so as to not have their screams disturb the grim work involved. Limbs are removed and replaced, and metal is grafted into flesh and welded into the bone of the fully aware subject. Nervous tissue is pulled from the brain and distributed from the body, giving the construct nearly perfect proprioceptive awareness while excising unnecessary or superfluous brain tissues associated with cognitive functions. The process renders the Reautomata fully obedient, but not mindless.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Arcana|XPHB} or {@skill Medicine|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks to {@action Study|XPHB} a Reautomata Each successful check reveals one of the following pieces of information:

entries.name: (16+) Dispassionate Metal and Flesh.
entries: You are aware of the Reautomata's Relentless Endurance trait, as well as its damage and condition {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: (19+) Limb Weapons.
entries: You know of the Reautomata's Arm Blades and Entrapping Rend attacks.

entries.name: (21+) Focused Killer.
entries: You learn the Reautomata's Wisdom, Intelligence, and Charisma saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Reautomata fight with outward ferocity and aggressive attacks which belie the cold, unfeeling calculation at the core of each solider. In battle, Reautomata launch themselves towards their foes in great leaps, impaling their targets upon their rending arm blades. The rending blades flense into flesh and latch on like hooks, allowing the Reautomata to restrain their targets. They then use their great strength to rend apart their restrained victims.

Reautomata unquestionably obey the orders of their creator and will fight until destroyed without regard for their own bodies. However, even with only general instructions, Reautomata fight intelligently and know how to utilize the environment to their advantage, making use of their climb speeds and jumping ability to prioritize dangerous targets.

The only time I ever felt like a pincushion. Incredible speed and furiosity, if they weren't a machine-corpse enemy I'd be impressed.

name: Reautomata Wrecker

entries: This monstrous construct is the size of an ogre. It lets out a low bellow like the droning cry of an approaching whale. Suddenly, it breaks into a charge like a thunderous rhinoceros, racing forward with uncanny speed despite its onerous bulk. It is covered in armored tanks with hoses attached to its head, directly into the ears, nose, mouth, neck which pump its body full of strange chemicals.
Since the death of Dr. Freed, his knowledge and works were nevertheless disseminated, including an unfinished schematics for this advanced Reautomata prototype.

Built as more of a living siege engine than a shock trooper, a Reautomata Wrecker is a furious and destructive machine. Constructed from a collection of parts taken from trolls, ogres, and humans, the wrecker is reinforced with armored plating to carry the tanks and machines that power its frame. At the core of the wrecker is a powerful drive engine which when overclocked can set the construct on a path of wanton fury before it explodes in blaze of alchemical doom.

entries: You know of the Reautomata's Arm Blades and Entrapping Rend attacks.

entries.name: (21+) Focused Killer.
entries: You learn the Reautomata's Wisdom, Intelligence, and Charisma saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Reautomata fight with outward ferocity and aggressive attacks which belie the cold, unfeeling calculation at the core of each solider. In battle, Reautomata launch themselves towards their foes in great leaps, impaling their targets upon their rending arm blades. The rending blades flense into flesh and latch on like hooks, allowing the Reautomata to restrain their targets. They then use their great strength to rend apart their restrained victims.

Reautomata unquestionably obey the orders of their creator and will fight until destroyed without regard for their own bodies. However, even with only general instructions, Reautomata fight intelligently and know how to utilize the environment to their advantage, making use of their climb speeds and jumping ability to prioritize dangerous targets.

This hulking monster thinks it's large and in charge. I wonder if that thing on it's back is explosive?

items.name: Reborn  Vladimir von Drakken

entries: Vladimir von Drakken stands awash in mighty power. Standing nearly seven feet tall, he is armored head to toe in ornamented and blood-drenched plate mail. The breastplate bears the ancient sigil of House von Drakken. Draconic wings unfurl from his back, the membranes colored a deep red like a dying star. His snarling face has the chiseled features of a calculating predator. He growls, bearing his long, sharp fangs which dribble fresh blood around his perfectly trimmed salt-and-pepper beard. In a single hand, he holds a vicious greatsword, which he points towards you, issuing a mortal challenge.
This is Vladimir von Drakken's normal form, once he has regained his full strength. In this form, he is a cunning and strategic adversary.
{@i The red-skinned woman steps forward, sunlight glinting in her raven hair as red magic swirls around her.}
An elder race—older than the elves, and as old as the dragons, they claim—red hags are the most cunning and longest-lived of the hags, with a lifespan of more than a thousand years.

entries.name: Beautiful and Strong
entries: Unlike many of their hag kin, red hags are not horrid to look upon, and most are considered comely in their own right. Few know anything about them, and the red hags do little to enlighten scholars, preferring seclusion.

entries.name: Tied to Nature
entries: Red hags have a deep connection with all elements of nature, and they often make their homes in deep forests, in caves, or alongside coastlines.

entries.name: Blood Magic
entries: Because of their connection to nature, red hags often serve as druids. Within their druidic circles they practice blood sacrifices and perform ritualistic blood magic—both to slake their craving for humanoid blood, but also as a means to venerate goddesses of dark magic. The ancient hags all answer to a hierarchy with the most powerful spellcasters at the top.

entries.name: Red Hags in Midgard
entries: Red hags are more sociable among their own kind than other hags are, and they sometimes live in small communities in remote areas. In ancient times, they settled together in larger clusters and ruled small cities of mixed populations—especially in Old Verrayne. Their current leader is Blood Mother Margase, an ancient druid.
Their greatest city, Talitheos, an island metropolis of vast wealth and magical knowledge, sunk during the cataclysm, and the hags have been seeking its ruins ever since.
{@i Bands of red swirl along the abdomen of this small, black spider.}

Red-banded line spiders are named for both the deep red swirls on their abdomens, unique to each spider, and for their peculiar hunting technique. The largest ones hunt in the dark canopy of temperate and subtropical forests.

entries.name: Hand-Sized Hunters
entries: These furry, brown spiders are not enormous monsters, but they are big enough to be alarming. A typical one is as big as a human hand with fingers spread wide, but some grow as large as small dogs.

entries.name: Webbed Line
entries: Line spiders don't spin webs but instead perch and watch for prey. When prey wanders near, the spider launches a line of webbing to snare it, then pounces unerringly along that line to deliver a deep bite. Their potent venom can incapacitate creatures much larger than themselves, and they quickly devour flesh with their powerful jaws.

entries.name: City Dwellers
entries: Line spiders are often found in cities, and their size makes them a good replacement for a garroter crab in certain forms of divination. They're favorites among exotic pet dealers—usually with their venom sacs removed, sometimes not. Goblins, kobolds, and some humans use them rather than cats to control a mouse or rat infestation, and they make reasonably good pets if they're kept well-fed. If they get hungry, line spiders may devour other small pets or even their owners.

{@i This grizzled, weather-beaten creature looks like a sour old man, complete with scraggly beard. It carries a great pike and wears a blood-soaked hat and heavy boots shod with iron. It grins with massive yellow teeth}.

entries.name: Blood-Soaked Caps
entries: Redcaps are exceedingly dangerous creatures who wear the mark of their cruelty and evil quite literally. The caps from which they take their name define their very existence—these caps must constantly be revived with fresh blood.

entries.name: Compelled to Kill
entries: Redcaps aren't cruel and murderous by choice, but by necessity. A redcap must frequently bathe its cap in fresh, humanoid blood to sustain itself. If it fails to do so every three days, the creature withers and dies quickly. A redcap whose hat is nearly dry is a desperate, violent force of nature that prefers to die in battle rather than waste away to nothing.

entries.name: Bandits and Mercenaries
entries: Most long-lived redcaps are drawn to serve in marauding armies or make a living through constant banditry.

name: Refuse Golem
entries: Many speak of trash becoming treasure, but trash is lifeblood for the refuse golem. Most common in areas with large amounts of magical food and drink, these beasts form when mounds of partially consumed waste are not disposed of properly. The resulting magical landfill develops an aggressive, sentient construct that is formidable in battle, most known for their poisonous stench and amorphous defenses.

name: Reindeer
entries: {@i Snow-Treading Wanderer}
{@color Most of the brown in this large deer's coast has shed, revealing white underneath. It appears ready for the winter as it bounds through the first flurries of the year.|006abe}

Wild reindeer can be found in vast herds in the coldest parts of the Northlands. They are acclimated to cold weather. Wild reindeer are skittish, but domesticated ones have been bred for centuries for their meat, to pull sleds, and for milk.

entries.name: Remnant Chosen
entries: All devotees of {@deity The Whispered One|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} are zealous followers, spending hours in silent meditation hoping to hear their long-dead master whisper a commandment from beyond. However, only a rare few hear the spectral voice of {@deity The Whispered One|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} as it worms its way into their minds, emptying out other thought and filling their heads with clarity and direction. Much of this direction involves the {@book Remnants'|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|2|The Remnants} plans to leverage secrets stolen from the Plane of Shadow to increase the cult's power in Tal'Dorei.

entries.name: Remnant Cultist
entries: All cultists of {@deity The Whispered One|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} endure horrific rites of initiation that force them to remove one of their own eyes and forever shackle themselves to the will of the cult's leaders. Every cultist can feel the presence of their foul god just beyond the fabric of the physical world, and many claim to hear him speaking to them when all else is silent.

The cultists of {@deity The Whispered One|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} still venerate their wrathful master with offerings of secrets and unwilling souls to gain his favor, learning what they can and keeping hidden that which they know. Cultists believe in cultivating evil in themselves and recognizing it in others, encouraging them to express it. They hope to seed the ruin of all who worship other deities until only those who kneel before {@deity The Whispered One|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} remain.

entries.name: Remnants
entries: The {@book Remnants|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|2|The Remnants} is a foul cult dedicated to seeing their lich leader, {@deity The Whispered One|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}, ascend to godhood. Cultists believe that self-mutilation and transitory failings are requirements to pierce the veil and see the world for the lie it is—including accepting that the true hidden world already belongs to {@deity The Whispered One|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}.

entries.name: Bitter Victory
entries: The {@book Remnants|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|2|The Remnants} have both won and failed in their dire goal, as {@deity The Whispered One|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} ascended but was banished beyond the Divine Gate. Yet they name him the Ascendant One, the Banished One, or—because all others gods are pretenders—simply the One, and prepare patiently for his final ascension.

images.altText: Two uncanny mages casting spells. One is a pale, skinny human man with a long beard and robes, manipulating white arcane energy. The other is a white woman with claw-like armored gloves and a circle of arcane energy around her head and through one eye.

name: Reveler of Song

entries: {@i Fiend of Music and Dance}

Revelers of song are Fiends of music and abandon who turn their art against their foes in destructive reverberation. The revelers dance and play at nearly all times and are known to fly into a murderous rage if their invitations to join the celebration are spurned. A variety of revelers of song exist, depending on the type of instrument a given reveler plays. Drone revelers play the hurdy gurdy and are surrounded by an accompanying swarm of bees. {@item Drum|XPHB} revelers play drums or cymbals, and the world shakes to their beat. Bell revelers play some variety of bell, chime, or gong, and the ringing overtakes all other sounds.

entries.name: Secret
entries: Revelers of song can't accept that any creature is more skilled at an instrument than they are and so can't refuse a musical challenge.

name: Reveler of Stories

entries: {@i Fiend of Legend and Folklore}

Timeless stories have inspired countless mortals, and the echoes of those stories in the Lower Planes have spawned fiendish embodiments of those tales—the revelers of stories. These Fiends twist the themes of their tales, turning inspiration into doom. The revelers' forms and powers change depending on the theme of stories they embody. Great beast revelers of stories rise from tales of terrible monsters. Hero revelers of stories embody the exploits of knights and other mighty heroes. Witch revelers of stories bring to life tales of wicked witches, wizards, and other magicians.

entries.name: Secret
entries: Revelers of stories exist because of fables, legends, and other tales, and reciting the moral of a story related to the reveler's theme robs the reveler of its potency.

name: Rhesh Turakbar
entries: Rhesh Turakbar is the infamous warlord of Turakbar's Fist, feared and despised by Brelish settlers throughout the Western Frontier. He is a powerful minotaur warrior, and his physical might is enhanced by his devotion to the Horned King. Guided by the overlord, Rhesh Turakbar is a brutal tyrant and a deadly foe.

entries.name: Warlord of Droaam
entries: During the Last War, Rhesh Turakbar personally led countless raids against Orcbone and Brelish settlements along the Border Road. Any adventurer with roots in the frontier may have lost friends or family to Turakbar's reavers—or narrowly escaped death at his hands. With the end of open hostilities, Turakbar has pulled his forces back to the Fist and plays the role of warlord rather than reaver. As warlord, Turakbar is responsible for maintaining order in the region around Turakbar's Fist. His reavers patrol the land, but Turakbar wishes to be feared even by his subjects. He maintains order, indeed—by making a brutal example of anyone who challenges the Daughters or Turakbar himself. Some of the villages under his watch are minotaur communities; others are primarily goblins or kobolds with a few minotaur overseers. Either way, each village has a chib that answers to Turakbar—and he will often challenge chibs to test their might, killing and replacing any who prove to be too weak by his standards. There is no question that Rhesh Turakbar is maintaining order, as is the duty of a warlord. But where elsewhere in Droaam the Daughters are working to unite the different species and cultures of the region and to give their people hope, Rhesh Turakbar still rules through fear.

entries.name: Fist of the Horned King
entries: Turakbar's Fist is an artifact of the Horned King, charged with the power of Tol Kharash. The Daughters of Sora Kell gave Turakbar the title of warlord, but he earned Rhesh on his own by slaying the previous ruler of the Fist and claiming its power. Turakbar's horns are engraved with sigils that bind him to the Horned King, so that the power of the Fist flows through his blood. Turakbar can sense the fears of creatures around him, a gift he uses to intimidate his enemies and undermine his rivals. Adventurers facing Rhesh Turakbar can feel the fiendish power flowing through him—feel that he is a vessel for something ancient and terrifying. Because of his size and physical might, it is easy for people to underestimate Turakbar's intelligence. But the warlord is no fool. He may choose to be reckless in battle, but he is a cunning strategist with keen instincts. However, as a vessel for the Horned King there are limits on his behavior, much as a paladin follows an oath. Turakbar cannot willingly show fear or weakness, and he must always look for weakness in others and spread fear where he can.

Rhesh Turakbar is not immortal. He's not one of the Lords of Dust; he's a minotaur champion who's laid claim to a terrifying power, and who now has to be a brutal tyrant to hold onto that power. A DM could choose to play up Turakbar's role as a willing vessel of the overlord's spirit. In this case, his power could grow even as his personality melts away, leaving a sliver of Tol Kharash cloaked in what's left of Turakbar's flesh. On the other hand, a DM who wants more complexity could say that Rhesh Turakbar knows this is happening and is afraid of it—he doesn't want to be a puppet of Tol Kharash, but he is in too deep and sees no way to escape that fate.

entries.name: Turakbar's Reavers
entries: Bands of reavers roam the lands around Turakbar's Fist. Those to the west of the Border Road are technically servants of the appointed warlord, maintaining order as instructed by the Daughters of Sora Kell. If they encounter easterners in the region, they will typically challenge them, questioning the business of the adventurers and possibly demanding a "toll for safe passage"—a tax for Turakbar's diligent work maintaining the peace. What such reavers want most of all is to generate fear and to assert authority; both of these things are like strong drink for a demonglass warrior of Tol Kharash. Challenging the reavers can result in violence. On the other hand, travelers who truly feel no fear and who demonstrate strength—typically, by making strong {@skill Intimidation|XPHB} checks—will be left in peace.

Reavers to the west of the road maintain order; as soon as they are on the road, they disrupt it. Reavers may attack caravans, or cross the road and raid Brelish villages. These attacks are swift and brutal, but usually not as deadly as they could be. The primary objective is to sow fear and to make the settlers feel weak and helpless; this is what delights the Horned King. They would rather leave wounded survivors to carry the scars and haunting memories of the attack than to actually drive settlers from the border. They are ruthless and will kill if they are posed with a serious threat, but Turakbar's reavers prefer to inflict trauma rather than just kill their foes.

Turakbar's reavers are a blend of minotaurs, ogres, Gaa'aram orcs, shifters, and gnolls who embrace their fiendish spirits. Almost all of them are embedded with small shards of demonglass, making them Demonglass Warriors; the leader of a squad will have one or more of the Demonglass Champion traits. They typically travel in small, swift groups that can quickly disappear into the Barrens. They can't carry much plunder, but they are more interested in sowing fear than gathering gold.

The Turakbar's Reavers table provides a few examples of champions who might lead a band of reavers, while the Reavers Missions table gives ideas for what a squad of reavers might be up to when adventurers encounter them.

entries.caption: Turakbar's Reavers
rows: {@b Byraka.} A minotaur with silver-white fur, Byraka is known as the Bloody Ghost. She has the Devil's Sight and Wrath of the Horned King traits. (Minotaur, she/her)
{@b Chwyyr.} A former Znir hwyri, Chwyyr now serves the Horned King and is chief shaman of Turakbar's Fist. (Gnoll Warlock of the Fiend, he/him)
{@b Hakaar.} Once a Tharashk hunter, Hakaar delights in playing with her prey and takes special pleasure in killing Sentinel Marshals. (Half-orc Assassin, she/her)
{@b Grimtongue.} The greatest wizard of the region, Grimtongue has carved chains hanging from his horns and is devoted to Tol Kharash. (Minotaur Mage, he/him)
{@b Nol Avesh.} A warrior who served Rhesh Turakbar's predecessor, Nol knows all the secret paths in Turakbar's Fist. (Shifter Spy, he/him)
{@b Hogra the Old.} While physically old, this ogress is a hollow one channeling a Horned Devil—one of the most powerful weapons in Turakbar's arsenal. (Ogre Berserker, she/her)

entries.caption: Reaver Missions
rows: {@b Reaving.} This squad is looking for blood and will leap at any excuse to fight.
{@b Intimidation.} The group has been sent to spread fear. They won't kill if it can be avoided, but they will cause pain and suffering in pursuit of their goals.
{@b Fury's Fangs.} This team is acting as the hand of Droaamite justice, pursuing a condemned criminal.
{@b Shadow's Eyes.} These reavers have been dispatched by Rhesh Turakbar to investigate a possible threat or crime.
{@b Bloody Revel.} This squad recently completed a raid; they are still bloody and carrying their plunder.
{@b Nothing To See.} These reavers have been sent on a peaceful mission. They could be serving as couriers, picking up supplies, escorting a mystic to a ritual site, or something similar.

name: Rhys Birchwalker
entries: An associate professor of conjuration at the Avium, this middle-aged mistral raptor has little in the way of mystic talent, but she makes up for it with an enthusiasm for learning and a wealth of knowledge on her chosen subject. She is well-versed in conjuratory theory, and can provide characters with any of the information they would otherwise find in {@b Conjuration Magic} (see {@adventure Into the Library|HWAitW|4|Into the Library}) if she is asked about the subject directly. Professor Birchwalker can also help a character perform the calculations to find the location of the conjuration circle within the Grove. Rhys uses the {@creature commoner} stat block, adjusted with the racial traits of a mistral raptor. She is neutral good.

name: Riffin, the Ash-Knight
entries: Riffin is a small stout strig, standing a few inches over three feet, whose plumage and proportions resemble a little owl. A traveling knight of the realm, Riffin lived in Ashbarrow before its destruction, and was carried to Alderheart by his friend Odwald, who saved him from the fire. Being one of the only knights to hail from Ashbarrow, folk began calling him the "Ash-Knight," a title which he now uses to keep the memory of his home alive. Riffin is a simple strig with a charming way of viewing the world. He is also a steadfast warrior who strongly believes in doing what is right, helping those in need, and honoring his debts. Riffin uses the {@creature strig knight|HumblewoodCampaignSetting} stat block. His alignment is lawful good.

{@i This enormous pig is as large as an ox, and its mouth bristles with mismatched tusks. Its body is a lopsided mass of tumorous flesh that gives way to eyes and vestigial mouths, while long tentacles trail from its sides.}

From time to time, a breach forms in the fabric of the multiverse, and the Material Plane is bathed in the energy of alien dimensions. Living creatures exposed to this incursion can undergo horrible mutations, turning into monstrous mockeries of their former shapes. One example of this phenomenon is the rift swine: once-ordinary pigs transformed into slavering horrors after being bathed in eldritch light.

entries.name: Destructive Herds
entries: Rift swine travel in small herds. Their effect on an area can be catastrophic—they eat nearly anything, possess a fiendish cunning, and delight in the destruction they cause. A rift swine has difficulty perceiving anything smaller than itself as a threat, leading it to attack most other creatures on sight and fighting until it is destroyed.

entries.name: Abyssal Meat
entries: Rumors of vast herds of hundreds of rift swine on strongly chaos-aligned planes, cultivated by the lords of those places as a food source, are thankfully unconfirmed.
{@i The long, crusty slug sparkles like ice, and long tendrils dangle from its gaping mouth.}

entries.name: Ice Burrowers
entries: The rime worm's tendrils help it burrow through ice and snow as well as absorb sustenance from prey. Their pale, almost translucent, skin is coated with ice crystals, making them difficult to spot in their snowy habitat.

entries.name: Spray Black Ice
entries: The worms are fierce hunters, and their abilities to spray skewers of ice and freeze their prey make them extremely dangerous.
{@i The long, crusty slug sparkles like ice, and long tendrils dangle from its gaping mouth.}

entries.name: Ice Burrowers
entries: The rime worm's tendrils help it burrow through ice and snow as well as absorb sustenance from prey. Their pale, almost translucent, skin is coated with ice crystals, making them difficult to spot in their snowy habitat.

entries.name: Spray Black Ice
entries: The worms are fierce hunters, and their abilities to spray skewers of ice and freeze their prey make them extremely dangerous.

This massive creature is made up of mutated, stitched-together body parts. The process of joining parts and intentional mutations has rendered the former patient into a mindless beast, nearly swallowed by its own growths. Its oversized arms carry a great whirling bone saw that spins and whirs as it lumbers forward, spraying gore and soaking its aprons in blood, bone, and grey matter. They wear a blood-soaked medical apron and mask.

A Ripper is a creation of a truly mad apothecary, though one ostensibly created as a "surgical assistant" for dissection and autopsy. In truth, a Ripper's only purpose is as a butcher, carrying out the grim task of dismembering corpses and collecting severed parts to supply fresh materials to create more abominations. Transforming morgues into abattoirs and surgery rooms into charnel houses, having a Ripper amongst their servants enables an Apothecary to work with startling efficiency.
Due to their horrific appearance and grim purpose, Rippers are seldom encountered outside an Apothecary's laboratory. Given their size and brutal skill, Rippers make ideal guardians.

entries.name: Parts Collectors
entries: Apothecaries stitch all manner of extra arms, hands, and limbs to their Rippers, which the creature uses to gather severed body parts and hold down subjects.

entries.name: Fear Engine
entries: The Ripper's tortured mind sympathetically responds when it senses a victim's fear and terror, but its twisted brain responds with adrenaline and bloodlust.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Arcana|XPHB} or {@skill Medicine|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks to Study a Ripper, learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (10+) Occult Science Construct
entries: You know of its Insensitive to Pain trait, as well as its damage and condition {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: (15+) Razor-Sharp Weapons
entries: You recognize the Ripper's Whirling Bonesaw attack, and it's Feed on Fear and Dismemberment traits.

entries.name: (20+) Formidable but Dim-Witted
entries: You learn the Ripper's Constitution, Dexterity, and Intelligence saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Ripper is an unsubtle and unsophisticated combatant, but it can follow its creators' orders intelligently. Unless directed otherwise, a Ripper usually begins battle by using its Gory Display to terrify its victims. It then ponderously moves towards its chosen target before lowering its Saw Blade down, preferring {@condition Frightened|XPHB} targets to benefit from its Feed on Fear trait. During its turn, a Ripper continues attacking with its Saw Blade until it misses. If it reduces a target to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it does not stop making attacks until its target dies.

{@i A body that might once have been human now has four legs and nightmarishly long, thick arms. What's worse, its skin has been flayed off, revealing the dead muscle and sinew beneath.}

entries.name: Spirit of War
entries: The risen reaver is an undead creature born from a warrior fallen on the battlefield. Its body becomes an avatar of combat, with four legs and a pair of long, heavy arms. In the process, it sheds its skin, becoming entirely undead muscle, bone, and sinew.

entries.name: Absorb Weapons
entries: When risen reavers take form, they absorb all weapons around them. Some of these weapons pierce their bodies, while others become part of the risen reaver's armament. Their four legs are tipped with blades on which they walk like metallic spiders. Their arms are covered in weaponry infused into their flesh, which they use to crush and flay any living creatures they encounter

entries.name: Battle Mad
entries: Risen reavers are battle-maddened spirits of vengeance and slaughter, obsessed with the chaos of combat that led to their own death. They hunt the living with the sole purpose of killing, and they thrive on violence and murder. As they died, so should others die.
{@i A tall, slender giant wades knee-deep through the river, holding a glowing fishing net in his hand.}
Shorter and slimmer than most other giants, river giants are found living along riverbanks throughout the Shadow Realm and in the mortal world where waterways cross or run alongside the shadow roads.

entries.name: River Travelers
entries: Capable boat pilots, these introspective giants sometimes transport travelers up and down the rivers of the Shadow Realm in their wooden skiffs, but they are most often found wading through the water with their glistening mooncatcher's nets. The giants use the nets to pull bits of souls and memories from the river. These fragments are bottled and traded to wizards and alchemists who use them to make memory philters and other potions.

{@i This powerfully muscled elf lord wears a cloak of foam-trimmed dark blue and a vest of woven green reeds and willow branches. His crown shines like the sun on a lake, and his flowing hair curls and moves even when there is no wind. An orb of blue light that ripples like water circles his hand}.

His Rippling Majesty, Ulorian the River King, also bears the titles Defender of the Pearl Tower and Master of the Deep Forest. A lean elf noble with whipcord muscles and flowing grace, the River King rules over the Rippling Court and ultimately all the river elves of the forest. His court resides just beyond the river's reflection, in a realm of fey glamour and silty water.

entries.name: A Fickle Friend
entries: The River King is a stern ruler with a great love for his people and a quick temper for those who threaten his domain. As much a force of nature as he is a monarch, the River King is known to sometimes forget promises that were made in sincerity, and dealing with him can be perilous at the best of times. "The river may change its course when it wills" is the usual expression among his court when His Rippling Majesty has had a sudden change of heart.

entries.name: Fey Lords and Ladies
entries: Fey are capricious, mischievous, and often dangerous beings. However, despite their chaotic reputations, they do follow a certain set of rules. These rules—widely misunderstood by outsiders—are codified and enforced by a cadre of lofty fey nobility. Befitting any courtly structure, the fey bow to lords and ladies: eldritch creatures of immense power who rule the courts.

entries.name: Heads of State
entries: The fey lords and ladies are beings of high station and prodigious personal power. Each rules over at least a great city if not an entire nation. No matter the scope of a fey noble's domain, in his or her eyes, a fey ruler's word is law. Outsiders might not understand the edicts and interdicts of a fey noble, but that's no protection against the harsh penalties that await any who break them, knowingly or otherwise.

entries.name: Vacant Thrones
entries: When a lord or lady of the fey dies, the court does not remain leaderless for long. Ambitious beings among the fey always hunger for more power and covet the stations of their superiors. After a traditional month or year of mourning, vicious power struggles winnow the weak and pave the way for the most cunning or the strongest to take the court's vacant throne.

entries.name: The River King's Lair
entries: The Court of the River King is a pair of small islands in the middle of a wide, swift river that flows from the mortal realm through a dimension of fey magic. The western keep houses servants, and the eastern is built above the Great Rippling Hall. The Great Rippling Hall is a bubble whose walls and ceiling are the river itself. A driftwood throne dominates the main hall.

{@i A charming grey cobblestone bridge arches over a stream of black brackish water. Crawling up and over the sides of the bridge, tendrils of thick black water coalesce into a helmed warrior bearing a sword—which it points toward you, as if daring you to use the bridge.}
River spirits are fey guardians that defend bridges and other crossing points over bodies of water.

entries.name: Stubborn Guardians
entries: River spirits are called into existence by the magic between water and shore, and they often appear quite suddenly, claiming a crossing point without any warning. Some river spirits allow travelers to pass over their bridges freely, but possessive or ornery spirits might bring all crossing to a complete standstill with challenges or demands. Since river spirits cannot truly die once they have bound themselves to a bridge, getting them to leave inevitably requires negotiation or powerful banishing magic.

entries.name: Unwavering Loyalty
entries: While river spirits are difficult to reason with, particularly patient or persuasive creatures can forge a friendly bond with them. River spirits may adjust their demands or even agree to guard different crossing points at the request of such a friend. Those who forge such a relationship gain their unwavering loyalty, and such a stout guardian may defend a location often long after the instigating creature has died. Fey bard often name and know of particular river spirits.

items.name: River

entries: River is a short tiefling woman in her late twenties. Her attire is practical and professional: a hip-length purple jacket with a high collar. Belted at her waist are several pouches and pockets. She wears five rings on her right hand. Two oddlyshaped dark brown horns sprout backwards from her flowing blue hair, creating the impression of two boats at sea. River has spotted brown skin and impish features: her teeth are too sharp, her tongue too long, and it's slightly unsettling when she smiles.

River is a communications expert and analyst. She aids the Academy's mission using spells such as {@spell Sending} and {@spell Rary's Telepathic Bond|XPHB|Telepathic Bond} to relay messages between field agents and Academy leadership, gathers information using {@spell Detect Thoughts} and {@spell Scrying}, and facilitates transportation of Academy assets from their distant strongholds to Emberwood Village via {@spell Teleportation Circle}.

entries.name: Personality Trait
entries: I converse using precise academic terminology, but amongst those I trust as competent and capable, I inject a wry and sardonic sense of humor.

entries.name: Ideal
entries: I like people who are professional, deliver results, and don't ask questions. I cannot stand fools who waste my time with buffoonery, haggling, and excuses.

entries.name: Bond
entries: Eldrick Runeweaver is my mentor, teacher, and friend.
I've worked alongside him for years, and any success he has will be mine as well.

entries.name: Flaw
entries: I grew up surrounded by the magical amenities of the Amethyst Academy, so I don't understand what life is like for those who had a more mundane upbringing.

River is not a combatant and never initiates violence. If she is attacked or finds herself in the midst of conflict, her sole objective is survival. Her first action is always to cast either {@spell Dimension Door} or {@spell Invisibility} and flee. She won't take risks with her own life, even to fulfill a critical objective for the Amethyst Academy or save someone she cares about. However, she will take the opportunity to help another ally escape by using {@spell Invisibility} on them or bringing them with her when she teleports.
The giver of gifts and knowledge—she is a strong ally and an old friend — weird brother.

entries.name: Rivermaw Brawler
entries: Many children in the {@book Rivermaw herd|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Rivermaw Herd} get into friendly brawls, but only the truly dedicated learn the art of fist fighting. Rivermaw brawlers usually lead the charge on the battlefield, using their exceptional strength, speed, and cunning to throw an enemy vanguard into chaos.

Beyond the {@book Dividing Plains|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Dividing Plains}, brawlers trained by the Rivermaw can be found in noble adventuring parties, working for the {@book Clasp|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|2|The Clasp} as muscle, in underground fighting rings, and as personal bodyguards. In {@book Emon|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Emon, the City of Fellowship}, the most famous fist fighters make a name for themselves within the {@book Brawler's League|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|2|Brawler's League} or the {@book Godsbrawl|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|10. Godsbrawl Ring}, representing the {@deity The Stormlord|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|Stormlord} in that annual holy tournament.

entries.name: Rivermaw Stormborn
entries: Countless goliath legends tell of heroes born beneath a raging storm: Kaldon Thunderhead, who slew the {@creature ember roc|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} of the south; Marydra Skysplitter, who defeated a champion of the {@deity The Ruiner|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|Ruiner} in single combat; and Yodrell Rumblechest, who halted a flash flood with only his voice, to name just a few.

Though the stormborn of legend were all {@book half-giants|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|4|Half-Giants}, more and more Rivermaw have begun to feel the {@deity The Stormlord|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|Stormlord's} power reverberate within them. These peerless warriors are blessed with preternatural skill with a blade and the uncanny ability to command lightning. Often destined to become mythic heroes, stormborn fight with reckless abandon—but many can be distressingly prideful and might need reminding that the songs of defeated or tyrannical stormborn are rarely sung by the bards.

The tyrant Kevdak's fearsome Herd of Storms was so named because of the many stormborn in its ranks, but that herd was broken at {@book Westruun|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Westruun} some two decades ago. Now the {@book Rivermaw herd|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Rivermaw Herd} is bolstered by those who were freed from Kevdak's rule. The few stormborn remaining from that broken herd are part of the Rivermaw, and more storm-blessed warriors have been born into the Rivermaw since, ready to forge new legends.

entries.name: Rivermaw Warriors
entries: The {@book Rivermaw herd|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Rivermaw Herd} is a nomadic society mostly composed of {@book half-giants|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|4|Half-Giants}, also known as {@book goliaths|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|4|Half-Giants}, and a mighty force for good on the {@book Dividing Plains|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Dividing Plains}. The herd was once conquered by a goliath tyrant named Kevdak, then formed anew after Kevdak was eventually defeated by Vox Machina. Free of Kevdak's martial cruelty, the Rivermaw see it as their duty to prevent any such tyrant from conquering the {@book Dividing Plains|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Dividing Plains} ever again.

Though most members of the {@book Rivermaw herd|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Rivermaw Herd} are {@book goliaths|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|4|Half-Giants}, their ranks include people of all races who wish to live beyond the stone walls of {@book Westruun|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Westruun} and the palisades of plains towns like {@book Turst Fields|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Turst Fields}. {@book Orcs|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|4|orcs}, {@book humans|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|4|humans}, {@book halflings|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|4|halflings}, and {@book gnolls|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|6|gnolls} make up most of the rest of the herd's warriors. Most of those warriors value strength and endurance over other qualities, but the brawlers and stormborn of the Rivermaw are better known for cunning, intelligence, strategy, and a unique attunement to the mighty thunder of the {@deity The Stormlord|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|Stormlord}.

images.altText: A male and female goliath stand next to each other. The male is bald, clad in leather and metal armor and bears a greataxe that crackles with green, arcane energy. The female has long, dark hair and wears spiked gauntlets.

entries: {@i The creature is humanoid but disturbingly roachlike. Its legs are too short, its arms too long, and its back is covered by a carapace. Atop those features is an incongruously humanlike face}.

Combining the worst of human and cockroach qualities, these nimble creatures have a talent for stealth and for fighting dirty. Due to their natural resilience against disease, roachlings are comfortable with filth. "Good hygiene" is a foreign concept. This leaves most humanoids repulsed by the roachlings' smell.

entries.name: Clever Combatants
entries: Though skittish and easily frightened, roachlings are practical, not cowards. They understand survival often depends on remaining unseen and out of reach, and they are adept at hit-and-run tactics.

entries.name: Cautious and Family-Oriented
entries: Because most humanoids shun roachlings, they are naturally cautious around others, and they extend their trust to non-roachlings slowly. They live and associate with a tight-knit, extended family, which is led by a male or female roachling lord, and they put the needs of their community above all. A roachling away from or without a family often bonds with those it trusts most.

entries.name: Fused Carapace
entries: Roachlings have prominent, whip-like antennae, a carapace covering much of their backs, and small spines on their legs and arms. They have short, noticeably bowed legs, and their hair is dark. Their thick, hardened skin appears shiny and slightly oily, although it is dr. Roachlings have an internal skeleton, however, not the exoskeleton of a true insect.
