Foot soldiers of a necromancer it reminds me of when you left the dishes too long in the sink.

It appeared from the darkness: a faceless wraith whose outstretched arms sought purchase on my mortal frame. In desperation, I cried to my companions for aid, but my voice was silent. When it stole my words, I knew my doom was at hand.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The bones of a mortal transformed into a scream thief remain imbued with its undead aura. A skilled magic item crafter using 200 gp of magical regents, and spending at least 5 days of effort, can create a {@item wand of silence|GrimHollowLairsEtharis} (see Appendix A of {@adventure Lairs of Etharis|GrimHollowLairsEtharis|21}) if they succeed on a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check.

A spellcaster can capture a psychic fragment's essence before it dissipates after death. The spellcaster requires a container worth at least 100 gp. Anyone who succeeds on a {@dc 13} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check can capture a portion of the defeated psychic fragment. The container can store up to 10 hit die worth of undead essence for 8 hours before they dissipate.

As an action, a container holding this spiritual essence can be thrown up to 20 feet, shattering on impact. All creatures within 5 feet of the broken container must make a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw. A failed saving throw results in {@dice 1d4} necrotic damage per hit die of essence stored, while a success deals half as much damage.

entries.name: Lore

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
items.entry: The scream thief is immune to necrotic and poison. The incorporeal nature of psychic fragments makes them resistant to nonmagical weapons.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
items.entry: The touch of a scream thief drains life that magic cannot heal; only time and rest can.

entries: A scream thief remains trapped in its place of death, often accompanied by spirit fragments of the creatures it has killed.
{@i This aquamarine dragon has a shark's head that tapers off into a sleek eel-like body. Its large fins double as wings.}

entries.name: Divine Dragons
entries: Sea dragons are the children of the ocean and believe they are semi-divine beings, worthy of worship. Given their size and power, they might be right; certainly, they are often companions or steeds to gods of the sea. Despite the solemn duties the sea dragons invoke thanks to their lineage, they are extremely whimsical. While these immense creatures are playful, their games can shatter hulls and drown sailors. The sea dragons course through the waves with tangible joy as they hunt whales and entire schools of tuna.

entries.name: Shipwreck Art
entries: Sea dragons love collecting treasure. They especially prize the sunken, treasure-filled hulls of ships lost to storm, battle, or their own handiwork. While they appreciate all wealth, they prefer hardy items that stand up to long exposure to sea water. Precious metals and gemstones add a dramatic luster to the dragon's lair when they catch stray beams of light. Sea dragons take more perishable treasures and place them on a reef-altar, to dissolve in the sea as a tithe to the sea gods.

entries.name: Sunken Memorials
entries: A sea dragon's lair is littered with meticulously arranged ships consigned to the deeps. These wrecks are often artfully smashed to allow the treasures in the hold to spill out onto the sea floor. It may seem haphazard, but it displays a complex aesthetic that only other sea dragons can truly appreciate. Because they arrange these wrecks so carefully, a dragon notices immediately if its hoard is disturbed.

entries.name: Priests of Seggotan
entries: Every sea dragon is devoted to the dragon god of the sea. As a result, many sea dragons use the innate spellcasting variant. Sea dragons favor spells that manipulate water or the weather, emulate storms, deal lightning or cold damage, divine the future, or conjure sea creatures to fight alongside the dragon.

entries.name: Sea Dragons in Midgard
entries: Sea dragons are the offspring of Seggotan, the dragon god of time and the sea. A sea dragon shares its god's idea that everything in the sea is the property of Seggotan, and they expect lesser beings to respect that truth. The sea dragons are among the most powerful allies of the Mharoti Empire, securing seaways and acting as a communion point for the tidal priests. Thankfully for the Empire's enemies, the most ancient sea dragons are too consumed with contemplation of time and their inscrutable duties in the depths of the ocean to make war.
Descendants of the great dragons of the mythic past still roam Etharis. They have little of the majesty of their ancestors, but they're still frightening.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Dragons are rare on Etharis, so materials from their corpses fetch a good price. A dragon's corpse can be sold for at least 100 gp times the Challenge of the monster.

Someone who has proficiency with alchemist's supplies can reduce the brain of a prismatic drake into an oil that can be used to fashion one arrow of dragon slaying. Brewing the oil takes 5 days of work, reagents worth 2,000 gp, and a successful {@dc 17} Intelligence or Wisdom check. Making the arrow is a trivial task, but treating it properly with the oil takes 5 more days of work.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
items.entry: Sea drakes are cunning grapplers resistant to cold, sky drakes are adept fliers and have a bite charged with lightning, and blight drakes collect diseases that don't kill them but make for a toxic bite.

items.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
items.entry: Prismatic drakes are the rarest drakes, rumored to be sorcerers transformed into dragons after they foolishly connected their minds to Gormadraug, the slumbering Prismatic Dragon. These drakes can cast spells.

name: Sea Lindwurm
entries: {@i Seal Snake of the Bitter Waves}

{@color At first, this creature resembles a normal, if gigantic seal with a disturbingly large mouth. But when it gets closer, you realize that the beast is anything but normal. Its skin is covered in fine scales, and short spiny ridges sprout from its back. It opens its mouth to reveal shark-like teeth.|006abe}

Unwary or ignorant hunters and sailors often mistake sea lindwurms for enormous seals. However, while their heads are vaguely seal-like, their bodies are more serpentine in appearance, with smooth, blackish-purple scales and large flippers that allow them to drag themselves up onto ice floes and beaches on the rare occasions when they leave the water's safety.

Sea lindwurms use their seal-like appearance to sneak up on unwary boats, but this is not their only means of capturing prey. Their bite carries a potent toxin that causes a spreading paralysis in their victims, and they can slap their flippers on the water's surface to stun enemies.
Sea lindwurms and common lindwurms sometimes meet out on the pack ice or in fjords. Typically, these meetings end in a furious struggle between the two monsters.

name: Sea Serpent
entries: {@i Swift Wave Snakes}
{@color Blue-green on top with white underbellies, these enormous eel-like creatures have prominent bony ridges on their heads and wide mouths with only four sharp fangs.|006abe}

Sea serpents are most often identified while approaching by the row of sail-like fins protruding from their backs. Wild serpents are dangerous predators, but those raised from an egg imprint on their owner and make formidable mounts or guards for raiding ships.

name: Seaweed Elemental
entries: Terrifying tales of seaweed elementals are told in many of the taverns along the Obojiman coastline—sailors wrapped in swaths of green kelp and being dragged to the bottom of the Shallows are a common thread in stories that send chills down the spine. For the most part, the Shallows are clear of kelp, so spotting a seaweed elemental is easy for a vigilant sailor, but for those who wish to explore the underwater realm, a seaweed elemental is a serious threat, especially if one wanders into its domain.

name: Seed Coin
entries: Besides the occasional silver, most seed coins grow to closely mimic the appearance of the local copper coin, using its limited psychic abilities to match its shape to the bearer's perception. This same psychic connection is also the coin's means for beginning its infestation of a creature's body. Grim speculations suggest that it purposefully takes the form of a copper piece to increase the likelihood of ending up in the possession of prey that can more easily disappear, such as common laborers or beggars.

name: Seed Coin Pollinator
entries: Once a seed coin has fully taken root in its host's mind, it begins to burrow into their flesh. From there, it begins to expand its vines through the veins of the deceased creature, utilizing the abundant moisture, nutrients, and direct access to the body's brain and lungs. Once it has spread, it puppets the form with these vines, though the bulk of it resides in the unmoving lungs and skull cavity. This rapid growth strengthens the body's cell walls, making them heardier and more plant-like below the skin's surface. The appearance changes little, but the pollinator is most certainly a plant and not a humanoid.

entries.name: Seed Coins
entries: Out of all the strange plants across the Material Plane, perhaps the most insidious among them is the seed coin. Taking the appearance of a humble copper piece, or occasionally a silver, they easily pass from hand to hand in marketplaces. When they take root, they develop into their second stage of growth, infested pollinators that only appear human. These walking 'flowers' latch onto and collectively build the third stage, a germination stall, which coordinates the coins and pollinators to further expand their reach.

entries.name: Pernicious Parasite
entries: Because it relies on such mundane and seamless camouflage, the danger of this plant's infestation is considerable. These simple but deadly plants have been known to eradicate entire cities, especially thriving and bustling trade centers. As such, many cities with large enough ports or roadways keep a constant team of investigators on hand to follow leads from their money changers.

In a city as large as Antronec, it's impossible to register every merchant and stall, so the Mercantile Guild's currency department focuses on careful and consistent examination of their coinage at their various Fiscal Exchange Centers. If the Federal Mint and Savings suspects an infestation, their first step is usually to offer the city's populace 11 freshly minted copper pieces in exchange for 10 used ones. They do this in order to test if the coinage is made from plant matter and burns, or metal that melts normally.
{@i This grinning humanoid looks like a handsome man, if not for his glowing red eyes, insectoid legs, and antennae.}

entries.name: Dark Satyrs
entries: The selang or dark satyrs are twisted and vicious fauns who have abandoned nature worship and instead venerate ancient gods of deep and malign intelligence. Selangs seek to help those evil gods enter the mortal world by opening dark portals and bridging a path to realms beyond mortal understanding.

entries.name: Battle Song and Laughter
entries: Selangs relish battle, pain, and torture. They find violence thrilling and bloodshed exciting, and they often laugh, sing, and boast shamelessly during combat. Although they are the diplomats and spokesmen of the old gods, their manic speech and alien logic can sometimes be hard to follow. They are most comfortable with the slithering tones of Void Speech.

entries.name: Blasphemous Music
entries: Selang cults and settlements are often found at the sites sacred to the dark gods, making hypnotic and alien harmonies with swarms of dorreqi. They are rarely the strongest soldiers, instead encouraging evil humanoids or other creatures of martial mien to fill the ranks, while the dark satyrs use their magic and poison against their foes.

name: Selkie
entries: {@i Seal-Skin Shapechanger}

{@color A young man dances on the shore, graceful upon the sand. When he notices you, he stops and reaches for a nearby cloak. As it swirls around his shoulders, he disappears. In his place, a seal slips beneath the ocean waves.|006abe}

Selkies are fey creatures that transform into seals using magical sealskins. Their humanoid forms are beautiful, with webbed hands and feet. If deprived of its sealskin, a selkie can't change its shape and will do all it can to retrieve the skin. Selkies vary in temperament; some are kind, while others are malicious tricksters.

Selkies live on secluded islands but travel to coastlands in summer to trade with coastal enclaves, sometimes even wooing or marrying fisherfolk. Selkies rarely remain, for the sea and its freedom call to them each high tide.

Selkies believe that long ago, an archfey of seals gave them their magical sealskins. Stealing a selkie's sealskin is considered the gravest of crimes, and they will band together to retrieve a stolen sealskin, often with violent consequences. Some selkies have learned to disguise their skins as items of clothing, especially disheveled or mundane clothing, such as belts, hats, vests, or cloaks, to avoid attracting the attention of thieves. An individual selkie's skin works only for them, becoming nonmagical when it dies, and can't be used by anyone else, even other selkies.

Legends tell of selkie tribes that use the skins of other sea animals to change shape. Such selkies use the skins of sharks, giant sea horses, or even orcas, and can assume those forms instead of a seal form.

name: Senmo
entries: Every now and then, Malgrotha tears at its own body in mindless rage, rending off a piece of its own flesh. This flesh then wriggles and grows, sprouting limbs and talons of its own as it struggles to its feet and lurches off into the forest to hunt. These are the Children of Malgrotha, and they tirelessly search the forest for their mother. They believe that every dara is the First Dara—the being that imprisoned their mother in the Crawling Canopy and who has the key to releasing them from this moving prison.

name: Sentient Planetoid

entries: The surface of the planet drifting before you suddenly begins to swirl and shift, mirroring the human features of a face within the canyons and ridges of its form. A telepathic voice booms in your ears as it leers at you with a cold stare glistening with curiosity and mild disdain.

Drifting through the void of the Space Between Worlds are planetoids which possess a well of knowledge about the cosmos. They silently float through the void on an endless pursuit of understanding. Their eternal quest for ultimate comprehension of the meaning of all things is an impossible and foolhardy errand, but nonetheless they carry on, observing and learning all they can.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill History|XPHB} or {@skill Nature|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine a Sentient Planetoid, learning the following based on the result.

entries.name: (10+) Mental Fortress
entries: You are aware of the creature's {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: (15+) Panoptic Arcanist
entries: You learn of the creature's All-Knowing Magic action.

entries.name: (20+) Unfathomable Strength
entries: You know the creature's highest and lowest ability scores.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Sentient Planetoids are not all hostile creatures. Some of them, who have knowledge of mortals deem them a pest or a problem, especially if traversing the Space Between Worlds. Like a mortal who finds a rat in their home, a sentient planetoid will attempt to remove the creature or kill it.

Some planetoids might wish to converse with mortals, wanting to learn information from them about simple concepts of mundane life, or ask questions they think a mortal would know, only to confuse them with esoteric concepts and broad ideas of the universe. This can sometimes frustrate a planetoid who may react by simply wanting to eradicate the creature who bothered it.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Aberration.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Contaminated Ichor.

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Plates.

entries.name: Dust:
entries: Aberrant Dust.
Would you believe that giant rock is alive? I would, because everything seems to have an agenda now. Can't sit anywhere.

name: Sentinel Marshal
entries: Sentinel Marshals are the pride of House Deneith. A Marshal on the frontier could be pursuing a fugitive that's seeking to shelter in Droaam, or they might be encountered as an elite bodyguard protecting a merchant or important emissary.
Sentinel Marshals are among the best the Blademarks Guild has to offer: they are dedicated to their work, and not easily swayed by taunts, vices, or other distractions.

name: Serevok
entries: Arcane cultist serving Angrboda

{@i The hooded cultist utters a sibilant phrase. Then, like a fading mask of fog, his face suddenly vanishes and in its stead leers a monstrous serpent's head. His terrible, slit eyes blaze unblinkingly as his scaly hands twist and contort in arcane gestures}.

entries.name: Priests of the Serpent God
entries: Grim tales are told of a prehistoric race of evil snake-people who, wearing the guise of a human cult, have surreptitiously built a monstrous religion around the worship of—the serpent god Yig. As an actor dons a mask, these fiendish humanoids use illusory magic to imitate anyone they wish. This disguise is often betrayed, however, by the presence of the serpentfolk's frightful, fetid scent.

entries.name: Under Cloak of Blasphemy
entries: Serpentfolk of Yig rely on natural cunning and the sorcery of their cold, reptilian bloodline to survive. These snake-people live in secret amongst the cities of civilized nations and plot to overthrow the warm-blooded inheritors of the world "when the stars are right." Known as "they that walk the night," the serpentfolk of Yig live to serve their dark god's hideous, evil agenda. Many seek to become powerful spellcasters and master assassins to better serve their cruel life's purpose. The Queen of Serpents (see {@i Creature Codex}) considers the serpentfolk abominations, corrupted versions of true serpents, and there is great enmity between her followers and the followers of Yig.

entries.name: The Snake That Speaks
entries: In defiance of the creation myths surrounding the World Serpent Veles, the serpentfolk worship their Great Old One progenitor as the true Father of Serpents, knowing him by many names—Set, Quetzelcoatl, and Ningishzida among them. As their insidious cults grow in size—swollen with allied horrors like the Servants of Yig, the scitalis (see {@i Creature Codex}), and other reptilian monstrosities—the serpentfolk move further and further from their shadowed jungle enclaves to corrupt the credulous kingdoms of man.
{@i The spotted and scaly quadruped runs on hairless leonine paws, while its draconic head perches atop a sinuous, serpentine neck.}

entries.name: Swaying, Snakelike Cats
entries: Serpopards are 13 feet long and weigh 600 pounds, with little gender dimorphism. They have feline bodies but long, serpentine necks topped by vaguely draconic heads. Their hairless paws have wickedly curved, retractable talons. A serpopard's neck is in constant motion, swaying like a cobra, allowing it to track foes on all sides and to strike in unexpected directions.

entries.name: Easily Distracted
entries: Serpopards are foul-tempered predators and scavengers, and they are known to occasionally cannibalize their weakest pack mate. They actively hunt humanoids when possible and also attack other predators to steal their kills—or to kill and eat the predators, then take their kills. Serpopards are not tenacious hunters, however. They can be distracted from a pursuit by the appearance of an easier meal.

entries.name: Musk Glands
entries: In some culture, serpopard pelts and musk glands are prized for use in fashion and perfumes. Images of these odd animals appear regularly in ancient tomb iconography and temple decoration.

name: Serum Brute

entries: {@i Cursed Giant Enhanced by Alchemy}

Serum brutes are descended from giants who suffered an enduring curse when they failed to take over a Fey domain. They have third eyes, usually in their foreheads, which channel the giants' curse into the world around them. All three of their eyes are sewn or otherwise sealed shut to contain the curse. Serum brutes are further enhanced with—and get their name from—a series of alchemical infusions, often delivered through implanted vessels and tubes, which seek to deaden their sorrow and pain, as well as the disturbing power of their third eyes. They form deep emotional bonds with any who offer them comfort and an escape from the pain of their curse, and they are often willing to die for those allies.

entries.name: Secret
entries: Serum brutes are dependent upon their curse, and magic that breaks curses can leave the giants debilitated and bereft.

images.credit: Humble Squid Creatives & Ona Kristensen & Suzanne Helmigh

name: Sewer Thing

entries: The murky sewer waters churn as something below the surface stirs. A mass of debris, algae, and waste slowly rises from the water, and a sloping mass of sewage emerges with a gurgling hiss. Before you, a great shambling form launches towards you, grasping with its writhing tendrils, moving through sewage with surprising speed.

No one knows how the Sewer Thing came to be. Some speculate its a person who drowned in the sewers before {@condition contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} took their form and merged with the raw sewage around them. Others suggest the creature is {@condition contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}, turning plants and debris into horrific monsters. Regardless, enough stories have spoken of avoiding the sewers for most to steer clear of those areas.

The Sewer Thing hunts in the sewers of Drakkenheim, absorbing anything that gets in its path. It is an unseen killer using its tendrils to pull victims into the sewage to be absorbed and causes others nearby to retch and vomit. It is depicted as a legend in the scrawlings of aquatic Dregs who call the sewers home. The Dregs and Ratlings speak of the terrible thing that feeds on their people.
Ratlings use the Sewer Thing as a cautionary tale for their young, telling them not to travel alone and to run when water churns.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Survival|XPHB} gains {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Nature|XPHB}) checks to Study a Sewer Thing, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (5+) Resilient Plant
entries: You know it's creature type, {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}, and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}

entries.name: (10+) Poisonous Engulfer
entries: You learn of the creature's Poison Absorption and Engulf features.

entries.name: (15+) Sense of Self
entries: You understand the creature's Wisdom and Charisma ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Sewer Thing waits for the opportune moment to strike.

It lets creatures approach, appearing as plant matter over some sewer debris. Once its prey is close, it springs to life, lashing out with its tendrils at any it has surprised, attempting to Engulf them. This tactic works well if it is in water or sewage, where it can pull victims beneath the surface.

The Sewer Thing starts combat attempting to Engulf surprised targets. Once a creature is Engulfed, the Sewer Thing retreats into the sewer water and flees. It is a hunter, consuming its prey by dissolving them inside of it. Once it has its food, it has no reason to stay and fight.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Plant.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Contaminated Ichor, Goopy Ooze, Venom, Sap.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Flowers, Flesh.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Tentacles.

entries.name: Hair:
entries: Leaves.

entries.name: Dust:
entries: Plant Dust.
{@i The gray unicorn appears desiccated with its skeleton clearly visible beneath its taut flesh. A haunting melody surrounds it.}

entries.name: Shadow Horses
entries: Shadhavar are natives of the Plane of Shadow. Although they resemble undead unicorns, they are living creatures imbued with shadow essences.

entries.name: Fey and Undead Riders
entries: While the shadhavar are intelligent creatures, they sometimes serve as mounts for the shadow fey, noctiny, hobgoblins, wights, or other creatures. They expect to be treated well during such an arrangement; more than one unkind rider has ridden off on a shadhavar and never returned.

entries.name: Deceptive Hunters
entries: Shadhavar use their hollow horn to play captivating sounds for defense or to draw in prey. They hunt when they must and are not discriminating about their quarry, but shadhavar primarily eat carrion. Despite their horrific appearance, they are not naturally evil.
{@i A mass of shadows and cloudstuff, never touching the ground, extends clawed hands as it reveals a glint of jagged teeth.}

entries.name: Called from the Void
entries: Shadow beasts are thought to be the result of shadow fey dabbling in the magic of the Void, transforming the shadow fey into something wholly different. Almost shapeless and largely incorporeal, through an act of will they can form rough semblances of their old bodies when needed.

entries.name: Hate the Past
entries: The motivations of these creatures are inscrutable. They despise light and anything that reminds them of light or of their former existence. Beyond that, little is understood about them.

entries.name: Cryptic Messages
entries: Shadow beasts are seldom found in groups, but when they are, they seem to have no difficulty or reluctance about operating and fighting together. They have been known to deliver cryptic and threatening messages, but speaking is difficult for them. At times, they perform arcane rituals with the aid of evil humanoids and the use of dark materials. In these rituals, they sacrifice magical energies and life blood as well as the tears of innocents and the souls of the damned.
{@i The stump of a blackened, frostbitten conifer stands upright on six leg-like roots and scuttles sideways like an arboreal hermit crab. Inky shadows fill a hollow near the base of the stump.}

entries.name: Born of Vampires
entries: When a vampire becomes a crimson mist (see {@i Creature Codex}), the terrified, bestial essence of the vampire initially flees and hides as it attempts to regain its senses. The mist lurks in the shadow of a tall tree in the icy northern lowlands and devours tree-dwelling insects and small animals until it is strong enough to once again hunt. The tree, weakened by the necrotic energy coming off the strengthening crimson mist, often succumbs to frostbite, animating the next sunset as a shadow blight.

entries.name: Spreading Parasite
entries: The shadow blight longs to spread the shadow that animates it to other dead trees. It also tries to find a door to the Plane of Shadows, allowing it to exist in secluded darkness forever. It is willing to slaughter anyone who prevents it from satisfying its desires.

entries.name: Red Flowering
entries: Shadow blights are sometimes cultivated by vampires, liches, or necromancers as particularly loathsome guardians. When they kill a living creature, they briefly flower. These blossoms resemble a pinkish dogwood or, in some climates, a flowering plum tree.
{@i A gray-skinned elf steps out of the darkness itself. Its pair of onyx horns seems to absorb the light around it. It gives a friendly smile, revealing small fangs}.

To most, the shadow fey are little more than a dancing shadow among the leaves. To savants, they are the creatures that taught the shadow dancers all they know—and kept many secrets to themselves. They were once elves like all others, dwelling in mortal lands beneath the sun. An ancient catastrophe drove them to darkness, and now they are creatures of the shadow. Though they can be found on the Material Plane, they are inextricably tied to the Plane of Shadow, and that is the seat of their power and culture. Their bond with darkness allows the shadow fey to slip through distant spaces, traversing darkness itself from one place to another.

entries.name: Shadow Elves
entries: Shadow fey superficially resemble other elves, but they're rarely mistaken for their light-bound cousins. Skin tones among the shadow fey range from alabaster white to ebony black, with shades of gray in between, but they otherwise lack color. A few have a scintillating shimmer to their skin. Many shadow fey grow horns that sweep out from their hair, varying in size from subtle nubs to obvious spikes. Others have shocking sets of teeth.

entries.name: Dual Natured
entries: The shadow fey are contradictory beings. They boast some of the best features of elves, tempered by aspects of a fouler nature. They can be deliberate and purposeful, but they're also given to perplexing whimsy. Mortal creatures trying to fathom shadow fey motivations are in for a maddening experience; they are often illogical, capricious, and seemingly thrive on annoying others.

entries.name: Split Rulership
entries: The Summer Court and Winter Court each rule the shadow fey in the appropriate season. The turning of these seasons follows no clear calendar or schedule, though it is skewed toward summer. The Queen of Night and Magic and the Moonlit King each claim dominion in turn, ruling over the Summer and Winter courts respectively.

{@i A grey-skinned elfin man steps from behind a black tree. He has a dagger held in his teeth and is casually juggling two more daggers. The figure's rough-looking traveling gear and leathers have clearly seen better days}.
Shadow fey who live outside the courts find their skills are suited to waylaying travelers on the shadow roads.

entries.name: Criminal Outcasts
entries: Shadow fey who dwell at court obsessively pursue both leisure and politics, so they find the idea of professional crime boorish at best. Shadow fey finding themselves relying on banditry are often forced to make difficult decisions due to banishment or desperation.

entries.name: Strength In Numbers
entries: The Shadow Realm is a dangerous place to wander alone, so shadow fey bandits often keep company with a wide array of creatures. It is not uncommon to find shadow fey bandits working with darakhul, monstrous fey, or in the service of hags.

entries.name: Shadow Fey Bandit Tactics and Nicknames
entries: While shadow fey bandits are ruthless, they are often quite polite and dashing—the better to get their victims to comply with a robbery. They pretend to have confederates in the trees or claim their weapons are dosed with poison. Sometimes this is true, but more often, it is meant to provide a way for a victim to save face later.

Shadow fey bandit nicknames tend toward the lurid and lordly: "The Duke of Daggers," "The Laughing Princess," and "Quickpenny Jack" are fairly well-known figures. Occasionally, a new bandit will take up the name of an older bandit who has retired.

{@i The pale-skinned elf wears a gleaming breastplate and tight-fitting clothing. He moves like the wind, evading blows with effortless skill. When he stops and smiles, his blade is slick with crimson}.

Shadow fey duelists are elite warriors, often of noble lineage. Swift and sure beyond compare, duelists are often taller and more wiry than others of their kind. Their armor, clothing, and weapons are of exquisite make, fashioned from only the finest materials, as befits their station.

entries.name: Deadly Nobles
entries: A nobleman or woman of the shadow fey is not to be taken lightly—many courtiers or politicians are deadly with their slim blades, and they are known to distill virulent poisons. Often a skilled duelist serves as a champion for her liege, standing in the noble's stead in challenges or serving as an elite bodyguard.
{@i This ravishing shadow fey woman moves with alluring grace. Her voice rings like a bell, and in her hearing, worldly cares and sorrows melt away.}
Beyond even great physical beauty, the sheer presence of a shadow fey enchantress can lay the most stalwart foes low. Almost universally female, Enchantresses are beautiful beyond compare.

entries.name: Enchanting Shadows
entries: Enchantresses are also powerful spellcasters who infuse their words and manner with the beguiling power of shadow to turn enemies against one another with a few words and a deadly smile. They augment the force of their minds with fey-wrought blades, infusing their weapons with power that shreds their victims' psyche as well as their flesh.
{@i The shadows flicker slightly, the only warning before a hail of arrows erupts from the concealed elf hidden in the gloom.}
Dressed in exquisitely wrought mail and leather jerkins, forest hunters are even more lithe and graceful than most shadow fey.

entries.name: Shadow Stalkers
entries: Forest hunters roam the deep woods connected to the Plane of Shadow, as well as the forests' dark reflections within the Plane of Shadow. They are skilled trackers and stalkers, hunting animals and more dangerous game. Many forest hunters serve in the Wild Hunt. A hunter that has at one time ridden at the Lord of the Hunt 's side is afforded great respect, even fear, because of the common belief that such a hunter can implore the Lord of the Hunt to notice an enemy.

{@i A hulking brute, this elvish figure towers over his fellows and wields massive weapons. Patches of his body are swallowed by inky blackness that writhes and crawls, and his eyes are hollow black pits.}

Shadow fey guardians are massive creatures trained and bred for battle. They appear as massive versions of shadow fey, but the stuff of shadow corrupts them even more than their brethren, expanding their size and power to an ogreish strength. Patches of shadow swallow parts of their body and crawl about, revealing and obscuring more by inches at a time. They stand nearly 10 feet tall and weigh over 700 pounds.

entries.name: Loyal Protectors
entries: Guardians are fanatically loyal to their superiors. Employed as house guards or even personal bodyguards for important shadow fey, guardians are unshakable in their duty. The shadow reaches into their minds and souls, so that not even powerful magic can bend their hearts or break their resolve. Guardians are independent thinkers, but they discharge their duty with single-minded dedication.
{@i A large, purple-skinned goblin lumbers toward you. He is easily twice the width, height, and weight of any typical goblin, and he clutches a heavy, bejeweled axe in his ham‑sized fists.}
Shadow goblin chieftains rule goblin groups with a hearty mix of intimidation and natural charisma.

entries.name: Court Players
entries: Shadow goblins thrive in the courts of the shadow fey and in their own courts and have built a complicated social network that mirrors fey politics. Shadow goblin chieftains are drawn from the ranks of the largest, eldest, and most cunning goblins.

entries.name: Shadow Hierarchy
entries: In shadow goblin clans or families, shadow goblin chieftains are second in power only to the moonshadow catchers, who wield strange and potent magic. Frequently a chieftain and a moonshadow catcher will work together to claim leadership of wealth or resources. This common arrangement is called a moon-chief clan. Others are either chieftain clans or moon-led clans.

entries.name: Goblin Clan Politics
entries: Shadow goblin clans are very tight-knit and loyal to their members. Even an evil shadow goblin chieftain will hesitate to betray or slight their direct kinfolk and families. Instead, their rage, trickery, and betrayals are directed at everyone not a member of the clan. The only exception is when a shadow goblin has sworn to accomplish some task (or just as often, not to undertake some foolish venture) and then breaks their word. "Broken words, broken fingers" refers to the chieftain's custom of smashing the hands or toes of those who cross the clan's interests.

{@i The boney, purple-skinned goblin with bright-yellow eyes pushes a pair of gold spectacles farther up on her long nose. She wears a flowy grey shirt stained with black blotches of ink. And she looks annoyed by the sudden interruption}.
Shadow goblin scribes are the notaries and executors of deals brokered between shadow fey and mortals.

entries.name: Contracts, Oaths & Consequences
entries: Shadow fey nobility possess notoriously short attention spans and have come to rely on shadow goblin scribes to record and enforce the day-to-day drudgeries associated with complex contracts. After a fey accepts a bargain, they call upon the scribe to work out the exact terms, catalog them, and occasionally deal with those desperate enough to attempt to break a contract.

entries.name: Limited Spellcasting
entries: Shadow fey are careful not to teach their goblin servitors too much magic, but scribes learn a small selection of practical spells that allow them to deal with testy mortals. Scribes are often the messengers of bad news, and their magic allows them to subdue aggressive individuals long enough to accomplish their business.

entries.name: Goblin Clan Politics
entries: Shadow goblin clans are very tight-knit and loyal to their members. Even an evil shadow goblin chieftain will hesitate to betray or slight their direct kinfolk and families. Instead, their rage, trickery, and betrayals are directed at everyone not a member of the clan. The only exception is when a shadow goblin has sworn to accomplish some task (or just as often, not to undertake some foolish venture) and then breaks their word. "Broken words, broken fingers" refers to the chieftain's custom of smashing the hands or toes of those who cross the clan's interests.

This nightmare is conjured from Arrevis' fear of the common folk's reprisal for his ill deeds. It appears as a large, shadowy, mapach-headed creature with disproportionately large forearms and a bristling hide made of fur as sharp as needles.
It moves hunched over, walking on its enormous forearms. Its face is a mask of rage, and it indiscriminately attacks anything not from the dreamscape.
{@i This mass of fist-sized black spiders flows like a creeping mist. While they move like a shadow across the ground, they do not cast one themselves.}

entries.name: Born of Darkness
entries: Shadowspiders are not alive in the traditional sense. A shadowspider swarm is a creeping mass of spiders formed out of the primordial darkness of the Shadow Realm itself. They are born in the oldest and darkest regions of the Shadow Realm, often in areas where the planar barriers have grown thin. Unable to survive outside of its swarm, a shadowspider separated from its swarm evaporates in a greasy swirl of black smoke.

entries.name: Affinity with Undeath
entries: While shadowspider swarms form in places where two planes are close, they are particularly common in regions where the Shadow Realm is coterminous with the Plane of Undeath. Because of this, shadowspider swarms are often found alongside the undead that sometimes spill forth in these regions.

entries.name: Insatiable Hunger for Warmth
entries: Shadowspider swarms are always hungry, especially for the warmth of mortals. When a shadowspider swarm senses the warmth of a living creature, it immediately moves to consume the creature.
Shards of dark metal pierce the skin of the foul creature. The metal pushes out from within the abomination rather than the other way.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Taking 1 hour to extract the shards of Shadowsteel from a Shadowsteel ghoul, someone can collect an amount worth 250 gp. A Shadowsteel ghast yields a quantity worth 500 gp.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
items.entry: Those who use Shadowsteel to power curses can become Shadowsteel ghouls upon death. These undead creatures seek out more of the metal. As the creature ages, it can regain a semblance of the arcane power it had in life, empowering similar creatures and cursing nearby foes.

entries: Shards of dark metal pierce the skin of the foul creature. The metal pushes out from within the abomination rather than the other way.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Taking 1 hour to extract the shards of Shadowsteel from a Shadowsteel ghoul, someone can collect an amount worth 250 gp. A Shadowsteel ghast yields a quantity worth 500 gp.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
items.entry: Those who use Shadowsteel to power curses can become Shadowsteel ghouls upon death. These undead creatures seek out more of the metal. As the creature ages, it can regain a semblance of the arcane power it had in life, empowering similar creatures and cursing nearby foes.

name: Shardmaul Manticore

entries: Swooping above on thick leathery wings is a large lion-like predator with a disturbingly human head contorted into an expression of fury. Its body bristles in a thicket of crystalline quills that painfully jut out through its mane, along its wing-tips, and down its spine. It has a long, chitinous tail ending in a cluster of wicked stingers. Each begins as a spike of blackened bone but ends as a glittering delerium shard.

Manticores were among the most commonly encountered monsters roaming Drakkenheim's hinterlands prior to the meteor strike. A few of the creatures would fly south from their nesting grounds in the Giantfrost Mountains to feast on the plentiful livestock and allegedly hapless travelers. Most folk would be able to tell a second-hand story about a neighbor or acquaintance who lost a prized animal to a manticore, or in more grim tales, a family member. Fortunately, their population was kept largely in check by the City Guard. As such, the only individuals regularly slain by manticores were usually would-be monster hunters looking to make a local name for themselves.

Once Drakkenheim fell and contamination caused people to abandon the towns, villages, and farmsteads near the city, the manticores found less easy prey. Growing bolder and more desperate, a handful of the monsters ventured into the city ruins in search of food and new lairs. The manticores were able to readily prey on the contaminated people and monsters inhabiting the city, but in turn, the corrupt flesh caused the manticores to mutate into fearsome Shardmaul Manticores.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain Advantage on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks to {@action Study|XPHB} za Shardmaul Manticore, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (10+) Mutated Manticore
entries: You're aware the creature has no special {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances} or {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities} but is a capable flier.

entries.name: (15+) Death From Above
entries: You recognize the manticore's Stinger and Wing Shards attacks.

entries.name: (25+) Strong, Fast, and Tough
entries: You learn the manticore's strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Shardmaul Manticore attacks from above, choosing whichever target looks weakest and the least armored. It descends from above suddenly, making Bite and Claw attacks against the weakest prey it detects. After its first descent, it lifts off again, using Wing Shards to cover its ascent. It then repeats its attack pattern.
A Shardmaul Manticore is bold enough to attack when outnumbered but typically flees if it faces stiff opposition that reduces it to half its Hit Points or fewer.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Monstrosity.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Monster Blood, Contaminated Ichor.

entries.name: Organs
entries: Eyes, Heart, Brain, Guts, Flesh.

entries.name: Bones:
entries: Skull, Spine, Ribs.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Teeth, Claws, Needles.

entries.name: Hair:
entries: Fur.

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Skin, Webbed Membrane.

entries.name: Delerium:
entries: The quills on its body are made of delerium and may be harvestable: {@dice 1d6 - 2} {@item fragment|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium fragments} can be collected from its quills (minimum 0).
{@i A skeletal humanoid made entirely of shark's jaws steps out from the water, dripping strands of seaweed.}

Made from numerous, interlocking shark's jaws, these horrors are animated through foul magic into a large, vaguely humanoid shape. Sahuagin priests animate them to guard sepulchers of bones. These sharkjaw skeletons lie among great piles of bones, waiting to rise up and attack any uninvited souls who invade the sanctity of sahuagin holy sites. Others guard pirate treasures or ancient shipwrecks.

entries.name: Undead Automaton
entries: Sharkjaw skeletons do nothing without orders from their creator, and they follow those instructions explicitly. A sharkjaw skeleton's creator can give it new commands while near the skeleton. Otherwise, a sharkjaw skeleton follows its last instructions to the best of its ability and to the exclusion of all else, though it fights back if attacked.
The sound of breaking glass startles most, but think twice before going to see what caused it if it is followed by the sound of moaning.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The glass from ten shatter corpses can be used to create a suit of {@item glass-studded armor|GrimHollowLairsEtharis} (see Appendix A of {@adventure Lairs of Etharis|GrimHollowLairsEtharis|21}) with a successful {@dc 10} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check by someone proficient with jeweler's tools. Crafting this item takes 10 days and costs 1000 gp.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
items.entry: Shatter corpses are a stronger kind of zombie that arises when someone dies from being impaled on broken glass.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
items.entry: Those that attempt to use a melee attack against a shatter corpse are likely to cut themselves unless they attack with carefully.

items.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
items.entry: Shatter corpses can launch volleys of broken glass.

name: Sheep Dragon
entries: These playful creatures are known to live among the rolling hills alongside livestock and other grazing beasts. Although their name and serpent-like body might confuse some, the sheep dragon is not a dragon, but rather more akin to a dog. These odd creatures aren't known to be violent but do have a variety of tools to protect themselves when they feel they're in danger.

entries.name: Iconic Symbol
entries: The sheep dragon is often regarded as the epitome of goodness and authenticity on the island. Their seen as a symbol of freedom and unwavering kinship, which is why their likeness can be found all throughout villages and towns as a way to let travellers know they're welcome.
{@i Despite being short and squat, this creature's relationship with a troll is undeniable. The kinship is most notable in the long arms and thick, pebbly hide.}

entries.name: Long Handed and Toad-like
entries: The shellycoat is a warped and spiteful creature also called the Iamh fada, or "long hands." They are frequently referred to as bridge trolls. Despite being fey, they are distantly related to true trolls. Unlike those tall, lanky creatures, a shellycoat is dwarfish and toad-like, with short, bent, legs and especially long arms with swollen, distended joints. It can further dislocate and stretch these joints to alarming lengths.

entries.name: Bridges and Pools
entries: The shellycoat can be found in abandoned wells or behind waterfalls, in deep tide pools, or beneath the ice of frozen ponds, but their preferred haunt has always been under bridges. They are most active during nighttime and on heavily overcast days, because of their mortal dread of sunlight. A shellycoat's favored tactic is to lie in wait under the water, ice, or bridge and surprise its prey. It strikes outward or upward from its hiding place to snatch passersby, livestock, and lone travelers or fishermen. Prey is dragged down to the shadows and water to be robbed and devoured.

entries.name: Shining Garments
entries: Shellycoats always fashioned themselves coats, cloaks, or shirts of colored pebbles, glass, and polished river shells. These adornments are crude but beautiful and sometimes magical.
A shieldhead has a broad bone faceplate to protect itself and to ram foes. An expert rider can also use the bone like a shield. People have domesticated shieldheads for riding.

name: Shifting Slime
entries: Deep in the murky marshes of the Mokk Fields, where water lays stagnant and the stench of decay permeates all, the worlds of life and death intertwine. Within this ominous mire lurk some of the most unusual natural predators in Humblewood. Collectively known as "slimes", these oozes move slowly through the muck, well-camouflaged by the dark and pungent waters, waiting to devour any hapless being that wanders within reach.

Slimes are easily provoked, and while it isn't difficult to outrun one, some who have strayed into a slime's territory only find out too late that they have been detected. Fortunately for many swampland travelers, slimes have a slow metabolism, and can go without feeding for long periods.

In addition to being an important part of the ecosystem, many slimes are either naturally magical, or yield organic materials which are in high demand among mages, scholars, and researchers. While slime hunting is a dangerous undertaking, the perch of Winnowing Reach was built on the labor of so-called "slime-wranglers", whose skill collecting valuable residue from live slimes is directly responsible for transforming the once minor outpost into a thriving site for scholarly innovation.

Three main types of slimes have been classified, but as magical creatures with strange properties, it's speculated that more elusive slime species might exist somewhere in the remote swamps. The three documented types are: {@creature caustic slime|HumblewoodCampaignSetting|caustic slimes}, {@creature shifting slime|HumblewoodCampaignSetting|shifting slimes}, and {@creature sticky slime|HumblewoodCampaignSetting|sticky slimes}.

entries.name: Shifting Slime
entries: A type of large and fluid ooze, shifting slimes have an iridescent hue to them which seems to shift as they move. According to slime-wranglers, they can use magical energy to create an eerie bioluminescence. Shifting slime residue is a highly sought after potent reagent, but it is hard to come by. Despite their size, these slimes are elusive and generally spend their time below ground where visibility is low. They can be quite difficult to locate when they conceal themselves in the subterranean darkness, though these strange creatures are known to leave trails of bioluminescent residue to lure in prey.

entries.name: Adaptive Defenses
entries: This type of slime can harness magical energy within its form. Shifting slimes absorb and store magic passively over time, but are also capable of absorbing magical jolts from spells. It is unclear exactly how much energy they can store, or for how long.

Shifting slimes can develop a temporary immunity to various types of magic after exposure. This immunity in turn makes it exceptionally difficult to destroy the slimes with a single type of magical energy. Luckily for slime-wranglers, shifting slimes are only capable of containing one energy type at a time.

entries.name: Manifestation of Stored Power
entries: After absorbing magical energy, these slimes will change color based on the type of power absorbed. Because of the rarity of shifting slimes, only a handful of people have witnessed these changes. But, over generations, skilled slime-wranglers have managed to record which color a shifting slime will turn in response to different types of magic.

name: Shoggoth

entries: It was a terrible, indescribable thing vaster than any subway train—a shapeless congeries of protoplasmic bubbles, faintly self-luminous, and with myriads of temporary eyes forming and un-forming... Still came that eldritch, mocking cry—"Tekeli-li! Tekeli-li!"
entries.from: H.P. Lovecraft, At the Mountains of Madness

entries: Shoggoths are vast sacks of protoplasm capable of forming limbs, eyes, and mouths at will. They are amphibious and exhibit strength that defies reality.

entries.name: Dangerous Allies
entries: Shoggoths grow more intelligent with age. Young ones are obedient brutes, but older ones may overthrow their masters and take over cults.

entries.name: Immortal Terrors
entries: Effectively immortal, some shoggoths labor in ruins long after their summoners perish, or sleep in sealed vaults awaiting release.
{@i The giant, gelatinous blob of flesh releases whistles, trills, and chirps as it rolls forward, forming and reabsorbing mouths, eyes, and ears across its body.}

A shoggoth is an intelligent, gelatinous blob capable of manipulating and reshaping its body. Created by an elder race as servants, the shoggoths rebelled long ago and slew their masters without pity. Since that time, they've lived in isolated or desolate regions, devouring whatever they encounter and absorbing its flesh into their own amorphous, shifting forms.

entries.name: Constant Growth
entries: Shoggoths continue growing throughout their lives, though the eldest among them grow very slowly indeed. Some shoggoths may shrink from starvation if they deplete a territory of resources.

entries.name: Mutable Form
entries: A shoggoth can form any number of eyes, mouths, tentacles, or other appendages as needed, though it lacks the control to take and maintain the shape of another creature.
{@i The translucent person calls out a name in a barely audible whisper.}

entries.name: Bitter Spirits
entries: Shrouds are transitional creatures: remnants of wicked people who died but refuse to rest in peace, yet have not grown strong enough to become shadows. They are aggressive enemies of all living creatures and the light that nurtures life. Shrouds blend naturally into darkness, but they stand out starkly in bright light.

entries.name: Thin Outlines
entries: Shrouds look like flickering shadowy outlines of the people they were before they died, retaining the same height and body type.

entries.name: Repetitive Speech
entries: Shrouds cannot converse, but they occasionally can be heard cruelly whispering a name, term, or phrase over and over again: something that must have had meaning to them in life.

name: Shrouded

entries: {@i Soul Corrupted by the Shroud}

Shrouded are the spirits of the dead—devoid of any ability to reason and corrupted by the deathly mists known as the Shroud. They are raw emotional energy, unfettered and unleashed, manifested into being. The shrouded are constantly whispering about a victim's incompetencies, weakness, foibles, and failings as they engulf their prey to drain the life from them, corrupting their soul.

entries.name: Secret
entries: Shrouded are bound by barriers and lines of iron, which is why cemeteries with iron fences keep them contained.

name: Shub-Niggurath

entries: Iä! Shub-Niggurath! The Black Goat of the Woods with a Thousand Young!
entries.from: H.P. Lovecraft, The Whisperer in Darkness

entries: Shub-Niggurath is a primordial entity of fertility and unrestrained life. Her cults embrace primal existence and renounce civilization, favoring growth and survival above all else.

entries.name: Twisted Promises
entries: Cults often begin in desperation, discovering ancient rituals that yield supernatural bounty in exchange for bloody sacrifices. The land flourishes, but at a horrific cost.

entries.name: Growing Demands
entries: As the cult grows, it demands more frequent and brutal sacrifices. Outsiders are lured in with kindness only to be slaughtered for Shub-Niggurath's hunger.

entries.name: The Land Revolts
entries: The land twists to defend the cult. Paths mislead strangers, beasts turn hostile, and locals must choose between allying with the cult or being destroyed.

entries.name: Corruption Runs Deep
entries: Eventually, her twisted offspring—the Dark Young—walk the earth. If not opposed, the cult spreads like a cancer, devouring kingdoms in vines and blood.

name: Shuck
entries: A red-furred dog that never leaves {@creature Dani Jenkin|CrookedMoon24|Dani's} side, Shuck was a stray before the Jenkins took him in. Unbeknownst to the family, Shuck is the reincarnated soul of Sally Lockwood, a victim of the Crooked House who escaped just before her death. Shuck guards Dani fiercely. If any of the characters are evil, or if they use supernatural abilities that are in any way associated with the Crooked Queen, Shuck growls at them if they get anywhere near Dani.

name: Shyla Denn
entries: A scarred, gray-and-russet-furred vulpin cleric of Kren, Shyla serves as Krall's lieutenant. Krall saved her life when she was a child, orphaned in the Wood, and she has been grateful to him ever since. Her loyalty to Krall is absolute, and she believes that Krall will only cut loose those who can't pull their weight. Shyla uses the {@creature vulpin priest of kren|HumblewoodCampaignSetting} stat block.

name: Sightless Agony
entries: Transforming into a Sightless Agony is the result of being afflicted with a {@spell Curse of Crushing Sensation|GrimHollowPG24}. Victims find themselves fleeing the company of others in search of peaceful solitude, as even the gentle sounds of nature become jarring and obtrusive to these poor souls. Such unfortunates have often left those behind who care for them, or perhaps even those who have the need for some rare skill the individual possesses.

A Sightless Agony seeks a dark, quiet place to hide itself. They often tear out their own eyes and claw away their skin to escape the agony of sensation, and the company of others becomes entirely unbearable. In such a state, they know only a boundless, white-hot rage.

When discovered, a Sightless Agony appears as a mutated gargoyle with skin flayed from its malformed figure. They attack with razor-sharp claws and a mouthful of fangs, and though a Sightless Agony possesses wings, they are loath to fly far, since the feeling of the wind is nearly unbearable. Even standing in one place, the Sightless Agony quivers and twitches as sensations from their immediate environment cause them to flinch at the unseen.

name: Sigkva Runigsdottir
entries: Light blue complexion. Short-cropped golden hair. Formally attired.
{@b Found In:} Area 1 or 10.
{@b Background:} Enjoys good relations with other cloud giant clans; frequently interacts with storm and lightning giant tribes.
{@b Personality Traits:} Attentive, kind, humble.
{@b Bonds:} Her family and the cloud giants in her charge.
{@b Flaws:} She naively assumes the best intentions in everyone with whom she interacts.
{@b Wants:} A successful moot with no hard feelings among the attendees, as well as assent from the assembled giants to help fight the Cult of Ragnarok.
{@b Talking to Sigkva:} She freely relates the following (in order):

items: She trusts Katlaug implicitly. The hallwarden understands the PCs' reasons for attending, and Sigkva tells them the thursir will attend to their needs while at the moot.
She hasn't met Izhova or Beli previously but knows Izhova's reputation as an accomplished diplomat.

She must resolve the dispute between the stone giants and jotuns before she can turn to the PCs' discussion. She figures smoothing things over between Sinmara and Glytta will entice them to pay attention to the party.

name: Signa
entries: Captive Trollheim warrior

items.name: Silver Order Cavalier

entries: Garbed in heavy armor with blue capes lined in silver trim, embroidered with the symbol of the Silver Order, the paladin's helmet has a large blue plume. A quiver of javelins rests upon their back.

The cavaliers are the griffon riders of the Silver Order. They are trained in both ground assault and aerial combat. Having reached the rank of paladin, these warriors have chosen to train further in mounted combat. Each cavalier creates a unique bond with a griffon, whom they can summon to them using their divine magic, and often the two are connected for life.

items.name: Silver Order Paladin

entries: Garbed in heavy armor with blue capes lined in silver trim, embroidered with the symbol of the Silver Order, the paladin holds a large kite shield, and a glowing radiant mace.

The Knights of the Silver Order are world renowned as the defenders of the Faith of the Sacred Flame. Taking on holy quests and religious missions for the Divine Matriarch, these holy knights have been known to ride griffons into battle, or march forth in force armed with plate mail, swords and shields, and divine magic to bolster their combat prowess. To some, these paladins have a reputation of being divine protectors, noble warriors, and divine symbols of the faith. To others, they are a terrifying and ugly example of the power of the Sacred Flame.

items.name: Silver Order Recruit

entries: These simple foot soldiers make up the bulk of the ground troops for the Silver Order. Fitted with decent armor and shields, a longsword, and the emblems of the Silver Order, they are the first lines of defense against otherworldly monsters and magical threats.

Once graduating from the position of squire, a recruit is now a skilled combatant able to take on simple missions of the Silver Order on their own. They often accompany paladins on more important quests, and make up the guards of Silver Order strongholds, and the forward troops in their armies. They no longer tend to the needs of paladins and are now trained to care for their own gear.

items.name: Silver Order Squire

entries: Dressed in leathers, and carrying a short sword, shield, and shortbow, the young squire hefts a small backpack of gear for maintaining and patching armor and weapons, griffon care, ammunition, and other essentials that may be needed on the field. They are eager to serve, and to prove themselves in battle.

Squires are the new recruits of the Silver Order. They are often assigned to a paladin for training and although they can perform in combat and go through rigorous training with both sword and bow, they are more often assigned to patch the armor, sharpen the weapons, and tend to the griffons of their paladins.

name: Sister Rain
entries: Sister Rain travels throughout the hollow espousing the bountiful blessings of the Patient Lady. She has no official residence in the village and instead lives in the natural environments outside of town.

She also sometimes stays with her congregants and preaches in the Founder's Round (area V9). Sister Rain's moods and demeanor are as fickle as the weather and nature that she reveres, often living a nomadic lifestyle travelling between the various communes dedicated to the Patient Lady that dot Wickermoor Hollow.

Sister Rain is a slight woman in her mid-thirties. She wears a green floral print dress that sets off her long, flowing, flaming-red hair. Her green eyes are bright with the fervor of her faith, and her features can flash between joy and anger in a moment. She wears a plain silver necklace with a pendant in the shape of a blossoming sunflower.

Sister Rain is the leader of the Fold of the Patient Lady, and she espouses the need to accept and protect the bounties of nature. Her presence is anathema to the most zealous and evil followers of the Crooked Queen.

Disease is no stranger to the people of Etharis. The virulent Weeping Pox has devastated towns and families, and the Tears of the Hungerer is rumored to be a poison designed by necromancers. Other afflictions, such as the Seven Shades of Sitri and the Faith Cough, are not deadly but can impede even the strongest body. These diseases can be carried by animals, breaking their normal method of transmission. A twist of nature or foul magic has created carriers, some intentionally and some aggressively, that spread sickness quickly.

name: Siv Harga
entries: {@creature Siv Harga|CrookedMoon24} is a tall, solidly built woman with blonde hair that she keeps braided. Growing up, her family moved around Wickermoor Hollow as animal herders. Siv finally settled down in Wickermoor Village as an apprentice to the town's butcher. When he passed, she took over the business and proved to be more than adequate. Siv shares a nearby house with her partner Holly Aster, Holly's two daughters, and her younger brother Ulf (Neutral Good, human {@creature Commoner|XMM}), who assists her at the shop while not in school.

Her knowledge of animals is a boon not just to her profession, but to the local farmers as well. Some think her connection with the animals she butchers is supernatural, and Siv does nothing to dissuade that attitude.

Her bond with the natural world led Siv to join the Fold of the Patient Lady. She believes that nature provides if believers are respectful and thoughtful about how to give back to nature in return. Even as she slaughters animals for her customers, she says a prayer of thanks to the Patient Lady and never allows cruelty to the animals in her care.

name: Skein Witch
entries: {@i Fell Fateweaver}
{@color The shambling figure is draped in writhing, diamond thread. Its skin is translucent, and dozens of quivering hourglasses are suspended inside its body in place of organs.|006abe}

Skein witches are curators of destiny and enforcers of what must be. They voyage across the planes, weaving the strands of fate at the behest of their goddess creator. Although they carry out their charge without regard to petty mortal concerns, they can be persuaded to bend fate for powerful petitioners whose interests align with those of their goddess.

Despite their supernatural abilities, a skein witch's physical body is frail. Because of that, they tend to surround themselves with undead, constructs, or other brutish, soulless guardians cut free from the thread of fate.
Legends say that if a Deck of Many Things is brought close to a skein witch, the witch emits a psychic wail and disintegrates.
{@i The androgynous humanoid appears mummified in writhing, diamond thread. Its skin is translucent, and dozens of quivering hourglasses sit suspended inside its body in place of organs.}

entries.name: Shepherd Destiny
entries: Skein witches are curators of destiny and enforcers of what must be. They voyage across the planes, weaving the strands of fate at the behest of their goddess-creator. Although they carry out their charge without regard to petty mortal concerns, they can be persuaded to bend fate for powerful petitioners whose interests align with those of their goddess.

entries.name: Surrounded by Guardians
entries: Despite their supernatural abilities, a skein witch's physical body is frail. Because of that, they tend to surround themselves with undead, constructs, or other brutish, soulless guardians cut free from the thread of fate.

entries.name: Fear of Cards
entries: If a deck of many things is brought close to a skein witch, the witch emits a psychic wail and disintegrates.

name: Skeletal Fish
entries: Skeletal Fish are a result of the Corruption that has infected the waters off the eastern shore of Obojima. Whether it is some strange property of the Corruption or whether it is Obojima's magic keeping them alive, the fish still swim—Both in water and in the air.

items.name: Skeleton Archer

entries: Soft blue light glows in the eye sockets of this skeleton, who carries a bow made from bone and ancient sinew. Shards of frost form on its arrow tip as it takes aim.

In the armies of the dead, one must have both melee and ranged troops as the backbone to one's forces. Skeletal archers are imbued with elemental magic and given bows that harness the power to chill their enemies with each shot.
A line of skeletons marches into the town square with military precision. They raise rifles and take aim at the temple in unison.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Firearms recovered from skeleton troopers are nonfunctional, but parts of them might be useful. Each firearm recovered can reduce the cost of making a similar firearm by 10 percent, up to 50 percent.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
items.entry: Necromancers with advanced training and hefty resources can make skeletons that are linked in death to their firearms.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
items.entry: A commander leads some platoons of skeleton troopers. This skeleton directs the attacks and enhances the efficiency of its undead underlings.

entries.name: GM Advice
entries: Skeletal troopers are effective when used as minions in the army of a higher-level threat. Cinematic battles focused on sieges or large battles are perfect for troopers. In these cases, having the troopers immune to turning until their powerful leader is defeated prevents anticlimactic encounters.

entries: Firearms recovered from skeleton troopers are nonfunctional, but parts of them might be useful. Each firearm recovered can reduce the cost of making a similar firearm by 10 percent, up to 50 percent.
