In these cases, having the troopers immune to turning until their powerful leader is defeated prevents anticlimactic encounters.

items.name: Skeleton Mage

entries: The tattered red robes worn by this skeleton reveal it as one of the vampires' failed thralls. Thunderous sparks and embers of flame dance around its boney fingertips as it prepares its next spell.

These mages are often former thralls, acolytes, or arcane prisoners to vampire lords. They are twisted in undeath into unholy mages, harnessing elemental magics against their foes and serving an eternal afterlife to the vampires who create them.
A line of skeletons marches into the town square with military precision. They raise rifles and take aim at the temple in unison.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Firearms recovered from skeleton troopers are nonfunctional, but parts of them might be useful. Each firearm recovered can reduce the cost of making a similar firearm by 10 percent, up to 50 percent.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
items.entry: Necromancers with advanced training and hefty resources can make skeletons that are linked in death to their firearms.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Religion}):
items.entry: A commander leads some platoons of skeleton troopers. This skeleton directs the attacks and enhances the efficiency of its undead underlings.

entries.name: GM Advice
entries: Skeletal troopers are effective when used as minions in the army of a higher-level threat. Cinematic battles focused on sieges or large battles are perfect for troopers. In these cases, having the troopers immune to turning until their powerful leader is defeated prevents anticlimactic encounters.

items.name: Skeleton Soldier

entries: This robust skeleton warrior is caked in mud and moss, it wears a skull cap, a single shoulder pauldron, and holds a thick rusted shield emblazoned with the arcane sigil of House von Drakken. In one hand It carries a long poison-tipped spear.

Most corpses on the continent are cremated; vampires must be clever about obtaining minions for their armies. Throughout the lands, there are ancient crypts of heroic warriors and divine soldiers. Sometimes, vampire lords have been known to infiltrate abandoned holy sites and old crypts to steal the dead, raising them as skeletal minions. Furthermore, they often keep prisoners in their own dungeons to feed on, leaving the bodies once they are expended to one day rise again as skeleton soldiers.

entries.name: Skeletons

entries: Ancient bones draped in rusted armor scraps rise up with unholy magic. Baring old weapons, they brandish their spears and charge toward you.

When a vampire is preparing for war, they have no shortage of soldiers. Their crypts are often filled with long-deceased thralls, remains of prisoners, vampire slayers, and anyone who mistakenly wandered into their manor or castle and was never seen again. The vampires use their dark magic to raise these skeletal remains from the crypt and into their legions. Clad in ancient armor and often given bows or spears, these skeletal warriors make excellent minions for a vampire. They do not need to be fed and are easily stored in tombs and crypts when not needed. Some of these skeletons possessed arcane abilities in life and carry that trait through to undeath, leading skeletal armies as mages. They harness what remains of their arcane fortitude to channel elemental fury at their foes.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Religion|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Religion|XPHB}) checks when taking the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine a skeleton, learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (5+) Unnatural Resistances
entries: You recognize the creature's {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: (10+) Deathly Violence
entries: You know the creature's basic attacks and Bonus Actions.

entries.name: (15+) Unliving Abilities
entries: You learn the creature's highest and lowest ability scores.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: These skeleton warriors are mindless foot soldiers in the wars of vampires. They march into battle with no care. They feel no pain. They only follow their orders and fight to the death on behalf of their vampiric masters.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Undead.

entries.name: Bones:
entries: Skull, Spine, Ribs.

entries.name: Dust:
entries: Undead Dust.

Odd mysteries surround these skeletal nightmares given renewed, violent purpose as a mockery of mortality. Rumors speak of a dark intelligence rooted within, seeking power and using their own bones, or even the wriggling worms that thrive within their corpses, as currency to trade with shadowy merchants.
entries.from: Apothecary

entries.name: Skeletons
entries: Skeletons are often the first creatures to be reanimated by aspiring necromancers, imbued with a vulgar imitation of life and reassembled into an approximation of their living forms. No trace remains of the life that once animated a skeleton, whose only purpose is loyalty.

Skeletons follow the orders of their creators until those orders are completed. Their obedient, tireless nature makes them perfect as disposable battle fodder, guards, or distractions—and, in great enough numbers, turns them into an overwhelming tide of bone, tooth, and blade.

entries.name: Undead Nature
entries: A skeleton doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Neutral evil.

name: Skeljaskra
entries: {@i Scaled Rolling Doom}
{@color A hippo-sized beast with blue-white, pangolin-like armor, spits burning poison at a nearby villager.|006abe}

The voracious skeljaskra is known for indiscriminately devouring creatures, vegetation, and structures over the course of several days of constant movement and destruction. A single skeljaskra can consume hundreds of pounds of food in a single day, whether that takes the form of an elk, a field of crops, or an entire small house. Once it has sated its legendary appetite, the skeljaskra finds a cave to slumber in for weeks while it digests its massive meal.

Fortunately, the skeljaskra is typically encountered alone. However, in ill-fated years, an entire pack can emerge from the wilderness, descending on a village and devouring everything in its path. Such an event sends all living creatures fleeing from the utter destruction and leaves almost nothing behind.
Although skeljaskra can consume virtually anything, they don't digest minerals. Their droppings often contain metal or stone remnants of past meals, from iron nails to coins to small gemstones.
Once every few generations, a skeljaskra hibernates in a place suffused by magic. Over many years, it grows into a threat to entire settlements. Such horrors are known as dread skeljaskra.

{@i A repulsive, batlike creature darts from the darkness. Its body consists entirely of rotting sheets of stolen skin. Though its large eyes are glassy and lifeless, an unmistakably evil intent glimmers within them as a toothless mouth spreads wide in hunger}.

Skin bats are undead creatures created from skin flayed from the victims of sacrificial rites. They are given a measure of unlife by a vile ritual involving immersion in Abyssal flesh vats and invocations to Camazotz and similar demon lords. They feed on the skin of living beings to replenish their own constantly rotting skin. Their acidic saliva acts as a paralytic poison and leaves ugly scars on those who survive an attack. The typical skin bat has an 8-foot wingspan. The color of their skin matches that of their prey, so a skin bat's coloration can change over time. A skin bat weighs about 15 pounds.

entries.name: Cliff and Dungeon Dwellers
entries: Skin bats prey on the unwary but do not develop sinister plots of their own. Their flocks can be encountered in isolated areas accessible only by flight or by climbing treacherous cliffs. Skin bats can exist in any climate. In cool climes, they feed only infrequently, because the cold preserves their forms and reduces the need to replenish decaying flesh. This also explains why they are attracted to the dark depths of ageless dungeons. In wet, tropical climes where their skin decomposes rapidly, skin bats are voracious feeders by necessity.

entries.name: Accidental Treasures
entries: Skin bats have no use for magic items or wealth, but occasionally a ring or necklace from a past victim gets embedded in their fleshy folds, where it becomes an unintended trophy.

name: Skin Crawler

entries: Out of the shadows you hear a sloping and squishing sound like someone dragging raw meat across the ground. The first thing you see are two arms reaching out from the darkness, the flesh sagging and drooping. The hands grasp the ground and slowly pull the creature forward revealing a squished pile of flesh resembling a human body without bones, organs, or muscle: simply a bag of skin that drags itself across the ground. Its empty eye holes and open mouth hang agape from its flopped over head, its legs dragging behind it as it pulls closer to you. It lets out a low guttural moan as it grasps towards you, hungry to fill itself with your insides.
One of the more horrible forms of undeath reported from the ruins of Drakkenheim are Skin Crawlers.

When a person becomes contaminated in a very short time, mutations occur in such quick succession that their body simply cannot withstand the changes. This abrupt mutation causes the person's organs to liquify and they die vomiting a black bile. Even their bones, eyes, brain, and other internal organs dissolve into a thick black contaminated sludge. They retch until they collapse to the ground as nothing but a sack of dead flesh sitting in a puddle of delerium sludge.

The sack of dead flesh does not stay dead. Horribly contaminated, it awakens in a desperate and starved state. It seeks out living creatures for their meat, hoping to fill itself back up with new flesh and take on a more complete form. The Skin Crawlers have been known to consume an entire creature like a python eating its prey, only once the crawler is filled, it assumes the form of the creature it consumed. There are unpleasant and grotesque signs of the Skin Crawler's guise. A creature consumed and transformed by a Skin Crawler will appear to wear their skin like a loose suit. Their eye sockets will droop, their mouth will be too open, their arms and legs will have loose and sagging skin. They appear almost as the person who was consumed, but with their skin hanging off in odd and disproportionate ways.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Medicine|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Religion|XPHB}) checks to {@action Study|XPHB} a Skin Crawler, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (5+) Unrestrained Undead
entries: You recognize the Skin Crawler's creature type, {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}, and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: (10+) Squeezing Death
entries: You are aware of its Crush and Consume {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: (15+) Deathly Aware
entries: You learn of the Skin Crawler's mental ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Skin Crawler is a mindless creature. It is nothing but animated flesh seeking to consume. If it senses a living creature nearby, it crawls towards it with total disregard for its own life.
It only wants to bind the living and squeeze them to death while slowly devouring their flesh, consuming it into itself.
A Skin Crawler is too focused to flee and continues to attempt to devour a target until either it or their target is dead.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Undead.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Contaminated Ichor.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Claws.

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Skin.

entries.name: Dust:
entries: Undead Dust.
I don't brook with tanners no longer. If ya' know what's good for you, ya' won't ask me why.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Skinweavers collect valuable artwork and other items that display their erudition and refinement. They're never without their custom-made suits of bespoke leather armor. This leather is so finely crafted that a suit of armor stitched from a skinweaver's own suit is better than almost any other tanner's creations.

If a proficient armorer or leather worker uses a skinweaver's suit to create a humanoid suit of light armor and succeeds on a successful {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Nature}) check, the armor acts as {@item +1 leather armor} and can be donned or doffed as a standard action. This process takes 24 hours and requires 250 gp of other components.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
items.entry: A skinweaver is resistant to fire damage because of its leathery skin and armor.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History}):
items.entry: A skinweaver's terrifying appearance can scare an opponent multiple times in the same fight.

name: Skinwing

entries: A flock of hairless, winged creatures, each roughly the size of a large dog, circle overhead. Each is a grotesque patchwork of various animals melded together through unspeakable magical experiments. Their bloated bodies are made from combinations of pigs, goats, and sheep torsos. Their featherless wings are poorly structured with visible bones and thin, tearing skin. Each has a ram-shaped head with mismatched, bulging eyes and twisted horns; the nose and mouth have been replaced with a curved avian beak, each disturbingly filled with rows of irregular teeth and leaking a foul, sticky saliva. The monsters move with an awkward gait, their strained bodies supported by sturdy but mismatched donkey legs, and forelimbs which end in a hodgepodge digits with different claws, talons, and claws.

Many apothecaries who delve into the secrets of reanimation and transmogrification are not bold enough to begin with human test subjects. Instead, most opt to begin their cruel experiments upon animals, knowing that these early investigations draw less suspicion and hostility.

Unfortunately, it is for exactly this reason that many apothecaries lose their sense of morality. In time, they come to view even humans with the same cold dispassion as their animal test subjects, seeing the cries of pain and mercy as no different from the barks, squawks, and howls of the animals they so cruelly tortured in their early days.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks to {@action Study|XPHB} a Skinwing, learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (15+) Flying Packs
entries: You know the Skinwing's Pack Tactics trait.

entries.name: (20+) Muddled Mind
entries: You learn the Skinwing's Dexterity, Intelligence, and Charisma ability scores

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Skinwings look for opportunities to gang up on a single target, relying on their Pack Tactics to swarm and overpower an enemy.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Monstrosity.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Monster Blood, Contaminated Ichor.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Eyes, Heart, Brain, Guts.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Claws, Teeth.

entries.name: Hair:
entries: Fur, Stitches.

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Skin, Webbed Membrane.
{@i This large beetle moves erratically, leaking noxious fluid from its cracked exoskeleton.}

entries.name: Ooze Vermin
entries: This parasitic ooze lives in the shells of monstrous vermin, such as beetles, scorpions, and spiders, which it has infested and killed. A skitterhaunt creature might be mistaken for its original, living version at a glance, but the sluggish, erratic movements and oozing carapace of skitterhaunts quickly reveal their true nature.

entries.name: Wide Range of Prey
entries: A skitterhaunt infection can decimate whole nests of vermin. When those are in short supply, these oozes move on to prey on other species, such as ants, crabs, and other creatures with exoskeletons or similar hard outer shells.

entries.name: Hosts Required
entries: Skitterhaunts can't survive long outside their host creatures; they quickly liquefy and lose their cohesion. A body abandoned by a skitterhaunt is an eerie, hollowed-out husk with a strong, acidic odor.

name: Skitterswarm

entries: {@i Fetid Fey Centipedes}

Disgusting Fey who delight in warping flesh and spreading sickness can gather into squirming masses of centipedes known as skitterswarms. These swarms lurk in places where foulness accumulates and often serve centipede hags.

entries.name: Secret
entries: Skitterswarms can't resist dead bodies and are drawn to the corpses of Humanoids.

name: Skogsra
entries: {@i Bloodthirsty Spirit of the Woods}
{@color A bewildered traveler wanders through the forest ahead of you, clearly lost.|006abe}

The skogsra is a malign forest creature that feeds on mortal blood. It often presents itself as a beautiful person of friendly temperament, seeking the help of a traveler or hunter. It entices its victims into the forest, where it tears them to shreds as it reveals its true form: a hollow, bark-skinned monster with long, twisted limbs tipped with venomous claws. The skogsra can extend fleshy vines out of its hollow form to grasp and tangle its prey. It uses these natural weapons to overcome and paralyze its target, pulling the helpless victim into its hollow body, where it can consume the poor soul later at its leisure.
When outnumbered or facing a potent enemy, the skogsra channels the power of the storm, calling forth mighty winds, hail, and lightning.

Skopps is a grizzled but imposing strig with an uncanny power over creatures. He has used this power to capture and exploit wild beasts and monsters for profit. He and his band of poachers live outside the law, selling their services to others who operate in the shadows.

name: Skretch

entries: A looming avian creature perches on the rooftop above, its body cloaked in dirty, ragged feathers. It curiously regards you with its two featherless heads, each borne on a long, crooked neck. Each head has large, round, bulging eyes and a hooked beak that drips corrosive saliva which hisses as it strikes the ground. The bird launches from its perch, opening its broad wings and short, fanshaped tail, revealing a hanging, bloated belly that shudders with whatever half-digested contents rot within.
Skretches are mutated scavengers with features reminiscent of various birds, including vultures, pigeons, and crows.

These cowardly opportunists feed on corpses and {@condition weakened|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} prey while steering clear of more adept aerial predators inhabiting the ruins. Attracted to the sound of conflict, Skretches patiently circle at great heights until the fight ends, then attack any wounded, dying, or survivors caught off guard.

A Skretch's digestive system is a disgusting mess. It is filled with the partially dissolved remains of its last meal, churning into a contaminated slop inside its bloated belly. Skretches shower their meals—whether corpses or still-living targets—with acidic vomit and expelled waste. This noxious mixture dissolves flesh and bones, turning prey into digestible goop that the Skretch then easily consumes.
These beasts maintain a significant distance from the Harpies residing in the highest spires of Drakkenheim since the more proficient hunters are not averse to killing and consuming

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Survival|XPHB} or {@skill Nature|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they {@action Study|XPHB} a Skretch, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (5+) Flying Scavenger
entries: You recognize it may be possible to distract it with meat, offal, or strong-smelling food.

entries.name: (10+) Acidic Vomit
entries: You learn of the Skretch's Expel Waste and Spittle actions.

entries.name: (15+) Dextrous and Sturdy
entries: You recognize the creature's strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Skretches keep to high perches and observe potential prey before attacking. A Skretch prefers to attack targets that are visibly injured, {@condition weakened|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}, or otherwise vulnerable.

Once it finds a suitable quarry, a Skretch circles their prey overhead pelting them with Spittle while waiting for their Expel Waste to recharge. Since its attacks require the Skretch to be directly overhead its target, they prefer to keep well above their targets to avoid any projectiles or ranged attacks.

A Skretch never enters close combat willingly. If it is engaged up close, it uses the {@action Disengage|XPHB} action to flee. As lazy scavengers, a Skretch doesn't pursue its prey very far or into buildings and flees if reduced to half its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or fewer.

name: Skrolmuk
entries: Great ogre in command of giantkin

name: Skull-Splitter
entries: Cultist in Lower Courtyard
Descendants of the great dragons of the mythic past still roam Etharis. They have little of the majesty of their ancestors, but they're still frightening.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Dragons are rare on Etharis, so materials from their corpses fetch a good price. A dragon's corpse can be sold for at least 100 gp times the Challenge of the monster.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
items.entry: Sea drakes are cunning grapplers resistant to cold, sky drakes are adept fliers and have a bite charged with lightning, and blight drakes collect diseases that don't kill them but make for a toxic bite.

name: Sky King
entries: The Sky King is the first and the oldest of the "Three Great Beasts" of Obojima—and perhaps the oldest being on the island. Its age is so great that its body, which was once a majestic glistening shark with a blue hue that was said to make the skies look dull, is now rendered to cartilage and bone. Still, the great beast continues to soar through the clouds and dive below the waves—the island's magic keeping the king's body intact.

entries.name: Historic Past
entries: It's said that the Sky King was once the great protector of Obojima—in an age when the Hunter was just a hatchling and the island was at war. The Sky King was a vigilant guardian who helped the Nakudama people and saw the end of a demonic rule over the island. Since that time, the Sky King has become more recluse. Its once watchful gaze over the island has subsided, aiding in the rise of the Hunter's role as the protector and adding to the mystery and intrigue that now permeates around the Sky King.

entries.name: Truth or Legend?
entries: Many believe that the Sky King is being kept alive by the Obojima for some reason. These rumors and stories have spread all across the island for hundreds of years and have been the catalyst for many famed adventurers and explorers to uncover the truth behind the Sky King and its mysterious past.

name: Skymir Godkiller
entries: Leader of the Blood Reckoning

name: Skywhale
entries: Peaceful denizens, skywhales typically travel over vast oceans, feasting upon the fish below and other small creatures above. Very few Rocborne hunt skywhales, instead preferring to count sightings as omens of good weather ahead. Unfortunately, these sightings are rare, as rocs consider skywhales a delightful delicacy.

name: Slagger
entries: Slaggers are thought to be ancient elemental beings born from the merging of magma and earth spirits deep in the mines. Many miners believe they are the jealous guardians of Obojima's riches, which is why miners must tread carefully in their domain. While not inherently malevolent, their moody and territorial nature makes them unpredictable. Miners often leave offerings of coal, hoping to avoid the destructive wrath of the slagger. There's more than one story of an entire mine being abandoned due to the stubbornness of one particularly irritable and enormous slagger.

name: Slaghund Pup

entries: No. Loud. Noises. Hundy is a sehr light sleeper und our insurance doesn't cover arson by fire-based fiends that you invite into your laboratory.
Type: Fiend
Creature Component: Hell hound and owlbear
Bonus Tamer Improvement: Growth I and +2 Hit Dice

Instinctive, impulsive, and prone to setting things aflame, this pyromaniac pup's psyche is almost entirely id. A biomantic mix of hell hound and owlbear, this fiery fiend is an offensive powerhouse, even when a tiny pup. Just be careful not to stand too close to it when you sneeze... slaghunds are jumpy creatures.
If any of the slaghund's traits or actions require saving throws, it is always against the slaghund's save DC, as calculated below.

entries.name: Save DC
entries.text: 8 + the tamer's proficiency bonus + the slaghund's Constitution modifier

entries.name: Monster Trainer
entries: In addition to the improvements you can normally give your companions, you can choose to grant the slaghund the following improvements using your Monster Trainer feature:

entries.name: Growth I
Prerequisite:
entries: become a tamer's companion.

entries.name: Type
entries: Passive (companion).

The slaghund's size increases to Small and its Hit Die size increases to a d6 (its hit point maximum consequently increases by 1 for each of its Hit Dice). The damage die of its Bite attack increases to a d8 and its Claws to a d6. The slaghund gains this improvement when it becomes a companion; it doesn't cost an improvement.

entries.name: Keen Senses
Prerequisite:
entries: 3rd-level tamer.

entries.name: Type
entries: Passive (companion).
The slaghund has advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|PHB}) checks.

entries.name: Hound's Speed
Prerequisite:
entries: 3rd-level tamer.

entries.name: Type
entries: Passive (companion).
The slaghund's speed increases by 20 feet.

entries.name: Growth II
Prerequisite:
entries: 5th-level tamer, Growth I.

entries.name: Type
entries: Passive (companion).

The slaghund's size increases to Medium and its Hit Die size increases to a d8 (its hit point maximum consequently increases by 1 for each of its Hit Dice). The damage die of its Bite attack increases to a d10 and its Claws to a d8.

entries.name: Multiattack
Prerequisite:
entries: 5th-level tamer.

entries.name: Type
entries: Active (action).
As an action, the slaghund can make two attacks: one with its Bite and one with its Claws.

entries.name: Trailblazer
Prerequisite:
entries: 5th-level tamer.

entries.name: Type
entries: Active (action).

As an action while the slaghund's Heatable Body trait is active, it can make its fires burn even hotter until the start of its next turn, leaving a trail of devastation behind it. After using this action, each space the slaghund moves into bursts into 5-foot-high flames until the start of its next turn. A creature that starts its turn within 5 feet of these flames, or one that starts its turn in the flames' space or moves into the flames' space for the first time on its turn, must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, a creature takes 2 ({@damage 1d4}) fire damage for each 5-foot-square of flames within 5 feet of it if it started its turn next to the flames, or 17 ({@damage 5d6}) fire damage if it is in the flames' space. On a success, a creature takes half as much damage. After the slaghund uses this action, it can't do so again until its tamer finishes a short or long rest. When the slaghund's tamer reaches 9th level in the tamer class, this damage increases to 3 ({@damage 1d6}) and 24 ({@damage 7d6}), respectively.

entries.name: Pack Tactics
Prerequisite:
entries: 9th-level tamer, Keen Senses.

entries.name: Type
entries: Passive (companion).
The slaghund has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the slaghund's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn't incapacitated.

entries.name: White Hot
Prerequisite:
entries: 9th-level tamer.

entries.name: Type
entries: Passive (companion & tamer).
The fire damage of the slaghund's Heatable Body and Heated Weapons traits increases to {@damage 1d8}. While the slaghund is summoned, its tamer has resistance to fire damage.

entries.name: Growth III
Prerequisite:
entries: 13th-level tamer, Growth II.

entries.name: Type
entries: Passive (companion).

The slaghund's size increases to Large and its Hit Die size increases to a d10 (its hit point maximum consequently increases by 1 for each of its Hit Dice). The damage die of its Bite attack increases to a d12 and its Claws to a d10.

entries.name: Trailblazer II
Prerequisite:
entries: 13th-level tamer, Trailblazer I.

entries.name: Type
entries: Passive (companion).

The damage of the slaghund's Trailblazer action increases to 4 ({@damage 1d8}) and 31 ({@damage 9d6}), respectively. The slaghund gains a +1 bonus to the save DC of this action. When the slaghund's tamer reaches 17th level in the tamer class, the damage of this action increases to 5 ({@damage 1d10}) and 42 ({@damage 12d6}), respectively.

entries.name: Fiery Aura
Prerequisite:
entries: 17th-level tamer, White Hot.

entries.name: Type
entries: Active (action).

As an action while the slaghund's Heatable Body trait is active, it casts the {@spell fire shield} spell on itself, choosing the warm shield option and requiring no material components. After the slaghund uses this action, it can't do so again until its tamer finishes a long rest.

entries.name: The Dreamers
entries: Found exclusively in dreamscapes, dreamers are the psyches of sentient creatures blocked from re-entering their corporeal form. The longer a psyche spends in a dreamholder's twisted realm, the more corrupted it becomes, losing the virtues, values, and empathy it once held dear.

entries.name: Damage
entries: The mind is a magnificent thing, capable of adapting to new realities, and parsing the stimuli in the best way it knows how. This, however, is the dreamers' weakness; while a blade doesn't technically exist in a dreamscape, the mind interprets the damage the blade should cause, creating internal psychic trauma in the host's corporeal body.

entries.name: Sleepwalkers
entries: A dreamer that has recently succumbed to a dreamholder's manipulations is known as a sleepwalker. These individuals are entirely deceived by their aberrant puppetmaster, and can be induced to attack others through manipulative illusions and deceit. With careful persuasion or use of magic, such individuals can be brought back to a lucid state and even induced to break free of the dreamholder's stasis

name: Sleipnirspringr
entries: {@i Eight-Legged Divine Horse}
{@color The eight-legged horse stomps its hooves in frustration, as if the entire world moves too slow for it.|006abe}

Descended from Wotan's horse Sleipnir, this breed of eight-legged horse tends toward dark pelts with elaborate and unusual markings. Larger, more intelligent, and far more willful than any breed of mortal horse, sleipnirspringr rarely allow themselves to be sold and are more likely to bond to kindred spirits that they encounter in the wilds, doing great deeds, or sowing chaos. They are exceedingly rare in the Northlands, and those who are honored with a sleipnirspringr's company are said to be heroes of great renown.
These large monitor lizards are native to the jungles of the Tanglewilds and have an upright stance with long limbs suited for running down prey. Their bite is powerful and venomous.

Slimes are magical oozes with strange properties. Slimes provide an important role in many ecosystems across Humblewood, as their bodies can digest just about anything. The bodies of slimes are also sought after for use in potion making.

entries.name: Slime Familiar
entries: A benign slime altered by magic and made into a familiar. These slimes come in a variety of colors and are intensely curious.

Slimes are magical oozes with strange properties. Slimes provide an important role in many ecosystems across Humblewood, as their bodies can digest just about anything. The bodies of slimes are also sought after for use in potion making.

entries.name: Slime King
entries: Lendarick's current form is a half-slime, half-luma monstrosity. A birdfolk skull adorns each of the Slime King's shoulders, making him look like a three-headed horror. The back of the partially decomposed body is decorated with cervan horns, swords, and other monstrous protrusions. The Slime King carries a greatsword hewn from the bone of some massive creature and infused with the powers of cursed slimes.

name: Slime Servant
entries: If a creature spends 1 continuous minute under the effect of the slime from an olothec's Devolving Tentacle attack, that effect ends and their flesh devolves into a translucent primordial state. The creature loses their memories and sense of self, becoming a slime servant NPC who is loyal to the olothec.

Slimes are magical oozes with strange properties. Slimes provide an important role in many ecosystems across Humblewood, as their bodies can digest just about anything. The bodies of slimes are also sought after for use in potion making.

entries.name: Slimesworn Cultist
entries: The cultists are folk from the roots who passed and were reanimated with slime magic woven into cloth. They can be of any race. In an attempt to make them look less frightening, Lendarick fashioned the magic cloth into robes, leaving only their heads and claws exposed. The robes are painted with dark slime in swirling patterns. The cultists are controlled by the robes, and if the robes are engulfed in fire, the corpse crumples to the floor.

items: [he/him]

A stoic and disciplined maran raptor who lost his right eye serving in the Coast Guard. Before he followed {@creature Petra Cloudburst|HumblewoodTales|Petra} into retirement, he acted as the ship's quartermaster. Slip is now in charge of security at The Crimson Rose. An expert in weaponry and a master of several birdfolk combat techniques, Slip gladly offers his expertise to any customers in need.

name: Slippery Oswald
entries: {@creature Slippery Oswald|CrookedMoon24} ({@creature Vermin Familiar (Centipede)|CrookedMoon24}) is a rough approximation of a centipede the size of a hound, with grotesquely human-like hands at the end of each appendage and an unsettling human grin. The familiar of Stonoga Blackstinger, he shares his mistress's glee in the horrid reshaping of flesh into new forms. He can command the squirming hordes of centipedes that crawl throughout Wickermoor Hollow.

Rather than being a collector of body parts like his weasel counterpart Filthy Jasper, Oswald prefers to create grotesque homes out of his master's victims. He burrows deep into Humanoid carcasses and rearranges the rotting innards to his liking, often lurking within for weeks at a time. Sometimes, he even digs into a healthy person to corrupt and prime their body for flesh shaping while they still live.
A sloth galloper is a hybrid sloth-ape that is an agile climber and fast sprinter. The beast's four apelike hands are sensitive, so it hesitates to move rapidly over rough terrain.
{@i Wisps of humid wind revolve around this spiny ball. Two massive black eyes and a dark mouth are the only features visible through its static-straight quills.}

Despite its perhaps comical appearance, a slow storm is a creature of wind, lightning, and chaos, able to send minute electrical shocks into creatures that cause pain every time the creature moves. It turns the bodies of physically able creatures against them, forcing them to choose between relative inactivity or ever-increasing pain.

entries.name: Small Central Core
entries: The nucleus of a slow storm is a sphere of ice and stone, and it is surrounded by protective, high-speed winds.

entries.name: Static Generator
entries: A slow storm has no internal organs other than its brain, and it lives on the energy and moisture it drains from opponents. Its quills not only deflect debris but also generate static electricity that it uses when attacking.

name: Slumber Phantom
entries: Of all the terrifying spirits and terrors that lurk within the Border Ethereal's gauzy embrace, none is more horrific than the slumber phantom. With its completely unknown origins, most people on the Material and Ethereal Planes know only legends of the phantom, calling it a sandman, boogeyman, or other such monikers. Regardless of name, one aspect of the stories is certain: if it decides to haunt your dreams or hunt you physically, you're best off praying to your deity of choice for a swift end.

entries.name: Undead Nature
entries: A slumber phantom doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.
{@i This large statue of emerald-green crystal has a humanoid body with the head of an ibis. Tiny symbols and runes are etched into it, and portions of it are inlaid with bits of gold.}

entries.name: Occult Initiates
entries: Smaragdine golems are crafted by disciples of occult esoterica to guard their secret meeting halls, sacred texts, and the arcane books of power.

entries.name: Emerald Body
entries: Though they seem to be made entirely of emeralds (and some are used in their construction), a smaragdine golem's body is closer to enchanted glass than to gemstones, a sad truth that has disappointed many plunderers.

entries.name: A Maker's Privilege
entries: Though smaragdine golems are sometimes given to powerful mages, scholars, theurgists, and hierophants as a token of esteem, they are always subject first to the magic and orders of their creators.

Smoke elementals are native to the Para-elemental Plane of Ash, where the Plane of Air and Plane of Fire collide. The ash that makes up a smoke elemental ranges from faint motes to fiery zephyrs. Its component mixture can cause breathing problems when inhaled, and it causes burning in the eyes when it attacks. Ironically, a strong wind can damage a smoke elemental, diluting its ashy substance.

Smoke elementals rarely travel to other planes, unless they are summoned by magic or travel through a portal. They might appear, however, in places where someone from a mortal world opens a portal to the Elemental Plane of Fire to immolate, to power a forge, or to drive arcane machinery. Those fighting large conflagrations all too often find themselves contending with confused and hostile smoke elementals that get pulled into their world.

rows: Swirling patches of white and black smoke.
Wispy spirits of those it's killed.

entries.name: Para-elementals
entries: Between the Elemental Planes of Air, Earth, Fire, and Water, which exemplify the elements that make up the multiverse, lie the Para-elemental Planes: regions where Elemental Planes collide and their elements mingle. These Para-elemental Planes are the Plane of Ash, the Plane of Ice, the Plane of Magma, and the Plane of Ooze. These planes are home to the para-elementals: ice elementals, magma elementals, mud elementals, and smoke elementals.

The young jerbeen Jerrin Hollowhome has gained an infamous reputation as the phantom thief, Snapshadow, who appears without warning before melting into the night. Snapshadow has worked for various criminal factions in the past, though she only steals from the wealthy, and often distributes the spoils of her crime among Alderheart's most needy. As a result she has become a folk hero in some circles, though this hasn't made her any less of a thief in the eyes of the Perch Guard.

Snapshadow dresses in loose clothing which hides many weapons. She usually keeps two daggers in spring loaded wrist sheaths, as well as a hidden hand crossbow mounted on a bracer. She is also known to carry a rapier hidden inside a plain looking walking stick.

A young female jerbeen agitator with a history of moving between criminal factions within Alderheart. She is linked to many of the most infamous crimes in Alderheart. Jerrin has blue eyes and reddish-orange fur dotted with white speckles, though she usually keeps her face concealed under a cloak. She often carries concealed weapons.

images.title: {@b Snapshadow}, 5,000 gp. Wanted For: Fraud, Extortion, Murder, Racketeering, Theft, & Smuggling

name: Snori
entries: Dark-skinned gnome

{@i This severe elf has pale, almost white skin and tightly braided blond hair. Her gown is exquisite, fashioned of luminous blue fabric that catches light and shines from within. Lacy ice crystals accent the gown, and a snow-white mantle cascades from her shoulders. Icicles radiate in a crown-like halo behind her head, drifting gracefully through the air}.

Her Crystalline Majesty, Morrinn, is the cold-hearted Snow Queen, Daughter of Boreas. The Snow Queen rules a northern kingdom in the remote, frozen reaches of the world. Perpetually shrouded in snow and ice, her domain is inhospitable to outsiders. She rules from a castle of delicate spires carved entirely out of ice. The dwelling catches and reflects even the faintest glimmer of light, shining like a beacon and enticing travelers to risk the dangerous winter realm.

entries.name: Queen of Giants
entries: The Snow Queen is proud and cruel to any who cross her. Her daughters, the ice maidens, roam her kingdom with ease. Travelers who can't give a good reason to be moving through the Queen's territory meet a quick end in the maidens' chilly embrace. The Snow Queen commands the loyalty of winter-born tribes of fraughashar, ogres, frost giants, thursir giants, and trollkin. She is said to have mocked both Thor and Loki and often leads their priests astray into winter storms.

entries.name: Fey Lords and Ladies
entries: Fey are capricious, mischievous, and often dangerous beings. However, despite their chaotic reputations, they do follow a certain set of rules. These rules—widely misunderstood by outsiders—are codified and enforced by a cadre of lofty fey nobility. Befitting any courtly structure, the fey bow to lords and ladies: eldritch creatures of immense power who rule the courts.

entries.name: Heads of State
entries: The fey lords and ladies are beings of high station and prodigious personal power. Each rules over at least a great city if not an entire nation. No matter the scope of a fey noble's domain, in his or her eyes, a fey ruler's word is law. Outsiders might not understand the edicts and interdicts of a fey noble, but that's no protection against the harsh penalties that await any who break them, knowingly or otherwise.

entries.name: Vacant Thrones
entries: When a lord or lady of the fey dies, the court does not remain leaderless for long. Ambitious beings among the fey always hunger for more power and covet the stations of their superiors. After a traditional month or year of mourning, vicious power struggles winnow the weak and pave the way for the most cunning or the strongest to take the court's vacant throne.

entries.name: The Snow Queen's Lair
entries: The Snow Queen's lair is a castle made of ice. Sunlight and moonlight flash through the delicate spires and translucent walls, setting the palace agleam even in the deepest night. The castle reflects its mistress: beautiful, cold, and unforgivingly deadly.

Camouflaged against the ice, a solitary snow sphinx is on the prowl. A shock of dark humanoid hair whips around a feline face, revealing piercing blue eyes that can freeze foes with a single glance. Compared to its desert-dwelling cousins, this sphinx is far less likely to be defeated with reason or logic. Although a snow sphinx can speak, it generally greets its prey with claws and teeth rather than riddles or philosophical conversation.

Physically, this fearsome creature is well adapted to harsh habitats, such as ice-covered mountains or arctic plains. It has wide paws to stop it sinking into soft snow and thick fur to ward out the cold. The sphinx's muscular wings carry the same spotted markings as its fur; they are strong enough to withstand the bitter winds that whistle across the tundra.

name: Snowball Spirits
entries: Snowball spirits are small, fist-sized spirits that are curious and playful. They can be found anywhere there is a thick blanket of snow and are easy to locate due to their clinking, tinkling laughter. But if a group of snowball spirits feel threatened they can swarm together to create a larger and larger snowball made up of their tiny bodies. The more and more grumpy a snowball spirit gets, the larger it grows, until it becomes a terrifying behemoth as big as a house. Even at this giant size, a snowball spirit is a surprisingly fast adversary that can shoot out snowballs like a cannon and can leap through the air to easily engulf a horse and rider.

name: Soda Slime
entries: Grape, Orange, Strawberry, and Cola, these ancient sodas and more can be found across the island, kept pristine by the magics of the First Age and Obojima. But when the magic protecting these delicious treats begins to spoil, a peculiar creature can start to form inside these colorful metal cans. Soda slimes have been the lament of adventurers and mages alike who have taken it upon themselves to explore the forgotten buildings left behind from the First Age. Also known by the name Sugar Slimes, these tiny oozes can be very territorial when they're not hibernating or searching for other slimes to consume.

name: Solomon Roderick
entries: Solomon Roderick is a heavyset, heavily scarred man of 40 years. His skin is as hairless and rough as the stone he works with, and his brown eyes are equally cold when dealing with strangers or customers.

Roderick lives above his workshop with his eight-year-old daughter, Sofia. Her mother left the village not long after she was born, leaving Solomon to raise the girl alone. She assists him in the shop when she's not attending {@creature Finneas Trout|CrookedMoon24|Finneas Trout's} lessons.

The most skilled mason in the hollow, Solomon understands his craft and the leverage that gives him. He works with subordinates who spend their time overseeing the removal of stone from the area's quarries, leaving Solomon to manage the building and maintenance of stone structures throughout Wickermoor Village.

While he comes across as cold, calculating, and strict, Solomon is as soft-hearted as they come while in private with the people he cares for. He dotes on his daughter, whose happiness and wellness are his chief goal. Solomon is a recent convert to the Brightsinger, and his newfound faith is strong, making large donations to the church and those in need.
{@i The massive wolf lumbers forward, malice gleaming in its black eyes. Two snake-like tongues slither in its jaws, and green scales peek from beneath its black fur.}

entries.name: Demonic Wolves
entries: Demonic black eyes, two snakelike tongues, and green-black scales beneath their black fur betray the sons of Fenris's unnatural origins.

entries.name: Hibernate Until Ravenous
entries: Sons of Fenris slumber beneath the snow for months, waking when they grow ravenous or when prey approaches. When hunting, they revel in wanton savagery and destruction, killing entire herds to delight in blood.

entries.name: Desperate Worshipers
entries: Despite their fierce nature, all the sons of Fenris are divine offspring and wise in divine lore, attracting desperate souls who offer them worship and sacrifice in exchange for aid. The sons of Fenris enjoy this adulation, and they provide protection and wisdom to their followers. Sometimes, they gather enormous war bands and go reaving.
{@i The creature walks on crab-like legs, carrying a fleshy, ectoplasm-filled mass on its back.}

entries.name: Merchants from the Lower Planes
entries: Soul eaters are soul-collecting fiends from the Lower Planes where they freely barter for prey. When a soul eater dies, the souls it carried are released and returned to their bodies or to their appropriate final destinations. Regardless, a dead soul eater has no souls for the demons and devils who value souls as currency. This gives soul eaters a measure of safety and power in the Lower Planes, and many of them operate as neutral merchants among other fiends.

entries.name: Hatred of the Sun God
entries: Soul eaters bear a particular antipathy for followers of the deities of the sun. They go to great lengths to kill any such deity's clergy, even defying the wishes of their fiendish superiors on occasion.

name: Soulbound Handler
entries: Handlers are a case study in misdirection Due to their imposing presence, musculature, and distinctly fiendish glare, they are often mistaken for a pygmy raksha's shapeshifting disguise. This is entirely intentional; the handler's sole job is to protect its fiendish master.

entries.name: Deals With Devils
entries: Who says crime doesn't pay? Stronger, more lethal, and more hardy than even a master-at-arms, handlers have traded their soul for infernal power. Sure, they're little more than a glorified cat carrier, but gosh, wouldn't it feel good to be that powerful? What are you going to do with your soul anyway...?

name: Soulfire Stoker

entries: {@i Engine-Born Spirit of Flame and Death}

Soulfire stokers are Elemental spirits of fire who inhabit furnaces, engines, and boilers that burn bodies or souls. The resulting creature is composed of ghostly flames and steam, with swirling plates of phantom iron that resemble the engine or machine that gave it form. A crackling blend of fire and negative energy, soulfire stokers burn away souls as much as flesh.

entries.name: Secret
entries: Soulfire stokers are compelled to burn corpses they can see, so dead things can bait the spirits.
A Southerner Champion may be a chieftain from Dunland, a bandit lord capable of uniting a number of fractious warriors into a small army, or just a particularly vicious brigand.

entries.name: Hostile Southerners
entries: The people of Bree call 'Southerner' every foreigner coming up the Greenway. The vast majority are simply moving away from some trouble, looking for lands where they can find some peace. Others are not so well-meaning...{@i "If room isn't found for them, they'll find it for themselves. They've a right to live, same as other folk..."}

entries.name: Evil Men
entries: Cruel individuals like brigands, marauders and slavers prowling the Lone-lands of Middle-earth fall within this category. Their malicious will notwithstanding, Evil Men are not servitors of Sauron, and they can end up opposing the Player- heroes for reasons not dependent on an allegiance with the Dark Lord.

When a particularly harsh winter has passed, Men from the South may assemble war parties and look for some isolated homestead to plunder, before retreating just as quickly back into the mists where they came from.

Others are not so well-meaning...{@i "If room isn't found for them, they'll find it for themselves. They've a right to live, same as other folk..."}

entries: Cruel individuals like brigands, marauders and slavers prowling the Lone-lands of Middle-earth fall within this category. Their malicious will notwithstanding, Evil Men are not servitors of Sauron, and they can end up opposing the Player- heroes for reasons not dependent on an allegiance with the Dark Lord.
When sovereign ooze vassals are near each other, they are compelled to join together. The process of merging two Sovereign Ooze Vassals takes one hour, resulting in a single Sovereign Ooze Lord.

The resulting sovereign ooze lord has a more evolved intelligence than its component creatures. They can think and plan, as well as communicate telepathically with other creatures on a more complex level. They can make bargains and—more importantly—break them if it furthers their goals.

In addition to the urge for self-preservation, the sovereign ooze lord has the drive to find others like itself, commanding its ooze vassals to seek them out. Ultimately, it searches for other ooze lords to merge with to form a Sovereign Ooze Monarch.
At its core, however, the sovereign ooze lord is driven to bring chaos and formlessness to everything around it.

entries.name: Sovereign Oozes
entries: Careless wizards, artificers, alchemists, and other creators of magical substances sometimes dispose of failed experiments haphazardly. They think city sewers or workshop basement grates are safe places to dump their magical waste. These remnants, often liquid in form and brimming with magical potential, interact with organic matter—blood, bodily waste, or dead flesh—to gain sentience and form. These newly formed creatures are sovereign oozes.

Sages who've studied the lore of these creatures believe that another factor may also contribute to a sovereign ooze's creation and its drive to transform the world into the same substance from which it is formed. These experts have proposed several possible catalysts: intervention by a great demonic power, such as Juiblex; influence from one of the planes of chaos, such as Limbo or Pandemonium; or manipulation by a god associated with chaos or entropy (perhaps with a tinge of evil), such as Ralishaz or Tharizdun.

Unlike many other oozes, sovereign oozes possess advanced sentience, and in the case of the more evolved sovereign oozes, sapience. This cognitive functionality allows the lord and monarch versions of the sovereign ooze to communicate and develop intricate plans that involve manipulating other creatures.

Sovereign oozes can assume rough shapes of other creatures they have encountered (or eaten). These forms cannot replicate fine details, but are refined enough to sometimes fool inattentive observers or those whose sight is obscured by darkness.

Sovereign oozes consume organic matter to gain energy, and they grow in power by combining with other sovereign oozes. Two Sovereign Ooze Vassals can join to become a Sovereign Ooze Lord, and two Sovereign Ooze Lords can join to become a Sovereign Ooze Monarch. Experts are unsure whether two or more monarchs can join, and they hope they never find out.
When two Sovereign Ooze Lords merge, the resulting creature is a Sovereign Ooze Monarch.

Sovereign ooze monarchs have an even greater capacity to think, communicate, reason, and plot. They also begin receiving messages from whatever greater power is linked to their existence (if any). In that case, they focus on carrying out the wishes of those greater powers. The Greater Power table below lists entities that may control the sovereign ooze monarch.
In the absence of a greater power's influence, the sovereign ooze monarch simply wants to consume organic matter and turn other creatures into sovereign oozes to serve it.

Ooze monarchs have antithetical feelings toward each other. If one sovereign ooze monarch ventures within 50 miles of another, they immediately attempt to destroy each other—or they convince other creatures to do so on their behalf.

rows: A deity of chaos and entropy
A demon lord looking to cause trouble
A lich in the area hoping for a distraction
An archmage building an ooze army

Experts are unsure whether two or more monarchs can join, and they hope they never find out.

Sovereign ooze vassals form when discarded magical experiments, especially alchemical concoctions and potions, mix with organic matter from sentient creatures. A magical spark animates the mixture, granting it life. These oozes are most likely to originate in sewers near alchemists' shops, in vast caverns beneath arcane schools, in the sub-basements of wizards' towers, or in places where magic-wielding folks congregate and work.

Sovereign ooze vassals cannot speak, but they possess a form of telepathy that allows them to communicate with other creatures on a rudimentary level. They can, however, convey complex thoughts to other sovereign oozes.

With no external stimuli, the sovereign ooze vassal is driven to consume organic matter to survive: flesh, plants, offal, etc. However, if they come into contact with another of their kind, they feel a strong compulsion to merge with it. They also readily obey commands from sovereign ooze lords or monarchs.

Melted wax from ritual candles that merged into a corpse
Inert Alchemist's Fire soaked into rat droppings
Tainted Potions of Healing soaked into carrion crawler remains
Corrupted Holy Water mixed with sewer water
Failed Potions of Growth saturating a mass of hair
