entries: Shuffling through the car is a {@creature Wayward Haint|CrookedMoon24} of an old man in a sailor's coat with a clay pipe. Grumbling, he purposelessly heaves sacks of mail from one end of the car to the other as if he was loading cargo on a ship. There is a distant regretful look in his eyes as he goes about his labor.

When encountered, he only cares to talk about the sea and his long career as a sailor, captain, and lighthouse keeper, bemoaning that he died inland. He regularly mentions that he wishes he could see the sea one last time with glum wistfulness.

Bringing the Mariner the landscape painting of the coastline, which can be found in the Lounge Car (area G3), fills him with a sense of awe and reverence. He sheds a tear and remarks on the beauty of the sea before breathing an unfettered sigh and fading away.
Alternatively, below are suggested resolution proficiencies:

items.name: {@item Navigator's Tools|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB}:
items.entry: Reminisce with the Mariner about times navigating dangerous waters.

items.name: {@skill Performance|XPHB} or {@item Musical Instrument|XPHB}:
items.entry: Sing or play a lively shanty to lift his spirits.

items.name: {@skill Deception|XPHB} or {@skill Medicine|XPHB}:
items.entry: Opine about all the worst parts of sailing, including scurvy, drowning, and other miserable conditions, to help him let go.

entries.name: The Mossbows
entries: The Mossbows are a family of strigs that live in the city of Alderheart. They are ordinary folk who have lived in the city for most of their lives, earning a modest living from their small, local bookshop.

name: The Phantom Trainhopper
entries: There is one soul aboard the train who doesn't have a ticket to ride: the Phantom Trainhopper ({@creature Shadow|XMM}). In life, they were a member of a secret cult in the living world that worships Kehlenn, the Crooked Queen. Tonight, they were ritually sacrificed so their spirit could sneak aboard the {@i Ghostlight Express} on this rare evening that {@creature Phillip Druskenvald|CrookedMoon24|Phillip} and {@creature Adela Druskenvald|CrookedMoon24} are passengers.

Granted exceptional power in death by Kehlenn's chief minion, the {@creature Crooked Man|CrookedMoon24}, this malevolent shade carries a curse aboard to corrupt the spirits that the Ghostlight Locomotive uses for fuel. With help from the devouring Shroud, the Phantom Trainhopper turns the ghost train against {@creature the Vagrant|CrookedMoon24} and strands the Druskenvalds—and coincidentally, the characters—in Wickermoor Hollow.

Once the shade releases Kehlenn's curse, it's just a matter of time before that curse reaches the Tender (area G8), and, ultimately, the locomotive. Unwittingly, the characters likely play an integral part in bringing about The Crooked Queen's goal by unsealing the final door and letting the curse in.

A band of old hunting buddies, the Ragtaggers are three humblefolk hunters who work together as a team to bring down large quarry. The Ragtaggers are made up of {@creature Snap|HumblewoodTales} (a thin and shrewd vulpin), {@creature Cackle|HumblewoodTales} (a good-humored and barrel-chested mapach known for his chuckle), and {@creature Podge|HumblewoodTales} (a very grumpy hedge and the de facto leader of the group). They may appear to be little more than bandit scoundrels, but underneath their suspicious exteriors are three devoted friends who are happy to help wanderers, sometimes even for free.

name: The Songstress
entries: Sitting in one of the velvet chairs is a {@creature Wayward Haint|CrookedMoon24} of a beautiful woman in a long, silky dress, smoking a cigarette while glumly looking out the window. Her whole being seems hollow. She only knows herself as a songstress who wished to be a famous singer in life.

When encountered, she feels empty, having never been able to find the perfect song that inspired her to give the performance of a lifetime for an audience that truly appreciated her talent. Her tastes are jazzy and romantic, and she wishes she could give one last soulful performance.

Bringing her the phonograph found in the Sleeper Car (area G2) and turning it on inspires her to sing the perfect final song. She stands at the center of the lounge and croons a love song that spurs Phillip and Adela to embrace and slowly dance to the performance. When the song concludes, she is freed, closing her eyes contentedly and fading away in peace.
When the song concludes, she is freed, closing her eyes contentedly and fading away in peace. The lyrics are as follows:
Impossible to think at all, without the thought of you  and me.
It all would fall, nothing left to hold the stars and seas apart.
Ridiculous, there ever was a world without a 'you and me.'
To not recall a 'you' at all would send it all crashing down.
Floating over the storm, love as soft as a cloud.
Incredible that through it all, the dashed and broken stardust fell,
And settled into 'you and me,' and all the time we need.
Alternatively, below are suggested resolution proficiencies:

items.name: {@item Musical Instrument|XPHB} or {@skill Performance|XPHB}:
items.entry: Join the Songstress in a duet for an emotional swan song.

items.name: {@skill Arcana|XPHB} or {@skill Insight|XPHB}:
items.entry: Consider cosmic or philosophical topics that speak to inspiration and creativity.

items.name: {@skill History|XPHB} or {@skill Investigation|XPHB}:
items.entry: Explore examples of artistic work that help inspire the Songstress.

name: The Sweetheart
entries: Within the third cabin is a {@creature Wayward Haint|CrookedMoon24} of a weeping young woman, looking wistful as she longingly stares at a locket of a handsome mustachioed man with the initials J.B. underneath the portrait. She only knows herself as his sweetheart.

She is lovesick and lonely, only barely registering the characters and bemoaning having to travel to the afterlife alone. She isn't complete without her dear love, and she doesn't want to spend an eternity without him.

Giving her the love letter from Jakob Braun found in the Mail Car (area G5) makes her realize that her love is already on the other side and is waiting for her in the afterlife. She weeps with joy, hugging the tear-stained letter and her locket as she is freed and fades from view.
Alternative resolution proficiencies are:

items.name: {@item Calligrapher's Supplies|XPHB} or {@skill Performance|XPHB}:
items.entry: {@action Help|XPHB} her compose a poem or song about her love so she has something to soothe her longing for him.

items.name: {@skill History|XPHB} or {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}:
items.entry: Commiserate with her with personal tales of lost and regained love or recite legends or tales of the same.

items.name: {@skill Investigation|XPHB} or {@skill Religion|XPHB}:
items.entry: Steer her to remember details of her love's qualities in a real and practical way, suggesting they will be reunited when she reaches her destination.

name: The Tall Man

entries: {@i Murderous Archfey of the Dark Wood}

The Tall Man is a mysterious entity that haunts an accursed forest. Once, he was an archfey who ruled a now-forgotten court, renowned for its dances that lasted for nights on end. Doomed now to walk his rotting forest, the Tall Man finds pleasure where he can by tempting travelers and forest denizens alike to play hide and seek with him—with deadly results.

entries.name: Secret
entries: Dancing forgotten steps once performed in the fey court that the Tall Man formerly ruled shreds his being.

entries.name: Tall Man's Lair
entries: The Tall Man's lair is the dark forest he now haunts, where his forgotten Fey court once thrived.

name: The Thousand Voices, Supreme Soul Vortex
entries: The Supreme Soul Vortex is directly responsible for the formation and disruptive actions of the Infinite Animarum, the widespread cult of disruptive and remorseless individuals that spread like an odorless toxin through the Material Plane. They actively manipulate Ochre Elson, the group's mysterious leader, to achieve their own ends. As one entity formed from countless lost spirits, the Thousand Voices seeks ultimate vengeance against the deities, both evil and good, and to upend the metaplanar system that caused its swirling souls to fall between the cracks of time and space. They actively recruit warlock followers in pursuit of this agenda, causing massive amounts of chaos and wanton destruction as they try to deprive the gods of their souls by making more Soul Vortices.

Those unlucky enough to face the Thousand Voices in open combat will have to face the combined knowledge and skill of hundreds of skilled spellcasters, masterful tacticians, and fearsome warriors. With potent spellcasting abilities and an ethereal form that allows them to escape most grasps, the Supreme Soul Vortex very rarely finds themself challenged enough to put forth their full strength. Most who challenge them are swiftly put down and, if they're lucky, are sent to one of the upper or lower planes. Especially while in the space between planes where Soul Vortices form, the Thousand Voices reign with confidence and might.

entries.name: The Space Between
entries: Though many believe this space to be simply an unchartable portion of the astral plane, there simply is not enough information available either way. By all accounts, only those unfortunate enough to fall into the Space Between or invited in by a Soul Vortex can access the space, as planar teleportation has thus far failed on every occasion. It is described as a true void, where even astral starlight dares not venture.

name: The Thrasvyr
entries: A dragon

Found in the {@i Creature Codex}, the xiphus is a speedy fey whose heart was replaced with clockwork long ago, granting it some power over time. In {@i The House of Reciprocities} (see {@i Tales from the Shadows}), a particularly successful xiphus, known as the Ticktock Man, resides in the Ticktock Tower in the Shadow Realm, where he collects stolen memories. The Ticktock Tower serves as his lair, and when encountered there, he has a challenging rating of 6 (2,300 XP). All temporal effects created by Ticktock Tower end abruptly when the Ticktock Man dies. All the clock doors become insubstantial and slowly fade from existence, except for the Nexus Portal, which remains.

entries.name: The Ticktock Man's Lair
entries: The Ticktock Man channels his obsession with time into the massive tower made of clocks in which he resides. Ticktock Tower is somehow connected to the flow of time itself. The Ticktock Man is a similarly connected to the Tower in a sort of symbiotic relationship, allowing him to further manipulate aspects of time while inside his lair.

name: The Vagrant
entries: The Vagrant, an amiable frogman with mottled green skin, serves as a "Stranger" (see chapter 1) who ferries the souls of the dead to the "other side." The Ghostlight Express is his chosen vessel for this sacred responsibility, and he serves as the ghost train's conductor and engineer. He wears the tattered garb of a vagabond, complete with a wide-brimmed hat where he always keeps three railroad spikes.

Bound by his eternal duty, the Vagrant offers safe passage to the souls of the dead who will be reborn in the realm of Druskenvald. A consummate storyteller, he believes each passenger that boards the ghost train has a tale to tell, which he is happy to do in the form of a song aided by his well-worn fiddle.

The Vagrant has a strange kinship with the Ghostlight Express as its sole caretaker. Through the eons, the few who have come to know this ferryman have wondered if the Vagrant himself is bound to the train just as much as the haints who cannot disembark. But none ever learned the truth of the frogman's origins, and his story remains a mystery.

name: The Vermintoll Abomination

entries: {@i Verminous Coven Amalgamation}

The magic that binds hag covens together is far more powerful than many spellcasters can fully comprehend. Vermintoll abominations come about when the magics of a centipede hag, a pigeon hag, and a weasel hag enmesh and fuse the witches into one mass, bound to their cauldron.

entries.name: Vermintoll Abomination's Lair
entries: The Vermintoll Abomination's lair is a decrepit hideaway, often hidden in plain sight such as an attic, basement, or a seized home.

name: The Weeping Widow

entries: {@i Matron of Malevolent Medicine}

Once a priestess committed to healing the sick through divine rites, the Weeping Widow abandoned the gods after a personal tragedy and turned to sinister science. Believing she knows how to best treat the suffering and make them stronger, she employs a harrowing regimen of alchemical and medical experimentation to wipe minds and alter bodies, whether the patient wants the treatment or not.

entries.name: Secret
entries: The only way to force the Weeping Widow to live up to her moniker is to remind her of the family she lost, such as her husband's sword or portrait, which forces her to confront what she has become.

entries.name: Weeping Widow's Lair
entries: The Weeping Widow's lair is the sanitorium where she conducts her horrific experiments.

name: The Whispered Promise

entries: Blossoming tendrils of chaotic shadow-stuff dart and weave through the air along with a chorus of whispers, like the sultry hum of sweet nothings lulling in your ears. Coalescing into a briefly coherent form, the being you perceive is strangely familiar, taking the shape of your very heart's desire. You see within the oscillating mass the image of all you love and strive towards, every ambition you've held, every dream and hope you've longed for, and, most hauntingly, an image of yourself as you wish you could be.

The Whispered Promise is a demonic entity who appears before mortals of great potential, offering to fulfill their every ambition and desire. It is a mind-reader and shapeshifter, who appears before mortals as their own reflections, but in a grand and idealized form. In this way, The Whispered Promise preys upon their insecurities and dreams simultaneously, showing mortals both their grand potential and many shortcomings through contrast. To those rare few who do not feel ambition or self-doubt, The Whispered Promise appears to be a writhing bundle of hairs.

The Whispered Promise preys upon hopes, dreams, and ambitions, seeking to manipulate and seduce mortals into their web of schemes, and ultimately, make countless powerful mortals utterly indebted to the demon lord. Perhaps The Whispered Promise stands behind the great heroes and villains of history, having spurred their ambitions and supercharged their desires. In particular, the Sorcerer-Kings of the Arcane Empire sought out he Whispered Promise and made countless bargains with the demon to advance their wealth and power. Summoning circles and magic items found within their ancient ruins still allow mortals to contact The Whispered Promise. There are even some tieflings who claim that The Whispered Promise is a distant ancestor through fiendish pacts made in those days. It is unknown whether The Whispered Promise had any influence in ultimately engineering the fall of the Sorcerer-Kings.

There is little The Whispered Promise cannot offer. Knowledge and information are their most common currency: teaching mortals forgotten magic and sharing deeply kept secrets. They have dealt in magical artifacts, granting mortals powerful magical items, or simply vast amounts of material wealth. The Whispered Promise also enjoys helping mortals undo a past mistake, solve a guilty conscience, get revenge on a hated enemy, or seize the reins of power for themselves. In exchange, The Whispered Promise seeks to extract a promise of future service from the mortal—a promise for a promise. While they try to keep the terms of this service as open-ended as possible, they reassure mortals they will never ask them to do any direct harm to their friends or loved ones, nor perform any task beyond their own capability to fulfill. In this way, they build a web of interactions and debts, trading services for services. The Whispered Promise plots to use their collected debts to fulfill their future bargains.

While an expert in the desires of others, determining The Whispered Promise's motives prove vexing. The Whispered Promise does not lie, and they seldom reveal their full intentions. They seemingly wish to construct a tapestry of promises, never making one of their own, but brokering the promises of others. A broken promise is a broken thread, pushing the entity to always keep their promises. Yet within this web of desire, The Whispered Promise is always at the center.

entries.name: Roleplaying Traits
entries: Capable of sustaining multiple separate telepathic conversations at once, The Whispered Promise addresses each character individually. They show images of the characters' desires and dreams, depicting them with outrageous fortunes and with immense power.

items: {@b Personality Trait:}  I whisper softly in mortal's ears... What do you yearn for? I have no interest in using it against you... only in making it a reality. Indulge yourself for a change...
{@b Ideal:} I want one thing, and one thing only... to provide you the thing you want most. Ask me, and I'll give it to you. What can I give you that you truly desire?
{@b Bond:} If there's ever a stranger you can trust, it's me. Any deal we made would be signed and sealed. Other demons may utter lies, but I whisper promises... and I keep my promises.
{@b Flaw:} Are you certain you would deny me? I dislike being turned down...why wait for what you deserve? If you change your mind...you need only whisper...and I'll be there...

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Arcana|XPHB} or {@skill History|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Religion|XPHB}) checks when they take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine The Whispered Promise, learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (20+) Demonic Power
entries: You are aware of its {@sense Truesight|XPHB} and {@variantrule Telepathy|XPHB}, its {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}, and Epic {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB}. You also know this eldritch entity is beyond life and death and can reform years later if killed.

entries.name: (25+) Enraptured Presence
entries: You are aware of the creature's Alluring Aura trait.

entries.name: (30+) Powerful Presence
entries: You know The Whispered Promise's highest and lowest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Whispered Promise regards battle as a physical expression of their ability to control others. It uses Alluring Aura to prevent attacks and they negate resistances to its psychic onslaught by grappling with its Unravelling Resolve trait. They sow discord using {@spell Mass Suggestion}, {@spell Dominate Monster}, and their Dominate power, revealing in the resentment, jealousy, disdain, envy, and anger its foes have towards one another.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Fiend.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Monster Blood.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Heart.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Teeth, Claws.

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Skin.

name: The White Worm

entries: {@i Eldritch Devourer of Memories}

Born of a forgotten realm beyond the stars, the White Worm is an eldritch horror resembling a humungous, pallid grub that ravenously hungers for memory. Greedily consuming the memories of any beings capable of remembering, its mere existence sends out shockwaves of alien psychic energy. It also serves as the queen of a hivemind colony of infinite wormlike spawn that seek mortal hosts to feast upon and control.

entries.name: Secret
entries: A specific series of constellations and star paths through the heavens is a deadly poison to the White Worm if it consumes that memory.

entries.name: White Worm's Lair
entries: The White Worm's lair is a secluded lake and the shores surrounding it.

name: The Wicker Man

entries: {@i Blazing Sacrificial Colossus}

The ultimate expression of a cult's dedication to its patron is the Wicker Man. This massive Construct is woven from wicker and bound with wire and iron bands in the shape of a great bipedal effigy. The chest cavity and limbs are hollow where sacrifices can be secured, with the wicker skin forming cage-like bars and gaps. Celebrated and protected with a cult's very existence, the Wicker Man stands silent and impassive until it is ignited while filled with living sacrifices. Then it comes to life and seeks to consume any nonbelievers—and sometimes even the faithful.

entries.name: Wicker Man's Lair
entries: The Wicker Man's lair is the hilltop where it is constructed and venerated.

Rising on one of the highest hills in the Barrow-downs, this burial mound conceals a vast underground complex, descending deep into the bowels of the earth, with dark and cold tunnels winding into many lesser burial chambers, where dozens of warriors are entombed with their gear of war and precious treasure. The stink of decay, stagnation, and rot chokes any who are foolish enough to push aside the great carven stone that blocks the entryway into this labyrinth of the dead.

This is the haunted lair of the Wight-king, the chief of all blighted creatures who dwell in Tyrn Gorthad. Some say he was the last King of Cardolan, buried in the Barrow-downs before the Great Plague. Others hold him to be the malicious spirit of some fell captain who once served Angmar. What is certain is that in the ages since the barrow was dug, the Wight-king has carved for himself a great throne room,

deep in the darkness. Concealed from the light of day, he sits and festers in his own hatred, his lust for death satiated only when intruders dare enter his domain, or on the rare occasions when he walks among the mists of the Barrow-downs under cover of darkness. Stories of his empty eyes, his broken blade, and his terrible song have kept most would-be tomb robbers from daring to come near his domain—and those who do are seldom heard from again.

Scant few have seen the Wight-king and lived to tell the tale, but mad tomb-robbers who have come out of the Barrow-downs tell of a fleshless warrior wearing the blackened raiment of an ancient noble. Empty black eyes burn behind a great, cracked helm, and a pitted blade is clutched in his left hand. All that is dead and yet still lives by sorcery or the will of the Enemy is his to command.

The Wight-king leaves the Great Barrow only at night, and moves in darkness and silence across Tyrn Gorthad, singing songs of hopelessness and sorrow in both the {@language Westron|TLotRR|Common Tongue} and the {@language Black Speech|TLotRR} of Mordor.

name: The Wild Hunt
entries: Few countryside stories are more prevalent than that of The Wild Hunt. Composed of myriad spectral predators and fallen hunters, the hunt roam the woods of both the Material and Ethereal planes in search of a worthy quarry. Scholars have recorded only a few accounts of surviving eyewitnesses, who mutter and wail about the terrible, echoing horn calls and endlessly trampling feet.

entries.name: Undead Nature
entries: The Wild Hunt doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.

name: The Wild Titan

entries: {@i Ferocious Giant of the Wilderness}

Wandering the most inhospitable mountain ranges, the Wild Titan is the wilderness made manifest, created long ago by a forgotten will for a purpose that none know. Favoring solitude in the most remote places of the world, when it encounters settlements and "civilized" people, it wants only to turn them to primal savagery or crush them beneath its immense bulk.

entries.name: Secret
entries: The name of the Wild Titan's forgotten creator is its undoing. Recovering the lost name and carving its glyph form into a stone creates a zone that severs the titan's connection to the wild.

entries.name: Wild Titan's Lair
entries: The Wild Titan's lair is a hollowed-out peak in the mountain range the creature stalks.

name: The World Ender

entries: A storm of black clouds and sheets of octarine lightning fill the air, and unnatural otherworldly thunder crashes as a steady contaminated rain begins to pour.

Rising from the shattered delerium heart in a plume of eldritch Haze, stands a creature as tall as a tower, its bulbous head adorned with octarine {@item crystal|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium crystals} that crackle and spark with arcane energy. These crystals protrude from its flesh down its neck and across its shoulders, as well as down its spine. Seven massive yellow eyes peer out from below a furrowed brow, over a reptilian snout with a wide set mouth that stretches across its head filled with rows of jagged teeth. Its large, elongated maw opens to reveal one hundred thin translucent tentacles that lash and dart out like one hundred tongues. Its wet skin is a mottled grayish purple, shimmering in unknown colors impossible to comprehend.

The Haze disperses in an instant as it rises from the Crater. Its four muscular arms end in hands with eight long spindly fingers, each tipped with a delerium clawed nail. Its large digitigrade legs end in veiny black hooves, and its rigid spine extends into three long, tentacle-like tails. The smell of ozone and sulfur fill the air, and a deep and booming voice utters words incomprehensible in a cadence unrecognizable to the human ear, merely coming through as a muffled tone of booming bass and high-pitched wails that causes your brain to seer in pain.

A colossal delerium crystal rests at the center of the Crater. This "Delerium Heart" is a piece of a distant unknown world utterly consumed and destroyed by the Haze. It is the largest source of the {@condition contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} spreading out from Drakkenheim. If there is any hope for stopping the slow progression of the Haze, it must begin with the destruction of the Delerium Heart. Characters mighty or foolish enough to accomplish this monumental task alone will not end the {@condition contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} of Drakkenheim, but instead unleash a destructive horror unlike anything the earth has ever known: The World Ender.

No two individuals who bear witness to the emergence of The World Ender can describe its arrival in the same terms. One hero perceives it breaking free of the Delerium Heart like a creature hatching from a great egg; another describes it suddenly appearing from the mist in a flash of thunder and lightning; while a third sees a small creature nearby haplessly mutate into a colossal being when exposed to the powerful forces released upon the destruction of the Delerium Heart.

The World Ender is only one possible moniker for this titanic engine of destruction. The Apocalypse, The World Eater, The Harbinger, Death, The Annihilator, The Last Nightmare, The Wrath of Gods, and The Chosen One are all other titles it may wear. It is unclear if the creature is a singular entity, or one of many which have appeared in the death throes of the countless worlds consumed by the Haze.

The World Ender cannot be reasoned with, bargained with, or understood; its origins and purposes remain shrouded in mystery—it simply is. The complexities of human civilization—the sprawling cities, political conflicts, bloody wars, and the rise and fall of monarchs, mages, heroes, and priests—are utterly meaningless before it. Once freed, it tramples cities without awareness or concern, obliterating armies and toppling nations with the same dispassionate ease with which natural forces reshape landscapes. Indeed, The World Ender's rampage is more akin to an unfathomable natural disaster, blind to the devastation it wreaks.

Efforts to understand or influence it are as futile as ants trying to comprehend a river that threatens to wash them away. In the face of such power, humanity is left scrambling for survival. Mortals become painfully aware that in the grand scheme of things, our existence might be as transient as raindrops in a storm, unnoticed by the forces that alter our world

entries.name: Horror from Beyond the Stars
entries: The mages of the Amethyst Academy have long researched delerium, and discoveries in the Crater enable them to paint a full picture about the origin of the stones. When delerium is left uncontained in massive quantities, it is possible it can slowly grow and seep into the heart of an entire planet, eventually rotting the core. The entire surface becomes a wasteland of octarine crystals as big as buildings, with a Haze-covered sky of eldritch storm clouds that blacks out the sun. Under these conditions, {@condition contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} runs rampant and no lifeform on the surface is free from endless mutation. As the planet festers and mutates to the point of destruction, the Haze and delerium cause all manner of abominations to grow and change. Given the hundreds of years it takes for delerium to infect an entire planet, the mutated monstrosities have ample time to grow to massive proportions. This creature is but the first of many which could be created if the Academy is not able to contain and control delerium.

Eventually however, the delerium begins to expand at an increased rate, and some of these creatures end up encased in the eldritch crystals, being forced into a state of hibernation. When the planet is fully contaminated, it explodes sending massive chunks of contaminated rock through the cosmos. Some of these meteors have mutated monstrosities housed within their cores, waiting for a time to break free upon a new contaminated world. We have received the remnants of a distant dead world, and we must contain it before the same thing happens to ours.

Grandmaster Wizard Eldrick Runeweaver postulates that containment of The World Ender is best achieved by sealing it back inside a massive delerium formation: essentially re-creating the Delerium Heart. Such a feat would require a massive flood of contaminated energy and a locus of {@item geode|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium geodes}.

entries.name: Catastrophic Mutation
entries: The Knights of the Silver Order are resolute that The World Ender confirms the destructive blight that delerium represents. It must be contained and destroyed lest it consume and contaminate the entire earth. This massive monstrosity is but the first of a new generation of titanic horrors which will devour the earth if delerium is not dealt with soon. The Knights have a blunt theory about how it was created: it's just another big mutant caused by the eldritch {@condition contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} of delerium. They cite the many documented instances when destroying or damaging a large cluster of delerium caused rifts between the planes or sudden surges of eldritch {@condition contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}. If the Delerium Heart is the largest piece of delerium ever encountered, then it stands to reason that shattering it would cause the largest {@table Arcane Anomalies|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} ever known. It's possible that the monster is the result of this catastrophe: it may have been conjured forth from some distant and unknown dimension of destruction, or perhaps a cascading mutation took root within a nearby creature.

entries.name: Harbinger of Sin
entries: The Followers of the Falling Fire believe a terrible sin has been wrought for destroying the Delerium Heart, and the salvation of this world is now in doubt. This cosmic being was meant to be The Harbinger of the Sacred Flame, but it has been unleashed before its preordained purpose. It is now an infant, mewling and raging at its destiny denied. Any hope we have must now be found in a monumental sacrifice.

Lucretia Mathias believes the only solution is to perform a special variant of the Sanctification of the Falling Fire upon the creature. Instead of using normal {@item crystal|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium crystals}, one of the player characters must sacrifice themselves before The World Ender, and the other characters must embed the sanctified delerium crystal bearing the sacrificed heroes' soul into The World Ender's body. Perhaps then, the righteous soul of the fallen player character will fill the creature and turn it into a divine vessel.

entries.name: A Grand and Cosmic Scheme
entries: Panic spreads amongst the Queen's Men as the scoundrels speculate that this creature came here on purpose. Mad rumors insist that it is a scout from a distant planet of huge lizard-creatures, and that The World Ender "piloted" the meteor into Drakkenheim with an intention to take over the world.

The Queen of Thieves laughs while dismissing such conspiracies, caring little about the origin of the creature. Instead, she sees opportunity. Instead, she sees opportunity and searches for a way to capture or control The World Ender. After all, if its power could be harnessed, if she could learn what the creature wants, tame it and use it against her enemies...well, who would be able to stop her then? She would have an even finer prize pet than Big Linda!

entries.name: Great Egg
entries: Amongst the Hooded Lanterns, a strange idea emerges that the Delerium Heart was in fact some kind of gigantic egg which bore The World Ender. Lain by some distant cosmic creature, its eggs shoot through the cosmos like meteors, eventually crashing into unknown and unsuspecting worlds. There, the egg incubates for a hundred or more years, changing the landscape around it into suitable conditions for its young. When the egg hatches, an infant version of this cosmic entity emerges, and the planet it finds itself on is its first hungry meal. This being cares not for the creatures inhabiting these planets, it won't even acknowledge them. It simply is following its own cycle of life, and we are unfortunate enough to be here when it awakens.

Lord Commander Elias Drexel is determined to destroy the beast by any means necessary, before it can spread destruction to the rest of Westemär. He looks to the characters and his soldiers to assemble a vast collection of siege weapons and artillery, which can be found in the arsenals of Castle Drakken. While it will take far more than these alone to bring the beast down, the cannons will no doubt be a useful distraction until The World Ender annihilates them.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they {@action Study|XPHB} The World Ender, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (20+) Force of Destruction
entries: You recognize The World Ender's {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}, {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}, and its Immutable Form trait.

entries.name: (25+) Blast of Energy
entries: You learn of the Ender's Charge Eradication Beam and Eradication Beam actions.

entries.name: (30+) Nearly Unstoppable
entries: You are aware of the The World Ender's Rejuvenation trait.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The World Ender is a force of utter destruction. It cares little for the creatures or structures around it and merely tramples through them without hesitation or remorse. The World Ender unceasingly proceeds forward, and never halts unless it is somehow prevented from moving. It does not flee or hide and has no conception for surrender or fear. It is a force of nature that levels cities to the ground, leaving a path of utter destruction in its wake.

Few creatures pose an actual threat to The World Ender, and it is content to simply smash them with its Necrotic Claws or devour them with its Bite. Indeed, it may not even attack them directly, making most of its attacks against structures or the environment itself and letting the falling rubble crush any it encounters. When confronted with a large obstacle or building, it stops to unleash its Eradication Beam to clear a path forward with no regard for anything in its way.

However, if The World Ender is actually damaged by an attack or spell, it snaps into action and unleashes its Bellowing Roar in response. It follows up with its Ground Slam and then continue attacking until whatever injured it is slain. If it senses it is under attack by multiple foes (such as an approaching army), it aims its Eradication Beam to destroy them. The World Ender calls down Octarine Lightning Strikes against airborne opponents who target it from above, or against groups of foes on the ground.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Aberration.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Monster Blood, Contaminated Ichor.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Eyes, Heart, Brain, Guts, Flesh.

entries.name: Bones:
entries: Skull, Spine, Ribs.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Claws, Teeth, Tentacles.

entries.name: Hair:
entries: Fur.

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Skin.

entries.name: Dust:
entries: Aberrant Dust.

entries.name: Mysterious origin
entries: Characters who confront The World Ender are the first to ever do so: none in the World of Drakkenheim have encountered this creature before nor know of its existence. There is no possible way to discover any information about this creature—not even its existence—until it is released. Even powerful divination magic fails to reveal anything other than a vague omen of unstoppable destruction and terrible consequences for destroying the Delerium Heart. For this reason, the details presented herein are framed as information that could be discovered following the emergence of the creature from the Crater.

entries.name: Destructive Rampage
entries: The World Ender's actions damage and destroy buildings and structures. A creature within 10 feet of a structure that is destroyed must succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw or take 28 ({@damage 8d6}) Bludgeoning damage. Any creature inside the structure when it is destroyed has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the saving throw.
My world changed from touching the Delerium Heart. The world changed from what was inside.

name: Theodora Mayville
entries: Theodora Mayville is a woman in her early 30s with a tall, slender build. She has white-blonde hair that's always set in a single ponytail, but it often falls into disarray under a brown leather hat. Her violet eyes are sharp and kind. She wears plain brown clothes and gold earrings in the shape of pigeons. She cherishes her beloved carrier pigeons as her children, and one of her birds is often roosting on her shoulder.

Theodora is really Golub Graygullet, the {@creature Pigeon Hag|CrookedMoon24} and leader of the Vermintoll Coven. She alters or doctors every single letter that comes and goes from Wickermoor Village, ensuring the information in the town is controlled as much as its people's minds. When the characters discover her true identity, it triggers the events in chapter 20. She won't hesitate to discreetly aid the characters in seeking out and killing her sisters Vessla (see chapter 12) and Stonoga (see chapter 16) in the name of furthering the Crooked Queen's machinations.

name: Thing with the Writhing Tail

entries: This eldritch housecat possesses a sleek, undulating body that stretches out, impossibly long and sinuous, covered in a coat that swirls in blue and purple like the midnight cosmos, speckled with tiny flickering stars. Its fur seems to absorb light, creating a silhouette that shifts and wavers, as if its true form is utterly incomprehensible to your mind. The creature's striking eyes are large, luminous orbs that resemble nebulae, surging with vibrant colors that no earthly cat's eyes would possess. Its paws are tipped with claws made of a material resembling a dark, glassy substance, capable of tearing through the fabric of reality itself. Each step it takes resonates with a soft, eerie echo, as if it walks not just on the physical ground, but also treads through the layers of time and space. Its tail is elongated and flexible, flickering through the air like a dark, wraithlike appendage, constantly moving in patterns that defy the bounds of physical space.

This esoteric cat-like entity is known by many names and wanders the realms of Dreamland and the Space Between Worlds. It was the scholar Killgar Copperpot who realized its multitudinous identities were one and the same and named it the Thing with the Writhing Tail.

Almost every warlock of the Thing with the Writhing Tail was approached by the creature as a child, appearing before them in the form of a common housecat, though one marked by some strange coloration, demeanor, or smell. It seems to favor those in unfortunate, neglectful, or powerless situations, such as street-wandering orphans or the mistreated offspring of narcissistic aristocrats. It casts itself in the role of their imaginary friend and confidant, sharing reassuring stories, protecting them from danger, and spurring them to precociously seek knowledge and adventure.

Its eldritch pact occurs with a seemingly harmless promise to keep their bond an important secret. In turn, the Thing with the Writhing Tail grants its warlocks a special familiar in the form of a cat, which acts as a direct proxy for the entity itself. The familiar accepts any name the child-warlock chooses, often becoming known by names typical of a household pet, such as Bruce, Dinah, Felix, and others. Since the Thing with the Writhing Tail acts through these familiars, its warlocks are able to converse with the entity on a regular basis through their telepathic bond. As such, the warlocks often exhibit the strange behaviors of having one-sided conversations with their cats.

Although it has appeared throughout history to countless mortals, the motivations of this creature are uncertain, even to its warlocks. It oscillates between agent of chaos and custodian of secret lore known only to cats and may be metaphysically connected to all felines. The Thing with the Writhing Tail is utterly indifferent to the human constructs of morality or duty and observes the Mortal World with a detached curiosity and occasional boredom. While most of the time its desires are guided by hungry impulses, it may suddenly fixate its attention on seemingly innocuous or strange patterns or magical phenomena incomprehensible to its human warlocks.

The Thing with the Writhing Tail rests in places defying logic. It basks within cosmic rays shed by dying suns, languishes atop a shifting nebula, and curls up in the dark corners of reality, where time and space convolute into impossible geometries. Its slumber is deep and filled with dreams of ancient chaos.

It is said that a strange place known as Ulthar, where no one may kill a cat, is especially sacred to the Thing with the Writhing Tail. The Thing with the Writhing Tail is not without its rivals, however. It seems utterly obsessed with one day consuming the {@creature Rat God|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}.

Since it goes by so many names, two warlocks who are both pactbound may not realize it at first, believing them to serve different beings. The Thing with the Writhing Tail seems to enjoy this state of affairs, even though it means its warlocks often act against one another. This may in fact be a strange way of weeding out the weak or seeking the most promising and talented warlock amongst its servants.

entries.name: Roleplaying Traits
entries: This cosmic entity's interactions are marked by caprice and whimsy.

items: {@b Personality Trait:} One moment, I might bestow affectionte purrs and nuzzles; the next, I display utter aloofness or sudden ire, swiping with claws of dark matter that rend the veil between sanity and madness.
{@b Ideal:} My actions are neither cruel nor kind. Mortals cannot know my unfathomable perspective, and that is why they will always be inferior.
{@b Bond:} I am endlessly entertained by the unpredictability of mortals; their fears, their surprises, and their schemes are like strings of yarn I cannot resist batting at with my cosmic paws.
{@b Flaw:} My boundless curiosity and the mere whim to explore the forbidden often lead me to stir chaos in realms both mortal and divine, sometimes unraveling threads better left untouched

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill History|XPHB} or {@skill Religion|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine the Thing with the Writhing Tail, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (20+) Eldritch Aberration
entries: You are aware of its {@sense Truesight|XPHB} and {@variantrule Telepathy|XPHB}, its {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}, and its Epic {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB}. You also know this eldritch entity is beyond life and death and can reform years later if killed.

entries.name: (25+) Fear and Madness
entries: You learn of its Purring Aura, as well as its spellcasting Epic Actions.

entries.name: (30+) Brilliant and Nimble
entries: You know the Thing with the Writhing Tail's highest and lowest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: In battle, the Thing with the Writhing Tail uses Manifest Duplicate to create numerous copies of itself. It teleports and swaps places with its duplicates as its rends its foes apart. The many duplicates vastly expand the range of its Purring Aura, sowing terror and madness in any who try to oppose them.

The Thing with the Writhing Tail may grow suddenly bored in the middle of combat, deciding to inexplicably flee or change tactics to a new fixation. Other times, it plays cat and mouse with its foes, toying with them like living balls of yarn.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Aberration.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Monster Blood.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Heart, Eyes.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Teeth, Claws.

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Fur.
I know one that holds his cat above all others. Putting that much faith into anything beyond yourself can only lead to problems.

name: Think Tank

entries: A severed head bobs gently aloft. The top of its scalp has been sawed off, exposing its pulsing brain, which is encased in a dome filled with bubbling, glowing liquid. A dozen thin mechanical arms emerge from its eye sockets. Around each delicate limb is coiled an elongated strand of the optic nerve, and upon the tip of each are curiously blinking human eyes of different sizes and colors. A haphazard bundle of tubes, hoses, and cables flows from its open neck along the still-attached spine, which connects via several sinewy strands to an array of fluid-filled glass tanks containing a throbbing heart, pounding lungs, and other nearly unrecognizable internal organs. Attached to the spine are spindly mechanical arms each ending in human hands.

Due to their dabbling in magical arts, many a maddened and maniacal apothecary has sought the secrets of elongating their life beyond anything deemed normal. Sometimes these studies do not begin with a malicious intent for greed or personal goals. Sometimes they are not targeted toward the apothecary at all, but a sick and dying loved one, the apothecary on the verge of finding the cure to save them; or a friend or colleague who is on their deathbed, whose research and assistance is the factor standing between a scientific breakthrough and absolute failure. It is in the desperate moments that apothecaries have pushed the boundaries of science and tested the limits on mortal physiology.

The Think Tank stands as a grotesque and hideous form of final desperation to an apothecary who has failed at all alternative options. Whether it be to keep a loved one alive, or an attempt to prolong the apothecary's own life, the Think Tank is a horrid and utterly dreadful procedure to endure, with no hope afterwards of being brought back to any resemblance of their former selves.

items: {@b Personality Trait:} Too many thoughts, all the time, my mind is free, uncontained!
{@b Bond:} I did what I had to! My mind was too valuable to let go to waste, I had to preserve it, to improve it!
{@b Ideal:} I avoided death to continue to pursue the vast unknown of my scientific study. My research will change the world, I just need more time!
{@b Flaw:} I cannot fathom the monster I have become, and to witness myself is a horror I cannot endure.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Medicine|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks to Study the Think Tank, learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (15+) Tear the Mind
entries: You recognize the Think Tank's Nightmare Aura.

entries.name: (20+) Gravity Control
entries: You know of the Think Tank's Unbind Gravity Epic {@variantrule Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: (25+) Protected Regenerator
entries: You learn of its Shield Generator and Life Support System traits and identifies its location.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Due to the nature of its Life Support System, the Think Tank is seldom encountered outside its lair, which is always a well-defended and secret location. The mastermind surrounds itself with powerful abominations, and protects its sanctum with traps, defensible locations, and escape routes. A Think Tank's lair may include elements that are outright hostile to living organisms, such as radiation, {@condition contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}, or deadly neurotoxin. As such, player characters encountering the Think Tank in combat must have already outmaneuvered it somehow to gain access to its innermost lair.

The Think Tank makes for a climatic encounter against a villainous foe. Before the player characters even get close to the Think Tank, it will have tested their abilities many times against its minions, using its telepathic eavesdropping to learn everything it can about them. The Think Tank knows when they are coming, how they are approaching, as well as their abilities, spells, equipment, and their expected tactics.

The Think Tank uses Unbind Gravity and Mind Cage to control the battlefield, while using Pluck the Puppet Strings to turn any remaining targets against its other foes. Its Telekinetic Grip can help it further control enemy positions while using Contaminated Blast to slowly contaminate them to death, picking on whoever has the most Contamination going into the encounter.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Monstrosity.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Contaminated Ichor, Chemical Solution.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Brain.

entries.name: Bones:
entries: Skull, Spine.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Tentacles.

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Plates.

name: Thomasin Ardor
entries: Thomasin Ardor is the village's most proficient tailor. As a child, she fell through a large pane of glass, but her life was saved with a critical medical procedure. This trauma, in conjunction with her quiet and cool disposition, leaves her the brunt of unfounded rumors and gossip.
She often keeps folks at a distance, and the only person in town she is close with is {@creature Randall Graham|CrookedMoon24} (see area V7), who stitched her up following her childhood accident.

While Thomasin is a benevolent member of the Followers of the Old Ways and reveres the Green Queen, {@creature Randall Graham|CrookedMoon24} is attempting to leverage their relationship to subtly guide her into joining the cult of the Crooked Queen. Whether she falls to wickedness or discovers Randall's plot and rebuffs him is up to you.
The temptation to aid a lost lamb should be tamped down when a thornlamm appears. Where there is one, there are many. And all lead back to a creature far more terrifying than any big, bad wolf.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: The sphere of annihilation a caprathorn leaves behind can be controlled and taken. At the start of each day there is a 2% chance the sphere disappears forever.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
items.entry: A caprathorn can detach a thornlamm to fight as its ally or consume one to heal.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
items.entry: The caprathorn can entomb a fallen foe and unleash a field of disintegrating force. This annihilation field recharges if a creature the caprathorn has entombed dies.

items.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}):
items.entry: When a caprathorn dies, it implodes into a sphere of annihilation, which pulls nearby creatures toward it.

name: Thrudgelmir Giant
entries: {@i Multiheaded Giant of Malice}

{@color Six distinct heads rise from the massive shoulders of this giant, which towers above its surroundings. Blue, runic tattoos adorn its exposed flesh, and it holds a black iron maul in each hand. It smashes the mauls together, releasing sparks of elemental energy as it prepares to attack.|006abe}

Millennia ago, a clan of giants in the far north discovered something alien in their endless realm of ice and snow. The exact nature of this object is not known, though some speculate it was a Hyperborean relic or perhaps a device from beyond the mortal plane. Whatever its origin, the strange item warped their minds and bodies, causing them to sprout additional heads and increasing their malevolence sixfold.

Thrudgelmir are intelligent and remorseless hunters that require substantial amounts of food to sustain their grotesque frames. Seldom do thrudgelmir giants gather in numbers, but when they do, the folk of the Northlands fear what may come of it.
{@i This raging cloud of animate mist and ice has icicle shards for eyes and claws.}

entries.name: Servants of the North Wind
entries: These fast-flying creatures of air and ice were created by the lord of the north wind, Boreas, to be his heralds, assassins, and hunting hounds. They appear as a swirling blizzard, often blending in with snowstorms to surprise their victims.

entries.name: Terrifying Blizzards
entries: Thuellai love to engulf creatures in their blizzards, to lash buildings with ice and cold, and to trigger avalanches with their whirlwinds. They thrive on destruction and fear, and they share their master's unpredictable nature.

entries.name: Immune to Steel
entries: Northerners especially fear the thuellai because of their resistance to mundane steel, their terrifying howls, and their ability to cause madness.

name: Thulsamir Wolfbrother
entries: Ruler of Wolfheim

name: Thunderbird
entries: Believed to be the product of an ancient Roc blessed or cursed by intense lightning energies, the thunderbird is both feared and revered by the denizens of the sky and the Rocborne. With intense grasp and control over various storm magics, the thunderbird claims vast swathes of the sky as its territory, especially areas like deserts that are prone to violent thunderstorms or monsoons.
{@i The giant's hair and beard are plaited with rings and other bits of decorative stone and metal, and it carries a large, rune-inscribed hammer.}

entries.name: Forge Masters
entries: Greedy and aggressively competitive, thursir dwell in vast caverns under frozen mountains where they labor to forge chains, armor, and massive engines of war. Smaller than many giants, thursir have a natural affinity for metalworking. Armor or weapons forged by a thursir giant are of the highest quality, and other giants often seek thursir smiths to outfit their people in times of strife.

entries.name: Enormous Appetites
entries: When not toiling at the forge, these giants entertain themselves with gluttonous feasts and boisterous wrestling competitions, or they raid human settlements for food and valuables.

entries.name: Divided Society
entries: Female thursir rarely leave thursir dwellings, tending the family and hearth and performing much of a community's labor, while male thursir spend their time crafting, metalworking, and going to war. However, female thursir have the most affinity for magic and make up the bulk of the thursir's priesthood and spellcasters. Priestesses hold especially high standing in thursir society and often operate as valued advisors to clan leadership or accompany the most powerful units of warriors into battle, tending wounds and boosting morale.

name: Thursir Giant
entries: {@i Canny Gluttonous Crafters}
{@color The giant's hair and beard are plaited with rings and other bits of decorative stone and metal, and it carries a large, rune-inscribed hammer.|006abe}

Greedy and aggressively competitive, thursir are smaller than most types of giants. They dwell in vast caverns under frozen mountains, where they labor to forge chains, armor, and massive engines of war. Items forged by a thursir are of the highest quality, and other giants often seek thursir smiths to outfit their people in times of strife.
When not toiling at the forge, these giants entertain themselves with gluttonous feasts and boisterous wrestling competitions, or they raid human settlements for food and valuables.

name: Thybolg Fredriksson
entries: Leader of Thor's temple

name: Thyrin the Black
entries: Leader of the Apostles of Inexorable Ruin

name: Tipsy
entries: Most fey on the Material Plane take abundant joy in the manipulation of mortals and instigation of drama, but the tipsy in particular delights in the chaos of drunken romance. These small, pastel-colored fey flutter around bars to cause mischief. The tipsy can use its subtle magic to encourage confession of true feelings and impulsive action, whether they are long-repressed or new temptations. Invisible to sober patrons, they whisper sweet nothings and bold encouragement as necessary, then watch the scene unfold. Softened by inebriation, individuals find themselves unwitting participants, unable to smother the truth any longer.
{@i This titanic green serpent raises its enormous head high, its body extending in seemingly endless coils.}

entries.name: Territorial and Aggressive
entries: Territorial and voracious, the rare titanoboa devours all trespassers in its domain. Stronger and faster than the giant anaconda, the true king of the rainforest is also more stubborn, fighting off entire groups of hunters and poachers. When stalking prey, these great serpents strike from ambush, swallowing even some dinosaurs in one bite.

entries.name: Blinding Scales
entries: Against groups of foes, titanoboas trust in their ability to dazzle their enemies with the light reflected from their scales, using this distraction to entwine the stunned foes in crushing coils.

entries.name: Slow to Mate
entries: Titanoboas mate rarely. They live for hundreds of years and never stop growing, which makes the need for propagation less urgent. When two titanoboas nest, the result is a brood of a half-dozen smaller snakes. An adult titanoboa is at least 80 feet long and weighs 6,000 pounds or more.

When a team of Korranberg scholars studied the region that is now Droaam, they concluded that the Horned King revered in the region was an interpretation of the Rak Tulkhesh, the Rage of War. They were mistaken. Both are spirits of war. But for Rak Tulkhesh, bloodshed and aggression are a goal in and of themselves. For Tol Kharash—the Horned King—war is just the means to an end. The Horned King is an overlord of tyranny and oppression, taking joy in the suffering of the conquered and the cruelty of the conquerors; he delights in mortals inflicting suffering on their own kin.

Tol Kharash can take any form, but his preferred avatar is that of a massive armored minotaur, flesh hidden beneath steel plates. Rusting, broken weapons are embedded in his armor, tokens of defeated foes. The Horned King crushes hopes, and those who see him must fight the urge to grovel or flee.

entries.name: Destroyer of Hope
entries: Tol Kharash drives the strong to oppress the weak. His essence is bound to the warped tower now known as Turakbar's Fist, and it seeps out into the surrounding lands. The minotaur clans of the region have been shaped by his power for countless generations, and the chib culture that flourished in the Barrens is a reflection of his influence. The efforts of the Daughters of Sora Kell have curbed his power in the region, but he cannot be driven from Turakbar's Fist. Around the Fist, the strong feel the urge to revel in their power, to prove their might and take what they desire—while people who are peaceful by nature find themselves more easily cowed, afraid to challenge aggression. Player characters can resist these passive effects. But when an adventurer is in a place where Kharash's influence is strong, the DM might occasionally ask them questions... Why do you let that wizard tell you what to do? Why do you let them laugh at you? Why don't you take what you deserve? Most likely, an adventurer will recognize these as the alien thoughts that they are... but the thoughts still linger, and provide a sense of the quiet corrupting power of Tol Kharash. People already driven to aggression—such as the minotaurs of the region, the Gaa'aram orcs and fiend-touched gnolls—can find these impulses especially hard to resist. However, unlike Rak Tulkhesh, the Horned King doesn't crave chaotic bloodshed. As people fall deeper under his sway they will be drawn to follow the strongest servant of Kharash. Thus, in the present day, both Rhesh Turakbar and Breggan Blackcrown have amassed a force of loyal, ruthless followers—all unwittingly being driven by the power of the Horned King, urged to serve the would-be conquerors.

entries.name: The Demonglass Horde
entries: Tol Kharash has relatively few fiendish minions. He has no immortal prakhutu, and no representatives among the Lords of Dust. What the Horned King does have is demonglass. Kharash himself is imprisoned in the demonglass tower of Turakbar's Fist. But many members of his fiendish host were trapped in smaller shards of demonglass. Some have been turned into tools or weapons, fiendish power fueling powerful enchantments. Most cultists of Tol Kharash have a small shard of demonglass embedded in their body, turning them into Demonglass Warriors. Demonglass Champions carry larger shards that grant greater powers, but over time the fiend in the shard eats away at the mortal within, turning them into a hollow one serving as a puppet for the fiend.

entries.name: The King's Prison
entries: Tol Kharash is bound by the Silver Flame, and he has no army of rakshasa studying the Draconic Prophecy and uncovering a path for his release. However, the nature of his prison gives him considerable power over the region around Turakbar's Fist even while he remains imprisoned—and there may be ways for him to increase that influence. The first obvious path is for servants that bear his demonglass shards to conquer in his name; the wider his dominion, the more power he gains. Beyond this, there are two paths that could allow Tol Kharash to walk the world. The first is to create a proper vessel—a mortal who can serve as his hollow one. He has planted his seeds in two mortals in the modern age: Rhesh Turakbar and Breggan Blackcrown. Tol Kharash needs these vessels to grow in power—both personal power and authority, becoming conquerors and embodying his ideals. It's up to the DM to decide exactly what steps would be involved in this, but it would definitely involve amassing a powerful army and conquering a region. Rhesh Turakbar would need to challenge the Daughters of Sora Kell, while Breggan would have to stake her claim as the descendant of Breggor Firstking and forge a new kingdom of the lost on the frontier. Beyond this, the vessel would have to embed more demonglass in their body, and undergo other rituals that would strengthen their flesh... but they could do this without knowing the deadly road they're on. Breggan could truly believe she's gaining the power she needs to challenge Droaam and Breland, not knowing she's becoming the anchor for an overlord. Ultimately, if one of these vessels follows the path, Tol Kharash would be able to manifest through them—creating an avatar with the statistics presented here. The mortal would still remain, and if that mortal died, the avatar would be destroyed. A second way Tol Kharash could be freed would be if the region itself was pulled deeper into his prison. By planting demonglass anchors in critical locations and performing the proper rituals, a piece of Droaam could be drawn into Khyber... allowing fiends to manifest freely, and Tol Kharash himself to rise from Turakbar's Fist. Once this had been completed, there would be no simple way to reverse it; it would take something as dramatic as Tira Miron's sacrifice to channel the Silver Flame to undo this damage. With either of these plots, Rhesh Turakbar would be a willing pawn who seeks to unleash the Horned King upon the world—while Breggan Blackcrown doesn't realize that she's a pawn in an overlord's schemes, and believes her ambitions are hers alone.
{@i An enormous bronze and iron statue filled with fire towers above the ring of chanting, frenzied worshipers.}

Worshipers of fire gods use tophets to incinerate sacrifices in their flaming maws. A tophet has a large opening in the front where the flames can be seen; sometimes this is an enormous mouth, and at other times it is a large hole in the tophet's belly. Horns and expressions of anger or wide‑mouthed laughter are common.

entries.name: Eager for Sacrifices
entries: Among fire cultists, it's widely known that when a tophet's hands are raised above its mouth, it is demanding a sacrifice to roll down its palms and into its fiery maw.

entries.name: Heed Musical Commands
entries: Flutes and drums can be used to control the actions of a tophet during sacrifices. They have the fortunate side effect of drowning out the cries and screams of living sacrifices.

entries.name: Magical Fires
entries: The fires within a tophet's bronze body are largely magical and fueled by sacrifices. They don't require more than a symbolic amount of wood or coal to keep burning, but they do require sacrifices of food, cloth, and living creatures to keep them under control. A tophet that is not granted a sacrifice when it demands one might go on a fiery rampage, burning down buildings, granaries, or barns until its hunger is satisfied.
Torcheaters are small batlike creatures that feed on fire, swooping down to douse torches and campfires.

{@i This humanoid wasp's gossamer wings beat out a soft, droning buzz. Flashing blades sing in each of her four clawed hands, and the air around her shimmers with magical dust. Dozens more humanoid wasps in a variety of iridescent colors surround her, weapons raised protectively}.

The tosculi are waspfolk that share the Golden Song of the hive, which unites them under the command of their queen. Each hive has its own song, and most tosculi hives are predatory, dangerous places.

entries.name: Bow Raiders
entries: Tosculi elite bow raiders are smarter and more capable than drones and common warriors, with midnight black or deep green carapaces that shine with colorful iridescence. Their wings are blood red streaked with dark crimson veins. As rare and prized members of the hive, a bow raider's life is never thrown away or risked unnecessarily. Seldom does a tosculi warband contain more than a handful of these elite soldiers, and they frequently hold positions of command. Elite bow raiders always lead the honor guard for their queen, both within the hive and on those rare occasions when the queen ventures outside.

entries.name: Drones
entries: Tosculi drones are the workers of the tosculi hive: the smallest, weakest, least intelligent, and most abundant of the waspfolk. Their carapaces are mostly iridescent blue with gold abdomens and lower legs, and they have vestigial wings, allowing them to glide but not truly fly. Drones function primarily as menial workers but, during times of war, they also act as highly expendable scouts and soldiers. Because the warriors know whatever a drone knows—thanks to the queen—a drone doesn't need to survive its scouting mission to deliver useful information.

entries.name: Warriors
entries: Tosculi warriors are overseers of work crews and battle groups of drones, directing activities and relaying commands. Though subservient to the queen's orders, they are capable of acting independently or following their own best judgment, if necessary. The warriors' most important role in the hive is procuring live hosts for incubating tosculi eggs. Creatures paralyzed by warriors are brought to the queen's chamber to have eggs implanted in them, and after a few weeks, the larva hatches, devouring its still-living host.

entries.name: Hive Queen
entries: The hive queen is the nerve center of a tosculi hive-city, simultaneously one of a hive's greatest strengths and weaknesses. The queen serves as a unifying force. She binds her swarm with an ironclad sense of purpose through a psychic web, known as the Golden Song, that links all tosculi within a hive. When the hive queen nears the end of her life, she selects the most promising of her immature heirs and feeds the heir a special concoction. This speeds the heir's maturation and makes her ready to become a full-fledged hive queen. The daughter's first action upon her metamorphosis is to devour her mother and all her sisters, absorbing and becoming the emitter of that hive's song. If a hive queen dies with no heir to anchor the hive mind or if the daughter's accession is disrupted, the hive-city plunges into chaos. Tosculi bereft of the hive-mind go berserk. A few fortunate ones might escape and become lone renegades, but their existence without the comforting presence of the hive is miserable and short. Unless one of the hive-queen's surviving daughters is mature enough and ruthless enough to step in and assert control, the hive is doomed.

If a hive queen dies with no heir to anchor the hive mind or if the daughter's accession is disrupted, the hive-city plunges into chaos. Tosculi bereft of the hive-mind go berserk. A few fortunate ones might escape and become lone renegades, but their existence without the comforting presence of the hive is miserable and short. Unless one of the hive-queen's surviving daughters is mature enough and ruthless enough to step in and assert control, the hive is doomed.

{@i This humanoid wasp's gossamer wings beat out a soft, droning buzz. Flashing blades sing in each of her four clawed hands, and the air around her shimmers with magical dust. Dozens more humanoid wasps in a variety of iridescent colors surround her, weapons raised protectively}.

The tosculi are waspfolk that share the Golden Song of the hive, which unites them under the command of their queen. Each hive has its own song, and most tosculi hives are predatory, dangerous places.

entries.name: Bow Raiders
entries: Tosculi elite bow raiders are smarter and more capable than drones and common warriors, with midnight black or deep green carapaces that shine with colorful iridescence. Their wings are blood red streaked with dark crimson veins. As rare and prized members of the hive, a bow raider's life is never thrown away or risked unnecessarily. Seldom does a tosculi warband contain more than a handful of these elite soldiers, and they frequently hold positions of command. Elite bow raiders always lead the honor guard for their queen, both within the hive and on those rare occasions when the queen ventures outside.

entries.name: Drones
entries: Tosculi drones are the workers of the tosculi hive: the smallest, weakest, least intelligent, and most abundant of the waspfolk. Their carapaces are mostly iridescent blue with gold abdomens and lower legs, and they have vestigial wings, allowing them to glide but not truly fly. Drones function primarily as menial workers but, during times of war, they also act as highly expendable scouts and soldiers. Because the warriors know whatever a drone knows—thanks to the queen—a drone doesn't need to survive its scouting mission to deliver useful information.

entries.name: Warriors
entries: Tosculi warriors are overseers of work crews and battle groups of drones, directing activities and relaying commands. Though subservient to the queen's orders, they are capable of acting independently or following their own best judgment, if necessary. The warriors' most important role in the hive is procuring live hosts for incubating tosculi eggs. Creatures paralyzed by warriors are brought to the queen's chamber to have eggs implanted in them, and after a few weeks, the larva hatches, devouring its still-living host.

entries.name: Hive Queen
entries: The hive queen is the nerve center of a tosculi hive-city, simultaneously one of a hive's greatest strengths and weaknesses. The queen serves as a unifying force. She binds her swarm with an ironclad sense of purpose through a psychic web, known as the Golden Song, that links all tosculi within a hive. When the hive queen nears the end of her life, she selects the most promising of her immature heirs and feeds the heir a special concoction. This speeds the heir's maturation and makes her ready to become a full-fledged hive queen. The daughter's first action upon her metamorphosis is to devour her mother and all her sisters, absorbing and becoming the emitter of that hive's song. If a hive queen dies with no heir to anchor the hive mind or if the daughter's accession is disrupted, the hive-city plunges into chaos. Tosculi bereft of the hive-mind go berserk. A few fortunate ones might escape and become lone renegades, but their existence without the comforting presence of the hive is miserable and short. Unless one of the hive-queen's surviving daughters is mature enough and ruthless enough to step in and assert control, the hive is doomed.

entries.name: A Tosculi Hive Queen's Lair
entries: Hive queens make their lairs deep within the most protected part of the hive. Dozens of corridors lead to her lair, allowing the hive's tosculi to reach their queen at a moment's notice should she need it. This is also the place where tosculi eggs hatch, making it a critical location for the survival of the hive. When encountered in her lair, the tosculi hive queen has a challenge rating of 13 (10,000 XP).
