entries: This is the stat block of the {@creature berserker}, adjusted with {@race vulpin|HumblewoodCampaignSetting} traits.

name: Vulpin Captain
entries: Captains are respected among the bandit forces, leading units on raids and ambushes, and sometimes running the operations of an entire camp. While captains are among the more skilled warriors in the coalition, involvement with day-to-day operations grants them a certain rapport with even the low-ranking bandits. This leadership, coupled with their prowess, allows them to rally or kowtow those foolish enough to consider desertion. Vulpins, with their natural ambition, cunning, and force of personality, can readily be found climbing to the rank of captain.
This is the stat block of the {@creature cult fanatic}, adjusted with {@race vulpin|HumblewoodCampaignSetting} traits.

As the elite spellcasters of the Devotees of {@deity Kren|Amaranthine|HumblewoodCampaignSetting}, these Gloomweavers are masters of shadow conjuration and baleful illusions. They hail from a land across the sea, where the leader of their sect supposedly lives.

Gloomweavers fight fearlessly, for they have given themselves fully to {@deity Kren|Amaranthine|HumblewoodCampaignSetting|Kren's} power and are convinced that they will be reborn at her side when they die.

This nightmare is conjured from Arrevis' shame and guilt at what he had become during his time working for the devotees of {@deity Kren|Amaranthine|HumblewoodCampaignSetting}. It is a devilish, vulpin-like creature with curved horns sprouting from its brow, and dark feathered arms with talons like a raptor. Should Arrevis fight it, it takes every opportunity to taunt him, calling him a fool for ever thinking he could ever be redeemed.

name: Vulpin Noble
entries: Although founded by birdfolk, Alderheart is home to several noble families of influential humblefolk. Among them are vulpins, who find both their charms and wiles perfectly suited to the political intrigue of Alderheart's high society. Some vulpin nobles can trace their lineage back to ancient royalty.

name: Vulpin Priest of Kren
entries: Priests of the Amaranthine Kren tend shrines in her honor, and share stories of her guile and cunning with visitors. These tales emphasize humility, wariness, and teach listeners to keep their wits about them at all times. In rare cases, these priests are given divine gifts by their Amaranthine. Conferred a portion of Kren's supernatural slyness, they often seek to humble those who have grown too proud.
This is the stat block of the {@creature spy}, adjusted with {@race vulpin|HumblewoodCampaignSetting} traits.

name: Wakewyrm
entries: Wakewyrms are massive reptiles that have aspects of both snakes and eels. On rare occasions they've been spotted close to the shores of the Talongrip Coast, though many are quick to dismiss these accounts. Their name originates from the powerful tidal waves their bodies cause, which pose a considerable threat to nearby vessels.

entries.name: Ocean Tales
entries: Despite their size, wakewyrms are elusive, able to hide within the vast expanse of the ocean. The rarity of this creature has bred many rumors about the exact nature of wakewyrms. All sailors know at least a few stories about bizarre creatures of the sea, including fantastical accounts of wakewyrms that lurk in the ocean's gloomy depths, able to sink an entire fleet of ships. Such tales are more often fabrications than not, as few have actually encountered these creatures.

entries.name: Devourer from the Deeps
entries: Wakewyrms are more than a 100 feet long and weigh over 1000 tons. Their lashing tails, snapping jaws, and huge bodies can deal significant damage to a ship's hull, though they prefer to swallow sailors whole, swiftly pulling them into the fathoms below with hardly more than a splash. Filling their gullet with as many creatures as possible, wakewyrms let their strong stomachs take care of their meals. While a fine tactic for devouring fish or other large marine creatures, wakewyrms that swallow adventurers whole sometimes find the snack too much to handle.

Though wakewyrms rarely encounter sailing vessels as they cross the ocean looking for food, the results are often violent. Afterwards, all that remains is nothing but a derelict phantom ship, found wrecked against the rocks of distant shores.

name: Walden Krane, Magistrate of Winnowing Reach
entries: A fastidious, easily agitated, middle-aged kindled corvum with drab black feathers. As the Magistrate of Winnowing Reach, he is a prominent political figure in the region. Walden isn't a particularly good or kind man, but he tries to be a reasonable and honorable one. He will not break his bargains, and likewise won't tolerate anything on the party's part which could be conceived as oath-breaking, dishonesty, or actions that might bring harm to the Reach. He cares deeply for his citizens, but that sometimes fails to come across as his political ambitions tend to get in the way. Walden has known Kenna Brightspark since she was but a fledgeling. Walden uses the {@creature noble} stat block, adjusted with the racial traits of a kindled corvum. He is lawful neutral.

Contaminated Elementals can be found all over Drakkenheim, often in areas where the eldritch magics are especially concentrated. Many who have encountered these elementals have spoken of the city itself coming to life to attack them. Reports of ruins reaching out and crushing adventurers, burning flames moving and hunting with minds of their own, or contaminated pools lurching to engulf passersby have been heard. Even the blowing air itself has mustered parts of the Haze into shifting clouds that stalk adventurers through the streets. These magical creatures are a constant reminder that nothing in the city can be trusted, and that nowhere is truly safe.

name: Walking Delerium Geode

entries: A rich outcrop of {@item crystal|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium crystals} glimmer from the collapsed ruin nearby. As you approach, the debris begins to shift and move. A hunched, bulking form, one vaguely humanoid, rises up with a chorus of crystalline clinks and grinding rock. The central mass of stone and crystal is supported by two short, stubbly legs of rubble, its arms and shoulders shaped from large boulders of brick and wood that end in balled fists bristling with delerium spikes. Its head, an elongated crystal, is marked by angles and fractures that gradually form into a sorrowful face.

More than once has an inattentive prospector confused a rich delerium deposit with a Walking Delerium Geode, only to end up as a red smear on the streets of Drakkenheim. These Contaminated Earth Elementals are found throughout the ruins, and are frustratingly common near especially large deposits of the valuable crystals.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they {@action Study|XPHB} a Walking Delerium Geode, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (10+) Dense Delerium
entries: You are aware of the elemental's {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: (15+) Pummeled Contamination
entries: Unsurprisingly, hits from this elemental's fists cause {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}.

entries.name: (20+) Deadly Destruction
entries: You learn of the creature's Death Burst trait, as well as its strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Walking Delerium Geode rests in wait unless disturbed by someone trying to harvest its {@item crystal|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium crystals}. Once awoken, it hammers targets with its Shard Slam.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Elemental.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Contaminated Ichor.

entries.name: Dust:
entries: Elemental Dust.

entries.name: Delerium:
entries: True to its name and nature, characters may be able to collect delerium from the remains of the Walking Delerium Geode, though its destruction tends to cause many crystals to shatter and break.

Roll {@dice 1d20} to determine what the characters can find: 1—nothing remains but broken splinters and ash; 2–9: {@dice 4d6} {@item chip|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium chips}; 10–12: {@dice 3d10} {@item fragment|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium fragments}; 13–16: {@dice 2d6} {@item shard|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium shards}; 17–19: {@dice 1d4} {@item crystal|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium crystals}; 20: 1 {@item geode|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium geode}.
These gargoyles defend the walls of Drakkenheim.

name: Wall Gargoyle

entries: These winged creatures resemble fiendish bats, often with grotesque exaggerated grinning or snarling faces. They are made completely of stone and remain motionless, but you swear that one is looking at you—and it was looking the other way just a moment ago, wasn't it?

These gargoyles defend the walls of Drakkenheim. When the walls were constructed, the gargoyles were placed every 50 feet along the entire perimeter of the walls. Using the combined craftsmanship of the dwarven stonework as well as magic from the Amethyst Academy, the gargoyles were designed as a defensive measure if the city were ever attacked. Any attempt to scale the walls of the city would see the creatures animate and defend the city at all costs. However, the Haze seeping into their magically imbued bodies has caused their arcane programming to falter, and now the creatures attack anyone who attempts to pass the walls of the city. They no longer differentiate friend from foe, and are always set to defend their territory to the death.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill History|XPHB} or any kind of {@item artisan's tools|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine a Wall Gargoyle, learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (5+) Resistant Form
entries: You know the creature's {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: (10+) Ceaseless Pursuit
entries: You learn of the creature's Faultless
Tracker trait.

entries.name: (15+) Simple-Minded Construct
entries: You are aware of the creatures highest and lowest ability scores.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Wall Gargoyles are found only along the city walls. They animate and attack characters who dare attempt any of the following: {@variantrule Climbing|XPHB} more than halfway up the walls or towers, flying within one hundred fifty feet of the city walls horizontally, or over them at any height, or lingering on the walls or towers for more than ten minutes.

The gargoyles attack directly, viciously, and without remorse. If they reduce their quarry to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, they spend their next turn tearing apart the creature's body before moving on to another target. The gargoyles pursue their quarry into the city to any distance until they or their quarry are destroyed, but give up pursuing characters more than three hundred feet outside the city walls.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Elemental.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Elemental Fluid.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Teeth, Claws.

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Plates.

entries.name: Dust:
entries: Elemental Dust

name: Walter Jenkin
entries: A handsome and affable sort, Walter Jenkin, lost his voice within weeks of arriving. No healer could explain the sudden silence. Now, he communicates through writing and sign language, which his family also knows and can translate. Entering the manor makes him nervous, sensing its malice, though he never speaks of his fears.

Known for his loyalty and dutifulness, Walter has an almost reverent respect for {@creature Wendel Somerton|CrookedMoon24|Mayor Wendel Somerton} and his other former employers. And in this new position, he has already become devoted to the Druskenvalds, despite having only just met them.

{@i A raven-haired young woman rises to the surface of the water as she swims, singing softly to herself. Her lower body is revealed to be that of a mountain lion, and her sweet song suddenly turns to a yowl of rage.}
Wampus cats are all born from an ancient shaman's curse. Trollkin, orc, goblin, and human shamans alike all claim to be able to transform those who practice forbidden magic into wampus cats.

entries.name: Forest Streams
entries: The wampus cat stalks the shores of woodland waterways, using her magic to disguise her true form and lure unsuspecting victims to the water's edge. She is particularly fond of attacking bathers or those pulling water from a stream.

entries.name: Hatred of the Holy
entries: While she prefers to feast on intelligent male humanoids, she holds special animosity toward holy men of any kind. Unless near starvation or if provoked, however, she will not kill women. Indeed, a wampus cat may strike up a temporary friendship with any woman who is having difficulties with men, though these friendships typically last only as long as their mutual enemies live. Some witches are said to gain their trust and keep them as companions.

entries.name: Swamp Team Ups
entries: Will-o'-wisps and miremals enjoy working in tandem with wampus cats; the wisps alter their light to mimic the flicker of a torch or candle and illuminate the disguised cat, the better to lure in victims, then assist the cat in the ensuing battle. Miremals use a tall story to lure travelers into a swamp when the hour grows late, then abandon them.

name: Wandering Door
entries: Only a handful of people on Obojima have seen the enchanted moving doorway. Every now and then, a ranger spots a wandering door while deep in the forest or a postal knight sees one running across the Gale Fields. Since no one has got close enough to a door to give a solid description, there's a good deal of speculation around if there is only one door or if there are multiple doors. To this day, no one really knows who enchanted these doors and no one has been able to catch one to study it.
{@i A beautifully manicured garden pond sits before you, complete with a white marble bench. The surface of its crystal‑blue water ripples gently, which seems odd, because there is no wind.}
Wandering ponds are a curious variety of ooze that possess a modicum of fey magic.

entries.name: Fairy Made
entries: Wandering ponds are suspected of having originated in the fey realms where schemes to trap and humiliate wanderers are widespread pastimes. Certainly, the pond's unique ability to weave a glamour over itself indicates these creatures are no ordinary ooze.

entries.name: Mysterious Motives
entries: Wandering ponds always operate in the same way. A pond disguises itself to attract prey and then pulls them in. Once unconscious, the victim is teleported to a random body of water within the area. It is unclear what benefit the pond receives from such a scheme, but it is regarded as further evidence of fey involvement.

name: Wandslinger
entries: A flamboyant duelist with a sharp tongue, this wandslinger is always ready for the next challenger. They could be a wand for hire traveling from town to town. They might be a colorful caravan guard, or an equally colorful brigand preying on caravans.
{@i The large, flightless bird dove in and out of battle, screeching defiantly as its rider drove a spear into its foes.}

In the wild, war ostriches are dangerous and skittish, prone to lashing out with punishing kicks while sprinting around the battlefield. Humanoids in grasslands use them to create chaos by driving a flock of fast-moving war ostriches into a caravan or enemy troop formations.

entries.name: Faster than Horses
entries: War ostriches have been domesticated for centuries. They are a fearsome sight on the field of combat when bearing warriors into battle. War ostriches are heavily employed in regions where horses are rare or impractical or where their leaping ability enables cavalry to charge over broken ground. Stubborn and willful, these creatures are difficult to train. Once trained though, they are loyal and fierce mounts, fighting to the death in battle alongside their riders.

entries.name: War Ostriches in Midgard
entries: War ostriches are commonly found throughout the Southlands both as wild and domestic animals. The people of Nuria Natal, in particular, use war ostriches as beasts of burden and mounts along the River Nuria, switching to camels for long treks across the Crescent or Sarklan Deserts. Further south, gnolls and nkosi both hunt and domesticate war ostriches, and many warriors decorate their armor, clothing, or hair with the feathers of favored mounts who helped the warrior achieve greatness in battle.
Once we have all the shiny, the Rat God will come and help us! We'll get food! We will eat! Lots of food! All the food! We will eat the whole world! All the earth! Yes yes yes!

Many ratlings worship a fiendish entity they call the Rat God. They construct crude effigies to the Rat God, who whispers to the most cunning and intelligent ratlings, granting them magic through eldritch pacts. Ratlings understand surprisingly little about the Rat God, and make up stories and fables about the Rat God's exploits.

name: Warlock of the Rat God

entries: A small ratling cloaked in old rags carries a bone wand in one claw and a skull set with {@item shard|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium shards} in the other. An eldritch glow crackles in the ratling's eyes beneath its drawn hood as it incants a spell. Pulsing energy thrums in its small, clawed, hands.
Once we have all the shiny, the Rat God will come and help us! We'll get food! We will eat! Lots of food! All the food! We will eat the whole world! All the earth! Yes, yes, yes!

Arare few ratlings possess magical powers, which they claim are gifts from the Rat God. Whether their magic truly comes from an otherworldly pact or is just a product of their contaminated mutations is unknown. Indeed, Warlocks of the Rat God will lie or embellish any whisperings or insight they have to convince other ratlings they speak directly to the great Rat God. They make robes out of rags, while carying gnawed bone wands, occult trinkets, bone effigies, skulls, and scrawled drawings. The Rat God's warlocks often whisper to themselves and take notes that only they comprehend.

Most ratlings fear and obey these warlocks. Warlocks seldom share their power with others, making it rare for a colony to have more than one, unless they are underlings of a more powerful spellcaster. Often, the warlock will hand-pick the fiercest {@creature Giant Ratling|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} to serve as a bodyguard, or keep a veteran {@creature Ratling Guttersnipe|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} as a personal assassin to remove potential rivals.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Religion|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks to {@action Study|XPHB} a Warlock of the Rat God, learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (5+) Otherworldly Pact
entries: You are aware these creatures have an excellent sense of smell, {@sense Darkvision|XPHB}, are capable climbers and swimmers and this ratling's damage {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}.

entries.name: (10+) Potent Spellcasting
entries: You learn of the ratling's Balefire and Conjure Swarms actions.

entries.name: (15+) Commanding but Frail
entries: You know the ratling's strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: A Warlock of the Rat God does everything in its power to put "lesser" ratlings between it and its enemies. They deem themselves far too valuable to be put in harm's way, but are also inherently overconfident in their powers, convinced the Rat God protects them from harm.

A Warlock of the Rat God will have likely cast {@spell Mage Armor|XPHB} on itself prior to rolling {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, as most keep this spell active when venturing out of their burrow, or at the first sign of danger. They conjure a Swarm of Rats to pester their enemies, and use Balefire to pummel their foes. When their defenses are exhausted they cast {@spell Invisibility|XPHB} on themselves and attempt to flee using {@spell Teleport|XPHB}.

name: Warp Marauder

entries: The creature has a lupine body composed of swirling energy that constantly shifts and changes, creating a visual effect that is disorienting and dizzying upon its sharp fine fur. The energy appears to be a mix of different colors and patterns, as if it is drawing on the chaotic magic of the Space Between Worlds. The beast has eight legs and no visible eyes or mouth, but in place of a head or tail, a mass of tentacles emerge from its body. The tentacles extend to great lengths, and along its back its spine splits open revealing a great maw of jagged bone and teeth that gives way to a temporal rift in space and time.

The Warp Marauder is a fearsome predator that lurks within the Space Between Worlds, preying on unsuspecting travelers who stumble into this realm. It is a creature with a body composed of swirling energy and tentacles, able to move freely between dimensions, planes, and realities.

A creature of pure instinct, driven solely by the desire to hunt and feed, these skilled hunters use their ability to navigate between dimensions to stalk prey before launching a surprise attack, and often preys on creatures that wander along Thin Places near the Space Between Worlds, drawing them into its own dimension where it can feast on their life force.

A Warp Marauder can detect dimensional portals and Thin Places, and will often wait near them for creatures to pass through before pouncing. Its tentacles are incredibly strong, able to crush bones and rend flesh with ease. It can also release blasts of eldritch energy, which can tear through matter and energy alike.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill History|XPHB} or {@skill Nature|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine a Warp Marauder, learning the following based on the result.

entries.name: (10+) Mentally Tough
entries: You learn the creature's {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: (15+) Reality Distortion
entries: You are aware of the creature's Swirling Color Field trait.

entries.name: (20+) Strong and Nimble
entries: You know the creature's highest and lowest ability scores.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Warp Marauder has control over the reality around it. It grabs creatures and drags them into extraplanar realities where it feeds on them. The lupine alien isn't afraid to be hit, relying on its ability to alter time and space from an incoming attack, directing an essence of chaotic circumstance back towards the creature.
Warp Marauders flee if they are reduced below half their {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

Nimble creatures that dodge without movement. Just plant your feet, dont end up in the gullet and you'll be fine.

These ethereal phantoms haunt the places where they died, grasping for any memory of their former identities. Their mental anguish breaks the minds of those who hear their wails, and they induce rapid mutations when they possess humanoid bodies.

name: Warp Witch

entries: A lone figure draped in ethereal robes listlessly glides through the air, clutching a wrought iron lantern that glows in eldritch hues and green flames. A tattered hood conceals its face, but as you approach, they draw back their hood to reveal furious eyes and a hateful glare. Their mouth stretches unnaturally as they unleash an ear-piercing scream.

The Faith of the Sacred Flame says the souls of the departed gently pass from the Mortal World into the Shadowlands, where they wander until they find their final fate. Although their ultimate destination is a mystery, it is well understood that the Shadowlands are a dark reflection of the Material Plane. As such, occasionally wayward spirits slip back into the Mortal World near the places they died, where they typically manifest as incorporeal undead such as ghosts and wraiths.

However, the eldritch energies of the Haze weaken and disrupt the metaphysical fabrics that separate the planes. This wild magic conjures extraplanar energies and creatures into the ruins and has a particularly insidious interaction with the Shadowlands. The forces that draw the souls of the dead into the Material Plane are greatly magnified. Worse, the eldritch contamination corrupts the soul, fragments the mind, and distorts personalities, transforming these spirits into Warp Witches. Grasping for any memory of their former identities, the vengeful spirits of those whose lives were stolen by the Haze haunt the ruins of Drakkenheim. Their hatred and envy for the living manifests in a powerful compulsion to transform others into monsters.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Arcana|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Religion|XPHB}) checks to {@action Study|XPHB} a Warp Witch, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (5+) Resistant Undead
entries: You learn of the Warp Witch's {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: (10+) Mutative Control
entries: You recongize the creature's {@variantrule Possession|XPHB} action and Mutate Host {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, but not the means to end the possession.

entries.name: (15+) Escaping Possession
entries: You are aware that the Warp Witch's {@variantrule Possession|XPHB} can be ended by reducing the possessed body to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, or by casting {@spell Dispel Evil and Good|XPHB}.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: A Warp Witch begins combat by using its Psychic Scream. The witch then selects a target amongst their foes to possess.

While possessing a host, the Warp Witch will try to use the body to deceive or trick allies of its host into not attacking or harming them, trying to suggest useless, ineffective, and halfmad courses of action to "help" the host "drive out" the spirit, such whistling, dancing, clapping, singing, drawing pictures, and other bizarre commands. Meanwhile, the witch continues to use Mutate Host to contaminate them. The Warp Witch leaves the host after they undergo a Monstrous Transformation, and then moves to repeat the process with another.

entries.name: {@book Watchers of the Faithful|GrimHollowCG24|13|Watchers of the Faithful}

entries: Though the gods no longer grace the heavens, the Arch Seraphs still guide the way.

Born in the fires of the Gods' End, the Watchers of the Faithful rose to prominence first in Castinella as part of its theocratic government. Priests, paladins, chaplains, and other clergy rallied to the remaining Arch Seraphs to hold the fabric of society together. Throwing their faith behind the Arch Seraphs, the major churches reformed into a large organization dedicated to preserving the old faiths in a new form.

This young faction is utterly devoted to Sagrado Valieda's Eternal Dogma: revere the Arch Seraphs, follow their laws as handed down by the Divine Speaker, and destroy all that is unholy and evil in their sight through any means necessary. Where the Arcanist Inquisition is militant in rooting out corruption, the Watchers instead pursue Valieda's mandate to fight for the Arch Seraphs with fiery words. Swords are well and good in defense of the faith, but the real battle is in the hearts and minds of the faithful.

Through preaching and persuasion, the Watchers seek to make the change in the world that they believe the Arch Seraphs desire. Edicts declaring heresy inflame the Inquisition to hunt for monsters or tainted spellcasters. A public proclamation that a government is straying from the true path causes citizens to rise up and force change. Decrees are issued creating new ecclesiastical rules that the faithful embrace over secular laws issued by less religious rulers. Slowly but surely, the Watchers guide the world to a better place.

entries.name: Agents
entries: The Watchers of the Faithful are not soldiers. While they may have some have martial training, their members are priests, spies, and evangelists. Watchers fight with words and not blades. They spur faithful populations to turn against those they deem heretical. They are not single heroes, but rather the voice behind the zealous mob. The most common missionaries are Watchful Priests who combine divine spells with an almost magical command of oratory to enflame crowds.

name: Watchwood Tree
entries: Appearing as one of the island's many deciduous trees, the watchwood is known for terrorizing small settlements and villages throughout the Gift of Shuritashi. Their presence alone is enough to stop trade and travel to a location, which is why skilled woodcutters are often employed all over the island. Though watchwood trees can be dangerous, they're more of a threat during the warmer seasons, as they're easily spotted during the winter, when they're the only tree with leaves still on it.
{@i The frog-headed, legless creature with wide, batlike wings opens its gaping maw and shrieks. Its long, sinuous tail whips around it, tipped in a barb dripping with poison.}

entries.name: Gliding Wings
entries: The creature has no legs or arms, but it sports a pair of wide, membranous wings. It uses its wings to glide beneath the water and to soar through the air.

entries.name: Scourge of Waterways
entries: Water leapers plague fresh lakes and rivers. They prey on animals that come to the water's edge to drink, as well as on fishermen that ply their trade in the water leaper's territory. Stories circulate among fishers of waterways known for broken lines and missing bait. Fishers give these areas a wide berth for fear of water leapers. Desperate or unwary fishers who ignore the warnings are never seen again; drifting, empty boats are the signs of their passing.

name: Wayward Haint

entries: {@i Lost Soul Bound to Regret}

Wayward haints are restless spirits stuck between the realms of the living and the dead. Be it a curse or an unresolved conflict from their previous life, a haint can't rest until their unfinished business is resolved.

Haints only show hints of who they were in life, taking on a more symbolic form related to the hurt or loss they can't let go of. They tend to repeat their monotonous actions—often imitating those performed in life or reenacting their sorrow—over and over for eternity. When provoked, they can display a volatile temper and lash out with a crushing wave of the grief and indecision that binds their spirit.

entries.name: Secret
entries: Wayward haints can be trapped in empty bottles if they're tricked or forced to pass over one.

name: Weasel Hag

entries: {@i Hag of Soul Twisting and Terror}

Covetous and bedecked in stolen and gifted teeth, weasel hags are Fey creatures that sow nightmares and temptation to wickedness. They often surround themselves with weasels and boogleswarms, using them as spies, thieves to steal trinkets (especially lost teeth), and to spread their malign influence.

entries.name: Secret
entries: Weasel hags' love of teeth goes beyond a mere quirk. They can't refuse a tooth willingly given by its owner and can't harm the owner for a time.

The Weeper is a carnivorous, living plant, a very dangerous foe, and it and the wood share an odd intimacy—when it awakens, so does the wood and many of the terrors growing in it, and some of those terrors act as its eyes and ears—and claws, and teeth. The Weeper emits a peculiar, maddening song throughout the wood, which {@i awakens} and draws any animal or beasts (and occasionally monsters) to it to feed or protect it. Some that try to resist the call are taken by madness.

entries.name: The Weeper's Mad Song
entries: When it awakens, the Weeper cries out a maddening cacophony that is part song, part fluting pipes, part screams, and part sob. This sound echoes across the wood and continues until it sleeps once again or dies. The sound can be blocked in the usual ways, but any beast (and occasionally monster) that hears it spontaneously awakens and is drawn to it. Sometimes creatures become confused or enraged by the song, but more often than not, they simply move meekly to the Great Midden to be devoured. The thorny edges of the wood also awaken after a fashion—entwining to form a prickly outer wall. Trees and plants awaken across the wood, too, but they are slow to wake and not generally coordinated enough to attack. They typically simply try to trick outsiders into getting lost and dying.

The deadening nature of the wood makes tracing the source of the noise difficult, but clever PCs may seek to use this as a means of guiding themselves to The Weeper with an animal. Such animals move at the fastest pace they can but may themselves get lost or confused on the way. Any animal guide must succeed on a DC 7 Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check when it enters a hex for the first time or become lost. Lost animals move randomly into another hex but are always eventually drawn to the Weeper's song again.
Animal companions and familiars are not affected by this awakening but are aware of something odd in the air and likely show signs of nervousness as a result.
{@i This twisted tree's face is made of cracked, black bark knotted into vaguely humanoid features, and thick tears of sap run down its face.}
Weeping treants clearly are related to other treants, but they are smaller than the normal variety. Their gnarled trunks are twisted, and their wood often groans when they move.

entries.name: Forest Wardens
entries: Weeping treants are protectors of dark, shadowy forests—particularly forests in the Plane of Shadow—and they are as long-lived as the trees themselves. They act as guardians for an entire forest or for something specific within the forest, and they have no pity for those carrying axes or fire.

entries.name: Skeptical Mein
entries: Weeping treants are terrifying and relentless when fighting in defense of their charge. They are inherently distrustful, particularly of anything not of the natural or shadow world, and they're notoriously difficult to fool or deceive.

entries.name: Enchanted Bitter Tears
entries: Sages and scholars debate why these creatures weep, but no one has come forward with a compelling reason beyond "it's what trees do." The weeping treants themselves refuse to speak on the matter. Their tears are occasionally components in druidic spells or items.

name: Weeping Willow
entries: The wise have been known to provide this advice: if you hear crying in a woodland or forest that has become strangely quiet, run as quickly as you can— though it may already be too late. The cry of a Weeping Willow is difficult to ignore and has often led the unwary to an untimely demise.

A Weeping Willow is the unfortunate victim of a {@spell Curse of Conceited Obsession|GrimHollowPG24}. Once a vain or narcissistic individual, they become a twisted half-tree, half-humanoid creature warped by self-love and malicious intent.

A Weeping Willow is obsessed with its own appearance, calling for brave heroes to aid it in its distress. Upon reaching the Weeping Willow, however, heroes find only a vicious predator, a grove of unusual shimmering trees, and a very likely fate worse than death.

Combating a Weeping Willow unprepared often ends in disaster. The creature's enthralling cries and illusory beauty are difficult to resist, drawing its prey closer. The touch of a Weeping Willow can transform any creature's into a tree, bearing mirrored leaves for the vain creature to gaze into. Survivors of these encounters say that if you can resist the creature's malignant lure, it's best to leave them alone with their gardens of reflecting trees and self-admiration.

name: Wellwyrm

entries: {@i Serpent Lurking Beneath the Surface}

Wellwyrms are serpents originally touched by cruel Fey masters. The wyrms live in shallow waters where land-dwelling creatures frequent, such as wells and watering holes, lying in wait to coil around unsuspecting victims. Wellwyrms then drag their prey into water, or into burrows they dig under seemingly safe ground, to drown or suffocate.

entries.name: Secret
entries: The sound of a hunting horn drives wellwyrms into a panicked frenzy.

name: Wendel Somerton
entries: Mayor Somerton is an officious, self-important man of 50 years. His short, wide frame is constantly clad in finely tailored suits that barely hold his ever-growing girth. He wears a matching bowler hat on his bald head, and his bushy gray eyebrows and handlebar mustache are waxed to maintain their shapes. His cravats are decorated with a jeweled pin in the form of an oak leaf. He does not need, but always carries, a mahogany cane with an emerald handle.

While he is tolerant and even welcoming to people of all ideologies, Mayor Somerton strongly believes in the Old Ways along with his family. However, he is completely ignorant of the wicked intentions of the cult of the Crooked Queen and only knows Kehlenn as the Green Queen, whom he deeply reveres. He serves as the leader of the Followers of the Old Ways, leading worship of the Green Queen and heading the rituals and rites to harness her power.

This has made him a useful pawn of the nefarious cult of the Crooked Queen, unknowingly enacting the plans of her servants. The most impactful of these decisions was the gifting of the Lockwood Estate to {@creature Phillip Druskenvald|CrookedMoon24} and preparing for his potential arrival. While most townsfolk, and even Wendel himself, viewed the move as a political maneuver, the idea was planted in his head by {@creature Randall Graham|CrookedMoon24} (see area V7), who knows that {@creature Phillip Druskenvald|CrookedMoon24|Phillip} is the critical piece of the final ritual to free the Crooked Queen and unleash {@creature the Horned King|CrookedMoon24}.
During full moons, inhabitants of Etharis stay inside with the doors barred and windows tightly shut. Even then, they look at those indoors with them with a suspicious eye. One never knows.

entries.name: Salvage
entries: Lycanthropes exist in a state of perpetual mental turmoil, and over time their memories fragment. As a result, many carry keepsakes of their past lives to strengthen the memories they do not want to lose. The pelt of a lycanthrope is prized by certain mages for the crafting of magical cloaks, particularly cloaks that allow a person to change their form such as the cloak of the bat or the cloak of the manta ray.

Weapons made from the fangs or claws of deceased lycanthropes have special properties and are known as {@item lycan weapon|GrimHollowLairsEtharis|lycan weapons} (see Appendix A of {@adventure Lairs of Etharis|GrimHollowLairsEtharis|21}). These weapons require a successful {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check by a proficient weaponsmith, consuming 500 gp worth of components, and requiring 10 days of work.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
items.entry: Lycanthropy is a common affliction in Etharis. The source is a curse that twists mind and body into that of a savage beast. Though they can change at will, the light of the full moon triggers the transformation no matter what.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
items.entry: In addition to the normal transmission of the curse through the bite of a lycanthrope, certain druidic sects also perform rituals to create new lycanthropes. This ritual is known as the Lunar Sacrament, used as a tool to protect druid groves from invasion.

items.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}):
items.entry: While the nature of the transformation tends to override the senses with bestial fury, some can control themselves. By finding a balance between man and beast, they gain greater control over the curse, gaining the ability to turn into a full animal and retain their mental faculties.

entries: During full moons, inhabitants of Etharis stay inside with the doors barred and windows tightly shut. Even then, they look at those indoors with them with a suspicious eye. One never knows.
